From infrastructure completion to market outcomes: cold-chain commissioning and tomato price instability in India
abstract: Introduction Whether completed cold-chain infrastructure translates into measurable market outcomes depends on the step from commissioning to actual service delivery. Methods We link India's Ministry of Food Processing Industries registers to monthly district wholesale prices (2013–2023) and evaluate the first documented commissioning of fruit-and-vegetable cold-chain projects. The primary outcome is the absolute exact-calendar-year-on-year change in tomato log modal price relative to the mean of onion and potato. Because these comparison commodities may also use cold-chain services, the parameter captures a differential commodity effect rather than the program's total price effect. We compare 20 commissioning districts with 59 unique same-state matched controls across common pre/post-commissioning windows, using stack weights that preserve the intended comparison. The 20 districts are a subset of 34 candidates, limiting external validity. Results During months 0–23, the corrected estimate is 0.0112 (standard error 0.0206; 95% confidence interval −0.0298 to 0.0521; conventional p = 0.588; wild-cluster-bootstrap p = 0.581). The equal-weight mean across 20 district comparisons is 0.0099 (95% confidence interval −0.0300 to 0.0497). A matching sensitivity fixed before outcome estimation reduces the pooled tomato pretrend standardized difference from 0.323 to 0.039 while retaining 1…

title: From Individual Learning to Market Equilibrium: Correcting Structural and Parametric Biases in RL Simulations of Economic Models
abstract: Abstract Applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to economic modeling reveals a fundamental tension: standard RL agents do not behave as competitive price-takers. While macroeconomic models typically assume agents take aggregate conditions as given, a naive single-agent RL algorithm learns to internalize its impact on the environment, effectively exerting market power. We illustrate this divergence in a search-and-matching model with concave production, showing that a standard RL agent converges to a monopsonistic allocation rather than the competitive equilibrium. Furthermore, we show that RL’s approach to time discounting distorts standard intertemporal economic trade-offs. To resolve these issues, we propose a Calibrated Mean-Field Reinforcement Learning framework that restricts the agent to optimize against an exogenous aggregate state to restore price-taking behavior, and recalibrates the RL reward structure to reflect true economic opportunity costs. By iteratively updating the aggregate state, our algorithm converges to a stationary fixed point that recovers the competitive equilibrium. This approach provides a method for embedding learning algorithms into dynamic general equilibrium models.

title: Vives, Erasmus, and the German–Speaking Book Market
abstract: Abstract The following contribution examines the relationship between Juan Luis Vives and Erasmus of Rotterdam within the framework of the early modern book market. It highlights two interrelated aspects: Erasmus’s abrupt resentment and withdrawal from a previously close personal and intellectual friendship, and the resulting displacement of Vives from the entire German–language book market due to Erasmus’s dominant influence. This process, which was simultaneously an expression of the marginalisation of a rising competitor, becomes all the more evident as Vives’s works concurrently found significant resonance in other markets and, later, in Reformed circles, particularly in Zurich. The paper concludes that Vives’s defensive behaviour towards Erasmus demonstrates how persistence and diplomatic skill can overcome both personal resentments and dominant market positions, ultimately paving the way for long–term scholarly prestige.

title: Modeling Response Processes to Achieve an Appropriate Factor Structure for the Bafacalo Logical Reasoning Test
abstract: Responses to reasoning tests may reflect not only the ability the tests were designed to measure but also response processes distinct from that ability, which can obscure their factor structure when left unmodeled. The BAFACALO Logical Reasoning Test has been openly available since 2021, but the previous factorial study relied on specific factors derived from an exploratory analysis and on an estimator that treats dichotomous items as continuous, and its model fell just short of acceptable fit. As a syllogism-based test, it is open to response processes such as illicit conversion, the atmosphere effect, and acquiescence. This study reexamines its factorial validity by modeling these response processes, with data from 292 Brazilian public high school students. Five confirmatory factor models were compared: a unidimensional model, the bifactor model of the previous study, and three bifactor models with theory-driven specific factors for illicit conversion and the atmosphere effect, for acquiescence, and for both. Models were estimated with WLSMV and, for comparison, ML and MLMV. No model reached acceptable fit with ML or MLMV. With WLSMV, only the models including illicit conversion and the atmosphere effect were acceptable, and the model that also included acquiescence was selected. The general factor (logical reasoning) and the illicit conversion and atmosphere effect factor sh…

title: Identification of miRNA targets in hop (Humulus lupulus L.) in response to Verticillium nonalfalfae infection using degradome sequencing
abstract: Verticillium wilt is a vascular plant disease caused by soil-borne fungi of the genus Verticillium sensu stricto. Verticillium species infect many agriculturally important plants, including hops ( Humulus lupulus L.), which are cultivated for the brewing and pharmaceutical industries. In our previous study, we investigated the interaction between hops and species Verticillium nonalfalfae at the miRNA level and identified miRNAs showing differential expression between resistant and susceptible hop cultivars during the early phase of infection. In the present study, we performed hop degradome sequencing using two libraries per cultivar, prepared separately from mock-inoculated and V. nonalfalfae -inoculated plants, each library consisting of pooled samples collected at multiple time points during infection. In total, 399 target genes for 76 miRNAs were identified, of which 142 were detected exclusively in the resistant cultivar. Gene Ontology and KEGG analyses revealed that resistant-specific targeted genes are mainly involved in transcriptional regulation, protein metabolism, and stress responses, with enrichment in plant–pathogen interaction pathways. Of the seven degradome-identified miRNA-targeted genes analyzed, expression profiling revealed cultivar-dependent temporal responses. LOV1 was significantly downregulated in both cultivars, with an earlier response in susceptible …

Cell-informed host-response profiling distinguishes neutrophil-like and PLA2G7-associated immunometabolic axes in systemic infection
abstract: Background Whole-blood host-response signatures can distinguish infection-positive from infection-negative systemic inflammation, but their signal combines changes in leucocyte composition with regulation within cells. We asked whether a retrospectively selected and subsequently fixed blood transcriptomic framework could relate candidate transcripts to granulocyte-associated and monocyte/macrophage-associated expression contexts rather than serve as another stand-alone diagnostic product. Methods A 12-gene framework was retrospectively derived from four contrasts across three studies (444 contrast-level observations; 443 unique arrays) and subsequently fixed for external evaluation using a single-sample transcriptome-rank score. Performance was examined separately across cohorts with different specimens, age groups and comparators. Transcript-score sensitivity analyses, donor-level whole-blood single-cell pseudobulk and cell-line qRT-PCR were used to assess candidate localization and cell-line expression-context concordance. Cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation and colocalisation were included as exploratory genetic context. Results In the closest target-context cohort, GSE134347, the fixed score achieved an AUROC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.764–0.889) for sepsis versus non-infectious critical illness. Performance was lower in pediatric day-1 SIRS comparisons, indicating dependence on popul…

Beyond the laggard myth: time-series analysis of AI job market dynamics in construction
abstract: Purpose This study presents one of the first time-series, cross-industry analyses of the artificial intelligence (AI) job market for the construction sector. It benchmarks construction against both digital and traditional industries to interrogate prevailing assumptions of linear diffusion and temporal catch-up in AI workforce adoption. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on 51 months of Lightcast job postings (January 2021–March 2025), with construction defined as ANZSIC Division E, the study employs an interpretable analytical toolkit comprising Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess decomposition (period = 12), month-of-year bootstrap tests on detrended series, cross-correlation analysis with bootstrap confidence bands, Newey–West trend estimation on sectoral share ratios and conservative one-step Exponential Smoothing State-Space (ETS) forecasts. All results are re-estimated excluding the partial final month (March 2025) as a sensitivity check. Findings Construction's AI hiring is very sparse, accounting for under 1% of AI postings and is more volatile than hiring in peer sectors, but it grew fastest: annual construction postings rose more than fourfold between 2021 and 2024, against increases of 13% and 9% in the digital and traditional sectors, whose postings peaked in 2022. title: Patient- derived gallbladder cancer organoids mirror tumor genetics and resistance phenotypes, enabling ex vivo testing of adjuvant chemotherapy response
abstract: Abstract Background Advanced gallbladder cancer (GBC) is an aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis, high recurrence rates, and limited treatment options. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) have emerged as promising preclinical models that faithfully mimic the epithelial architecture of tumors, offering valuable insights into cancer biology, drug resistance, and potential therapeutic strategies. Despite advances in GBC research, well-characterized GBC PDOs are lacking, and their potential to reflect patient-specific adjuvant chemotherapy outcomes and identify resistance-associated pathways remains underexplored. Methods In this study, we established and characterized eight PDOs from a cohort of Chilean patients with resectable advanced (stage IIIA and IIIB) and metastatic (stage IV) GBC. Histological analysis, whole-exome sequencing, and confocal microscopy were used to compare PDOs with their parental primary tumors. Ex vivo drug response assays with 5-FU, cisplatin, and gemcitabine were performed and compared with clinical response from patients. Gemcitabine-resistant PDOs were characterized by Tandem Mass Tag (TMT)-based quantitative proteomic, coupled with screening of 103 FDA-approved compounds to identify alternative therapeutic vulnerabilities. Results We successfully generated GBC-PDOs from 66.7% (8/12) of patient samples, and these organoids closely recapitulated the h…

title: Effect of Environmental and Ethical Disclosures on Market Value of Listed Consumer Goods Firms in Nigeria
abstract: The study examined the effect of environmental and ethical disclosures on the market value of listed consumer goods firms in Nigeria using a sample of 16 firms selected using purposive sampling technique from a population of 24 listed consumer goods sector firms. The study employed secondary data extracted from the annual report of the firm from 2014 to 2025 and adopted the Panel Corrected Standard Error regression technique to analyze the data. The result revealed that environmental disclosure does not significantly influence the market value of listed consumer goods firms in Nigeria. However, ethical disclosure has a significant negative effect on the market value of the listed consumer goods firm. The study recommended that disclosure should focus on areas that directly improve operational efficiency such as energy conservation, waste reduction, and resource efficiency which have positive links to firm value.

A paradox theory perspective of boundary spanning gains and losses: locally hired parent country nationals in emerging market multinational corporations
abstract: Purpose This study, by examining how locally hired parent country nationals (PCNs) in emerging market multinational corporations (EMNCs) experience and manage paradoxical tensions through boundary-spanning practices, provides an integrative perspective of how the gains and losses of boundary spanning are co-produced. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on 73 semi-structured interviews with locally hired PCNs and organizational expatriates in Chinese MNC subsidiaries in Japan, this study employs an abductive analysis informed by paradox theory to identify boundary-spanning roles and the paradoxes associated with locally hired PCNs. Findings Locally hired PCNs enact four boundary-spanning roles – coordinative link-pin, relational broker, operational mediator, and knowledge facilitator – that expose them to performing, belonging, organizing, and learning paradoxes. The same practices that provide benefits also create strain and vulnerability, suggesting that gains and losses are interdependent and co-produced. Furthermore, the findings suggest that paradox management reproduces and intensifies tensions for boundary spanners. Originality/value This study advances boundary-spanning research by theorizing gain–loss interdependence and conceptualizing boundary spanning as a paradox management practice. It also extends paradox theory by demonstrating how managing paradoxes may reinforc…

title: Response of sunflower varieties to silicon in the coastal region of Bangladesh
abstract: Silicon is known as a beneficial plant nutrient element; however, its beneficial role in sunflower grown at coastal ecosystem of Bangladesh is yet not documented. This experiment was conducted in a coastal region to examine the effect of Si supplementation on the growth, yield and Si uptake of different varieties of sunflower. The experiment was set at Kartikpasha village of Dumki upazila, Patuakhali district during Rabi (dry) season of 2024. The field trial followed 2- factorial design with two doses of Si (0 and 60 kg Si ha-1 from CaSiO3) and six varieties of sunflower (Chuni1, Chuni2, Unisun, Hysun36, BARI surjomukhi1, and BARI surjomukhi2). Silicon application to soil significantly increased seed and straw yields of sunflower showing 2.97 and 5.23 t ha-1 in 60 kg Si ha-1 treatment, and 2.76 and 4.64 t ha-1 in Si control treatment, respectively. Silicon application had greater effect on straw yield than on seed yield. However, varieties Chuni2, Unisun, Hysun36 and BARI surjomukhi2 were found more responsive to Si application. The Si concentration of straw widely varied showing a range of 0.80-1.57 % over the varieties, with no significant variation for Chuni1 and Chuni2 varieties. Thus, Si application at 60 kg ha-1 rate could be suggested for improvement of yield and Si concentration of sunflower having Unisun, Hysun36, BARI surjomukhi1 and BARI surjomukhi2 identified as hig…

Triglyceride-glucose index and the incidence of peripheral artery disease: a dose-response meta-analysis of longitudinal studies
abstract: Background The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been increasingly investigated as a predictor of cardiovascular diseases. However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD. Methods PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched from inception to June 28, 2026. Longitudinal observational studies evaluating the association between the conventional TyG index and incidents PAD in adults were eligible. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) comparing the highest versus lowest TyG categories were calculated using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models. Linear and nonlinear dose-response meta-analyses were performed using restricted cubic spline models. Results Five longitudinal studies involving 417,499 participants and 7,800 incident PAD events were included. Compared with the lowest TyG category, a high TyG index was associated with a significantly increased risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.49, 95% CI 1.06 to 2.10; p = 0.02), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I 2 = 88.4%). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated robust findings. In the linear…

title: Conscious entrapment: how institutional modalities produce response–resolution decoupling on a Chinese online governance platform
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how institutional modalities produce and sustain the response–resolution decoupling on a Chinese online governance platform, addressing the gap between quantitative findings on what correlates with responsiveness and qualitative understanding of how it operates. Design/methodology/approach This paper involves a qualitative single case study combining document analysis with semi-structured interviews with practitioners involved in platform-based responsiveness, analyzed through structuration theory’s three modalities (signification, domination and legitimation) and their recursive interplay. Findings Three modalities jointly produce response–resolution decoupling (RQ1). Interpretive schemes construct demands through power-laden priority logics. Through power relations, scarce resources are channeled toward response production. Normative justifications, meanwhile, reward procedural compliance over resolution. Their recursive interaction reproduces the decoupling (RQ2), an unintentional structural emergence where actors recognize the gap yet cannot escape it (“conscious entrapment”). Case-grounded conjectures derived from the analysis are offered for further testing. Practical implications Partial reform risks are absorbed by the unreformed dimensions of the system. Breaking the recursive cycle requires action across all three modalities simultan…

When technologies transform: a consideration of open innovation's contributions to operations management
abstract: Purpose This paper examines what an open innovation (OI) perspective contributes to operations and supply chain management when a technology transition reshapes an industry. Earlier operations management research implicitly defined OI as a small set of isolated practices. This paper recovers its fuller depth as bidirectional knowledge flows and a mindset anchored in the business model. Design/methodology/approach The study traces innovation in the global automotive industry across three phases, then develops illustrative case studies of four Chinese electric vehicle (EV) entrants, Kandi, BYD, Xiaomi and Chery, analyzed through outside-in flows, inside-out flows and business model innovation. The cases build on a structured review of Chinese-language academic and industry literature, corroborated against company reports, trade press and industry data. Findings Chinese EVs have attained industry leadership, yet no dominant EV innovation strategy has emerged. All four firms drew heavily, but differently, on external knowledge, much of it from consumer electronics and smartphones, outside the automotive supply chain and each treated the vehicle as a platform. BYD and Chery also pursued inside-out flows, BYD through divisionalization and an open vehicle architecture, Chery through technology exports and internal suppliers. The contribution runs both ways: OI extends operations manag…

title: When processing feels smooth: brand placement mode and contextual influences on purchase intentions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to use processing fluency as an integrative lens to examine why placement prominence does not yield a stable persuasive advantage and how contextual influences shape explicit and implicit placement effectiveness in narrative media. Design/methodology/approach Four between-subjects experiments (2 × 2 factorial designs) were conducted using authentic Korean drama clips. Each study examined one potential disruption source: product category, brand familiarity, endorser image valence or parasocial interaction, comparing explicit and implicit placement with purchase intention as the dependent variable (n = 616). Findings Results were consistent with a processing-fluency explanation. Product category and parasocial interaction (PSI) each interacted with placement mode (ps < 0.001): explicit placement favored search goods and low-PSI characters, whereas implicit placement favored experience goods and high-PSI characters. Brand familiarity moderated effects (p = 0.039), with a larger implicit-placement advantage for unfamiliar brands. The endorser-valence study showed main effects only. Practical implications Managers should tailor placement modes to contextual conditions rather than maximize visibility, reducing potential disruption to viewing experiences and enhancing purchase intentions. title: Constructing the Adjudication Standard for Interest Attribution under the Accelerated Maturity System for Subscribed Capital Contributions: An Interest-Balancing Analysis of the "Storage Rule" and the "Direct Settlement Rule"
abstract: Article 54 of China's Company Law as revised in 2023 establishes a system of accelerated maturity for subscribed capital contributions, yet it does not specify how the resulting interests are to be attributed once shareholders have paid their contributions ahead of schedule, which has given rise to major controversy in both theory and judicial practice. Judicial interpretations and judicial practice have not yet produced uniform adjudication standards on this point, instead, the matter is largely left to the judge's discretion in the light of the circumstances of each case. In the absence of a unified adjudicative framework, divergent judgments readily emerge. This paper therefore undertakes an in-depth balancing and comparison of the interests involved in the "storage rule" and the "direct settlement rule." Proceeding from the principles of the independence of legal-person property, the equal protection of creditors, and the prohibition of the abuse of rights, it constructs an adjudication standard whose principal factors are the company's bankruptcy status, the exercise of rights by other creditors, and the recovery rate. It ultimately advocates clarifying, through systematic adjudication criteria, the attribution of the relevant interests in contributed capital once shareholders have paid their contributions in advance.

title: How firms achieve Quality 4.0 implementation performance: a configurational analysis of Chinese manufacturing
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify pathways to Quality 4.0 (Q4.0) implementation performance across digital contexts from a configurational perspective, addressing underexplored context dependence in Q4.0 outcomes. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from manufacturing firms in Jiangsu Province, China. Necessary condition analysis (NCA) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) were combined to identify necessary conditions and sufficient configurations for high and non-high Q4.0 implementation performance. Firm size was incorporated to compare configurational patterns between small firms and medium- and large-sized firms. Findings First, Q4.0 implementation is context-dependent, with digital maturity serving as a boundary condition. Second, multiple equifinal configurations lead to high performance. Small firms exhibit greater configurational diversity through three distinct combinations of organisational resources, digital-quality capabilities and process digitalisation, whereas medium and large firms converge on one synergistic configuration. Third, non-high performance is consistently associated with the absence of organisational resources, highlighting a key source of transformation traps. Originality/value This study advances Q4.0 and quality management research by identifying equifinal pathways to implementation performance. It demonstrat…

Prevalence and Management of Suspected and Confirmed Bloodstream Infections Among Acute Leukaemia Patients Receiving Chemotherapy at Kenyatta National Hospital, Kenya
abstract: Patients with acute leukaemia receiving chemotherapy are highly susceptible to infection because of disease-related immune dysfunction, chemotherapy-induced neutropenia, mucosal injury, and frequent use of invasive vascular devices. However, evidence on bloodstream infection and its management in this population in Kenya remains limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of suspected and confirmed bloodstream infection and to evaluate antibiotic utilisation and adherence to evidence-based treatment guidelines among patients with acute leukaemia receiving chemotherapy in adult wards at Kenyatta National Hospital. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using medical records of patients aged ≥13 years with acute myeloid or acute lymphoblastic leukaemia who received chemotherapy in adult wards at Kenyatta National Hospital between January 2018 and December 2025. Of 332 eligible records identified after screening, 139 were selected using simple random sampling. Data were abstracted using a structured tool and analysed descriptively with IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. Of 139 patients, 58 (41.7%; 95% confidence interval: 33.4–50.4%, exact Clopper–Pearson method) met the composite definition of bloodstream infection. Of these, 12 (20.7% of cases; 8.6% of all patients) were microbiologically confirmed and 46 (79.3% of cases; 33.1% of all patients) were clinicall…

title: Fosetyl-Al stem injection for chestnut ink disease management: efficacy and dose-dependent phytotoxicity in saplings
abstract: Abstract Fosetyl-Al (aluminium tris-(ethyl phosphonate)) is a low-toxicity phosphonate commonly used to control oomycete-related diseases in crops. Trunk injection (endotherapy) delivers the fungicide directly into the vascular system, potentially improving efficacy while reducing off-target losses. This two-year study evaluated the efficacy and phytotoxicity of stem-injected fosetyl-Al to manage ink disease caused by Phytophthora cinnamomi in Castanea sativa saplings. Fifty saplings received fosetyl-Al injections at 0–4% using pressurized devices, followed by stem inoculation with the pathogen; a 2% soil irrigation treatment was included for comparison. Stem injections at 1%, 2% and 4% significantly suppressed stem necrosis after inoculation with P. cinnamomi and reduced root infections compared to irrigation and untreated control. Protection persisted for at least two years as reflected by reduced relative Area Under the Disease Progress Curve (rAUDPC) values. However, stem injections also induced phytotoxic symptoms, including leaf burn, necrosis, and occasional plant death, with a clear dose-dependent relationship. Most plants recovered from moderate phytotoxicity, whereas irreversible damage occurred at the highest doses, highlighting the critical need for precise dose adjustments, particularly in small-diameter trees. title: System or self: the role of slaveholding on Congressional behavior in the US North, 1789−1861
abstract: We use the 2022 Washington Post’s database of congressional enslavers to ask how much the direct interest of Northern politicians in slavery affected voting. Comparing systemic to self-interest parallels efforts to replace vocabulary, e.g., slaveholder with enslaver, which emphasizes individual agency (and culpability) over societal constraints. Northern slaveholders voted differently from their non-slaveholding Northern colleagues. But this gap was much smaller than the overall North−South divide. Slaveholding had minimal explanatory power over voting in both chambers, except for two periods in the Senate, notably in the 1850s with a slaveholding cluster. But the rise of the GOP diminished their power.

title: Research on early content virality recognition integrating morphological features and signal-to-noise separation features of signals
abstract: Purpose To overcome the inability of existing approaches to detect weak, multimodal and emerging early signs of virality, this study proposes a novel recognition framework. By integrating morphological and signal-to-noise separation (SNS) features, the framework accurately identifies authentic viral signals and predicts their growth trajectories. Design/methodology/approach The proposed framework constructs content signal morphology by combining multimodal sentiment analysis based on BERT and ViT, CRITIC-based influence weighting and HDBSCAN clustering. Three SNS features, frequency orderliness, temporal dependency and semantic novelty, are extracted to characterize the separation between emerging viral signals and background noise. An LSTM model is then employed for dynamic classification of early-stage virality signals. Findings Experiments conducted on a large-scale Sina Weibo dataset demonstrate that the integrated framework significantly outperforms traditional approaches and single-feature baselines in terms of precision, recall and overall accuracy. The results confirm the complementary and synergistic effects of morphological and SNS features in distinguishing authentic early-stage virality signals from noisy content streams. Originality/value This study advances early content virality recognition by integrating signal morphology and SNS features within a unified analyt…

title: The Effect of Member Participation in Cocoa Farming Product Marketing on Cooperative Business Performance: Empirical Evidence from Sisa Hasil Usaha (SHU) at KSU Sendana Baru
abstract: Cooperatives depend on active member participation as both owners and users to maintain sustainable business performance. In agricultural cooperatives, especially those involved in cocoa marketing, members’ transactional participation through marketing activities has a strategic role in strengthening business capacity and generating economic benefits reflected in cooperative surplus. However, empirical research specifically examining the contribution of member participation in agricultural product marketing to cooperative business performance remains limited. This study aims to analyze the effect of member participation in cocoa marketing activities on cooperative business performance measured by Sisa Hasil Usaha (SHU) at KSU Sendana Baru, Majene Regency. This research employed a quantitative approach with an associative research design. The study involved 273 cooperative members as the population, with 50 members selected as respondents using proportional random sampling. Data were collected through Likert-scale questionnaires and supported by cooperative administrative documents. Data analysis was conducted using validity and reliability tests, simple linear regression analysis, t-test, and coefficient of determination (R²) to examine the effect of member participation on cooperative business performance. title: The role, challenges, and innovations of rifampin in the management of periprosthetic joint infections: a narrative review
abstract: Abstract Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains a severe complication due to persistent bacterial biofilms. Rifampin is traditionally valued for its unique biofilm-penetrating properties, yet its clinical role is increasingly viewed as context-dependent. While current evidence supports the efficacy of rifampin in two-stage revision arthroplasty, its application in debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) remains a subject of ongoing debate. Landmark randomized trials once reported superior cure rates for DAIR combined with rifampin, but contemporary large-scale retrospective data show no statistically significant difference in remission rates, often accompanied by a significantly higher incidence of adverse events. Furthermore, the timing of administration is critical; early initiation within five days post-DAIR has been linked to increased treatment failure. These challenges, alongside profound drug-drug interactions, have spurred interest in localized delivery innovations like microencapsulation and nanoparticles. While these bioengineering approaches show preclinical promise in overcoming PMMA chemical incompatibility, they remain at the proof-of-concept stage. Consequently, rifampin should be employed as a targeted adjunct rather than a universal standard, requiring careful consideration of surgical strategy, patient tolerance, and optimal timing.

title: Urgent Challenges for Improving Competition Policy
abstract: The author proposes the participation of specialists from antitrust authorities of each country in cooperation with international structures to develop an adequate joint policy against unfair collusions. This work presents a paradigm-shifting “atomic” model of perfect competition, positing that market efficiency is governed not by the sheer quantity agents, but by the structural, bipolar balance within the market core. For practical recommendations for maximally fast economic improvement, driving a theoretical parallel with physics electrodynamics, we adapt Ohm’s Law to formalize the natural strength of competition. We demonstrate that artificial market oversaturation with countless micro-agents induces severe transactional friction, leading to systemic “short-circuits” characterized by structural crises. The findings offer a new physics-grounded diagnostic framework by antitrust regulation for market stabilization and author presents principles for maintaining of maximally perfect competition against hidden monopolies.
venue: London Journal of Research in Management and Business

title: Risk-sensitive safe reinforcement learning for joint cyber insurance and cybersecurity investment planning in cyber-physical power systems
abstract: Abstract Cyber insurance and cybersecurity investment are tightly coupled in smart grids because cyberattacks can produce physical outages, financial losses, regulatory exposure, and insurance claims through the same operating event. This study develops a risk-sensitive safe reinforcement learning framework for joint cyber insurance and defense investment planning in cyber-physical power systems. The formulation treats the utility as a sequential decision maker that observes physical grid states, cyber exposure, insurance contract status, posterior threat beliefs, and budget conditions, and then selects coverage, deductible, hardening, monitoring, redundancy, backup-control, and incident-response actions. The framework combines a constrained Markov decision process, conditional value-at-risk loss control, an optimal power flow (OPF) safety shield, and a Benders-style decomposition between long-term policy learning and short-term security correction. The mathematical presentation separates model-specific cyber-physical-insurance equations from standard reinforcement-learning components, so that the novel coupling among insurance, defense, physical feasibility, and tail-risk control remains explicit. A simulation benchmark on IEEE test systems evaluates expected cost, 95% CVaR, physical-security violations, shield corrections, policy sensitivity, and belief-update degradation. Un…

title: Orchestrating inter-organizational technology networks to build data analytics capability: the case of a professional service firm
abstract: Purpose This study examines how professional service firms (PSFs) orchestrate inter-organizational technology networks to develop data analytics capability. Adopting an organizational information processing perspective, we examine how PSFs vary orchestration modes across networks to mobilize distributed resources and increase their information-processing capacity. Design/methodology/approach We conducted a longitudinal single-case study of a global PSF in the UK construction sector, triangulating 37 interviews with observations and project documentation. Using an abductive theory-elaboration approach, we explain how the PSF accessed, bundled and leveraged network-embedded resources to build analytics capability. Findings We identify three interrelated components of analytics capability: data capture, data transformation and processing, and data visualization and interpretation. Closed-mode orchestration enabled standardized data capture across the supply network; hybrid orchestration combined broad open engagement with selective closure to integrate technological expertise from SMEs; and open-mode orchestration within the client network fostered use-case elicitation, sensemaking and interpretive alignment. We theorize how inter-organizational network orchestration enables PSFs to assemble information-processing capacity from distributed data, technical expertise and interpretiv…

Perioperative pulmonary embolus: diagnosis, classification and management
abstract: Post-surgical patients are vulnerable to the development of pulmonary emboli, a condition associated with significant mortality and morbidity. This review discusses the diagnosis, classification and treatment modalities available for pulmonary emboli. A pulmonary embolus is diagnosed by amalgamating clinical symptoms, signs, blood tests and imaging results. The European Society of Cardiology schema is commonly used to risk stratify patients with a pulmonary embolus. The treatments available are medical (oral anticoagulation and systemic thrombolysis), interventional (catheter-directed treatments) and surgical (embolectomy). This review aims to discuss these domains with a perioperative focus, acknowledging the uncertainty associated with decision-making surrounding bleeding risk with perioperative anticoagulation.

title: THE REGIONAL SOCIAL ECONOMY SUPPORT SYSTEM AS AN ORGANIZATIONAL FIELD: THE ROLE OF REGIONAL CENTRES FOR SOCIAL POLICY IN COORDINATING ACTORS AND RESOURCES
abstract: This article examines the regional social economy support system as an organizational field, focusing on the role of Regional Centres for Social Policy (ROPS) in coordinating its actors. The analytical framework combines organizational field theory with a governance perspective, which explains non-hierarchical mechanisms of cooperation and interest alignment, and a systems approach, which captures flows of information and resources between the support system and its environment. The analysis draws on legislation, policy documents, materials concerning the social economy support system in Małopolska, the activities of the Małopolska Social Economy Development Committee, and findings from regional research and evaluations. The findings show that the regional social economy field comprises actors with complementary but unevenly distributed resources, whose interdependence persists despite the formal allocation of responsibilities.…

title: Brand Image, Advertising, and Product Quality Effects on Consina Purchase Intention in Bogor
abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of brand image, advertising, and product quality on consumers’ purchase intention toward Consina products in Bogor City. This study employed a quantitative research method, with data collected through questionnaires distributed to 150 respondents who use Consina products. The data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, and t-tests and F-tests. The results indicate that brand image, advertising, and product quality each have a positive and statistically significant effect on purchase intention. Simultaneously, these three variables also have a significant effect on purchase intention. These findings suggest that strengthening brand image, implementing appropriate advertising strategies, and improving product quality can increase consumers’ purchase intention toward Consina products in Bogor City.

title: Organizational ambidexterity and green performance in emerging markets: examining the role of environmental dynamism in sustainability-oriented performance management
abstract: Purpose This study examines how organizational ambidexterity influences green performance in emerging market firms and investigates the role of environmental dynamism as a contextual condition shaping this relationship. Responding to growing calls within productivity and performance management research for sustainability-oriented performance frameworks, the study explores how firms integrate exploratory innovation and exploitative efficiency to achieve environmental performance outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed using data collected from 249 firms operating in the Greater Kumasi Metropolitan Area of Ghana. Structural equation modeling using Analysis of Moment Structure was applied to test the direct effects of organizational ambidexterity and environmental dynamism on green performance, as well as the moderating influence of environmental dynamism. Findings The results show that organizational ambidexterity significantly enhances green performance, demonstrating that firms capable of balancing exploratory innovation with exploitative efficiency achieve superior environmental outcomes. Environmental dynamism also exhibits a strong positive direct effect on green performance. However, contrary to contingency expectations, environmental dynamism does not significantly moderate the relationship between ambidexterity and g…
venue: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management

title: Bureaucratic Reform and Regional Financial Management Quality in Relation to Audit Findings: The Moderating Role of Local Government Integrity
abstract: Background: Indonesian local governments reported rising numbers of audit findings in 2021–2023 despite ongoing bureaucratic reforms. It remains unclear whether formal reform and financial-management assessments are associated with fewer findings, and whether institutional integrity modifies these associations. Objective: To examine the associations of bureaucratic reform and regional financial-management quality with audit findings and evaluate whether government integrity moderates either association. Methods: This observational quantitative panel study analyzed 381 of 508 Indonesian regency/city governments during 2021–2023 (1,143 government-year observations), using official secondary data. Fixed-effects panel regression and moderated regression analysis (MRA) assessed the relationships. Results: Bureaucratic reform was positively associated with the number of findings (β = 0.694747, p = 0.0012); financial-management quality showed no statistically significant association (β = 0.024320, p = 0.0967). The reform × integrity interaction was negative and significant (β = −0.082746, p = 0.0229), whereas the financial-management quality × integrity interaction was not significant (β = −0.001859, p = 0.4507). Conclusion: Higher-rated bureaucratic reform and regional financial management quality have not been associated with a corresponding reduction in the number of audit findings…

title: A new lease on life? A survival analysis approach to the study of professional sport stadiums and arenas
abstract: Purpose The length of time that a sport facility remains in use is a critical piece of information for sport organizations and the municipalities that allocate hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars to fund them, rather than contributing funding to societal issues. Despite this fact, prior approaches have either truncated their durations at present day or arbitrarily analyzed subsets of data. Design/methodology/approach As a solution, we analyze a dataset of more than 200 professional sport facilities using survival analysis, and discuss differences based on type of facility, tenants, and whether it is a single or multi-tenant facility. Findings Results indicate that lifetimes vary based on whether measures of central tendency or survival methods are applied. Specifically, results reveal that facility lifetimes are considerably longer than previously calculated. Research limitations/implications This study makes a unique and novel contribution to the stadium literature in its utilization of an advanced data analysis technique to quantify the lifetime of sport facilities. Practical implications These results provide empirical evidence that municipalities negotiating with sport franchises may have a substantiation for significantly longer lease agreements, a novel managerial implication. Originality/value These data may be used by financiers to better assess and plan for the im…
venue: Sport, Business and Management: An International Journal

title: Perceived authenticity in ethnic and cultural restaurants: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Purpose This study aims to address fragmented evidence on perceived authenticity in restaurant contexts by developing an integrated understanding of its key antecedents and customer outcomes in ethnic and cultural dining settings. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review identified 100 studies, with 50 meeting the inclusion criteria for meta-analytic synthesis. Effect sizes were synthesized using random-effects models, and moderator analyses were performed to examine the roles of culture, age and gender. Findings Perceived authenticity is strongly shaped by tangible cues, particularly brand image and food quality. In turn, authenticity exerts robust positive effects on customer satisfaction, revisit intention and word of mouth. Moderator analyses further show that individualism strengthens the authenticity–positive emotion relationship, that older consumers place greater emphasis on authenticity in forming memorable dining experiences and that female customers are more sensitive to interpersonal cues. Practical implications The findings provide guidance for restaurant managers on developing and communicating authentic dining experiences in ways that support favorable customer responses. They also highlight the value of considering cultural and demographic differences when designing and delivering authenticity-related experiences. Originality/value This study c…
venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Reported expulsion and displacement of the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system in women with adenomyosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Forecasting geopolitical and trade policy uncertainties for ESG stock markets in developed and developing countries
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the influence of trade policy uncertainty (TPU) and geopolitical uncertainty (GPU) on ESG stock performance and further examines their interconnectedness across developing and developed markets. Design/methodology/approach This study used GARCH-MIDAS and DCC-GARCH techniques for data analysis. The study collected monthly and daily TPU and GPU data from https://www.matteoiacoviello.com/. The daily data of ESG Leader indexes were obtained from MSCI and span from 2014 to 2024. Findings The findings show that ESG stocks serve as a safe-haven asset, making them an attractive option during times of GPU. ESG stocks tend to increase significantly during periods of high GPU, reinforcing that ESG stocks remain resilient. This highlights their potential as a reliable choice for investors navigating turbulent market conditions. It gives high returns during periods of uncertainty. ESG stocks are a strategic option for those seeking growth and stability in their portfolio. The Results found a positive impact of TPU on UESGL, CESGL and JESGL, while a negative influence on CHESGL and IESGL, reflecting the sensitivity of these markets to regulatory rigidity and trade disruptions. The DCC-GARCH results indicate that UESGL, CESGL and JESGL act as net receivers of shocks while CHESGL and IESGL serve as net transmitters. The result of net directional connectedness re…
venue: Journal of Economic and Administrative Sciences

title: Explainable hour-ahead traffic-volume forecasting with condition-stratified evaluation: an interstate I-94 case study
abstract: Introduction Hour-ahead traffic-volume forecasting can support traveler information, staffing, and advance corridor management. However, reliable evaluation requires attention to data quality, temporal variation, and forecasting uncertainty. This study evaluates an auditable, condition-stratified forecasting framework using traffic observations from westbound Interstate I-94 in Minnesota. Methods The Metro Interstate Traffic Volume dataset was audited for duplicate records, repeated timestamps, physically implausible rainfall observations, and missing hourly intervals. After preprocessing, 40,574 usable hourly timestamps yielded 28,855 valid gap-aware forecasting sequences with 24-hour input windows. The evaluated models included persistence, a 24-hour seasonal-naive baseline, LightGBM, XGBoost with and without weather variables, DLinear, GRU, a compact iTransformer-style model, and the Temporal-Mean Residual Network (TMRNet). Trainable models were evaluated using five prespecified random seeds. Performance was assessed through forecasting accuracy, paired statistical comparisons, direct forecasting horizons, rainfall-stratified errors, empirical prediction intervals, grouped permutation importance, TreeSHAP, and Integrated Gradients. Results XGBoost without weather achieved the lowest mean test MAE of 141.67 ± 0.31 vehicles/hour, followed by LightGBM (142.63 ± 0.41) and all-fe…

title: Spatial and vertical price transmission in potato markets in India
abstract: Purpose This paper has examined the dynamics of price transmission and co-movement across geographically dispersed markets and in the wholesale–retail supply chains for a perishable crop (potato) in eight major Indian cities, evaluating the interconnection among the wholesale and retail prices and market arrivals of the crop. Design/methodology/approach It has applied various unit-root tests, a standard vector autoregressive model, the Granger causality test and a correlation method to monthly potato prices and market arrivals data from January 2010 to December 2022. Findings It has offered evidence for spatial and vertical integration of potato markets. The wholesale prices were transmitted across the cities involved in potato trading. The prices were transmitted between wholesale and retail markets in most cases. While market arrivals have influenced the prices and marketing margins, these factors in turn have some effects on market arrivals in some cities. There exists evidence of significant co-movement of prices in the spatial and vertical markets. Research limitations/implications In the markets with significant cross-market price transmission, the effects and incentives of any policy are likely to be transmitted to all the markets without requiring much intervention. The policies to reduce price variability and enhance market integration should focus on facilitating trad…
venue: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies

title: Electric Vehicle Price Prediction Using Real-World Online Listings: An Explainable Machine Learning Approach
abstract: The recent gains in the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) have triggered the emergence of secondary markets concerning EVs, where the determination of prices accurately and transparently is an extreme challenge. In the current study, we propose an explainable machine learning model to predict the advertised price (in Jordanian dinars) of used EVs, using actual online advertisements obtained in the Jordanian market. An EV-oriented and custom-made dataset of 2,165 listings was used that specifically includes battery capacity and driving range along with the typical vehicle features. The coefficient of determination (R²), mean absolute error, and root mean squared error were used to assess the performance of three tree-based regressors: CatBoost Regressor, Extreme Gradient Boosting Regressor, and Random Forest Regressor trained with a leakage-safe pipeline and evaluated using grouped, repeated cross-validation. SHapley Additive exPlanations were applied to the fitted models to quantify the global contribution of each feature to price predictions and to assess the stability of these contributions across validation folds, providing a transparent account of the price-determination mechanism. The empirical data indicate that battery capacity and driving range are the most dominant EV price determinants that continue to overshadow conventional predictors of price, including brand, mi…
venue: Journal of Computational and Cognitive Engineering

title: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity and international positioning of carbon emission factors of electricity in China
abstract: In the context of China’s dual carbon goals, the electricity sector is both the primary source of carbon emissions and a key driver of socioeconomic development. A systematic assessment of the evolution of electricity carbon emission factors is critical for tracking electricity system decarbonization and formulating effective emission-reduction policies. This study develops an integrated analytical framework for examining the spatiotemporal heterogeneity and international positioning of electricity carbon emission factors of China. Based on official national- and provincial-level data, the framework combines the statistical analysis modules including spatiotemporal characteristics analysis, spatial autocorrelation analysis, policy-stage comparison, and international benchmarking to characterize the ECEF patterns. Results show that China’s electricity sector has achieved substantial low-carbon transition progress. Based on the available benchmark-year observations, China’s national average ECEF decreased by 13.03% between 2015 and 2023, while interprovincial disparities widened and maintained a “high in the north, low in the south” spatial pattern. The spatial correlation structure has continuously evolved, with weakened global positive spatial autocorrelation, contracted High-High and Low-Low clusters, and strengthened High-Low heterogeneity, indicating diminished geographic pr…

title: Neuro-symbolic AI for proactive risk forecasting: bridging large language models and dynamic Bayesian networks
abstract: Purpose Periodic risk reports constitute a substantial repository of operational data for project management. Despite the inherent informational value, archived records remain largely unstructured and highly fragmented. This study proposes a fully local neuro-symbolic approach for dynamic risk forecasting by translating qualitative project narratives into a quantifiable predictive engine to support decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The proposed methodology adopts a mixed-methods architecture including four layers: (1) spatial morphology reconstruction using a Y-axis density clustering algorithm; (2) a hybrid pseudonymization filter; (3) a local large language model (LLM) with chain-of-thought reasoning; and (4) a symbolic causal engine powered by a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to quantify causal propagation into a dynamic risk index. Findings An empirical evaluation across 28 reporting cycles spanning a 33-month large-scale infrastructure project indicates that the symbolic layer provides a temporally coherent aggregation of the output of a zero-shot perception layer operating at a macro F1-score of 53.62%. By quantifying causal risk propagation, the DBN captured a 93.59% risk-saturation state, for which the retrieved evidence identifies chronic site-clearance bottlenecks. Notably, using an alert threshold selected by sensitivity analysis together with an analytic …

title: A Review of the Accuracy and Computational Cost of AI Regression Models for Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting
abstract: Short-term wind power forecasting models must meet both accuracy requirements and computational limits. Published comparisons use different datasets, forecast horizons, and timing boundaries. In this focused narrative review, twelve publications on artificial intelligence (AI) regression models and their evaluation are examined. Support vector regression, random forests, XGBoost, and long short-term memory networks are the main model families discussed. Prediction errors and computational costs are compared within studies, and changes in input information are examined. Under the reported experimental conditions, lower prediction errors do not always require higher computational costs. Runtime rankings can also differ between training and inference. Meteorological inputs and data enrichment affect accuracy and the performance gaps between models. However, cost reporting remains incomplete. The evidence cannot establish whether these accuracy gains require longer computation times or more resources. A conditional screening procedure is therefore suggested. The forecasting task and input availability should be checked first. Parameter search, training, and inference costs should then be compared separately. Results should also be tested across several time windows. These recommendations can support model screening under operational constraints. Their applicability still requires v…

A Statistically Robust Machine Learning Framework for Thyroid Dysfunction Prediction Using Classical Classifiers
abstract: Abstract—Thyroid dysfunction is a common endocrine problem whose symptoms may overlap with many non-thyroid conditions, making timely screening important. This paper presents a conference-style classical machine-learning framework for predicting thyroid dysfunction from structured clinical and laboratory variables. Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Decision Tree, k-Nearest Neighbors, and Gaussian Naive Bayes are compared under a leakage-aware preprocessing and validation protocol. The framework emphasizes rigorous statistical evaluation through stratified nested cross-validation, bootstrap confidence intervals, receiver-operating-characteristic analysis, probability calibration, DeLong comparison of AUCs, and McNemar testing of paired classification errors. Accuracy, Precision, Recall, Specificity, and F1-score are reported with their mathematical definitions. In the illustrative project experiment, Random Forest provides the strongest overall discrimination and balanced error profile, while Logistic Regression remains a transparent baseline and calibrated SVM is competitive. Feature analysis identifies thyroid-stimulating hormone and free-thyroxine-related variables as the dominant predictors. A lightweight web prototype demonstrates patient/laboratory input and real-time prediction output for hypothyroid-pattern and euthyroid cases. The framework is …

title: Reply to the comment by Kuzukıran Kocataş on “Can full-stay lactate burden predict ICU mortality? The importance of a defined prediction time”
Development and internal validation of a serum ferritin-based prediction model for coronary artery aneurysms in Kawasaki disease
abstract: Abstract Background: Kawasaki disease is the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children, and coronary artery aneurysms represent its most important cardiovascular complication. Identifying children at risk for coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks after disease onset is clinically important. Serum ferritin may reflect systemic inflammation in Kawasaki disease, but its incremental predictive value remains uncertain. This study developed a ferritin-based model for predicting coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks. Methods: Patients with Kawasaki disease were retrospectively identified at a single centre and randomly divided into training and internal validation cohorts in a 6:4 ratio. Predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and reclassification metrics. Results: Among 378 patients, 98 (25.9%) had coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks after disease onset. The ferritin-based model included male sex, platelet count, serum ferritin, albumin ≤ 31.5 g/L, and baseline maximum coronary artery Z score ≥ 2.5. Adding serum ferritin increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.853 to 0.899 in the training cohort and from 0.842 to 0.868 in the internal validation cohor…

title: Adverse Drug Reaction Detection with Drug Prediction Using BERT–LSTM–SVM
abstract: Social media can be a useful resource for assessing patient-reported drug experiences. Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are an important public health issue, but finding social media posts in which adverse reactions are described is a difficult task, since not all posts are related to ADR. The proposed work in this research is a hybrid model of BERT-LSTM-SVM for detection of ADRs and drug classification. The input is preprocessed as follows: the text is cleaned, tokenized, normalized, and noise is removed. Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) is used to produce contextual representations of the text, and a Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM) is used to model sequential dependencies to aid binary classification of ADR and non-ADR text. Then, a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier is used to classify the associated medicine based on the extracted textual features. In our validation of the method, the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity and precision were 0.99 with a recall. The proposed framework combines contextual language representations, sequential modeling, and supervised classification approaches to facilitate the automatic detection of ADRs and medicine identification.
venue: Journal of ICT Research and Applications

title: Physics-Constrained Machine Learning Based Long-Term Performance Prediction Method for Asphalt Pavements
abstract: Long-range pavement forecasting should incorporate nonlinear dependencies between traffic, structure, climate, and material aging processes without creating unrealistic degradation paths. In this work, a physics-constrained machine-learning architecture is proposed, utilizing the Federal Highway Administration Long-Term Pavement Performance (LTPP) data set. Multivariate time series consisting of annual records of International Roughness Index (IRI), rutting depth, cracking severity, traffic loads, structure characteristics, material properties, and climate factors are used for training of the two-layer Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network. The loss function consists of prediction error and soft constraints on deterioration continuity, untreated section monotonicity, cumulative traffic damage, climate aging, and physically realistic condition boundaries. The forecasting performance is examined at 5, 10, 15, and 20-year horizons for random forest, XGBoost, and unphysical LSTM methods. For 20-year forecasts, IRI, rut depth, and cracking RMSE errors were 0.284±0.031 m/km, 2.18±0.26 mm, and 5.73±0.61 percentage points, respectively. Deterioration direction violations were reduced to 2.7±0.8% and the deviation of the timing of the serviceability threshold violation was 1.34±0.29 years. The results indicate that embedding engineering deterioration knowledge improves both long-…

title: Towards Clinically Interpretable Early Seizure Prediction in Pediatric Epilepsy Using Hybrid Deep Neural Networks and Multi-Resolution EEG Analysis
abstract: Early seizure prediction in Pediatric epilepsy remains a significant clinical challenge due to complex neurophysiological dynamics, high inter-patient variability, and the non-stationary nature of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. Although deep learning models have demonstrated promising performance in seizure detection, their translation into clinical practice is limited by insufficient interpretability and inadequate modelling of multi-scale temporal patterns preceding seizure onset. Addressing these limitations, this study proposes a clinically interpretable hybrid deep neural network framework for early seizure prediction using multi-resolution EEG analysis in paediatric patients. Multi-channel scalp EEG recordings obtained from the CHB-MIT Scalp EEG Database were pre-processed using adaptive bandpass filtering and artifact suppression techniques to enhance signal quality. A discrete wavelet transform–based multiresolution decomposition strategy was employed to capture time–frequency characteristics across delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands, enabling robust representation of preictal dynamics. The extracted feature maps were integrated into a hybrid CNN–BiLSTM architecture designed to simultaneously learn spatial correlations across EEG channels and long-range temporal dependencies. To enhance clinical transparency, gradient-based attribution mapping and SHAP-driv…

title: Self-HArm one-year Risk Prediction in personality disorders (SHARP-PD): a clinical risk prediction model development and internal-external cross-validation study
Blockchain-Federated Learning using advanced Bayesian LSTM-FAN for Real Option Valuation prediction
abstract: Real Option Valuation (ROV) forecasting is an estimate of the value of flexible investment opportunities in the presence of uncertainty treating them as financial options. Unlike conventional valuation techniques, ROV considers the acknowledgment of strategic choices that can be decided by managers, like waiting, growing, or shelving a project depending on evolving market conditions. Forecasting methodologies tend to employ simulations and complex models, such as Deep Learning (DL), to predict uncertain variables affecting option value. This strategy delivers a more realistic and flexible evaluation, enabling organizations to make more informed decisions in the context of uncertainty. This work aims to design a hybrid DL model for ROV prediction. The key objective is to design a blockchain-Federated Learning (FL) model integrated with DL for ROV prediction. FL constructs a global model by aggregating locally trained models on the blockchain so that the collaboratively trained global model can give improved and more accurate predictions. The local model learns with the proposed Bayesian Long Short-Term Network-Fourier Analysis Networks (BayesianLSTM-FAN), a fusion of Bayesian Long Short-Term Network (BayesianLSTM) and Fourier Analysis Networks (FAN). The data is preprocessed first by data cleaning and scaling (StandardScaler) and then by statistical feature extraction (Rolling w…

Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Viral Nanobody Epitope Prediction
abstract: Abstract Rapid development of therapeutics against emerging viral pathogens increasingly depends on machine learning (ML), both to generate candidate binders and for structural validation. Nanobodies (Nbs), or single-domain antibodies, are promising antiviral therapeutics, but accurate in silico prediction of viral epitopes remains challenging. Here we benchmark three ML-based structure prediction models, Boltz-2, Chai-1 and AlphaFold3 (AF3), against a curated data set of viral antigen-nanobody complexes deposited after the AF3 training cutoff. AF3 outperformed the other models: success (interface DockQ > 0.23) rose from 33% with a single seed to 50% and 65% with 10 and 100 seeds-per-target, respectively, compared with 18% for Boltz-2 and 30% for Chai-1. Using an expanded data set, we evaluated confidence metrics and found that a strict ipTM cutoff of 0.8, or a combination of ipTM ≥ 0.6 with a CDR3 loop pLDDT ≥ 60, reliably excluded incorrect predictions while retaining most successful ones. We further establish best practices for two AF3-specific capabilities, the choice of antigen multimeric state and the inclusion of N-glycosylation, both of which can be decisive for epitope success depending on the target. Finally, we apply these guidelines to two design problems: ranking a library of VEEV-neutralizing nanobodies and mapping the epitope of the broadly neutralizing nanobo…

title: Digital Twin Modeling for Fault Prediction and Health Management of Metal Structures in Water Conservancy Projects: A Review
Simulated Feature Fusion for Parkinson’s Disease Prediction Using Non-aligned Public Handwriting and Voice Datasets
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that affects over 10 million people worldwide, with prevalence increasing due to aging populations. Early symptoms such as tremor, micrographia, bradykinesia, and voice changes often remain undetected until substantial neuronal loss has occurred, leading to irreversible damage and increased treatment costs. This paper presents a comparative study of five machine learning models—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (RBF Kernel), K-Nearest Neighbors, and XGBoost—for Parkinson’s disease prediction using handwriting and voice-based features. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC, 5-fold cross-validation, ROC curve analysis, feature importance analysis, and SHAP-based explainability.XGBoost achieved the highest test-set F1-score (0.7407) and AUC (0.8329), while SVM achieved the highest average cross-validation F1-score. Decision-level fusion further improved recall (0.88) while maintaining competitive overall performance. K-Nearest Neighbors produced the lowest overall performance, while XGBoost achieved the best balance between classification accuracy, F1-score, and AUC.

Cultural Perceptions and Country Brands in the Global Art Market
abstract: This study bridges a gap in the literature concerning brand image, country of origin, and consumer perceptions of luxury products, specifically exploring the relatively unknown roles of geographic distance and sales transaction location. Utilizing the luxury art market, data encompassing 1726 transactions over thirty years was collected. The study examined the relationship between sale price and cultural indulgence, as well as the relationship between sale price and the distance between the sale location and the artist's home nation. The methodology employed three separate multiple linear regressions: a base model incorporating artist nationality, gender, and art history textbook representation; the base model plus cultural indulgence; and the base model plus geographical distance. Results indicated that auction houses located in more culturally indulgent areas command a premium, as do those located farther from the artist's home nation. The data is limited to two-dimensional artworks post-1750, included in prominent art history texts, and only includes auction sale price information. It is suggested that future researchers explore different art transactions or other industries like collectible luxury sports cars. The findings offer practical implications for practitioners in choosing sales office locations for premium goods and for brokers seeking higher prices by considering …

Journey to immunization service: identifying barriers and enablers to routine immunization service uptake among communities residing in urban slum areas of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 2023
The Influence Mechanism of Housing Affordability Stratification on Community Public Service Accessibility
abstract: The issue of housing affordability has become an important factor that defines not only where people can live but also where they can actually access the services of the city. This research explores the impact of housing affordability stratification on public service accessibility in New York City and transmission of such effects through public service resource density and transit connectivity. The data obtained from the 2023 American Community Survey about socioeconomics of census tracts of New York City is merged with housing data from NYC PLUTO, public service facilities' data from NYC Open Data and pedestrian network data from OpenStreetMap. Housing cost burden of households is divided into three strata using the Jenks natural breaks classification. Healthcare, education, parks, libraries and public transit accessibility is calculated using an advanced version of the network-based two-step floating catchment area method and is weighted using entropy weights. Further analysis includes spatial autocorrelation analysis, spatial durbin modeling and mediation analysis. As a result of simulation of the proposed research design, tracts with high cost burden have a lower value of accessibility index (Mean = 0.486, SD = 0.137) compared to low burden tracts (Mean = 0.672, SD = 0.118). The effect size of the total spatial Durbin model is -0.254***. The contribution of the mediator var…

title: Does Green Brand Equity Buffer or Burn? Understanding Boundary Conditions in Justice Evaluations of Sharing Economy Service Failure
abstract: Abstract The authors investigate green brand equity as a representation of firm phenotype in terms of its impact on the relationship between perceived justice of service recovery and customer citizenship and behavioral loyalty behavior. The firm phenotype of GBE can perform different roles as a moral signal, a normative expectation or a value laden identity cue. The purpose of this study is to identify the role/s performed in the fair recovery of sharing economy service failure. Drawing on the tradeoff between expectation-disconfirmation versus judgment assimilation-categorization, this study seeks to understand the buffering/incendiary influence of green brand equity in the context of service recovery in a sustainable services context. The findings of the conceptual model are empirically verified through surveys distributed to 804 digitally engaged sharing economy consumers using Partial-Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. The results reveal that while consumers demonstrate desirable citizenship towards the firm when it is perceived to be a high green brand equity firm that delivers fair service recovery, it does not extend the same leeway in terms of service re-patronage. The conclusion of the study is that sustainability signaling, though morally rewarded in the long-term through citizenship connoting judgment assimilation may not necessarily transform into a short-t…

title: Reconsidering green logistics adoption: the role of perceived behavioral control and ESG information in shippers' selection of logistics service providers
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how perceived behavioral control and environmental, social and governance (ESG) information shape shippers' adoption of green logistics service providers. Specifically, the study aims to (1) investigate the presence of an intention–behavior gap in green logistics adoption and (2) assess whether ESG information enhances perceived behavioral control, thereby facilitating actual adoption behavior within an extended theory of planned behavior (TPB) framework. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a quantitative survey-based research design. Data were collected from shippers involved in logistics service provider selection and analyzed using structural equation modeling. The research framework integrates the Theory of Planned Behavior with persuasion theory, incorporating ESG information as an external antecedent influencing perceived behavioral control, behavioral intention and actual adoption behavior. Findings The results show that environmental attitudes significantly influence behavioral intention, while subjective norms do not. Behavioral intention does not directly translate into actual green logistics adoption, indicating a clear intention–behavior gap. Perceived behavioral control has a strong and direct effect on actual adoption behavior. ESG information significantly enhances perceived behavioral control, indirectly s…
