title: Cerium-doped IrO2-Ta2O5/Ti anodes for enhanced acidic oxygen evolution stability and extended service lifetime
Service use following violence: insights from the linked administrative data in South Wales
abstract: Abstract Background To better support victim-survivors of violence and inform violence prevention initiatives, it is important to understand potential barriers and facilitators for using services such as healthcare and police. Administrative data are often limited to the users of a particular service, while linked data provides an opportunity to examine factors associated with the use of multiple services or one over the other. The present research used linked emergency department (ED) and police data from South Wales to understand the individual and contextual factors associated with the use of healthcare and police support. Methods Analyses of the sociodemographic characteristics of victims and characteristics of violent incidents were conducted for the incidents that appeared in the police data only, ED data only, and both services. Adjusted logistic regressions were used to examine factors associated with contacting both services and police first. Results Victims of violent incidents that happened at the victim’s home rather than on the street were more likely to approach the police in addition to the ED. Those who experienced violence from a current or former partner were also more likely to approach the police first than those who experienced violence from a stranger. If a violence incident happened at a workplace, victims who used the ED were less likely to approach the …

title: The contingent effects of AI transparency in service recovery: a moderated mediation model of perceived warmth and competence
abstract: Purpose This research investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) transparency shapes consumer responses in service recovery. By revealing the reasoning process behind AI decisions, transparency functions as an anthropomorphic cue that humanizes the system's communication. Drawing on social cognitive theory, the research develops and tests a generalizable mechanism framework linking AI transparency, consumer cognition and recovery satisfaction, while identifying boundary conditions. Design/methodology/approach Three scenario-based experiments were conducted. Study 1 (N = 98) tested the direct effect of AI transparency on recovery satisfaction. Study 2 (N = 230) examined the parallel mediating roles of perceived warmth and competence. Study 3 (N = 284) tested the moderating role of service failure severity and the corresponding conditional indirect effects. Findings AI transparency significantly improves recovery satisfaction, indirectly through perceived warmth and competence. Service failure severity moderated the effects of transparency on both mediators. The indirect effects through warmth and competence were significant under low service failure severity but not under high severity, identifying severity as a boundary condition for the effectiveness of AI transparency in service recovery. Originality/value This research conceptualizes AI transparency as a form of anthropom…

title: The Effect of Service Quality, Customer Relationship Management, and Corporate Image on Workplace Accident Insurance Participant Satisfaction
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of service quality on the satisfaction of workplace accident insurance participants, the effect of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) on the satisfaction of workplace accident insurance participants, the effect of company image on the satisfaction of workplace accident insurance participants, and the simultaneous effect of service quality, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), and company image on the satisfaction of workplace accident insurance participants at the Makassar Branch of the BPJS Employment. This study used a quantitative approach, with the research object being the Makassar Branch of the BPJS Employment. The sample consisted of 100 workplace accident insurance participants. Data analysis techniques included instrument testing, classical assumption testing, multivariate regression analysis, and hypothesis testing. This study found that service quality had a positive and significant effect on the satisfaction of work accident insurance participants. Customer Relationship Management (CRM) had a positive and significant effect on the satisfaction of work accident insurance participants. Corporate image had a positive and significant effect on the satisfaction of work accident insurance participants. Simultaneously, service quality, customer relationship management, and corporate image have a significant effect on the satisfa…

title: Low-dose IL-2 therapy in autoimmune diseases: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and future strategies for precision immune regulation
How are Perfectionistic Strivings and Perfectionistic Concerns Differentially Associated with Emotion Regulation
abstract: Perfectionism includes perfectionistic strivings and perfectionistic concerns, and both dimensions lead to different emotion regulation. This review looks at how the two dimensions link with emotion regulation and why these differences happen. Past studies show that perfectionistic strivings usually connect with better emotion regulation strategies, like cognitive reappraisal and accepting bad feelings. But perfectionistic concerns link with negative emotions, rumination, expressive suppression and emotion-regulation problems. These differences can be explained by their motivation types. Perfectionistic strivings connect more to approach-oriented and autonomous motivation, while perfectionistic concerns connect to avoidance-oriented and controlled motivation. However, researchers still disagree on whether perfectionistic strivings can buffer perfectionistic concerns when both are very high. So, the link between perfectionism and emotion regulation is not just about single dimensions, but also depends on how they work together.
venue: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media

title: TECHNOLOGY, REGULATION, AND THE DIVERGENT TRAJECTORIES OF RETAIL AND CROSS-BORDER CENTRAL BANK DIGITAL CURRENCY
abstract: Background. Central bank digital currency (CBDC) sits where fast-moving cryptographic and ledger technology meets fast-moving regulation, yet the two are usually studied separately, and retail and cross-border uses are usually treated as one object. Between 2024 and 2026 major jurisdictions made sharply different regulatory choices. Research Purpose. This review examines how advanced cryptographic solutions and hybrid blockchain architectures interact with evolving regulatory frameworks to shape economic outcomes and user adoption, and how that interaction differs between retail and cross-border implementations. Research Method. We conduct a critical review. A Scopus search on 8 October 2026 (1,418 records, 1,045 retained) maps the field, and a purposive selection of peer-reviewed studies and official publications is synthesised around four research questions. Findings. Technology and regulation terms co-occur at about the level expected by chance, and evidence on cryptographic feasibility and on adoption comes largely from separate literatures. Hybrid, two-tier architectures dominate, and the tension between privacy and anti-money laundering is increasingly handled through cryptographic design. Retail adoption is weak in every live system reviewed, while wholesale cross-border arrangements show the clearest technological value but are limited by governance. Regulatory choices …

title: Experimental and numerical investigation of biomimetic Serpenoid geometry for deformation control and stiffness regulation in reinforced concrete frames
Emotion regulation, academic resilience, and perceived stress in health professions students: a cross-sectional analysis of indirect associations
abstract: Background Health professions students face substantial academic and clinical demands that may increase perceived stress. Previous studies have examined emotion regulation and academic resilience separately, but little is known about whether academic resilience is related to the association between emotion regulation and perceived stress. Academic resilience was examined because students who regulate their emotions more effectively may be better able to cope with academic difficulties, and greater resilience may in turn be associated with lower perceived stress. This study examined the associations of emotion regulation with academic resilience and perceived stress, as well as their indirect associations with perceived stress through academic resilience. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 180 health professions students recruited from a medical university in Taiwan using convenience sampling. Participants completed measures of emotion regulation, academic resilience, and perceived stress. Cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression were analyzed separately. Pearson correlation analyses and PROCESS Model 4 were used to examine the proposed associations and statistical indirect associations. Results Cognitive reappraisal was positively associated with academic resilience (B = 1.04, p < .001), whereas expressive suppression was not significantly associated…

title: Association between self-reported resistance-exercise frequency and abdominal adiposity among Chinese adults: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Resistance exercise is included in adult physical activity recommendations, but the weekly frequency associated with abdominal adiposity in free-living adults remains unknown. We examined the association between self-reported weekly resistance-exercise frequency and abdominal adiposity; an exploratory secondary analysis compared ≥3 days/week with 2 days/week. Methods This single-center cross-sectional study analyzed 913 Chinese adults selected from the 3,411 adults consecutively screened at the Health Examination Center of Taizhou People’s Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing Medical University between November 2025 and July 2026. Self-reported resistance exercise was grouped as 0, 1, 2, or ≥3 days/week. Body roundness index (BRI) was the primary outcome, with waist circumference, body mass index (BMI), and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) as the secondary outcomes. Multivariable linear regression analyses with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors were adjusted for age, sex, aerobic moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), sedentary time, smoking history, and alcohol consumption. The primary analysis used complete cases; multiple imputation was used to evaluate robustness in the 2,958 participants remaining after clinical exclusions, alongside additional sensitivity analyses. Results Of the 913 participants, 613 (67.14%) reported no weekly resistance exercise, 90 (9…

Parental technoference and preschoolers’ emotional and behavioral problems: the serial mediation of emotion regulation and self regulation
abstract: Introduction The present study explores how technoference in parent -child interactions is linked to emotional and behavioral problems in preschool aged children and examines whether emotion regulation and self-regulation function as serial mediators in this relationship. Methods To evaluate the proposed associations, mediation analysis was carried out using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). A crosssectional research design was employed in the present study. The study sample consisted of 518 children attending independent preschools located in the central districts of Denizli, Türkiye, along with their parents. Among the children, 304 were girls (58.7%) and 214 were boys (41.3%). Of the children, 216 (41.7%) were 5 years old, and 302 (58.3%) were 6 years old. Data were collected using the Technoference Scale in Parent Child Relationships, Emotion Regulation Scale, Psychological Well-Being Scale for 5 and 6 Year Old Children (PWBSC), and the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). The technoference Scale in Parent -Child Relationships was completed by parents, whereas the other measures were completed by teachers. Results Results demonstrated that the link between parent -child technoference and children’s emotional and behavioral problems was indirectly explained through a serial mediation process involving emotion regulation and self-regulation (B = 0.083, 95% bootst…

title: Self-directed coaching: repositioning the client as the internalizing agent of developmental self-regulation a conceptual framework and research agenda for coaching theory and practice
abstract: Coaching has become one of the most widely deployed developmental interventions in organizational, educational, and health-professions settings, and the literature offers substantial evidence for its short-term benefits. Evidence on whether those benefits persist after formal coaching support is withdrawn is thinner and less systematic, and the question points to an unresolved tension at the field’s core. Coaching is justified by its capacity to build independent, self-regulating professionals, but it is typically structured in a way that locates diagnosis, goal setting, strategic planning, and accountability in the coach rather than the client. The result can be improvement that does not outlive the engagement. This paper introduces Self-Directed Coaching (SDC) as a theory-based framework that repositions the client as the principal agent of their own developmental regulation. Grounded in self-determination theory, intentional change theory, regulatory focus theory, self-directed and self-regulated learning, cybernetic control theory, and attachment theory, SDC reframes coaching as a scaffolded process whose intended end-state is reduced dependence on formal coaching support. The framework’s central mechanism is self-regulatory internalization, the progressive transfer of coaching functions from an external agent to the client’s own regulatory repertoire. SDC is organized arou…

title: Low-frequency in situ acoustic measurement of sedimentary layers 100 m below the offshore seafloor
Exit without Migration: Cloud Switching and Operational Continuity in EU Law
abstract: Abstract EU law can make cloud exit legally enforceable while leaving migration operationally uncertain. This article asks why a customer with a binding right to leave a cloud provider may still lack a workable way to continue the service elsewhere. Reading the EU Data Act alongside the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), it shows how switching and operational continuity depend on conditions governed by different obligations and actors. The Data Act addresses provider-side switching obstacles but bounds the departing provider’s responsibility where reconstruction also depends on the customer, the destination environment and differentiated service functionality. In finance, DORA requires financial entities to prepare for continuity of critical or important functions. These limits on provider responsibility can be proportionate, even as migration remains operationally uncertain. The article argues that DORA’s existing requirements for feasible, tested and continuity-preserving exit plans should substantiate a credible path for reconstituting and continuing the regulated function after exit. More broadly, it shows how individually defensible regulatory duties can leave a shared operational outcome insufficiently substantiated when responsibility is distributed across instruments.

title: Correction to “Spectroscopic Evaluation of AlN/n-Si MIS Structures through Frequency-Driven Dielectric Characterization”
More Than a Coin Flip: Forced-Choice Performance Above the Binomial Mean and Word-Frequency Bias on the Word Memory Test Under Sham Random Responding
abstract: Abstract Below-chance performance on forced-choice performance validity tests (PVTs) is typically interpreted against a binomial model that assumes a .50 probability under uninformed responding. We tested whether this assumption holds for the Word Memory Test (WMT) and whether item-level lexical properties account for departures from the binomial expectation using a sham extrasensory perception (ESP) paradigm to elicit uninformed (i.e., “random”) responding. Fifty-five undergraduates completed the WMT Immediate Recognition (IR) trial without prior exposure to the study list. Total scores and item-level responses were tested against exact binomial expectations. Pair-level lexical contrasts (target minus foil) for log word frequency, age of acquisition, concreteness, and orthographic distance were derived from the English Lexicon Project and examined as predictors of item selection in ordinary least squares (OLS) and generalized estimating equation (GEE) models. Mean IR performance was 24.15 of 40 (60.4% correct), exceeding the binomial mean, t(54) = 8.40, p < .001, d = 1.13. Eighteen IR items deviated from .50 after false-discovery-rate correction, predominantly toward the keyed-correct word. Target-foil word-frequency asymmetry was the dominant predictor of IR item selection (bivariate r = .56; OLS and GEE p < .001); concreteness and orthographic distance were unrelated to IR s…

title: Dupilumab-associated eosinophilia in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: frequency, temporal dynamics, predictors, and clinical consequences—a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Dupilumab may cause a treatment-emergent rise in circulating eosinophils, but the frequency, temporal pattern, predictors, and clinical consequences of hypereosinophilia (HE) in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) remain incompletely defined. Methods We performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis of PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase.com studies reporting post-treatment circulating eosinophil outcomes in dupilumab-treated CRSwNP. Potentially overlapping reports were linked at the cohort and outcome level. The primary outcome was post-treatment HE ≥1,500 cells/µL, synthesized using a binomial-normal random-effects generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with a logit link. Results The combined searches identified 368 records; after deduplication, 255 records were screened, 72 reports underwent full-text assessment, and 50 eligible reports mapped to 42 study/cohort clusters. Six independent cohorts contributed 172 HE events among 1,047 patients, yielding a pooled HE proportion of 7.9% [95% confidence interval (CI), 2.8%–20.1%; τ = 1.19]. Following outcome-specific risk-of-bias reassessment, a sensitivity analysis excluding the two high-risk cohorts retained four studies (166 events among 865 patients) and yielded 12.1% (95% CI, 3.9%–32.0%; τ = 1.06). Across seven longitudinal cohorts…

title: Functional contribution of the gut microbiota to digestive capacity during ontogeny in greater amberjack (Seriola dumerili) larvae
abstract: Introduction The intestinal microbiota is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to host digestive physiology; however, its potential contribution to digestive capacity during fish larval development remains largely unknown. Here, we investigated the coordinated development of host digestive physiology and gut microbial function throughout larval ontogeny in greater amberjack ( Seriola dumerili ) larvae sampled at 10, 19, 32, 40 and 60 days post-hatching (dph), covering the main dietary transitions from live prey feeding through co-feeding with formulated diets to post-weaning. Methods Intestinal digestive enzyme activities were quantified in parallel with the enzymatic potential of the associated bacterial community, allowing, for the first time in marine fish larvae, the estimation of the potential contribution of the microbiota to digestive capacity. These analyses were integrated with 16S rRNA gene sequencing, FAPROTAX functional prediction, indicator taxa analyses and zymography to characterize the taxonomic and functional maturation of the intestinal microbiota. Results Host digestive capacity underwent marked ontogenetic changes associated with major dietary transitions. In parallel, the bacterial community progressively acquired a broader digestive repertoire. Bacterial proteolytic and chitinolytic activities increased markedly during development, while bac…

An adaptation of the WHO 4-step Integrated Care for Older People locomotion pathway with blended eHealth resistance training associated with enhanced locomotor capacity in community-dwelling older adults: a retrospective, quasi-experimental study
abstract: Abstract Background The World Health Organization Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) pathway has yielded inconsistent effects on locomotor capacity, partly because transitions from assessment to intervention are fragmented in community settings. We merged ICOPE steps 1 and 2 for the locomotion domain into a single encounter (4-m walk test [4MWT] and five-times sit-to-stand test [FTSST]), followed by a four-movement progressive resistance-training program and week-8 reassessment, delivered through a blended eHealth and community model embedded in Taiwan’s Long-Term Care 2.0 tier-C network. Methods In this retrospective, quasi-experimental study, 858 community-dwelling adults aged ≥ 60 years were assessed at baseline; after seven exclusions, 851 were analyzed (811 intervention; 40 self-selected, assessment-only comparators, 15 with baseline impairment). Participants were stratified by baseline locomotor status (impaired: 4MWT speed < 1.0 m/s and/or FTSST > 10.8 s). Sensitivity analyses included three-level mixed-effects models with random intercepts for participant and district estimated group-by-time effects; inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), cluster-robust standard errors, wild-cluster bootstrap, and leave-one-district-out analyses. Results Group-by-time interactions favored the intervention: 0.13-m/s greater gain in gait speed (95% CI 0.04 to 0.22, P = 0…

Building capacity in institutional voids: carbon competency development among quantity surveyors in Nigeria’s weak institutional environment
abstract: Purpose This study assesses the training needs and competency strategies that quantity surveyors (QSs) perceive as important for enhancing embodied carbon estimation (ECE) in Nigeria’s weak institutional environment. It addresses gap in understanding how global sustainability norms may be taken up by a profession traditionally focused on cost management, in a setting where institutional pressures remain limited. Design/methodology/approach This organization-based study collected data from 132 quantity surveying firms (QSFs) in Lagos, Nigeria, using a structured questionnaire covering 21 training needs and competency strategies. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to rank the perceived importance of these items and to identify the underlying competency clusters. Findings The factor analysis identified two clusters of perceived training needs and competency strategies: (1) technical and operational capacity building comprising skills for lifecycle assessment and the use of carbon digital tools; and (2) knowledge infrastructure and strategic integration, comprising systemic support such as carbon databases and online resources and industry guidelines. All 21 competency strategies were rated as highly important, suggesting that respondents did not strongly differentiate among them and regarded all of them as priorities for impro…

title: Capacity and Electrochromism Decoupling Strategy for Real-Time State-of-Charge Monitoring of High-Areal-Capacity Electrochromic Batteries
abstract: Abstract State-of-charge (SOC) is a central parameter in battery management systems for electric vehicles, directly affecting driving range, power delivery, safety, and battery lifetime. However, real-time and high-precision SOC monitoring remains a challenge for practical batteries. Here, we report a capacity and electrochromism decoupling strategy for real-time SOC monitoring of high-areal-capacity electrochromic batteries. The bilayer cathode combines a pure electrochromic coloration layer with an underlying conductive, high-loading capacity layer, thereby spatially separating optical readout from high-capacity storage. The device delivers an areal capacity of 3.4 mAh cm–2 with 97.8% capacity retention after 300 cycles. The monotonic SOC–Hue relationship with 1% SOC intervals was established by converting in situ reflectance spectra into Hue values. The modulation of reflectance-peak wavelength shift retains 81.2% after 1000 coloration cycles. This architecture provides a route toward batteries with built-in optical state reporting for advanced battery management.

title: Household affordability of sanitary landfilling is governed by cost allocation rather than metropolitan economic capacity
abstract: Abstract Open dumping remains a dominant municipal solid waste disposal practice globally, including in megacities whose populations and economic output rival that of small countries. Sanitary landfilling is a common transition away from open dumping, yet system-level feasibility does not translate into household affordability. Here we quantify this divergence using an integrated city-scale framework that combines spatial landfill siting, engineering-based net-present-value modeling, and satellite-derived metropolitan gross domestic product. Applying this framework across six developing megacities with over 100 million residents, we find that all cities possess surplus land meeting screening-level suitability criteria. Required cost-recovery tipping fees range from 54–130 US dollars per tonne, with 5 th –95 th -percentile intervals of ±25%–30% under joint parameter uncertainty. Under full household cost recovery, these fees imply annual disposal costs equivalent to 1.2%–2.0% of the minimum wage, whereas associated revenue requirements represent only 0.26%–1.04% of metropolitan gross domestic product. Across cities, household affordability is uncorrelated with metropolitan economic capacity. Landfill depth is the dominant engineering control on affordability, particularly in high-rainfall systems, but cost allocation exerts greater leverage than any design parameter. Thus, techn…

title: Security Indexing Coding under the Eavesdropper Model: A Review of Capacity Boundaries and Secure Indexing Methods
abstract: With 5G and Internet technology developing quickly, broadcast and multicast communications are widely applied in many scenarios such as the Internet of Vehicles, edge distributed networks and group transmission for the Internet. Wireless broadcast channels are open, but transmitted signals are easy to intercept and pose a risk of data leakage. This study focuses on a survey of secure index encoding. This work defines the secure index encoding model, adversary model, strong security and weak security. Based on the above, it discusses how to use and where to use linear coding and random linear coding. Through analysis, this paper find that secure index encoding also have some troubles, like inaccurate minimum rank, difficulty in solving optimal coding solution and hard to achievement. This paper reviews the theoretical framework of secure index encoding based on existing research, which can provide a reference for more in-depth research in the future.

title: It’s all in my head: informal visitor knowledge and capacity constraints on Vermont agritourism farms
abstract: Agritourism, opening farms to visitors, can contribute to food systems sustainability goals, including economic prosperity and livelihoods, social engagement, environmental quality, and human health. Agritourism is particularly important in states like Vermont where direct-to-consumer sales and community engagement are part of the rural fabric. While much scholarship has focused on farmer motivation and economic outcomes, less research has examined how operators come to know their visitors and what limits their use of marketing information. We report on year one of a multi-year project on how Vermont agritourism operators understand their visitors, what visitors’ information they currently collect or want, and what capacity constraints affect their ability to use it. We conducted semi-structured interviews with operators of 10 farms (December 2025-January 2026) and analyzed them thematically. Findings indicate that all 10 operators relied on informal, memory-based visitor knowledge, and nine had no formal system for collecting or analyzing visitor data. All 10 named word of mouth as a visitor discovery channel; nine used social media, at widely varying levels of activity. Operators most wanted to know what activities visitors are interested in and how visitors find the farm, and all farmers wanted to use visitor data for planning. Several farmers cited time constraints, a lack …

title: VALUE IDENTITY AND PSYCHOLOGICAL RESILIENCE: COLLABORATIVE MECHANISM BETWEEN NATIONAL SECURITY EDUCATION AND MENTAL HEALTH EDUCATION IN THE CONTEXT OF PRECISION IDEOLOGICAL AND POLITICAL EDUCATION
abstract: The integration of mental health education and national security education has become an important issue in higher education, particularly in promoting students’ psychological development, value identification, and civic responsibility. Based on the concept of precision-oriented ideological and political education, this study explores a collaborative education model that integrates curriculum content, teaching methods, learning environments, and evaluation systems. It proposes a “national security–people’s security–psychological resilience” framework, arguing that security awareness should be transformed from knowledge acquisition into emotional identification, psychological resilience, and responsible action. By connecting psychological mechanisms with value-oriented education, this study provides a new perspective for developing students’ security literacy, psychological resilience, and responsible citizenship, while offering practical implications for innovation in higher education.

title: Plastisphere Formation on Microplastics: A Key Mechanism for Potential Toxic Element Accumulation in Wetlands
Analysis of the Coercivity Mechanism of High-Performance Nd-Fe-B Magnets Prepared by Synergistic Diffusion
abstract: Abstract The grain boundary diffusion process is an important approach for preparing high-performance Nd-Fe-B magnets. In this study, Nd-Fe-B diffusion magnets with both high remanence and high coercivity were prepared via a two-step synergistic diffusion process. The process combined Pr70Ga30 pre-diffusion with subsequent DyH3 diffusion. Compared with DyH3 diffusion alone, this two-step synergistic diffusion strategy increased the coercivity increment from 3.30 to 3.84 kOe while maintaining a remanence of 15.03 kG. Microstructural and elemental analyses showed that Pr70Ga30 pre-diffusion modified the grain-boundary phase and promoted Dy diffusion to greater depths. The modified grain boundaries facilitated the formation of continuous (Dy, RE)2Fe14B shells around the main-phase grains. These shells increased the local magnetocrystalline anisotropy and strengthened the grain edges against reverse-domain nucleation. Micromagnetic simulations indicated that a complete core-shell structure increased the demagnetization nucleation field at grain edges, thereby suppressing magnetic domain reversal. This study establishes a direct relationship between grain-boundary modification, shell continuity, and coercivity enhancement in Nd-Fe-B magnets.

title: Failure mechanism of rotational landslide on red bed triggered by heavy rainfall–a case study from the Wushanping landslide, Chongqing Province, China
Solvent Effects on the Photophysical Mechanism of a 2’-Hydroxybenzochalcone Derivative with TICT Characteristics
abstract: Abstract 2’-Hydroxybenzochalcone derivatives serve as solid-state laser materials and promising high-sensitivity fluorescent probes with TICT and ESIPT dual photophysical pathways, yet their solvent-dependent mechanisms remain ambiguous. Herein, synthesized 2’-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzochalcone (HMBC) was systematically explored via spectroscopic characterization and theoretical calculations in three aprotic solvents of varied polarity. Increasing solvent polarity induces a gradual red shift in the absorption peaks, and dual fluorescence emission is observed with a significantly large Stokes shift for the long-wavelength band. DFT and TD-DFT results reveal that the initial hydroxyl proton configuration plays a critical role in directing the excited-state relaxation of HMBC. In combination with the extremely low fluorescence quantum yields measured in dilute solution, the excited-state behavior of HMBC was shown to be predominantly governed by TICT rather than ESIPT. Moreover, a clear correlation among solvent polarity, excited-state molecular torsion, charge-transfer character, and luminescence behavior was established. This work offers guidance for the rational design of advanced fluorescent probes toward environmental and biomedical detection based on 2’-hydroxylchalcone template.

title: Exploring the formation mechanism of new energy vehicle technology innovation network: a stimulus–response model analysis
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore the formation mechanism of technology innovation network in new energy automobile industry based on the stimulus-response model and to analyze the dynamic interaction process among innovation subjects, platform and government under the market mechanism, platform participation and government regulation. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts static regression analysis to study the formation mechanism of technology innovation network in new energy automobile industry. Multiagent simulation model is used to explore the dynamic evolution mechanism of innovation network formation. Findings The research findings indicate that the innovation behavior of technology receivers is significantly influenced by their own technology cross-border search and technology internalization capability, and technology ecological niche of technology senders, information stimulation intensity, the level of platform participation and government regulation. The simulation results show that in the interaction among innovation subjects under the market mechanism, a greater number of enterprises choose technology-restructuring innovation. However, in the interaction between innovation subjects and the environment, a higher number of technology-distributed innovation subjects is observed. Originality/value This paper reveals the “black box” of technological innovation…

title: Research on the Mechanism of Offline Retail Visual Marketing Influence on Consumer Purchase Decisions
abstract: With the the rapid growth of online shopping, offline physical stores face declining customer traffic and intensified competition. Compared with online consumption, which is largely based on information presented through digital interfaces, offline stores use visual elements such as display windows, lighting, product displays, and digital displays to influence consumers' perceptions of the store environment, product value, and brand image, affecting purchase decisions. Based on SOR (Stimulus-Body-Response) theory and referencing foreign research on retail and consumer behavior from 2023 to 2026, this paper analyzes the pathways of visual marketing's influence on consumer decision-making from three perspectives: visual perception, emotional experience, and consumer behavior. It further explores the moderating roles of individual consumer characteristics, shopping contexts, and product attributes in shaping the effects of visual marketing. The study finds that a coordinated and orderly visual environment can boost consumers' perceived value of stores and products, enhance positive emotions, extend dwell time, and promote purchase intention formation. Issues such as visual information overload and chaotic spatial layout increase consumers' psychological burden, hence reducing shopping experience and purchase tendencies. Based on the research results, this paper proposes optimizati…

title: Biostimulant potential of Limnospira platensis biomass fermented with lactic acid bacteria in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris): strain characterization, biochemical shifts, and growth promotion
abstract: The excessive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides in conventional agriculture poses significant risks to soil health, environmental quality, and food security. Plant biostimulants derived from microorganisms, microalgae and cyanobacteria offer a sustainable alternative. Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and cyanobacteria such as Limnospira platensis are recognized for their plant growth-promoting characteristics. However, the combined effects of LAB-fermented L. platensis biomass on common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) remain underexplored. This investigation assessed the phytostimulant potential of L. platensis extracts, live LAB, and LAB-fermented L. platensis extract on growth parameters, yield, soil microbiota, and chlorophyll content of P. vulgaris under field conditions. Five treatments were evaluated: T 1 (water, negative control), T 2 (commercial biostimulant containing humic/fulvic acids, amino acids, N-P-K, and micronutrients), T 3 (0.5% L. platensis biomass extract), T 4 (live LAB culture, 1.4 × 10 8 cells mL -1 ), and T 5 (0.5% extract of L. platensis biomass fermented with LAB). Foliar applications were applied weekly from week 2 to week 9. Phenological parameters, chlorophyll concentration (SPAD-calibrated), root nodulation, soil CFU, and final yield (kg ha -1 ) were measured. Results indicated that T 5 consistently yielded the highest values across all parameters…

title: Exogenous benzyl cyanide activates the somatic embryogenesis program in Arabidopsis
abstract: Abstract Phenylacetic acid (PAA) is a naturally occurring auxin whose biosynthesis and function during plant regeneration remain poorly understood. PAA may be synthesized from phenylalanine via the CYP79A2-dependent phenylacetaldoxime pathway, in which benzyl cyanide/phenylacetonitrile (BnCN/PAN) is a potential intermediate and substrate for NITRILASE (NIT) enzymes. Here, we investigated whether exogenous BnCN/PAN promotes somatic embryogenesis (SE) through NIT-dependent PAA biosynthesis. Low concentrations of BnCN/PAN stimulated somatic embryo formation in Arabidopsis thaliana , whereas exogenous PAA also promoted embryogenic induction. Transcriptome profiling revealed that BnCN/PAN upregulated genes associated with SE, including key embryogenic regulators and EMBRYO DEFECTIVE genes. RNA-seq data further indicated enhanced auxin signaling, which was independently confirmed using the pDR5::GUS reporter line. Inhibition of NIT activity by heatin reduced the embryogenic competence of BnCN/PAN-treated explants, supporting the involvement of NIT enzymes in this response. Collectively, our findings provide the first evidence that exogenous BnCN/PAN can promote embryogenic transition, and suggest that NIT-dependent metabolism may contribute to this response.

title: The assessment power of Gaokao English: washback, regulatory mediation, and educational inequality in the context of China's Double Reduction Policy
abstract: This conceptual analysis examines the assessment power of Gaokao English in contemporary China, focusing on how high-stakes foreign-language assessment influences teaching, learning, family investment, supplementary education, and educational inequality. Drawing on selected policy documents and published research on assessment washback, test impact, assessment as language policy, and linguistic capital, it develops a conceptual model of assessment power and regulatory mediation. Assessment power captures the capacity of a consequential assessment to organise expectations, preparation, and resource allocation, while regulatory mediation describes how policies governing the conditions of preparation reshape actors’ responses to assessment incentives. The analysis argues that Gaokao English exerts influence beyond the test event through anticipatory washback and broader test impact. The Double Reduction Policy illustrates how regulation can reshape the conditions and channels of preparation without removing the underlying incentives generated by high-stakes assessment. Students, schools, and families differ in the resources and opportunities available to them, and regulatory change may therefore shape differentiated forms of adaptation and reconfigure how educational advantage is pursued. By integrating the established distinction between washback and broader test impact and theor…

title: Euclid preparation. CXV. Galaxy power spectrum and bispectrum modelling
abstract: Higher-order correlation functions of the large-scale galaxy distribution offer access to information beyond that contained in standard two-point statistics, such as the power spectrum. In this work we assess the potential of the Euclid mission to provide such functions using synthetic catalogues of H,α galaxies based on the 54Ģpc Flagship 1 simulation, which is designed to reproduce the Euclid spectroscopic sample. We comprehensively validate the one-loop galaxy power spectrum and tree-level bispectrum predictions from perturbation theory in both real and redshift space. Assuming scale cuts consistent with our previous power spectrum study on the same catalogues, this modelling yielded unbiased cosmological constraints for the bispectrum up to ̊m max = 0.15̨Mpc in real space and 0.08 , (0.1)̨Mpc at the lowest (highest) redshift, corresponding to z=0.9 (z=1.8), for the monopole and quadrupole in redshift space using statistical uncertainties corresponding to the full simulation volume. With these scale cuts, adding bispectrum information to the power spectrum improves constraints on the amplitude of scalar perturbations and the matter density by up to 30%, increasing the overall figure of merit for key cosmological parameters by a factor of about 2.5. A simple rescaling of the statistical uncertainties to a Euclid -like volume indicates similar conclusions, highlighting the add…

title: Phenotyping replication strongly influences genomic predictive ability in sweet sorghum (Sorghum bicolor [L.] Moench)
abstract: Article summary Genomic selection can accelerate breeding when the phenotypic and genomic information used to train prediction models is sufficiently reliable and relevant to the prediction target. Using a sweet sorghum breeding population evaluated in three Haitian field environments, we quantified the effects of phenotyping replication, training population (TP) size, TP–validation population (VP) genomic relatedness, and prediction model on genomic predictive ability for grain yield, plant height, stem weight, and total soluble solids. Increasing phenotyping replication consistently improved predictive ability across traits and environments and increased the precision of phenotypic estimates, with particularly large effects observed for grain yield. Larger TPs generally improved predictive ability; however, when TP sizes of 150 and 200 individuals were compared, the effect of increasing phenotyping replication was consistently greater than that of increasing TP size. Greater TP–VP genomic relatedness was also generally associated with higher predictive ability, whereas differences among prediction models were comparatively small and inconsistent across traits and environments. These results provide empirical evidence that genomic prediction performance in sweet sorghum depends not only on prediction model choice but also on the design and quality of the TP. In particular, for…

title: Development of a UAV for vision-based fault detection in power transmission systems using deep learning
abstract: Purpose Reliable operation of power transmission systems depend on timely detection of insulator faults, yet conventional manual inspection is costly, hazardous and inconsistent. This study presents an unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)-based vision inspection approach integrating platform development, autonomous flight validation and a controlled multi-generation You Only Look Once (YOLO) benchmark for binary insulator fault detection. Design/methodology/approach A lightweight quadrotor UAV was developed and validated through six autonomous missions along a 132 kV transmission corridor near Prayagraj, India. A dataset of 3,951 annotated insulator images combining 3,173 UAV-collected images and 778 from a publicly available source, comprising 2,847 normal and 1,104 defective instances, was assembled with an 80:10:10 split and flight-level data leakage prevention. Five YOLO variants (YOLOv8s–YOLOv12s) were trained under matched conditions from Common Objects in Context (COCO)-pretrained weights. A FLUKE TiS75+ thermal camera was used separately as complementary qualitative evidence. Findings YOLOv8s achieved the best test-set performance: precision 0.895, recall 0.810, mAP@0.50 of 0.879 and mAP@0.50–0.95 of 0.482 at 142 FPS, outperforming all four newer YOLO generations. Thermal imaging at defective locations revealed hotspot temperatures of 83.5°C–197.6°C against backgrounds below…

Advanced Practice Nursing Students’ Experiences of the Virtual Learning Cafe Method
abstract: Background: The Learning Café method based on educational constructivism may increasingly be used as Online Learner Collaboration facilitated by the teacher. Purpose: This qualitative study draws together Advanced Practice Nursing students’ experiences of the Virtual Learning Café method. The findings can be useful when evaluating the suitability of the method for students undertaking Master-level health or social studies, especially from the perspective of developing evidence-based clinical practice and interprofessional collaboration. Materials and Methods: 28 nursing students earning a Master’s Degree in Advanced Practice Nursing were requested to write an essay reflecting on a Virtual Learning Café experience. The data was analyzed using inductive content analysis. Results: The study participants agreed that the Virtual Learning Café could be effectively used for both learning and development, or as a collaborative learning structure and as a model transferable to the development of health service practice. According to the participants, the method may be effective in development efforts for individual professionals, in interprofessional teams, in and between organizations, and between citizens and health service professionals. The participants appreciated the dialogic and participatory nature of the method and emphasized collective construction of knowledge. Conclusion: Th…

title: Virtual reality as HR firewall: using simulation performance to de-risk global venturing
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to address international assignment failures during global venturing. It shows how chief human resources officers (CHROs) can transition pre-departure evaluation from an administrative checkbox into a data-driven barrier that protects corporate investments. Design/methodology/approach This paper bridges research with practice. It extends empirical findings on international service performance to a new corporate framework where candidates are evaluated in immersive virtual reality environments to establish uniform readiness metrics. Findings Traditional resume screening and passive orientations fail to predict international success. This paper demonstrates that an individual’s virtual reality (VR) simulation performance could help predict on-the-ground capability. Strategic HR can systematically de-risk global mobility budgets by using specific performance metrics as deployment gatekeeping mechanisms. Practical implications Practitioners gain a visual framework to automate global mobility pipelines. The paper outlines operational metrics for using VR simulation tests to halt high-risk deployments before field costs occur. Originality/value This paper reframes global talent mobility as a strict financial risk discipline. Instead of using virtual reality purely for training, it introduces a model where VR performance scores serve as an HR firewall, giving t…

Responses of soil-plant systems to anthropogenic disturbance in alpine-cold wetlands on the southeastern Tibetan plateau
abstract: Alpine-cold wetland ecosystems are highly sensitive to human disturbance, yet the responses and relationships of soil–plant systems to anthropogenic disturbance remain poorly understood. Taking the Napahai alpine-cold wetland in north-western Yunnan as the study area, this research assessed the responses of soil and plant systems to different disturbance types and explored the potential relationships among soil properties, microbial indicators, and vegetation characteristics. By combining vegetation surveys with laboratory analyses, we measured vegetation traits, plant total C, N and P contents, soil physicochemical properties, soil enzyme activities, and microbial biomass. Results showed that human disturbance significantly altered soil properties ( P < 0.05). Grazing, trampling and agricultural management markedly affected soil bulk density and total porosity, while agricultural management also influenced soil moisture. Under mowing, soil moisture and porosity were higher, and bulk density was lower. Vegetation cover, height, above-ground biomass and diversity were also strongly affected, with trampling causing the greatest structural damage and the lowest biomass, whereas agricultural management sites exhibited the highest plant diversity. Plant total C, N and P contents showed no significant differences across disturbance types. Soil microbial indicators responded marked…

title: The Supreme International Crime: On Power and Inequalities in Light of the Special Tribunal for Aggression Against Ukraine
abstract: Abstract The crime of aggression remains underexplored from a criminological perspective. This article addresses that omission by structuring it around three lines of inquiry. Firstly, it places the crime of aggression within the study of political and state crime, arguing that it occupies a marginal position in the literature and resists clean classification under existing theoretical definitional frameworks. Secondly, it examines impunity and the structural inequalities sustaining it through the lens of the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine. While the Tribunal represents an important step towards accountability and a significant development in international criminal law, it finds that immunities embedded within its jurisdictional architecture risk reproducing existing power inequalities. Finally, the article considers how these patterns might be challenged. It argues that a victim-centred approach, informed by the transitional justice paradigm, could offer a structural corrective, capable of contesting these inequalities while contributing to addressing survivors’ demands for justice.

title: Co-Design of a Low-Power RISC-V Processor and a Reconfigurable Neural Network Accelerator for Edge AI Computing
abstract: The operational efficiency of the compact edge AI accelerator is susceptible to variations in network structure and data transmission speed. To address this issue, this study proposes a collaborative design scheme for digital integrated circuits. By adjusting the working mode of the computing array and coordinating with storage and power management, the operational efficiency of the accelerator is improved. The research tested three network models trained on the publicly available Digits dataset. The results showed that the average accuracy of integer reasoning ranged from 96.78% to 97.33%, and the average loss was at most 0.11 percentage points compared to floating-point reasoning. In a cost model with 64 processing units and 8 KiB memory, compared to a fixed array, this scheme reduced the inference delay by 14.83% to 18.74%, decreased the single-inference energy consumption by 6.86% to 8.81%, and increased the area by 7.58%. Further experiments demonstrated that reducing the waiting time between data transmission and computation plays a major role in improving operational efficiency. Allowing the computing array to flexibly adjust its working mode can also increase the utilization rate of processing units, but this improvement is still limited by data transmission capabilities. In the hardware resource allocation test, the scheme with 64 computing elements and 1 KB memory fur…

title: Determining grafting compatibility for some selected intraspecific pumpkin as rootstock (Cucurbita moschata) with watermelon (Citrullus lanatus)
Constant-Power Hydraulic Drive and Dynamic Volume-Compensated Leakage Detection for a Grain Silo Sweep Auger
abstract: A constant-power hydraulic drive and a leakage-detection method based on dynamic volume compensation are developed for a grain silo sweep auger to address insufficient torque under low-speed heavy-load conditions and false flow-balance alarms caused by rapid pressure variations. A variable-displacement axial piston pump and a load-sensing circuit provide adaptive pressure-flow regulation. A flow residual is established from the supply, return, and motor case-drain flow rates, and dynamic volume compensation attenuates the effects of fluid compressibility, line elasticity, and accumulator charging and discharging. Within the constant-power envelope, the drive extends the low-speed heavy-load operating range by trading rotational speed for torque. The compensated residual suppresses transient flow disturbances during load variations while retaining the imbalance caused by sustained external leakage. At 45 kW, the predicted torque reaches 6900 N·m at approximately 62.3 r/min, or 2.10 times the rated torque of the original electric drive. Leakage decisions additionally require residual persistence and agreement with reservoir-level trends to separate hydraulic faults from sensor failures.

title: Leadership in virtual teams of technology-based companies: an abductive thematic analysis
abstract: Purpose Technology-based companies (TBCs) often rely on virtual teams (VTs), which allow them to overcome the limitations of face-to-face teams. However, VTs have their own challenges in terms of relationships. The relational dynamics and the influence of the organizational context on VTs is not yet entirely clear. In this study, the authors aims to explore some leadership dynamics in teams working in TBCs. Design/methodology/approach This research explores how the leadership role has been adapted to TBCs adopting agile methodologies. The authors conducted an abductive thematic analysis of the accounts of seven leaders and nine members of six VTs operating in Latin American TBCs. Findings The authors’ results suggest that team cohesion depends directly on open communication and active listening, informal relationships and spaces for growth. Some of the interviewed leaders indicate that they implement these practices to incite bonds within their teams. In this sense, the participants of the authors’ study place great value on interpersonal relationships that emerge in informal spaces to strengthen communication and trust. Furthermore, the authors’ findings suggest that agile methodologies enable the creation of a formal structure. Specifically, these methodologies clearly establish workflows, roles and individual responsibilities. Originality/value The authors’ study explores le…

title: Modification Strategies for Hard-Carbon-Based Anode Materials in Sodium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries offer abundant resources, low cost, and high safety, making them promising for large-scale energy storage. Hard carbon, a key anode material, enables Na+ storage through its disordered structure, enlarged interlayer spacing, and abundant defects and pores. However, these features also cause electrolyte side reactions and sluggish Na+ transport, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), poor rate capability, and limited low-voltage plateau capacity. This paper explores the correlation between hard carbon microstructure and sodium storage, and the mechanisms by which different modifications improve electrochemical performance. Drawing on representative studies published in recent years, this review summarizes the progress in hard-carbon anode modification, with particular emphasis on structural regulation, sodium-storage mechanisms, and electrochemical performance optimization. It also discusses the advantages, limitations, and potential synergies of different modification strategies. The results reveal that the electrochemical performance of hard carbon is influenced by multiple factors like surface structure, carbon layer arrangement, pore characteristics, and the transport process, while a single structural optimization cannot simultaneously meet the requirements of ICE, rate performance, and plateau capacity. The coordinated regulation of multi-s…

title: Formaldehyde Emission from Passenger Vehicle Interior Materials: Sources, Release Dynamics, and Formaldehyde-Free Alternatives
abstract: Passenger-vehicle cabins contain a large exposed material area within a small air volume, so emissions from seats, carpets, headliners, dashboards, door trim, seals and adhesives can accumulate when ventilation is limited. This paper examines how interior-material composition and manufacture determine formaldehyde formation, migration and release, and whether nominally formaldehyde-free alternatives can be regarded as low-emitting throughout service life. A structured secondary-data synthesis was developed around source chemistry, the initial emittable concentration (C 0 ), material-phase diffusion coefficient (D m ), material-air partition coefficient (K), environmental conditions and ageing. Published chamber and vehicle studies show that temperature strongly changes emission parameters and cabin concentration, while multilayer construction and concealed adhesive layers complicate source attribution. Field evidence further shows that formaldehyde concentration is not described adequately by a single universal release period: early depletion can be followed by slower diffusion, humidity-sensitive hydrolysis, thermal reactivation or secondary formation. Formaldehyde-free preparation routes include isocyanate, polyurethane, epoxy, polyvinyl acetate, hot-melt and bio-based adhesive systems, but replacing formaldehyde as a feedstock does not establish zero lifetime emission. The m…

title: Comparative HPHC Emission Profiles of Combustible and Alternative Nicotine Products in South Africa: Development of a Relative HPHC Emission Index
abstract: Abstract Alternative nicotine and tobacco products are increasingly available in South Africa, yet independent comparative data on their harmful and potentially harmful constituent (HPHC) emission profiles remain limited. The aim of this study was to compare mainstream emissions from an illicit combustible cigarette (Brand X), IQOS ILUMA heated tobacco products (TEREA Amber and TEREA Turquoise), a VEEV Now Ultra Mint disposable electronic nicotine delivery system, and ZYN modern oral nicotine pouches, with the 1R6F reference cigarette included as a combustible benchmark. Combustion-related markers CO, NO and NOx were evaluated in TEREA aerosols under synthetic-air and nitrogen atmospheres, while nine WHO-priority HPHCs were quantified using standardized analytical methods. Emissions were normalized to 100 cm3 of nominal puff volume where applicable. Brand X produced high emissions across the measured HPHC panel, including 4.91 ± 0.28 mg/100 cm3 CO, 248.67 ± 14.55 μg/100 cm3 acetaldehyde, 23.66 ± 2.27 μg/100 cm3 acrolein, 11.33 ± 1.43 μg/100 cm3 formaldehyde, 17.20 ± 0.75 μg/100 cm3 1,3-butadiene and 13.29 ± 1.01 μg/100 cm3 benzene. TEREA aerosols generated CO, NO and NOx concentrations below the BSI PAS 8850:2020 combustion-marker thresholds under both atmospheres, supporting the absence of combustion under the tested conditions. Across the WHO-9 panel, TEREA aerosols showed su…

title: Subacute carbon monoxide exposure alters AgNOR number and area ratio in the cerebral cortex of rats
abstract: Abstract We aimed to evaluate the effects of hypoxia induced by different levels of subacute carbon monoxide (CO) exposure on the total AgNOR area/total nuclear area (TAA/TNA) ratio and mean AgNOR number in rat cerebral cortical tissue. Eighteen Albino Wistar adult male rats were randomly divided into three groups (control as group A, 1000ppm and 3000ppm concentration of CO gas exposed as group B and C, respectively). CO gas was chronically given as 30 min a day during seven days. Statistically significant differences were found among the groups for both mean AgNOR number (χ2 = 12.051, p = 0.002) and TAA/TNA (χ2 = 12.316, p = 0.002), respectively. When the two groups are compared in terms of TAA/TNA ratio, statistically significant differences were detected between control and 1000ppm (Z = -2.882, p = 0.004), between control and 3000 ppm (Z = -2.882, p = 0.004) for TAA/TNA ratio. Statistically significant differences were found between control and 1000 ppm (Z = -2.882, p = 0.004), between control and 3000 ppm (Z = - 2.887, p = 0.004) for mean AgNOR number. It is important to determine new markers with high sensitivity and easy to apply in order to determine the effect of toxication in different organs and tissues (especially brain tissues) that are subacutely exposed to carbon monoxide intoxication. It seems that AgNOR may be used for this purpose.

title: Synergy of Pyridinic Nitrogen and Fe–Co Bimetallic Species on N-Doped Carbon for Highly Selective Ammoxidation of Aromatic Alcohols to Nitriles
abstract: Abstract Catalytic ammoxidation of alcohols to nitriles under cyanide-free conditions has attracted considerable attention. Conventional approaches often rely on toxic cyanide sources, which create environmental and safety concerns that conflict with the core principles of green chemistry. Herein, we report the synthesis of an efficient Fe–Co bimetallic catalyst supported on N-doped carbon, denoted as FexCoyN–C (where x and y represent the nominal Fe/Co molar ratios of the metal precursors used during catalyst preparation), for the selective ammoxidation of aromatic alcohols to nitriles using ammonia as the nitrogen source. In the ammoxidation of 1-naphthalenemethanol, the Fe3Co7N–C catalyst delivers outstanding performance, affording a remarkable 99.9% yield of 1-naphthonitrile. Across the catalyst series, the catalytic activity shows positive correlations with the relative proportions of pyridinic N and Fe2+ species. Together with the mechanistic experiments and literature precedents, these observations suggest that pyridinic N may facilitate interfacial electron transfer, while Fe2+/Fe3+ redox chemistry may contribute to alcohol dehydrogenation. Time-dependent product distribution experiments and stepwise catalytic tests confirm that 1-naphthalenemethanol is first oxidized to 1-naphthaldehyde, which then undergoes ammoxidation to yield 1-naphthonitrile. This work offers new …

title: Initial affect shapes risk-benefit information processing and public support for carbon dioxide removal technologies
abstract: Abstract Given the accelerating climate crisis, carbon dioxide removal (CDR) technologies are becoming increasingly important, while public support may play a relevant role in their implementation. This support is influenced by how citizens inform themselves about the technology. While prior research has examined public support under conditions of no or predefined information provision, little is known about the factors that shape how individuals actively select information about CDR and integrate it into their preferences about the technology. Here, we investigate how initial affect towards CDR shapes laypersons’ selection and evaluation of benefit-related versus risk-related information about the technology and how these processes influence subsequent policy support. In a preregistered study with 714 U.S. participants, we introduced a novel information-sampling task, in which participants could freely choose which information about CDR to attend to, followed by a policy choice experiment assessing public support of CDR technologies. In line with our hypotheses, participants’ initial affect influenced their information search: more initial positive affect towards CDR was associated with a higher likelihood to select benefit-related versus risk-related information about CDR. This confirmatory information search, in turn, was associated with immediate changes in affect towards t…

title: Pump-Guided Directional Amplification of Spontaneous Emission in Single-Crystal MAPbBr3
abstract: Abstract We report directional amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in a MAPbBr3 single crystal, which is produced by a single-pass excitation of femtosecond pulses at 560 nm and propagates coaxially with the pump beam during amplification interactions. The chirp in the pump pulses induces a delayed interaction between the photoluminescence (PL) produced by the shorter wavelength components and the excitation by the longer wavelength components, forming a “chasing–overlapping–leaving” process. The group velocity dispersion performance on the falling edge of the absorption spectrum of the MAPbBr3 crystal favors a large extension of the interaction length, facilitating such an ASE process along the pumping channel. The ASE interactions produce a yellow beam with a peak wavelength of 575 nm and a pulse energy of 0.47 nJ for a pump pulse energy of 1.2 μJ. The output ASE beam has the same quality as the pump in the small divergence and high-quality transverse mode.

Climate risk and corporate carbon emissions: a cross-country study
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether country-level climate risk influences corporate carbon emissions. It also investigates how financial slack shapes firms’ responses to climate risk. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of 10,834 firm-year observations from 42 countries over the period from 2010 to 2024, we applied regression models on panel data estimated with robust standard errors. We also addressed endogeneity using propensity score matching, two-stage least squares and difference-in-differences approaches. Findings The findings show that firms exposed to climate risk exhibit higher carbon emissions, consistent with the resource-constraint perspective. Indeed, climate-related risks can hinder corporate environmental performance by limiting the financial capacity required to implement sustainable carbon reduction strategies. This positive association is significantly weaker among firms with greater financial flexibility, proxied by long-term and short-term financial slack, and significantly stronger among financially constrained firms. This positive association is also attenuated in the post–Paris Agreement period (2016 onward), among firms with a sustainability committee and among those operating under more stringent environmental policy regimes. These results point to institutional pressure and internal governance as additional channels that offset the positive effe…

title: Extracorporeal carbon dioxide removal as a de-escalation strategy from veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in acute respiratory distress syndrome: A case report
abstract: Background Extracorporeal carbon dioxide removal (ECCO2R) can be used to wean patients from venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). However, its use remains minimally explored in the literature. This case reports the use of ECCO2R in a patient with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), an infected ECMO cannula, and persistent hypercapnia. Case summary A 39-year-old man placed on venovenous ECMO for ARDS secondary to viral pneumonia developed acute kidney injury, circuit air embolism, and pulmonary hemorrhage during his course. After 80 days on ECMO support, purulent discharge was noted at the femoral cannula site, and the patient remained dependent on sweep gas despite multiple weaning attempts. ECMO support was subsequently de-escalated to ECCO2r and he was decannulated after improvement in blood gases parameters. Conclusion ECCO2R successfully facilitated de-escalation of respiratory support from venovenous ECMO in this complicated case of persistent hypercapnia. The optimal timing and safety of transitioning to ECCO2R still need to be evaluated in larger studies.

Association of Intraoperative End-tidal Carbon Dioxide, Ventilation, and Hypotension with Postoperative Mortality in Noncardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background: Low intraoperative end-tidal carbon dioxide (ET co 2 ) has been associated with increased postoperative mortality in retrospective studies. However, whether this association is independent of intraoperative hypotension, a strong predictor of mortality, and minute ventilation, a primary determinant of ET co 2 , remains uncertain. The authors hypothesized that low intraoperative ET co 2 is independently associated with postoperative mortality after adjustment for both intraoperative hypotension and minute ventilation. Methods: The authors conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing noncardiac surgery during general anesthesia with mechanical ventilation between 2010 and 2020 at a tertiary care center. Primary exposures were intraoperative mean ET co 2 , minute ventilation, and hypotension (severity and duration). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression estimated the independent association between ET co 2 and mortality after adjustment for predefined confounders. An interaction between ET co 2 and hypotension was tested. Results: Among 185,455 patients (in-hospital mortality, 0.85%), lower intraoperative ET co 2 was nonlinearly associated with increased mortality (adjusted odds ratio per 5-mmHg decrease from the median, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.36 to 1.86) independent of minute ventilation and hypotension. Dual Activation and C–N Coupling of CO 2 and N 2 Mediated by Small Fe n + Clusters
abstract: Abstract We present a combined experimental and theoretical study on how small iron clusters activate dinitrogen (N2) and carbon dioxide (CO2) under ambient conditions. Mass spectrometry shows these clusters can cleave the N≡N triple bond, producing a range of odd-nitrogen species, with Fe3N7+ and Fe4N7+ appearing as major products. Introducing CO2 into the downstream flow-tube reactor yields distinct FenNmCO+ and FenNmO+ species, indicating that the CO2 also undergoes C═O bond dissociation under this condition. Thermodynamics and kinetics analyses reveal that the formation of Fe3,4N5CO+ proceeds via C–N coupling pathways and generates a stable N2O molecule. The empty d orbitals of Fe atoms facilitate the coordination of N2 and CO2; meanwhile, not only Fen+ but also the Fe3,4N7+ clusters exhibit delocalized electrons and superatomic states. This allows the half-filled superatomic P orbital to engage in superatom–atom bonding with carbon and oxygen atoms, thereby modifying the covalent coordination and active sites for reactions with N2 and CO2. These findings advance mechanistic insight into nitrogen fixation by iron clusters─highlighting the role of electron delocalization─and point to a promising route of plasma-assisted catalytic conversion of atmospheric CO2 and N2 into value-added products under mild conditions.

Study on the coupling effect characteristics of multiple RFID sensors for crack monitoring in aluminum alloy structure
abstract: Purpose The aircraft skins are prone to fracturing, leading to serious safety hazards, due to manufacturing defects, overstress, fatigue and harsh environments. Therefore, a method with high reliability, low cost and simple networking was needed to achieve structural life evaluation through continuous monitoring. This paper aims to investigate using a sensing system consisting of densely arranged multiple tags for crack monitoring in aluminum alloy structures. Design/methodology/approach In this paper, a sensing system was composed of four tag arrangements, and the variation of gain and impedance caused by the coupling effect among tags was analyzed via simulation. The reliability of sensor systems for crack detection was studied by constructing a test platform. Findings The simulation results showed that as the crack depth in the coverage area of Tag 1 increased, the real part of the impedance of Tag 1 remained constant. In contrast, the value of the imaginary part tended to increase, while the impedance values of other tags remained unchanged. The gain of Tag 1 decreased, while the gains of the different tags remained unchanged. The test results indicated that the backscattered power tended to decrease as the crack depth increased when a single tag was placed on the surface of the aluminum alloy structure. The backscattered power of Tag 1 increased, while the backscattered po…

title: Produced-Gas (PG) Versus CO2 Foam in Carbonate Porous Media: Residual-Oil Sensitivity
abstract: Abstract Foam is commonly evaluated with pure CO2 for gas mobility control, yet field operations may inject a CO2-rich produced-gas stream containing methane and nitrogen. This study compares the transport behavior of foam stabilized by the branched nonionic surfactant G12 in pure CO2 and produced gas (PG) in Indiana limestone under reservoir conditions. Foam apparent viscosity was evaluated as a function of the superficial velocity, foam quality, residual oil, and surfactant concentration. Both CO2 and PG generated strong foam and substantial mobility control. Under oil-free conditions, the PG foam generally exhibited higher apparent viscosity than the CO2 foam over the tested velocity and foam-quality ranges. However, residual oil reduced the PG foam strength more strongly than the CO2 foam strength. The CO2 foam showed similar velocity-dependent behavior with and without residual oil, whereas the PG foam exhibited lower apparent viscosity and a changed shear-thinning response in the oil-bearing core. Power-law fits showed similar velocity dependence for CO2 foam with and without residual oil, whereas the PG system showed a larger difference between oil-free and residual-oil conditions. Foam-quality scans similarly showed that the PG foam was more strongly affected by residual oil, particularly at intermediate foam qualities. These results indicate that pure CO2 does not nece…

title: Intelligent Energy Consumption Model for a Smart Building
abstract: Background The increasing deployment of smart meters in buildings has created opportunities for data-driven energy management, but the detection of abnormal electricity consumption remains challenging because energy-use patterns vary with time, operational schedules, and environmental conditions. These smart meters and connected monitoring technologies continuously create electricity consumption data, which can be used for energy management, fault detection, operational monitoring, and predictive maintenance. Methods In order to monitor building electricity consumption, this study developed an intelligent anomaly detection system based on a Support Vector Machine (SVM) with a radial basis function (RBF) kernel. Electricity consumption data sourced from smart meters was used as the developed model achieved reliable anomaly detection, identifying irregular energy consumption with improved detection and achieved dependable anomaly detection. Results The overall performance metrics of the model was Accuracy of 97.79%, with a macro-averaged F1 Score of 0.8842, Precision of 0.925, and Recall of 0.8513 The results showed reduced false alarms and enhanced adaptability to changes in energy use patterns. Conclusion The study contributed to energy efficiency, cost reduction, and sustainable building management, while also providing a reliable framework for intelligent energy monitoring in…

title: Fire Bloom: Energy-Efficient Cluster-Based Routing Protocol for Scalable Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have been used in smart agriculture, industrial automation, and environmental monitoring applications, which require efficient and reliable routing with energy efficiency. Particularly the selection and operation of the cluster heads (CHs) play significant role in the performance of the network. In this work, we introduce a scalable, reliable and energy efficient cluster-based routing protocol (Fire Bloom), which combines adaptive CH selection and energy-aware routing. The cluster map and the packet flow intensity map even show the communication loads on the base station. The packet delivery ratio (PDR) of Fire Bloom is 97.2%, which is 6–10% better than the competing protocols. Fire Bloom achieved a PDR greater than 91% under a scalability test with 100–500 nodes, which means it can maintain good performance as the density of the network becomes denser. Energy usage is roughly proportional to the traffic volume but lower than previously reported values. Near-linear scalability at runtime is also proposed: increasing the number of nodes from 100 to 1,000 took from 1.2 s to 14.1 s. In general, Fire Bloom lowers overall end-to-end delay, increases load balancing across CHs, boosts energy efficiency, and it is resilient to changes in network conditions and maintains successful packet delivery. These results prove that it is capable of scalable and en…

title: Wsn Cluster Head Selection for Energy Balancing Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Model
abstract: Energy efficiency is a critical design consideration for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), particularly in heterogeneous environments. To optimize energy utilization and enhance network longevity, this study integrates deep learning models into the cluster head (CH) selection process. The proposed methodology employs a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to analyze spatial attributes such as residual energy, node density, and proximity to sinks, and a Recurrent Neural Network with Long Short-Term Memory (RNN-LSTM) to capture temporal variations in energy depletion and workload distribution. The outputs of these models are combined through a hierarchical decision framework, enabling dynamic and adaptive CH selection. Comparative analysis with I-SEP and OptGACHE demonstrates that the proposed methodology maintains a residual energy of 9.89 J at a node density of 150, surpassing I-SEP and OptGACHE by 1.34% and 1.33%, respectively. Cluster lifetime is extended to 0.63 ms for 20 clusters, reflecting improvements of 16.7% over OptGACHE and 57.5% over I-SEP. Additionally, the packet delivery rate (PDR) reaches 450,000 kbps at a node density of 150, representing enhancements of 28.6% over OptGACHE and 50% over I-SEP. These findings validate the proposed methodology as a robust solution for energy-efficient CH selection, improving the sustainability and performance of WSNs in diverse oper…
