title: AI-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality–Emotional Attachment–Loyalty Pathway in 2025–2026
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although online-shopping participation should not be interpreted as a direct measure of AI adoption or retailer-specific investment. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). The study considers a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establ…

title: Holistic Community Service at Lembaga Kesejahteraan Sosial Anak Widya Asih Blimbingsari: Spiritual Empowerment and Social Support by STT Bethel Indonesia Doctoral Program
abstract: This community service program aimed to provide holistic support—encompassing spiritual enrichment, educational assistance, and essential daily necessities—to children at Lembaga Kesejahteraan Sosial Anak (LKSA) Widya Asih Blimbingsari, Kecamatan Melaya, Kabupaten Jembrana, Bali. The program was jointly implemented by doctoral students and lecturers from Sekolah Tinggi Teologi Bethel Indonesia (STT Bethel Indonesia), Petamburan Jakarta, coinciding with the institution's commemoration of its 50th Golden Anniversary. A participatory approach was employed, integrating direct service delivery with academic inquiry through interviews with LKSA management and community figures. Core activities included a joint worship service, a devotional sermon, and the distribution of educational materials (notebooks, pens), personal hygiene items (bathing soap, shampoo), and institutional-branded t-shirts to all children. The results demonstrate that the program successfully strengthened the spiritual well-being and academic motivation of the children, provided meaningful material support, and fostered enduring relational bonds between STT Bethel Indonesia and the Christian social welfare institution. The participatory and holistic model employed in this program highlights the pivotal role that theological higher education institutions can play as partners in community-based social welfare, contr…

title: Consumer Protection in the Digital Economy Era: A Literature Analysis of E-Commerce Regulation in Indonesia
abstract: The growth of Indonesia’s digital economy has driven a significant transformation in transaction patterns while posing new challenges regarding consumer protection. Although the Consumer Protection Law and Personal Data Protection Law have been passed, they are not considered optimal in responding to the complexity of the digital ecosystem. This research uses a descriptive qualitative approach based on a structured literature review combined with doctrinal legal analysis and thematic synthesis. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of consumer protection regulations in e-commerce transactions in Indonesia by examining legal studies, consumer behavior, and international regulatory comparisons through a literature review approach. The study’s results show that regulatory implementation weaknesses, low digital literacy, insufficiently standardized online dispute resolution mechanisms, and institutional enforcement and supervisory gaps remain important obstacles. Additionally, an overly rigid ex-ante regulatory approach has the potential to stifle digital innovation. Therefore, adaptive, participatory policy reformulation based on the principle of equitable consumer protection is needed.

title: Microfluidic Brillouin platform for frequency-resolved mechanics of complex fluids
abstract: We introduce an integrated microfluidic platform that combines pressure-flow rheology with depth-resolved Brillouin microspectroscopy to investigate complex fluids in extensive frequency ranges. Apparent viscosity is measured via calibrated pressure-flow in a rectangular polydimethylsiloxane microchannel, while GHz-frequency Brillouin spectroscopy probes longitudinal mechanics under identical steady-flow conditions. Using semi-dilute methylcellulose solutions in a cell-culture medium as a model, we reveal mild shear-thinning behavior, whereas the Brillouin frequency shift and linewidth values remain constant throughout the flow rate range, mainly influenced by polymer concentration. This confirms the decoupling between steady-shear and GHz-frequency acoustic responses observed previously. The platform offers a compact, calibrated approach for frequency-resolved mechanical analysis of flowing soft materials and perfused media.

title: The Differential Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis in Solanum lycopersicum ‘Micro-Tom’ Embryo by SEM
AI-generated advertising in agricultural livestreaming and the auditability of disclosure regulation: a three-layer audit of public Douyin data from China
abstract: Agricultural products are credence goods, and in livestreaming, the grower’s visible presence signals the price. China has required labeling of deep-synthesis content since January 2023 and, since 1 September 2025, of AI-generated synthetic content. Whether public platform data can verify compliance in a market where the authenticity premium is especially salient remains unclear, given that growers themselves sell produce. We audited three layers of public Chinese platform data: 189 policy snippets, 19 accounts retrieved by AI technical terms, and 455 unique authors retrieved by crop names. In the one policy coding field with complete intercoder agreement ( κ = 1.000), only 6 of 189 snippets name authenticity as a farmer asset. Retrieval by technical terms returns intermediaries: 13 of 19 accounts sell AI tools or tutorials, and none discloses using AI to sell its own produce. Among AI-announcing cases retrieved by crop-name queries, an expanded text-field detector validated at 94.7% recall flags 10 of 455 authors: seven supply-side or service-provider accounts, one incidental non-agricultural mention, and two product-query artifacts; none discloses grower own-use of AI livestreaming. Checks of API-exposed platform metadata for all 575 video records and cover images for 472 records found no platform-side AI label or visible AI/AIGC/statutory AI-generated notice. AI was announce…

title: Effect of Peer Support on Resilience and Emotional Regulation among University Students: Mediating Role of Stress Management
abstract: This current study was carried out to analyze the impact of peer support on resilience and emotional regulation in university students considering the mediating influence of stress management. Quantitative correlational research approach with a convenient sampling technique was used for the current study. Information was gathered from 150 university students of Pakistan (n = 81 males and n = 69 females) with ages between 18-27 years using standardized measures: Friend subscale of the multidimensional scale of perceived social support (MSPSS), perceived stress scale (PSS-10), brief resilience scale (BRS), and emotional regulation questionnaire (ERQ). Pearson correlation, regression analysis and mediation analysis using bootstrapping approach was performed. It was found that peer support had a significant positive effect on emotional regulation (B = .34, p < .001), however, its direct effect on resilience was not significant. Most importantly, stress management partially mediated the link between peer support and resilience (B = .39, p < .05) as well as emotional regulation (B = .32, p < .05). The current study underscores the important significance of peer support network along with stress management interventions in enhancing psychological well-being of university students.

title: Regulation Mechanism of Well-barrier Thickness on Optical Gain and Loss for High-Power Ultraviolet Semiconductor Lasers
Sequence-Engineered Multifunctional Peptide Nanozyme Gel for Catalytic Microenvironment Regulation in Diabetic Infected Wounds
abstract: Abstract Chronic diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent infection, redox imbalance, and dysregulated enzymatic activity, yet current biomaterials largely function as passive dressings, with limited capacity to actively intervene in the stalled healing cascade. Here, we report a sequence-programmed peptide nanozyme that encodes multiple enzyme-mimetic activities within a single supramolecular framework for adaptive microenvironment regulation. By mimicking the coordination motifs of natural hydrolases and superoxide dismutase, a de novo peptide sequence, C7-RD(S)HHEEH, was rationally engineered to encode integrated nitrogen/oxygen metal-binding sites. The incorporation of a side-chain–modified serine enhances coordination adaptability, while glutamate residues facilitate catalytic functionality. Upon Cu2+ coordination, the peptide self-assembles into a nanozyme exhibiting hydrolase (HYD)-, oxidase (OXD)-, peroxidase (POD)-, and superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activities within a unified framework, thereby enabling coordinated regulation of enzymatic debridement, antibacterial defense, and redox homeostasis. Incorporated into a sprayable gelatin hydrogel, the nanozyme provides conformal wound coverage while maintaining excellent biocompatibility and sustained catalytic functionality. In a diabetic bacteria-infected wound model, the nanozyme gel significantly accelerates …

title: Environment-Related Technological Innovation and Ecological Footprint in India: Aggregate and Component-Wise Time–Frequency Analysis
abstract: This study investigates the time-frequency dynamics between environment-related technological innovation and environmental quality using the ecological footprint as a comprehensive measure of environmental quality and its components for India. To capture time-varying and frequency-dependent relationships, the study adopts a wavelet coherence framework, which allows simultaneous analysis of short-, medium-, and long-run dynamics between environment-related technological innovation and environmental quality for the period between 1990Q1 to 2022Q4. The results indicate that the relationship between environment-related technological innovation and environmental quality is strongly time-varying and scale-dependent. In the aggregate ecological footprint, the significant coherence is concentrated on the short and medium horizons, while the long-run interactions are weak and non-persistent. The phase dynamics show that the rise in ecological footprint precedes the adoption of environment-related technological innovation. In components analysis, it shows a strong short-term coherence between technological innovation in the environmental field and single parts of the ecological footprint. At the same time, the medium-run effects are intermittent, and the long-run relationships are mostly insignificant or driven by boundary effects. The results suggest that the environmental benefits from…

title: Low-voltage, ultra-broadband wearable MEMS ultrasound: a frequency-merged, wafer-scale framework for continuous in vivo cardiovascular imaging and monitoring
Roadmap for inferring metabolic regulation using multiomics, machine learning, and genome-scale modeling
Complexity of frequency fluctuations and the interpretive style in the case study of a set of musical pieces of bass viola da gamba
abstract: Based on a computational musicology framework that bridges the gap between scientists and musicians, this case study investigates the feasibility of capturing the relationship between the presence of complex frequency fluctuations and the interpretive style. Because there is no well-known method for capturing such a relationship, we propose a preliminary formulation for identifying differences in musical interpretation. In particular, we focus on a set of musical pieces performed by the same interpreter on the bass viola da gamba. We analyzed digital audio data to best identify statistical regularities in audio frequencies (Hz) and their complex network properties in musical notation. Based on an interdisciplinary approach, we computed the spectral decomposition and translated its frequency components into a network of sounds. We applied a best-fit analysis for identifying the statistical distributions that most precisely describe the behavior of these frequencies, and we computed the centrality measures and identified cliques for characterizing such a network. Our findings reveal statistical regularities in the type of statistical distribution that best describes frequency fluctuations. The centrality measures confirmed the most influential and stable group of sounds in a piece of music, while the identification of the largest clique indicated functional groups of sounds that …

title: Corrigendum to SLAMF7 regulates the inflammatory response in macrophages during polymicrobial sepsis
From pathogen burden to host response: complement remodeling as a marker of TB activity
abstract: Abstract Tuberculosis (TB) progression is shaped by host inflammatory remodeling, not only by pathogen burden. Here, we investigated whether peripheral complement dysregulation represents a host-response program associated with tuberculosis disease activity, disease severity, and clinical outcomes. We integrated public peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) transcriptomic data, clinical qRT-PCR validation, serum complement profiling, single-cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, and 6-month outcome assessment. A treatment-responsive C1q-centered classical complement module emerged across datasets: C1q-related genes were increased in active TB, decreased after anti-TB treatment, and were further enriched in severe disease. Clinical PBMC analyses confirmed increased C1r, C1QB, and CR2 in active TB and enrichment of C1r, C1QB, and C1QC in severe TB. At the serum level, increased C1q and soluble membrane attack complex (sMAC), together with reduced soluble complement receptor 2 (sCR2), were consistent with complement activation and altered complement receptor-related regulation; CD46 was also increased in severe disease. Complement-related measures tracked systemic inflammatory and clinical indices, while associations with 6-month outcome provided additional evidence linking this response to disease progression. Single-cell and flow cytometry analyses localized complement-associat…

title: Response to Dr Lee: Caught in the Middle: Navigating Uncertainty in the Future of Pediatric Hospital Medicine
Improving healthcare safety through patient safety incident response
abstract: World Patient Safety Day 2026, observed on 17 September, highlighted the importance of safe care for people living with noncommunicable diseases. This article explores the community nurse's role in promoting patient safety, examining how the NHS Patient Safety Incident Response Framework supports compassionate engagement, systems-based learning and continuous improvement.

title: R0 resection after a marked response to pertuzumab, trastuzumab and vorhyaluronidase alfa in HER2-positive locally advanced anorectal adenocarcinoma: a case report
Knowledge, attitudes, practices and demand for processed fruits and vegetables among low-income consumers and retailers in Kenya
abstract: Postharvest loss of perishable fruits and vegetables is a significant challenge which can be mitigated by processing them into shelf stable products. This study investigated the knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) on consumption as well as drivers for consumer demand of selected raw and processed fruits and vegetables among low-income consumers and retailers in Kenya. Mango, tomato and indigenous green leafy vegetables and their corresponding processed products, mango juice, tomato paste and cereal flour with dried milled indigenous green leafy vegetables, were the focus of this study. A cross-sectional survey was undertaken in urban, peri-urban and rural areas of Central, Coast, Eastern and Nairobi regions. Purposive sampling was used to select sixteen sites predominantly inhabited by low-income consumers. Simple random walk technique was used to sample 1,281 households and 176 retailers. Semi-structured questionnaires were employed to collect qualitative and quantitative data. The results obtained indicated a stronger consumer preference for fresh over processed fruits and vegetables. Nevertheless, respondents acknowledged benefits of processing including shelf life extension and nutrient conservation. Respondents had a high acceptability for processed products with attributes such as ‘natural taste’, ‘high nutritional value’ and ‘safe’. Almost all sampled households ded…

title: Morphophysiological response of ornamental cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. acephala) to the combined application of biochar and mycorrhizal fungi in a green wall system
abstract: Abstract Background Considering the challenges associated with growth medium limitations, moisture fluctuations, and environmental stresses in green wall systems, identifying biological strategies to maintain the growth and visual quality of ornamental plants is essential. Objective This study aimed to investigate the interactive effects of biochar and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) on the morphological and physiological traits of ornamental kale ( Brassica oleracea var. acephala ) in a green wall system. Methods A factorial experiment was conducted in a randomized complete block design with three replications under open-field conditions. Treatments included four levels of biochar (0, 2, 3, and 5% w/w of the substrate) and four levels of mycorrhizal fungi (control without inoculation, Glomus intraradices , G. mosseae , and a mixture of both strains). Results Both main factors and their interaction had a significant effect on plant growth and physiology. The 5% biochar treatment combined with dual inoculation of both mycorrhizal strains resulted in the highest vegetative growth, with a 62% increase in leaf number and a 112% increase in shoot dry weight compared to the control. From a physiological perspective, moderate to high levels of biochar combined with AMF improved plant water status and cellular health. Specifically, 2% biochar with G. mosseae showed the highest relat…

title: Musa acuminata LRR-RLK genes are involved in the response of banana to Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense tropical race 4
Retraction Note: Effect of Diabetic Neuropathy on Reparative Ability and Immune Response System
Nuclear cGAS governs transcription to control lipid metabolism, tumor growth, and therapy response
abstract: Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) is a cytosolic DNA sensor critical for host defense against microbial infections. To prevent aberrant activation, nuclear cGAS is restrained by nucleosome tethering or by barrier-to-autointegration factor–mediated restriction of its access to DNA. However, its physiological roles beyond enzymatic suppression in the nucleus remain poorly understood. Here, we present a genome-wide map of cGAS chromatin localization in human cells and unexpectedly find its binding beyond nucleosome tethering, where cGAS is recruited to chromatin by AP-1 transcription factors via a potentially previously uncharacterized transactivation domain. Integrated CUT & RUN , RNA-seq, and metabolomics analyses reveal that cGAS transcriptionally regulates cholesterol homeostasis. Mechanistically, cGAS promotes LGALS3 transcription, which inhibits ACAA2 activity to suppress fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-CoA production, thereby lowering intracellular cholesterol levels. Reduced cholesterol lowers plasma membrane phosphatidylinositol [3,4,5] triphosphate [PI(3,4,5)P 3 ] levels and decreases mTOR complex 2 (mTORC2) activation. In contrast, cGAS depletion results in cholesterol accumulation and elevated PI(3,4,5)P 3 , driving mTORC2/Akt signaling, promoting xenografted tumor growth, and conferring resistance to DNA-damaging agents. In vivo, the elevated hepatic cholesterol levels o…

title: Diagnostic Analysis of Incorrect Response Patterns in Economics among Senior Secondary School Students in Enugu North Local Government Area of Enugu Education Zone, Enugu State, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined incorrect response patterns in Economics among Senior Secondary School students in Enugu North Local Government Area of Enugu Education Zone, Enugu State, Nigeria. The study was guided by three research questions. A descriptive diagnostic research design was adopted. A simple random sampling procedure was used to select 342 Senior Secondary School Economics students from a population of 2,341 students. The instrument was the 30-item Economics Misconception Diagnostic Test (EMDT), developed by the researcher. Three experts, comprising one expert in Economics Education and two experts in Measurement and Evaluation, validated the instrument based on relevance, clarity, appropriateness, adequacy of content coverage, and alignment with the objectives of the study. Internal consistency reliability was determined using the psych package in R statistical software, yielding a reliability coefficient of 0.75. Data were analysed using frequencies and percentages. The findings showed considerable variation in incorrect responses across the 30 EMDT items, with percentages ranging from 23.10% to 88.89%. Item 20 recorded the highest proportion of incorrect responses (88.89%), followed by Items 11 (82.75%), 22 (81.29%), and 29 (80.12%). Twenty-one of the 30 items recorded incorrect responses from at least 50% of the students. Furthermore, six items were classified as very h…

title: A SYSTEM OF KPI INDICATORS FOR EVALUATING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF REGIONAL PR ACTIVITY: OPPORTUNITIES FOR APPLYING ER, SOV AND ROI
abstract: The article examines how the effectiveness of regional public relations (PR) activity can be evaluated through a system of key performance indicators (KPIs). It discusses three indicators that are widely used in communication evaluation but rarely combined in regional practice: Engagement Rate (ER), Share of Voice (SOV) and Return on Investment (ROI). For each indicator, the definition, calculation logic, data sources, limitations and potential uses in regional management are outlined, and an integrated framework linking them to the stages of communication results is proposed. It is argued that ER and SOV are suitable for ongoing monitoring of outputs and outtakes, whereas ROI in PR is usually conditional or indirect and should be interpreted together with qualitative evidence. The framework may help regional authorities responsible for tourism and investment promotion to set measurable goals and report results more transparently.
venue: Central Asian Journal of Academic Research

title: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) vs. morphology-based blastocyst selection for transfer: cost-effectiveness analysis within Israel’s publicly funded IVF system
abstract: Abstract Background Israel operates one of the most extensive publicly funded in vitro fertilization (IVF) programs worldwide. Alongside IVF, adjunct technologies aimed at improving reproductive outcomes, such as preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), have been increasingly adopted. PGT-A is designed to identify chromosomally normal embryos before transfer. Despite its growing use, PGT-A is not included in Israel’s National Health Basket. Given the local high utilization of IVF and the substantial public expenditure, evaluating the economic value of PGT-A is essential for evidence-based health policy decision-making. Most available analyses of PGT-A originate from private or mixed healthcare systems, where treatment costs and reimbursement structures differ from Israel’s fully publicly funded IVF model. This study aimed to determine whether PGT-A is cost-effective when provided as part of Israel’s IVF program. Methods A theoretical model-based cost-effectiveness analysis using a Markov decision framework compared PGT-A with morphology-based embryo selection from the perspective of the Israeli public healthcare payer. The model simulated repeated embryo transfers for various age groups and blastocyst availability scenarios. Relevant cost estimates of the two strategies were based on Israeli Ministry of Health data (2025). The probabilities of main clinical outco…
venue: Israel Journal of Health Policy Research

title: Sales growth conditions the relationship between cost management and business liquidity
abstract: Background Cost management and business liquidity are determinants of the stability of industrial firms, but little is known about how it depends on the commercial context. It was determined whether cost management influences the liquidity of an industrial firm in Pomalca, Peru (2011–2025), under the moderating effect of inventory turnover and sales growth. Methods An applied, quantitative, non-experimental, longitudinal and correlational-explanatory study with the financial statements of the firm (2011–2025, census sampling, n = 15), analyzed by means of a documentary file and linear regression with robust HAC/Newey-West errors in R 4.6.1. Results Cost management did not show a direct effect on current liquidity (β = 0.072; p = 0.146), but its interaction with sales growth was significant (β = 0.001; p = 0.009). Current liquidity, acid test, and net working capital significantly influenced cost management (p = 0.043; 0.040; 0.003), moderated by sales growth (adjusted R 2 64.0%–68.9%). Conclusions Cost management does not directly influence liquidity; its effect only appears with sales growth, while liquidity does directly influence cost management, which functions as a limiting condition of this relationship.
authors: DAMARIS MARLENY SANCHEZ DIAZ DE GUEVARA

title: Managing commitments for reliable planning: evidence from action research
abstract: Purpose Low planning reliability in construction projects has been linked to weaknesses in commitment management within the Last Planner System (LPS). While the Linguistic Action Perspective (LAP) provides a strong theoretical explanation of commitments as conversations for action, empirical evidence of operational systems that translate these principles into practice remains limited. This paper evaluates a Commitment Management System (CMS) designed to improve commitment reliability and planning performance in construction projects. Design/methodology/approach An action research approach was adopted through a longitudinal, multi-project intervention in four construction projects, two in Chile and two in Colombia, with different levels of LPS maturity. The CMS was implemented through structured interventions embedded in weekly planning meetings. Quantitative and qualitative data were collected to assess commitment-related indicators, LPS maturity, Percent Plan Complete (PPC), PPC variability, engagement behaviours, and schedule deviation. Findings The results indicate that CMS implementation increased LPS maturity levels across all projects and improved commitment performance. Projects exhibiting higher CMS assimilation and engagement showed lower PPC variability and more stable planning outcomes. Schedule deviation was reduced in all cases, with an average improvement of 5.39%…

title: Agent-based simulation of shared autonomous electric vehicle fleets: application to Montreal Olympic Park
abstract: Abstract Many cities now offer shared vehicle fleets as an alternative mode of daily transportation. These fleets can be further enhanced through the use of autonomous or electric autonomous vehicles, which reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, lower staffing requirements, enable automated charging, and provide smoother operation. This paper proposes an agent-based simulation framework to model a fleet of shared electric autonomous vehicles (SEAVs) providing one-way, short-distance trips. A case study is conducted for Montreal’s Olympic Park, encompassing five strategically located stations. By varying key fleet parameters, 105 scenarios are generated and analyzed. Results indicate that a fleet of 20 vehicles with a 50 km range and 30 parking spots can meet demand across all tested customer arrival frequencies, achieving service performance rates of 90% or higher. Vehicle range is shown to have minimal impact on performance compared to fleet size and demand probability. Additionally, reducing the number of parking spots decreases the number of rejected customers but increases the number of empty trips.

title: A data-driven predictive system for shellfish biotoxin risk assessment
abstract: Diarrhetic shellfish poisoning (DSP) toxins pose a major threat to the aquaculture industry and public health. Traditional monitoring methods suffer from delays and high costs, and intelligent early warning systems are urgently needed. The study utilised machine learning to predict shellfish biotoxin levels in shellfish by integrating multiple data sources, including phytoplankton monitoring, climatic variables, and historical toxin records. Data from seven shellfish production areas in Northern Ireland from 2011 to 2021, covering DSP-OA + dinophysistoxins and AZAs toxin concentrations, seven phytoplankton taxa or taxonomic groups, and three climatic variables was used to inform the model. Using the Lale Machine learning framework, the study constructed 42 initial modelling scenarios across regions, shellfish species, and toxin combinations. SHAP analyses quantified feature contributions and identified the main predictors across the retained scenarios. After data filtering and performance screening, model performance varied across the region-species combinations. The final regression models showed limited predictive performance, while the classification models showed stronger performance for the two evaluated region-species combinations, Belfast mussels and Dundrum mussels, with F1 scores of 0.766 and 0.950. The results of the study show predictive potential for toxin occurrenc…
venue: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology

title: White coats in the news feed: the effects of content features on physicians' engagement behaviors in online academic medical communities
abstract: Purpose Online academic medical communities (OAMCs) have become central channels for physicians to exchange medical knowledge. Yet a substantial share of physician-generated medical content on these platforms fails to elicit meaningful peer engagement, constraining the dissemination of medical knowledge. Given that the intrinsic features of content in OAMCs are likely key drivers of peer engagement, understanding what makes content appealing is essential. However, the relationship remains unclear. This study aims to address this gap by examining how distinct content features influence different forms of peer engagement in OAMCs. Design/methodology/approach Leveraging data from a leading Chinese OAMC, we operationalize six content features (complexity, subjectivity, professionalism, completeness, informativeness, multimodal information presentation) via natural language processing and examine their effects on physicians' collecting and interacting behaviors and the moderating role of disease severity. Findings Peer physicians prioritize information-rich content for collecting, while favoring discussion-oriented content for interacting. Multimodal, comprehensive content is welcomed, whereas overly sophisticated, highly specialized content is less effective. Disease severity moderates these relationships, with physicians exhibiting greater selectivity in collecting but more intera…

title: When traditional culture meets digital games: pathways and boundary conditions linking cultural identity to purchase intention
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how cultural identity is associated with purchase intention for paid digital games featuring local cultural elements. In the context of Black Myth: Wukong, it further investigates whether perceived value and immersive experience explain this relationship and whether price sensitivity conditions these associations. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 1,167 mainland Chinese and international gamers were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) and cross-sample model comparisons were used to examine group differences. Findings Cultural identity was positively associated with purchase intention, with significant indirect effects through perceived value and immersive experience. In the full sample, price sensitivity weakened the links between cultural identity and both mediators and their indirect effects. Mainland Chinese gamers showed higher cultural identity and perceived value, and stronger direct and indirect effects of cultural identity, than international gamers. The moderating effect of price sensitivity was not significant in the international subsample. Practical implications Managers can strengthen culturally grounded digital products by embedding culturally resonant narratives, symbols and aesthetics into product design, communicating their relevance to target consumers and ado…

title: Therapeutic Benefit of Panchashirisha Agad Ghan Vati with Phalatrikadi Kwath Ghan Vati in Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (Garavisha Janya Yakrut Vikara): A Randomized Comparative Clinical Study

title: Artificial Intelligence and Religious Policy: Ethical Governance in the Digital Public Sphere
abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates religious communication, knowledge, and participation in the digital public sphere, yet research remains fragmented across digital religion, human rights, and AI governance. This study examines how AI-mediated religious communication shapes authority, visibility, and participation; identifies associated ethical and rights-based concerns; and analyzes the institutional conditions relevant to its governance. Using a qualitative, non-experimental, exploratory-analytical design, the study draws on academic publications, policy documents, regulatory instruments, institutional guidelines, human-rights reports, and documented analyses of digital religious practices. Materials were purposively selected for substantive relevance and examined through structured reading and extraction, open and focused coding, thematic synthesis, source triangulation, and iterative cross-source comparison. The analysis identified three interconnected domains: access, visibility, and religious authority; religious freedom, inclusion, and algorithmic risks; and accountability, contestability, and institutional responsibility. AI-mediated technologies can broaden access to religious resources while simultaneously shaping the visibility and perceived authority of religious actors and interpretations. Expanded access can coexist with unequal representation, privacy…

title: Tendinopathy: Current Concepts in Pathophysiology, Clinical Presentation, and Management – An Updated Review
abstract: Tendinopathy is a common musculoskeletal disorder characterized by tendon pain, impaired function, and reduced loadbearing capacity. It affects both athletic and non-athletic populations and represents a significant cause of disability and healthcare burden worldwide. Traditionally regarded as an inflammatory condition, current evidence suggests that tendinopathy is a multifactorial disorder involving mechanical overload, extracellular matrix degradation, collagen disorganization, cellular dysfunction, oxidative stress, neurovascular ingrowth, and a failed healing response. Commonly affected tendons include the Achilles tendon, patellar tendon, rotator cuff tendons, and lateral elbow extensor tendons. Several intrinsic and extrinsic risk factors, including aging, obesity, diabetes mellitus, repetitive occupational activities, and sports-related overuse, contribute to disease development and progression. Advances in imaging modalities such as ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging have improved the diagnosis and monitoring of tendon pathology. Management strategies include exercise-based rehabilitation, physiotherapy, extracorporeal shockwave therapy, pharmacological interventions, platelet-rich plasma therapy, regenerative medicine approaches, and surgical treatment in refractory cases. Emerging therapies such as stem cell therapy, growth factor delivery, gene therapy, …
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Carbon Footprint Estimation of a Higher Education Institution as a Baseline for Sustainable Technological Management: The FIMAZ-UAS Case
abstract: The carbon footprint has positioned itself as a fundamental tool for the evaluation and management of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in higher education institutions, due to their patterns of energy consumption, resource use, and mobility, which present dynamics comparable to those of small urban areas. In this context, the objective of the present study was to estimate and analyze the institutional carbon footprint of the Faculty of Computer Science Mazatlán (FIMAZ) of the Autonomous University of Sinaloa (UAS), considering the consumption of electricity, drinking water, solid waste generation, and the mobility of students and faculty during the period from January to December 2024. The research was conducted using a quantitative approach, with a non-experimental, descriptive, and longitudinal design, employing a case study based on the guidelines of the GHG Protocol and the ISO 14064-1:2018 standard. The quantification of emissions was carried out using activity data obtained from institutional records and mobility surveys, which were combined with reference emission factors at the national and international levels, allowing for a systematic estimation of the emissions generated by each analyzed source. The results show that electricity consumption is the main source of emissions, with an annual footprint of 220,887.24 kg of CO₂, associated with the intensive use of computing…

title: Marinas act as persistent introduction hubs driving the decadal accumulation of non-indigenous fouling species in an oceanic island system
The influence pathway of internal audit attributes on credit risk management in emerging economies: evidence from Tanzania
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how internal audit function (IAF) attributes, namely competence, independence, and leadership, influence credit risk management (CRM) in Tanzanian commercial banks, focussing on the mediating role of the IAF's sphere of influence. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 131 relevant employees across all 34 licenced commercial banks in Tanzania. A cross-sectional survey design was applied, and partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used to test direct and mediated relationships. Findings Results show that IAF competence and independence significantly enhance CRM both directly and indirectly through the sphere of influence, while the relationship between leadership and CRM is fully mediated by the sphere of influence. Moreover, the sphere of influence exerts a significant positive effect on CRM, underscoring the importance of organisational influence in translating audit insights into effective risk governance. Practical implications The findings suggest that banks in emerging economies should reinforce auditor independence and competence while fostering organisational cultures that empower internal audit functions. Regulators are also encouraged to refine their supervisory frameworks to emphasise the institutional role of internal audits in risk oversight. Originality/value This study extends internal auditi…
venue: Journal of Accounting in Emerging Economies

title: Fiscal Forecasting to Support Public Sector Human Resource Planning in European Countries
abstract: Fiscal constraints can affect the affordability of public-sector workforce plans, but aggregate fiscal data do not identify staffing requirements. In this exploratory study, we examine whether historical revenue and expenditure shares jointly explain cross-country variation in their 2018 values and discuss a possible connection to personnel budgeting. We estimate two ordinary least-squares regressions using 28 countries belonging to the European Union in 2018 as observations, with nine annual fiscal shares from 2009–2017 as predictors. The data are percentages of GDP from a fixed Eurostat publication vintage, extracted by Eurostat on 12 May 2019. The revenue and expenditure specifications are jointly significant, with R² = 0.995248 and 0.976869, respectively. These results describe in-sample fit; we did not evaluate forecasting accuracy on independent data. Severe multicollinearity, the small sample, and influential expenditure observations constrain interpretation. In our proposed HRM framework, we link fiscal scenarios to approved personnel allocations and then to costed workforce options. We explain this connection through an illustrative example, but we do not empirically test the framework because the dataset contains no payroll, employment, vacancy, or service-demand indicators. Practical use therefore requires independent forecast validation and institution-specific fina…

title: Institutionalizing Religious Moderation as Public Policy: Strategies for Addressing Social Polarization
abstract: Religious moderation has increasingly entered public-policy agendas in Indonesia, yet existing scholarship often examines its educational, community, institutional, and communicative dimensions separately, leaving their integration as an institutional policy process insufficiently explained. This study examines how religious moderation is institutionalized as public policy for addressing social polarization, the strategies and implementation conditions involved, and the monitoring and evaluation arrangements relevant to implementation and social outcomes. A qualitative documentary analysis was conducted using official Indonesian policy and strategic documents on religious moderation issued or enacted between 2020 and 2025, complemented by scholarly literature on documented implementation experiences and relevant social processes. The materials were examined through thematic analysis involving familiarization, analytical coding, cross-source comparison, and interpretive synthesis. The findings show that religious moderation has acquired a formal institutional architecture through policy direction, organizational mandates, implementation arrangements, coordination, and monitoring. Substantive implementation, however, depends on institutional capacity, multi-level coordination, meaningful participation, local adaptation, educational practice, rights safeguards, and public communic…

title: Development and structure of a multiscenario prehospital triage classification system: a Colombian framework proposal
abstract: Abstract Purpose Colombia has established legal frameworks for prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) but has no nationally standardized prehospital triage system. Given a high trauma burden and marked geographic heterogeneity, we aimed to develop a structured, nationally adapted prehospital triage classification framework and describe its design. This article reports a consensus-based development and design study; it describes the framework’s structure and does not constitute a clinical validation. Methods The framework was developed through a three-phase process: (1) review of Colombian regulatory instruments and international triage literature; (2) structured expert consensus using the Nominal Group Technique with a ≥ 90% agreement threshold across ten virtual consensus sessions, conducted with the technical committee of the Colombian Association of Trauma, Prehospital Care, and Emergency Medical Systems (ACTAEM) and the Meditech Foundation research group; and (3) geographic and operational adaptation to Colombia’s response infrastructure. No patient-level data were collected. Results The framework defines three operational modalities (information-and-communication-technology [ICT]-mediated dispatch triage; on-scene one-to-one triage; and multiple-casualty-incident triage), a four-level colour-coded priority classification comprising 91 syndromic conditions with object…
venue: Journal of Emergency and Disaster Medicine

title: Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Penile Injection After Failed Oral Medical Management of Erectile Dysfunction
abstract: Objective: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection is an evolving regenerative therapy in the management of erectile dysfunction (ED). This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of autologous intracavernosal PRP injections in patients with ED who failed oral medical management. Methods: The single-arm prospective interventional study included men with all grades of ED who received two PRP injections (prepared using the TriCell TriPReP TUBEX system) one month apart. The primary endpoint was the percentage of men who achieved the minimum clinically important difference (MCID). Secondary endpoints included change in International Index of Erectile Function-Erectile Function (IIEF-EF) domain scores from baseline to 1- and 3-month post-treatment, adverse events, and overall treatment satisfaction. Results: Thirty out of 32 enrolled patients completed the study protocol (mean age 36.53 years). Mean IIEF-EF scores significantly improved (p < 0.001) from baseline (13.01) to 1 month (15.9) and 3 months (18.03) post-treatment. MCID was achieved by 30% of patients at 1 month and 53.3% at 3 months, across all grades of ED. More importantly, patients with mild and mild-to-moderate ED showed superior response rates in achieving MCID (90% at 1 month, 100% at 3 months) compared to moderate and severe ED patients (0% at 1 month, 30% at 3 months). No adverse events were reported, and pati…
venue: NATIONAL BOARD OF EXAMINATIONS JOURNAL OF MEDICAL SCIENCES

title: Comparative Study of Lateral Internal Sphincterotomy and Medical Management in Chronic Anal Fissure
abstract: Background: Chronic anal fissure is a common condition that affects the anorectal region and causes considerable pain and reduced quality of life for the patient. LIS surgery and medical therapy are standard treatments. The present study sought to assess the outcomes of LIS surgery and medical therapy among patients with chronic anal fissure. Methods: A Comparative observation study was carried out at the Department of General Surgery of a tertiary care hospital from March to August 2026. The total number of 260 patients having chronic anal fissure was selected and equally distributed in two groups (LIS = 130, Medical management = 130). The outcome measures include fissure healing, pain score, time required for fissure healing, recurrence, hospitalization period, resuming regular activities, need for further treatment, and patient satisfaction. Results: There was a high proportion of healing after 1 month with LIS compared to medical treatment (90.8% compared to 65.4%; p<0.001), and after 3 months 95.4% vs 77.7% (p<0.001). The mean healing time was shorter with LIS. There was a significant difference in pain scores at 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months with LIS (p<0.001). There was a low proportion of recurrence after 6 months with LIS (3.1%) compared to medical treatment (10.8%), (p=0.028). Conclusion: LIS was found to have better healing rate, more pain reduction, less recurrence …

title: Efektivitas Penggunaan E-Layanan Bebas Temuan pada Inspektorat Daerah Provinsi Sulawesi Barat: Analisis Berdasarkan Dimensi Campbell
abstract: Digitalizing personnel administration services is part of bureaucratic reform, yet studies on digital services developed independently by regional inspectorates remain scarce. This study measures the effectiveness of the E-Layanan Bebas Temuan, an online service for issuing the Surat Keterangan Bebas Temuan (SKBT, a certificate of no outstanding audit findings) to civil servants at the Regional Inspectorate of West Sulawesi Province, using Campbell’s five measures of effectiveness. A descriptive quantitative approach was applied to 100 civil servants selected by simple random sampling, with the sample size determined by the Slovin formula. Data were collected through a 27-item Likert-scale questionnaire that proved valid and reliable (Cronbach’s Alpha = 0.851), complemented by interviews with three informants, observation, and documentation. Overall effectiveness reached 89.58% (Very Effective), with dimension scores between 88.65% and 90.07%. Input efficiency scored highest (92.00%), whereas accessibility scored lowest (87.00%). Interviews indicated that processing time fell from 3-7 working days to 1-3 working days. Improvements are still needed in user assistance, administrator capacity during peak periods, automatic status notifications, and database integration. The findings imply that the success of internal digital services in local governments depends on user readiness …

title: Evaluation of transfer learning in hydrological forecasting using ensemble LSTM models: a statistical approach to uncertainty and accuracy
abstract: Global change poses significant challenges to water resource management. Water Table Depth (WTD) is a critical variable linking subsurface dynamics to land-surface processes; however, real-world observations remain sparse. Transfer learning can support WTD monitoring, but assessing prediction quality in locations without observations is challenging. This contribution explores a method using an assessment tool to estimate prediction quality in such locations. We implement an ensemble of 100 Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to predict WTD using the physically-based Terrestrial Systems Modeling Platform Groundwater to Atmosphere (TSMP-G2A) simulation dataset, spatially split into training and transfer subsets. The training subset is temporally split into training and testing time periods, while the transfer subset evaluates transferability to unseen locations within the TSMP-G2A dataset during the testing period. Each ensemble LSTM member was trained on a spatial sample of the training subset, randomly sampled based on geographic location. By leveraging the ensemble spread, we develop spread-skill relationships to assess prediction quality in the transfer subset. Results indicate good generalization and transfer abilities on the TSMP-G2A dataset within the study domain. Additionally, expanding each ensemble member's training subset from 100 to 400 grid cells improves global …

Phase-aware photovoltaic forecasting with multi-basis quantum covariance graphs
abstract: Abstract Short-horizon photovoltaic forecasting without future weather information requires effective use of periodic, phase-sensitive, and rapidly changing patterns in recent power histories. This study proposes PhaseQCov-GNet, a hybrid quantum–classical model that converts four phase-sensitive spectral tokens into a sample-dependent signed graph using a four-qubit, two-block data-re-uploading circuit. Connected Pauli correlations measured in the Z / Z Z and X / X X bases define the graph, which is processed by a signed relational mixer and a seasonal-residual decoder. The model uses 48 h of historical power and deterministic calendar variables to jointly predict 1-, 3-, and 6 h-ahead power on the three-zone GEFCom2014 Solar dataset under a leakage-controlled cross-zone protocol. Across the three held-out-zone folds, PhaseQCov-GNet achieved mean RMSE values of 0.092 28, 0.119 41, and 0.131 10 at 1, 3, and 6 h, respectively. It obtained the lowest mean RMSE among the evaluated models at 1 and 6 h, while TinyPatchTST was lower at 3 h. Relative to ClassicalCovGraph, RMSE decreased by 7.59%, 6.73%, and 0.69%; relative to the exactly parameter-matched ClassicalFeatureMapGraph, the reductions were 11.29%, 3.41%, and 1.31%. Graph replacement and whole-set derangement confirmed functional dependence on the generated relations, while ablations showed sensitivity to the controlled- Z la…

title: The Genome Lab: designing a simpler interface for genome assembly and annotation
abstract: Background Galaxy is a web-based platform for analysing data, particularly biological data such as DNA. While genome assembly and annotation is a typical starting point for users, navigating this process can be challenging: many factors affect which tools and settings are appropriate, and researchers with genomes to analyse often have deep taxonomic expertise but less bioinformatics experience. Methods To better present relevant resources, we built the Genome Lab: a domain-specific interface for genome assembly and annotation. Informed by user experience considerations, the design targets discoverability and navigation, and is intended to reduce the effort required to find resources and to understand the genome assembly process. Applying six key design decisions, we gave the Lab a clear, simple layout showing an organised set of tools and workflows, so that new users can get started quickly and experienced users have their frequently required resources at hand. Results We present a worked example of genome assembly and annotation, carried out the way a researcher might use the Genome Lab. Working from Nanopore sequencing reads, the curated path produced a genome assembly, a completeness assessment and gene models, viewed in a genome browser. Conclusions The Genome Lab has been implemented as a generic framework that other communities have since used to build Labs for their own …

title: Comparative Analysis of Statistical, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Models for USD/IDR Prediction Using Macroeconomic Indicators and Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The USD/IDR exchange rate is a key daily barometer of Indonesia's economic health. Accurate forecasting is vital for trade, inflation, and monetary stability. However, its volatile and nonlinear dynamics pose challenges. While research has applied statistical models, machine learning, and deep learning, few studies offer a comprehensive comparison integrating predictive accuracy with model interpretability, particularly using banking stock prices as exogenous predictors. This study addresses this gap by developing and evaluating eight forecasting approaches—a naive random-walk baseline, two statistical models (ARIMA, SARIMAX), three tree-based ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM), and two recurrent neural networks (LSTM, GRU) using daily data from January 2015 to July 2026 (3,005 observations). Five major banking stocks (BBCA, BBRI, BMRI, BBNI, BDMN) are included as one-day-lagged exogenous features. Models are assessed via hold-out testing and five-fold walk-forward cross-validation using RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R². Contrary to expectations, the naive random-walk consistently achieves the lowest error (RMSE=115.24, MAE=63.80, MAPE=0.39%) and the most stable performance, with LSTM as the best-performing complex model (RMSE=269.59, R²=0.785). Diebold-Mariano tests confirm statistical significance (p<0.001). To enhance transparency, SHAP-based Explainable AI is applied to Ra…

Application of long short-term memory and convolutional neural networks for real-time bridge pier scour prediction
abstract: Purpose Scour around bridge piers poses a major threat to structural safety, yet existing empirical and machine learning approaches are limited in accuracy, generalisation and real-time applicability. This paper aims to evaluate the effectiveness, efficiency and generalisability of deep learning models for real-time bridge pier scour forecasting. Design/methodology/approach The study formulates scour forecasting as a multivariate time-series prediction problem using real-world sensor data from monitored bridges in Alaska and Oregon (2006–2021). Multiple variants of long short-term memory (LSTM) and temporal convolutional neural network (CNN) models are designed and systematically evaluated. Random-search heuristics and sequential evaluation are used to optimise hyperparameters, improve robustness and assess computational efficiency. Findings Results show that LSTM models achieve high predictive accuracy for larger data sets, with a mean absolute error as low as 0.024 m for one-week-ahead forecasts. Fully convolutional networks deliver comparable accuracy with substantially lower training and inference times. Feature analyses indicate that historical scour time series dominate predictive performance, with flow-related features contributing only marginal or site-specific improvements. Research limitations/implications Model performance depends on data availability, noise levels a…

A deep learning-based method for enhanced prediction of long-term diaphragm wall deflections using multi-source data
abstract: Abstract Machine learning-based autoregressive models are widely applied to deformation prediction of braced excavations, yet they often suffer from pronounced error accumulation and deteriorated accuracy in long-term forecasting. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multi-source information fusion framework for predicting diaphragm wall deformation that integrates construction information with historical wall-deflection data. By incorporating construction-related dynamic features as auxiliary inputs, the proposed model effectively strengthens long-term dependency learning and reduces the propagation of autoregressive errors. A depth-weighted loss coefficient is further introduced to prioritize accuracy in shallow regions where deformation is most critical, and a 1D U-Net decoder is employed to enhance profile-level reconstruction through multi-scale spatial feature extraction. The framework is validated using two deep excavation projects on Nanjing Metro Line 11. For excavation-induced deformation, the model demonstrates stable and accurate multi-step prediction performance for diaphragm wall deflection, even under long forecasting steps. Comparative analyses further confirm that the proposed fusion architecture provides superior long-term robustness under limited monitoring data. The results highlight the method’s potential as a practical tool for deformation f…

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Next-Hour Prediction Using Three Meteorological Variables and Historical PM2.5 Data
abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) remains one of the most consequential urban air-quality hazards, yet forecasting its next-hour concentration accurately and transparently remains challenging owing to the non-linear, multivariate nature of pollutant-meteorology interactions and the black-box character of high-performing ensemble models. This study proposes an explainable machine learning framework for next-hour PM2.5 concentration prediction that integrates Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with a parsimonious set of predictors comprising three meteorological variables (air temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed) together with historical PM2.5 concentrations. Using 43,824 hourly observations from the Beijing PM2.5 dataset (2010–2014), lag, rolling-statistic, and cyclical calendar features were engineered, and model hyperparameters were systematically tuned through Bayesian optimization using the Optuna framework with the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator over 30 trials under a strictly chronological training validation testing split. Model interpretability was achieved through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. The tuned XGBoost model achieved a root mean squared error of 16.50 µg/m³, a mean absolute error of 9.89 µg/m³, a mean absolute percentage error of 21.75%, and a coefficient of determination of 0.9478 on the test set, corresponding to reduction…

Development and internal validation of prediction models for maternal adverse pregnancy outcomes in HELLP syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China
abstract: Introduction HELLP syndrome is uncommon but can cause serious maternal adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). We investigated whether routinely available clinical and laboratory variables could support outcome-specific risk prediction. Methods We included all women with HELLP syndrome treated at Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital from January 2013 to June 2023. Five outcomes were modeled: placental abruption (PAB), posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and a severe maternal composite outcome. The primary analysis used repeated nested cross-validation in the full cohort. Missing-data filtering and imputation, predictor screening, model-family selection, hyperparameter tuning, and threshold estimation were performed within each outer training fold so that the held-out fold evaluated the entire modeling process. Candidate families were ridge logistic regression, elastic-net logistic regression, and random forest. A paired sensitivity analysis using multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) was conducted to assess the effect of replacing mean/mode imputation. Results Among 272 women, PAB occurred in 33 (12.13%), PRES in 23 (8.46%), PPH in 19 (6.99%), DIC in 9 (3.31%), and the severe composite outcome in 25 (9.19%). The corresponding AUCs were 0.715, 0.677, 0.833, 0.907, and 0.742. Ri…

title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics and clinical features for preoperative prediction of high-grade meningioma: a two-centre retrospective study
abstract: Background Preoperative identification of high-grade meningioma remains challenging using clinical and conventional imaging features. We compared MRI radiomic and clinical models and assessed whether their integration improved external discrimination. Materials and methods This retrospective two-centre study included 284 patients, with 227 used for training and 57 for independent external testing. Radiomics from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI), T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) underwent training-cohort screening, correlation filtering, and LASSO selection. The primary comparison assessed external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for joint-clinical versus clinical logistic regression (LR) models. Secondary comparisons assessed adding clinical predictors to joint imaging and combining sequences relative to T2WI. Bootstrap-based normal-approximation comparisons with paired resampling and Holm correction evaluated these three contrasts. Calibration, decision curves, and K-nearest neighbour (KNN) models were exploratory. Results The external cohort contained 48 low-grade and 9 high-grade tumours. All four imaging-only LR models had higher external bootstrap-mean AUC point estimates than the clinical model (0.663; 95% CI, 0.467–0.840). title: School leader coaching: building principal capacity in small, rural districts
abstract: Purpose Leadership coaching can help build the capacity of school leaders and support school improvement efforts. The purpose of this research is to describe how leadership coaching methodologies, grounded in traditional community building practices, change based on context and location. Design/methodology/approach A conceptual autoethnographic approach reflects on and explores how Community Learning Exchange (CLE) axioms were used as a framework to coach school principals in small, rural districts. The CLE framework shaped the interpretation of this experience by emphasizing the social, dynamic, and asset-based nature of learning and leadership. Findings Coaching school leaders in small, rural districts required an approach that incorporated building relational trust, collaborative problem-solving, contextualized coaching, embedding self in the community, and the identification of school and community assets. Originality/value Community Learning Exchange axioms have traditionally been used in settings to bring together communities and in classrooms to establish community among students. These same principles were reimagined and utilized successfully in two small, rural districts to build a foundation for improving schools.
venue: International Journal of Mentoring and Coaching in Education

title: Equivariance of the Source Measure Off the Pure Limit: Contact Sensitivity, Channel Capacity, and the Invariance of Selection Cost
abstract: This paper quantifies how partial sidechain cleavage affects the orientation sensitivity and alignment selection cost of stacking contacts in a self-separating substituted-chrysene stock. In the one-reagent limit where every sidechain is a hydroxyethoxy arm, the registration filter of the self-separating source reads the alignment of a stacking contact solely through the initiator, pricing the exogenous supply of alignment at one bit per contact. Extending this analysis to mixed arm words generated by partial cleavage establishes the exact magnitude of orientation sensitivity across operating regimes and demonstrates that the unconditional alignment price of one bit per contact remains invariant. The orientation sensitivity exhibits a sharp quadratic onset. Writing σ(π_h) for the probability that a contact drawn from the admitted stream is orientation-sensitive when each arm is cleaved to the phenol h independently with probability π_h, exact arithmetic shows that σ is a degree-8 polynomial with rational coefficients. At the uncleaved limit, σ(0) = f_I² = 2.47 × 10⁻⁷, arising solely from initiator pairs; the linear correction carries a coefficient of 9.40 × 10⁻⁶, while the quadratic π_h² term dominates with a coefficient of 4.00009. Across the three standard operating points of the separation process, partial cleavage increases orientation sensitivity over the pure limit by fac…

title: Aqueous Extract of Gembili (Dioscorea esculenta) Tubers Exceeds Its Ethanol Fractions in Phenolic Content and Antioxidant Capacity
abstract: Gembili (Dioscorea esculenta) tubers are used in Indonesia mainly as a source of inulin, recovered from hot-water extracts by ethanol precipitation, but how antioxidants partition during this step is unknown. A hot-water extract (AE) was compared with its ethanol-insoluble (EIF) and ethanol-soluble (ESF) fractions for total phenolic (TPC) and flavonoid (TFC) contents and for 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), 2,2′-azinobis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS), and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) activities. AE had the highest TPC (214.9 ± 6.1 mg gallic acid equivalents/g) and TFC (159.7 ± 6.5 mg quercetin equivalents/g), the lowest IC50 values (DPPH 30.0 ± 0.8; ABTS 28.5 ± 1.9 µg/mL), and the highest FRAP (269 ± 42 mg ascorbic acid equivalents/g). EIF exceeded ESF in all assays except FRAP (p < 0.001), and antioxidant capacity followed TPC across nine determinations (DPPH IC50, r = −0.94). The inulin-rich precipitate therefore retains part of the antioxidant capacity of the tuber.

title: Ion-Conductive Elastomers with Enhanced Mechanical Performance and Electrical Conductivity via a Nano-Synergistic Transport Mechanism
abstract: Abstract Flexible ion-conductive elastomers have emerged as promising materials for wearable humidity sensors owing to their excellent stretchability and efficient ion transport capability. However, simultaneously achieving high ionic conductivity and excellent mechanical performance remains a significant challenge, primarily because the incorporation of high loadings of ionic components often induces solvation effects within polymer networks and compromises their mechanical stability. To address this challenge, we developed an ion-conductive elastomer with enhanced mechanical robustness and efficient ion transport capability by constructing a hydrogen-bond-anchored micro/nanostructured conductive network. Specifically, amino-functionalized SiO2 serves not only as a nanoreinforcing phase but also as a “bridging node” for ion transport through multiple hydrogen-bond anchoring interactions with polyurethane chains, enabling the formation of a continuous micro/nanoscale ionic conductive network while preserving the structural stability of the polymer matrix. The resulting ion-conductive elastomer exhibits high ionic conductivity (1.4 × 10–2 S/m), high tensile strength (2.17 MPa), and recyclability, achieving an effective synergy between mechanical performance and ion transport properties. Based on a humidity-induced ion transport mechanism, the fabricated flexible humidity sensor …

title: How does perceptual distortion occur? Unraveling the interference mechanism of environmental color in the perception of original colors of cultural artifacts
abstract: Color design within museum interiors constitutes a critical factor in shaping visitors’ perception of the authenticity of the original colors of cultural artifacts. Drawing upon multi-source qualitative data, including in-depth interviews and professional texts, this study employs grounded theory to exploratorily construct a theoretical model of the interference mechanism through which environmental colors affect the perception of artifact original colors. The findings reveal that optical-physical, cognitive-psychological, semantic-cultural, and emotional-value jointly constitute four core dimensions underlying such interference effects. At the physical level, environmental colors generate initial chromatic signals, which subsequently produce perceptual deviations through cognitive processing, trigger semantic reconstruction, and ultimately influence value judgments via emotional experiences. These dimensions may operate independently or synergistically, with cognitive processing and semantic association functioning as the central mediating pathways. The study provides an empirically grounded cognitive-psychological explanatory framework for understanding the dynamic relationship between environmental colors and the perception of artifact original colors, thereby offering theoretical support for museums to more effectively address the challenge of chromatic distortion in artifa…

title: Mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles for intrauterine adhesions: from cargo and mechanism to product standardization and local delivery
abstract: Background Mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) are being developed as cell-free regenerative products for intrauterine adhesions (IUA), but the translational literature is limited by inconsistent terminology, heterogeneous products, and predominantly rodent evidence. Main body This review integrates the inflammation-fibrosis circuit of IUA with reported MSC-EV cargo-target pairs, including galectin-1/JAK-STAT, miR-202-3p/MMP11, miR-543/N-cadherin, UBR4/YAP, and miR-340-3p/METTL3-HMOX1. It distinguishes direct uterine evidence from mechanistic extrapolation, discusses parent-cell source and culture effects, and evaluates collagen scaffolds, decellularized matrices, and injectable hydrogels as local delivery systems. Recent pooled animal evidence supports improvements in endometrial thickness, gland number, fibrosis, and embryo-related outcomes, but pregnancy-rate evidence remains uncertain. MISEV2023-aligned characterization, mechanism-linked potency assays, standardized dose metrics, biodistribution, and reproductive toxicology are essential before efficacy can be interpreted across studies. The trial landscape has also changed: an IUA-specific study of intrauterine hUCMSC-EV administration was registered in 2026, although peer-reviewed clinical efficacy data remain unavailable. Mechanistic claims are graded by whether primary experiments provide c…

title: Low-overhead trust mechanism for efficient cross-domain authentication in internet of vehicles based on blockchain sharding
abstract: Introduction To solve the problems of inadequate scalability, sluggish synchronization of authentication information, and high authentication overhead, an efficient authentication strategy based on a double-layer shard blockchain was presented for the cross-trust domain of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). A double-layer shard blockchain architecture was developed for multiple cross-trust domain message authentication by constructing blockchains on different entity levels in all domains in order to boost system scalability and provide secure and efficient cross-domain information flow. Methods A blockchain sharding technique based on the Metis graph partitioning algorithm for IoV was presented to increase the efficiency of syncing a large quantity of authentication data on the chain. This technique adjusts to the unequal distribution of authentication data on various road segments in the IoV and balances the burdens of each shard. A batch authentication method based on certificateless public-key cryptography (CL-PKC) was proposed, which reduced the authentication overhead of cross-domain messages by permitting batch authentication of communications from several trust domains. Results and Discussion The suggested technique successfully increases the authentication efficiency of cross-trust domain communications, according to experimental data. It decreases the computational overhe…

title: Preventive Health and Health Services Block Grant Flexible Funding Mechanism Is Associated With Improved Population Outcomes
abstract: ABSTRACT Objectives: To investigate the association between Preventive Health and Health Services (PHHS) Block Grant (BG) funding and population health outcomes. Design: A state-level panel data set (2000–2019) for 50 US states was compiled from USA Spending, PHHS BG administrative system, US Census Bureau, and America's Health Rankings. The long-term population health outcome was years of life lost (YLL), measured as deaths before age 75 years per 100 000 population. We used a generalized method of moments (GMM), along with a Koyck distributed lag model and a 2-way fixed-effects approach, to assess the impact of PHHS BG funding on YLL. We also provided several sensitivity analyses. Setting: This study examines the effects of PHHS Block Grant flexible funding on the population health outcomes during the period of 2000–2019. Participants: Fifty US States were included in the study. Main Outcome Measure: YLL before age 75, per 100 000 population. Results: During 2000–2019, a $1 per capita increase in PHHS BG funding was associated with a 1.5%–11% reduction in YLL (110–832 fewer years lost per 100 000 population). Conclusions: Increasing use of PHHS BG funds is associated with substantial years of life savings.

Nipa Palm (Nypa fruticans) Utilization: Implications for Blue Carbon and the Sustainable Bioeconomy – A Systematic Review
abstract: Background Nypa fruticans (nipa palm) provides ecological and economic benefits in tropical mangrove ecosystems but remains underrepresented in blue carbon inventories and bioeconomy policy. This review assessed its uses, carbon sequestration potential relative to other mangroves, and contribution to a sustainable bioeconomy. Methods A systematic review followed PRISMA 2020. Scopus was searched for “Nypa fruticans,” “Nipa Palm,” and “Nipah.” English-language, open-access journal articles published from 2016 to 2026 were screened in six stages using predefined criteria. Data were extracted into a structured database and analysed using bibliometric analysis and qualitative synthesis. Results Of 454 records identified, 175 studies were included. Research mainly originated from Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, with publication output increasing after 2019. Eight themes emerged: bioenergy; food and functional products; health and pharmaceutical products; materials; livelihoods and value chains; cultural ecosystem services; blue carbon and ecosystem support; and sustainability risks, including invasiveness. Mean carbon fraction was 42.48% (range 41.45–43.50%), while reported carbon stocks ranged from 7.26 to 38.10 Mg C ha −1 , below values reported for Rhizophora apiculata and Bruguiera gymnorrhiza. Nipa may contribute to carbon storage in degraded coastal areas and dense stands, w…
