title: Digital Transformation and ESG Synergy in Enhancing Enterprise Market Value
abstract: Coordinating digital transformation with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices is essential for corporate sustainability. Examining how this coordination affects enterprise market value clarifies the value implications of integrating the two strategies. Drawing on 26,486 firm–year observations for Chinese A-share firms during 2011–2024, this study constructs a digital transformation–ESG synergy (DESG) index using a coupling coordination degree (CCD) model that integrates annual-report digital transformation frequency and Huazheng ESG performance scores. A two-way fixed-effects model is used for estimation. The reported baseline shows a significant positive association between DESG and enterprise market value after controlling for firm characteristics and firm and year fixed effects. First-link mechanism analysis indicates that DESG is positively associated with firms’ internal conversion capacities (absorptive, innovation, and adaptive capabilities), operational green transformation, and external corporate reputation. Moderation analysis further shows that all five internal and external moderators positively shift the marginal DESG–market value slope: media coverage and green governance recognition amplify the positive association across all quartiles, whereas entrepreneurial spirit, new quality productive forces, and analyst attention exhibit threshold effects …

title: Winner or Loser? Opening to Export Markets and Gender‐Specific Labour Market Adjustments
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines the effects of a positive export shock on gender‐specific labour market outcomes using nationally representative household and firm‐level data from Vietnam. We exploit exogenous variation in provincial exposure to tariff reductions induced by the U.S.–Vietnam Bilateral Trade Agreement. We find that opening to export markets is associated with stronger wage growth for men than for women, widening the estimated gender wage gap, although we find little evidence of gender differences in working‐hour responses. Opening to export markets is also associated with workers' transitions out of unpaid family work and into formal employment. However, these responses do not differ significantly between women and men. By contrast, women are significantly more likely than men to transition into non‐manual occupations in provinces more exposed to U.S. tariff reductions. Moreover, a positive gender composition effect provides an additional channel through which trade shapes gender disparities. As complementary evidence, the firm‐level analysis shows stronger growth in female employment in trade‐exposed regions, while female workers are more concentrated in larger firms that experience lower wage growth. Our findings show that increased export market access can generate divergent effects along the employment and wage margins, helping reconcile conflicting results in t…

title: The Effect of Enterprise and Primary Market Metrics on Underpricing
abstract: The growing number of investors through the end of 2025 suggests an improvement in financial literacy. Nevertheless, many individuals continue to experience investment losses, particularly when investing in companies undertaking Initial Public Offerings (IPOs). Investors therefore need to understand essential information about the companies whose shares they intend to purchase. Accordingly, this study aims to identify the factors that influence IPO underpricing. The method used to analyze this data employs a quantitative approach. The data is secondary, and the documentation technique was used to collect it. The data analysis technique employed is multiple regression analysis, with the research sample consisting of 146 companies that went public (IPO) between 2023 and 2025. The sampling technique used was saturation sampling. Thus, the research sample consists of 146 companies. The factors influencing underpricing are company size, with a significance value of 0.000, and IPO proceeds, with a significance value of 0.003. Meanwhile, the factors that have no significant influence are sales growth, with a significance value of 0.352; ROA, with a significance value of 0.928; and DER, with a significance value of 0.989. Investors should carefully evaluate relevant information before making investment decisions to improve their prospects of earning returns on stocks with differing val…

title: Post-Harvest Losses, Bargaining Power, and Market Inefficiencies in Jordan’s Potato Value Chain
abstract: Potato production plays an important role in Jordan’s agricultural economy and food supply, while producers face challenges mainly related to post-harvest losses, market volatility, limited storage capacity, and weak market coordination. This study analyzes the potato value chain in Ramtha District, northern Jordan, with a focus on post-harvest losses, market relations, and opportunities for value-chain upgrading. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 115 actors involved in potato production, marketing, logistics, storage, and consumption. Quantitative data were complemented by a limited number of open-ended responses to capture actors’ views on key constraints and potential improvements. The findings indicate that market and post-harvest constraints are important sources of pressure on value-chain performance. Price volatility was identified by 91.2% of respondents as a factor reducing net profit margins, while 88% reported that wholesalers held the greatest bargaining power. Technology adoption was limited, with only 6.1% reporting the use of technologies such as grading, packing, price applications, or tracking systems. Affordable cold-storage facilities, standardized packaging processes, better market regulation, and greater price transparency during the season were among the other areas that respondents identified as needing improvement. The results suggest that upg…

Renewable-Hydrogen Sector Coupling for Electricity and Ferry Decarbonization on a Non-Interconnected Island: A Feasibility Assessment of Gavdos, Greece
abstract: Gavdos is assessed as a non-interconnected island without mainland electricity exchange over the adopted planning horizon. A configuration with 340 kWp of photovoltaics, an 800 kW wind turbine, and surplus-fed electrolysis is evaluated for electricity supply and ferry hydrogen. Twelve public HEDNO monthly day-ahead files were concatenated into an 8760 h rolling-year demand series. RETScreen-based F-chart solar calculations and a Weibull wind distribution (k = 2) provided twelve representative monthly 24 h renewable profiles, mapped by month and hour to the dispatch chronology. Renewable generation first serves demand; deficits are assigned to conventional generation and surplus to electrolysis. Annual demand is 662.630 MWh, of which renewables supply 650.633 MWh directly (98.19%); the residual deficit is 11.997 MWh across 419 h. The 302.6 kW baseline electrolyzer produces 34.488 t H2 year−1 gross versus a ferry demand of 33.890 t H2 year−1. Although daily production is lower than demand in 130 days, accumulated hydrogen keeps the gross inventory non-negative. The maximum seasonal drawdown is 947.4 kg, giving a usable hydrogen-mass requirement of 1133.1 kg including a two-day reserve. The results demonstrate gross-production compatibility under the adopted assumptions; net ferry-fuel adequacy requires detailed assessment of component operation, auxiliary loads, storage, delivery…

title: Corporate Zombification, Accounting Conservatism, and Stock Price Crash Risk: New Evidence from Emerging Market
abstract: The article examines the relationship between the degree of accounting conservatism and stock price crash risk in zombie firms. It investigates whether zombie firms delay their loss recognition by following conservative accounting practices. Next, it explores how conservative reporting behaviors influence the likelihood of firms’ stock price crashes. Finally, the study examines the moderating role of stock pledging in this relationship. Using panel data from 2011 to 2024, the study finds that zombie firms exhibit lower levels of accounting conservatism. Moreover, zombie firms that follow less conservative accounting are more vulnerable to stock price crash risks. The results further show that firms engaging in share pledging face even higher crash risks due to reduced conservatism. It addresses the endogeneity concern by using the propensity score matching technique to create a treatment group of zombie firms and a control group of non-zombie firms with comparable observable characteristics, enabling a more reliable estimation of the effects of accounting conservatism. To the authors’ knowledge, this work offers a novel contribution to the literature, offering new evidence on how corporate zombification impacts stock price crash risk using conservatism principles in an emerging economy like India. JEL Codes: G32, G31, G33, G38

title: INTEGRATED TECHNICAL CONDITION ASSESSMENT OF AGING PORT HANDLING EQUIPMENT FOR SERVICE LIFE EXTENSION
abstract: The operation of port handling equipment that has been in long-term service under marine conditions is accompanied by intensive cyclic loading, corrosion, fatigue damage, deformation, and mechanical wear. The integration of engineering diagnostics, condition-based maintenance, structural assessment, and residual service-life evaluation provides a reliable basis for decision-making regarding repair, strengthening, modernization, controlled operation, and service-life extension. Purpose. To investigate modern European approaches to maintenance management of aging port handling equipment and assess their applicability to extending crane service life under long-term marine conditions. Method. The study considers the principal degradation mechanisms identified during technical inspections, including corrosion, fatigue cracking, permanent deformation, and wear of structural and mechanical components. The obtained data are used to assess technical condition, structural integrity, operational safety, and residual service life. The application of Condition-Based Maintenance and Structural Health Monitoring is also considered. Results. The analysis confirms that corrosion, fatigue, deformation, and wear are the main factors limiting the service life of aging port cranes. An integrated maintenance approach improves maintenance planning, reduces operational risks, and supports economically…

title: Evaluation of Digital Literacy Skills for Effective Library Service Delivery among Library Staff in Adamawa State University, Mubi
abstract: This study evaluated digital literacy skills and their influence on effective library service delivery among staff of Adamawa State University, Mubi. With the growing demand for digital information services, the research aimed to assess staff competencies, identify skill gaps, and examine challenges affecting digital performance. A descriptive survey design was employed, and data were gathered through a structured questionnaire and interviews with library personnel. Descriptive and inferential statistics, including correlation and ANOVA, were used to analyze the data 0.05. Findings revealed that library staff possessed moderate to high proficiency in basic digital skills such as word processing and internet use but exhibited limited competence in advanced areas like digital preservation and database management. Results further showed a significant positive relationship between digital literacy and the quality of library service delivery. Major challenges identified included unstable power supply, poor internet connectivity, and inadequate training opportunities. The study recommends continuous capacity-building programs, improved ICT infrastructure, and institutional support to enhance staff digital competencies and ensure efficient, technology-driven library services.

Deciphering natural alkaline water-induced human molecular homeostatic regulation via non-invasive sweat metabolic profiling
abstract: Natural alkaline water, a weakly alkaline NaHCO 3 ‐enriched solution, has been postulated to modulate systemic metabolic homeostasis, but its clinical metabolic effects remain poorly characterized due to the scarcity of non-invasive, longitudinal molecular evidence. Conventional flexible microneedles for sweat analysis are limited to single‐analyte detection, failing to meet the need for simultaneous profiling of multiple biomarkers required to assess systemic homeostasis. To address these challenges, we engineered a hierarchical metal‐carbide (MXene)‐based flexible microneedle array integrated with high‐performance mass spectrometry, establishing a non‐invasive, high‐throughput sweat metabolic profiling platform. Here, we show that the hierarchical architecture, featuring a petal‐like AgNWs@MXene heterostructure, creates synergistic hotspots that enhance laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI‐MS) signal intensity by more than twofold compared with pristine MXene, allowing robust detection of 77 ± 8 metabolic features from a single sweat‐patch sample. In a cohort study (n = 107), this platform enabled simultaneous dynamic monitoring of key metabolic features associated with uric acid, lactate, and glutamine (p < 0.001). Overall, this work reveals the regulatory effects of natural alkaline water on metabolic homeostasis and provides a scalable, high‐throughput str…

title: Frequency of cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea in traumatic head injury with pneumocephalus
abstract: Background: rain injury from trauma continues to pose a major public health obstacle on a worldwide scale. It stands as the principal cause of disability and death internationally, with lower and middle-income countries experiencing the most severe disease burden. The procedure known as "decompressive craniectomy" involves removing a bone flap after opening the dura mater to control cerebral swelling and alleviate dangerously high intracranial pressure. Decompressive craniectomy has become an established and regularly performed surgical technique in neurosurgical medicine. Objective: To determine the frequency of cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea in traumatic head injury with pneumocephalus Setting: This Randomized controlled trial study was conducted at Department of Neurosurgery Bolan Medical College Hospital Quetta. Methodology: Total 144 patients meeting the established inclusion criteria were enrolled in the study. All enrolled patients underwent surgical intervention performed by a single surgical team under general anesthesia, with oversight provided by a research team member. Patients were monitored postoperatively for the development of complications, and statistical analysis was conducted utilizing SPSS version 24.0. Results: The findings demonstrated that the mean patient age was 33.3±7.8 years, with males comprising 73.6% of the cohort. Regarding clinical outcomes, 20.…

title: Building public health capacity: evaluating the intermediate Field Epidemiology Training Program of Papua New Guinea
abstract: Introduction Field Epidemiology Training Programs (FETPs) use a work-integrated learning model to equip graduates with skills in disease surveillance, outbreak response, data analysis, and evidence-based decision-making. The intermediate-level Field Epidemiology Training Program of Papua New Guinea (iFETPNG) was established in 2013 to strengthen the country’s public health workforce. This study presents the results of a theory-based evaluation of iFETPNG. Methods An FETP impact evaluation framework was used to guide data collection using a theory-based convergent mixed-methods design. Online surveys were administered to all 75 iFETPNG graduates from 2013 to 2019 (49 responded), and in-depth interviews were conducted with a purposeful selection of 20 graduates and 8 senior managers/executives from the provincial and national levels in PNG. Data were analyzed using Microsoft Excel, R, and NVivo. Results The evaluation found that iFETPNG substantially improved graduates’ skills in surveillance, outbreak response, operational research, and evidence-based public health practice. Since completing iFETPNG, graduates reported investigating 588 outbreaks, conducting numerous surveillance evaluations, and implementing a range of public health interventions. Individually and collectively, graduates helped strengthen public health systems in PNG. The program also supported the development …

abstract: Currently, developments in the field of additive manufacturing are gaining increasing popularity, including the construction industry. However, the widespread use of 3D printing in construction is hindered by a number of challenges, including difficulties in reinforcing structures during the printing process, a lack of data on strength and deformability of such structures under load, the lack of a regulatory framework for the design of 3D printed structures, large dimensions of the structures–which necessitate large-format printers–and other factors. Efforts to advance the technology are primarily focused on developing specialized concrete mixes for printing and studying and improving their properties. Research, however, should be focused on studying and standardizing strength and strain properties of structural materials produced by additive manufacturing. Purpose: The aim of the work is to develop the experimental program of studying column fragments and reference samples of cubes and prisms to determine the strength and strain properties of 3D printed materials, and compare them with the structural parameters of in-situ concrete. Research findings : The experimental program of studies is developed for column segments and reference samples to determine strength and strain properties of structural materials, i.e., those obtained in conventional in-situ mold and 3D printed. Is Loneliness a Mechanism Linking Sleep Disturbance with Symptoms of Generalised Anxiety, Social Anxiety, Depression, and Eating Disorders in Adolescence? Findings From a 6-Year Longitudinal Study
abstract: Abstract Study Objectives: Sleep disturbance and loneliness have both emerged as potentially important risk factors for generalised anxiety, social anxiety, depression and eating disorders in adolescents. Further, theories suggest sleep disturbance may increase risk for these social-emotional disorders, in-part, by increasing loneliness. This study investigated whether loneliness is a mediating factor linking sleep disturbance with symptoms of social-emotional disorders across the course of adolescence. Methods: As part of the wider Risks to Adolescent Wellbeing Project, these constructs were assessed longitudinally in a cohort of 528 adolescents over seven annual waves of data collection, spanning ages 11 to 17. Sleep (morningness/eveningness preference, school night sleep duration, daytime sleepiness), loneliness and symptoms of generalised anxiety, social anxiety, depression and eating disorders were measured via self-report questionnaires. Results: Cross-lagged panel models showed sleep disturbance predicted worse symptoms of generalised and social anxiety, depression, and eating disorders over time. Higher loneliness also predicted worse symptoms of social anxiety, depression and eating disorders. Loneliness significantly mediated the relationship between sleep disturbance and social anxiety and depression. Yet, generalised anxiety, social anxiety and depression also media…

ESG Ratings and Corporate Sustainable Growth Under Financing Constraints: A Dual-Route Mechanism of Green Technological Innovation and Resource Improvement
abstract: Under China’s dual-carbon and high-quality development goals, this study examines whether and how third-party ESG ratings are associated with corporate sustainable growth, defined as the internally financeable growth rate of Higgins. Using 25,683 firm-year observations of Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2022 and Huazheng ESG ratings, of which only seven of the nine levels (C to A) are observed, we estimate a moderated mediation model (Hayes Model 21). A one-level rating upgrade is associated with a 1.42 percentage-point-higher sustainable growth rate (1.69 points when profitability controls mechanically linked to the dependent variable are excluded), and a one-standard-deviation increase corresponds to 10.5% of the standard deviation of the growth rate. The association holds under instrumental-variable estimation, propensity-score matching, firm fixed effects and alternative measures. Green technological innovation, measured by green patent applications, partially mediates the relationship, but the indirect effect (0.0020) accounts for only 14.2% of the total effect; supplementary tests suggest that lower financing costs and reduced operating and crash risks are potential complementary channels behind the direct effect. Financing constraints weaken the first stage of the green technological innovation route, whereas a stronger market competitive position…

title: A Trusted Edge Scheduling Method for Computing Power Network Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In multi-party collaborative scenarios where computing power networks and edge intelligence work in synergy, trusted edge scheduling methods optimize resource allocation through intelligent scheduling, ensuring that computing tasks of each participant are executed on independent edge nodes, thus effectively improving computing efficiency and resource utilization. However, distributed edge nodes and their supporting communication networks usually require independent deployment and operation and maintenance, making efficient scheduling a critical challenge. This paper proposes a trusted edge scheduling method based on deep reinforcement learning, which realizes privacy protection through smart contract technology. Computing and network resources are stored on the blockchain, scheduling is performed using the Edge Routing Model (ERM) in smart contracts, and the hash values of scheduling results are recorded on the blockchain. ERM aims to meet users’ computing demands while selecting the optimal routing strategy to maximize network bandwidth utilization. The method adopts deep reinforcement learning with a prioritized sampling mechanism to constrain the action space, and combines graph neural networks to learn features of network topology, thereby enhancing the generalization ability. Experimental results show that, compared with traditional scheduling models, ERM can schedule edge…

title: Thermal and nutritional optimization of a TiO 2 nanoparticle‐coated passive solar dryer for meat using hybrid RSM ‐ Bald Eagle Search optimization
abstract: Abstract The thermal and nutritional efficiency of a passive solar dryer, using a TiO 2 (titanium dioxide) coated absorber plate was studied experimentally. Empirical models were developed between the measured chamber temperature, drying time, and coating thickness with the protein retention and final moisture content, respectively, using a Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and Central Composite Design (CCD). The resultant models exhibited excellent predictive power with R 2 values of more than 0.97. The fitted RSM response surfaces were then used in Bald Eagle Search to determine the optimal operating conditions in the experimental regions. The moisture content at the end of the experiment was 4.9% with a protein retention of 91.2%. Experiments showed that the maximum surface temperature of the TiO 2 ‐coated and uncoated configurations was 76.4°C and 66.2°C, respectively, while the maximum thermal efficiencies were 44.2% and 36.8%, respectively. The dryer under the optimized condition obtained a maximum experimental protein retention of 91.2%, and the moisture content at the end of drying was 4.9%, and there was a significant reduction in drying time compared to the uncoated system. The TiO 2 ‐coated absorber also improved the uniformity of drying, increased effective heat use, and improved the thermal efficiency without compromising product quality.

Joint Direction and Distance Estimation of Low-Energy Photon Point Sources Using a Spatial–Global Dual-Branch CNN
abstract: An uncollimated scintillator array encodes source direction and distance in both its spatial response and total count rate. We modeled an isotropic 11.6 keV point source and a 12 × 12 yttrium orthosilicate array in Geant4 11.3.2, using a scintillation yield of 15,300 photons MeV−1. A spatial–global dual-branch convolutional neural network, Full, combined normalized response patterns with six global descriptors for joint localization conditional on known emitted exposure. The response library comprised 272 training and 96 validation positions, with a 72-position multi-distance evaluation grid and 18 fixed-distance diagnostic positions. On the multi-distance grid, Full achieved three-seed mean directional and distance MAEs of 10.4° and 26.0 mm. At 300 randomly sampled positions and 4 million primaries, the corresponding means were 15.6° and 52.6 mm. An input-matched multilayer perceptron gave 16.7°/55.2 mm at 4 million primaries. Same-coordinate exposure controls and independent Monte Carlo repetitions characterized statistical sensitivity. A forward-response inverse estimator performed better in a far-field, near-axis subset. The results support combining spatial and rate information for localization under the simulated conditions and identify exposure and viewing geometry as major limits on accuracy.

title: Reliable Gas Solubility from Molecular Simulations: Benchmarking Insertion and Alchemical Free Energy Methods in Liquids and Polymers
abstract: Abstract Reliable prediction of gas transport in polymeric materials requires accurate estimation of solubility and diffusion coefficients within dense, heterogeneous matrices. In this work, we systematically benchmark four molecular simulation approaches for solubility calculations, including free energy perturbation (FEP), Bennett acceptance ratio (BAR), thermodynamic integration (TI), and widom test-particle insertion (TPI), using a two-level strategy. First, methane hydration in water is employed as a stringent reference system to assess accuracy, convergence, and bias-variance behavior. Second, the validated methodologies are applied to gas solubility in amorphous isotactic polypropylene (iPP) for H2, O2, N2, and CO2 at 300 K. The different approaches provide broadly consistent estimates for methane hydration in water within the reported statistical uncertainties. In amorphous polypropylene, however, differences are observed between the finite-sampling insertion estimates and the alchemical free-energy results. These discrepancies highlight the challenges associated with adequate sampling of favorable insertion configurations in heterogeneous polymer environments and the need for careful convergence assessment. The resulting solubilities, expressed as Henry coefficients and corrected to an amorphous-phase basis, agree well with experimental data and reproduce the expected …

title: Transport and Storage of Metal-Contaminated Sediments from Historical Zn–Pb Mining in Elm Creek, Picher, Oklahoma
abstract: Abstract This study investigated transport and storage of trace metal-contaminated sediments in Elm Creek, in the Tar Creek Superfund Site in northeastern Oklahoma, to evaluate contamination risk from historical Pb–Zn mining and remediation effectiveness at the Bird Dog site. Channel bed sediments were sampled quarterly over 16 months at Bird Dog South (BDS), immediately downstream of a remediated chat pile, Distal West (DW), 2.1 river km (R-km) downstream, and at nine sites extending 15 km toward the Neosho River. Alluvial deposits were cored at six wetland transects between BDS and DW and at five downstream floodplain transects. Discharge, turbidity, and rainfall monitoring at DW enabled flux estimation for 12 storm events. Mean BDS concentrations of Cd (192 mg kg −1 ), Pb (13,500 mg kg −1 ), and Zn (36,300 mg kg −1 ) exceeded regulatory thresholds by one to two orders of magnitude. Concentrations declined exponentially downstream (r 2 = 0.64–0.86), with Zn persisting above the consensus-based probable effects concentration threshold at 13 km. The aggraded wetland segment stores contaminated sediment to depths exceeding 1 m and widths up to 66 m, a large remobilizable inventory. Downstream deposits contain contaminated sediment to at least R-km 4.7 with bench and floodplain erosion posing lateral risk. Low sediment flux at DW (< 0.06 Mg day −1 ) confirms a storage-dominated s…

title: Strategy for Optimizing Idle Land to Increase Non-Aeronautical Revenue: A SWOT and VRIO Approach
abstract: The decline in air traffic at Adisutjipto Airport, Yogyakarta, following the opening of Yogyakarta International Airport calls for revenue sources that do not depend on passenger volume. This study analyzes the existing condition of idle land, the internal and external factors influencing its optimization, and the company’s resource advantages, and then formulates a strategy for optimizing idle land to increase non-aeronautical revenue. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed in a single case study of the 4,945 m² Babarsari idle land owned by PT Angkasa Pura Indonesia, Adisutjipto Yogyakarta Branch Office. Primary data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with nine purposively selected informants; secondary data came from the partner selection document and the highest and best use (HBU) study. The data were analyzed through reduction, display, and conclusion drawing using weighted strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis, value, rarity, imitability, and organization (VRIO) analysis, and a value creation assessment. Data trustworthiness was tested through triangulation, member checking, and an audit trail. The results show that the land has clean and clear legal status, that the company’s strategic position lies in SWOT Quadrant I (+0.88; +1.68), and that four of the six resources generate sustained competitive advantage. Corporate re…

Pulsed Electric Field Surface Engineering: A Reagent‐Free Technology for Valorising Biomass Fly Ash in Natural Rubber Composites
abstract: ABSTRACT Fly ash is an abundant but weakly reinforcing filler for elastomers, owing to coarse particles, low surface activity and poor adhesion to rubber. Here, pulsed electric field (PEF) processing is explored as a reagent‐free treatment for biomass fly ash (BFA) from rubber‐wood combustion. Sieved BFA (< 250 μm) was dispersed in distilled water (1:2 by mass), exposed to 2.5 kV cm −1 pulses for 10–40 min (94–375 kJ per kg of ash), dried and compounded into natural rubber (NR) at 0–45 phr. X‐ray fluorescence identified an alumino‐ferric mixed‐oxide ash (Al 2 O 3 28.3, Fe 2 O 3 9.6, SiO 2 7.6 wt%). Two‐way analysis of variance showed that ash loading dominated the scorch time, optimum cure time and tensile strength, whereas the treatment dominated the hardness and elongation at break. The ash shortened the scorch and cure times; the treated ash raised the hardness by 3–8 Shore A, to a maximum of 58.6 Shore A at 94 kJ kg −1 , and increased the tensile strength at 45 phr from 15.0 to 18.5 MPa (+23%), while the elongation at break fell from 1051%–1133% to 943%–1044%. Fracture surfaces showed debonded untreated and textured treated particles; surface area and chemistry were not measured. Energy balances bound the bulk slurry heating to ≤ 41 K and show that drying, not the pulses, dominates the energy demand. Because the untreated reference was not slurried, the field, heating and a…

title: Field characterization of urban road traffic noise sources: effects of road class and vehicle composition
abstract: Routine road traffic noise assessment describes the source by traffic volume, speed and vehicle-category shares, whereas monitoring usually reports a measured source-side level with a total vehicle count only, so that the operating conditions behind that level remain unidentified. This paper addresses that gap with a multi-city field study of 25 urban road sections in Guangzhou, China, covering four road classes and three operating periods. Each section-period was measured three times for 20 min with Class 1 instrumentation and counted by vehicle class, giving 75 observations analyzed with an explicit metrological and statistical treatment. Levels ranged from 58.5 to 79.8 dB(A); arterial sections alone spanned 15.0 dB(A) and night-time measurements 21.3 dB(A). Vehicle-class flow was more strongly associated with L A e q than average speed, medium-vehicle flow showing the strongest association ( r = 0.867, 95 % CI 0.797-0.914). The expanded uncertainty of a single level was about 0.8 dB ( k = 2). The results support recording vehicle-class counts alongside L A e q , so that a measured level can be attributed to traffic volume, fleet composition or both.

title: Reducing uncertainty in fractured carbonate reservoir models throughmultiscale discrete fracture network integration and dynamic calibration
abstract: Abstract Fractured carbonate reservoirs are highly heterogeneous, and their multiscale fracture systems make it difficult to reliably characterize fracture geometry and hydraulic properties. This study presents an integrated discrete fracture network (DFN) approach for a Carboniferous fractured carbonate reservoir in the Kappa Field. Seismic interpretation and curvature attributes were used to identify fracture-related structural features and constrain their spatial distribution at the field scale. These results were integrated with fracture orientations and occurrences identified from borehole image logs and core observations to constrain fracture geometry at the well scale. Dynamic well-test data were then incorporated through transmissivity (KH) calibration to constrain fracture aperture and permeability and to evaluate the hydraulic behavior of the modeled network. The integration of these datasets provides complementary constraints on fracture geometry and hydraulic properties across different observation scales. The resulting DFN model shows improved consistency with the observed reservoir pressure response and provides a more reliable representation of fracture connectivity and hydraulic communication. This study demonstrates that integrating seismic interpretation, curvature attributes, borehole image logs, core observations, and dynamic well-test data provides a robust…

title: DEPENDÊNCIA DE MARKETPLACES NO VAREJO: GESTÃO DE MARGENS DIANTE DE COMISSÕES, PUBLICIDADE PAGA E DEVOLUÇÕES
abstract: O lojista que decide vender em marketplace confronta uma comissão, um gasto com publicidade na própria plataforma e um custo de devolução que a lei brasileira lhe atribui. Este artigo mede a margem efetivamente disponível para suportar esses três itens. A fonte é a Pesquisa Anual de Comércio de 2024 do IBGE, com dados extraídos da interface programática do Sistema IBGE de Recuperação Automática, e a camada normativa foi obtida em duas fontes oficiais independentes para cada diploma. O primeiro resultado é de leitura: a taxa de margem divulgada pelo IBGE é calculada sobre o custo das mercadorias, não sobre a receita, e as comissões incidem sobre a receita. No comércio varejista, a taxa publicada de 38,6% corresponde a uma margem sobre a receita de 27,85%. O segundo é de estrutura: entre os oito segmentos varejistas não alimentares examinados, a correlação entre a participação da internet na receita e a margem sobre a receita é de -0,90 no coeficiente de Pearson e de -0,93 no de postos. O terceiro é aritmético: com comissão de 20%, publicidade de 3% e devolução de 10% dos pedidos, a contribuição do canal no varejo é de 3,26% da receita, contra gastos com pessoal de 7,17%. Os segmentos mais dependentes do canal são aqueles em que o canal menos paga.

title: Emissions Performance as a Capability‐Based Organizational Outcome: Evidence From Interpretable Machine Learning in Hospitality and Tourism
abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing corporate greenhouse gas emissions has become a central strategic challenge for firms, yet substantial heterogeneity persists in emissions performance even among organizations facing similar regulatory and market conditions. Existing research has largely attributed emissions outcomes to governance mechanisms, ESG initiatives, or financial capacity, often assuming linear and additive effects. This study advances a capability‐based perspective by conceptualizing firm‐level emissions performance not as a capability in itself, but as an emergent organizational outcome reflecting how effectively firms deploy and coordinate capability‐related workforce, operational, and managerial systems. Using firm‐level ESG and financial data from 110 publicly listed hospitality and tourism firms over the period 2015–2024, we apply ensemble machine learning techniques, bagging, random forest, and boosting, to model emissions performance. Boosting models consistently outperform alternative approaches and are analyzed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and partial dependence plots (PDP) to ensure interpretability and theory development. Across four progressively enriched model specifications, the results show that workforce quality, resource‐use efficiency, and managerial effectiveness, the empirical proxies for underlying organizational capabilities, are the most influenti…

title: Influence of Digital Resources and Information Sharing on Supply Chain Sustainability
abstract: ABSTRACT Although supply chain digitalization has received considerable research attention, the mechanisms through which digital resources contribute to sustainability outcomes are not fully understood. This study examines how digital technologies, particularly big data analytics (BDA), support sustainability practices and performance in supply chains through information sharing. Building on the resource‐based view (RBV) and the dynamic capabilities perspective, a conceptual framework is developed and empirically tested using cross‐industry survey data from Finland and partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM). The results show that digital resources and BDA indirectly contribute to supply chain sustainability by enhancing information sharing among supply chain partners. More effective information sharing improves transparency and coordination across the supply chain, thereby supporting the achievement of sustainability goals. This study makes two contributions. First, from an RBV perspective, it shows that information sharing is a key resource through which digitalization translates into sustainability outcomes. Second, from a dynamic capabilities perspective, it extends the emerging literature by showing how digitally enabled capabilities support sustainability transitions in supply chains.

title: Exercise Right Atrial Stiffness From Pressure-Volume Loops and Prognosis in Pulmonary Hypertension
abstract: BACKGROUND: In pulmonary hypertension (PH), risk assessment focuses on right ventricular function and may overlook exercise-related right atrial (RA) functional limitation. We investigated whether RA stiffness during exercise reflects impaired right-heart filling reserve and is associated with prognosis beyond conventional measures. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 68 participants in this observational study, including 42 with precapillary PH. Participants who had PH ruled out and patients with postcapillary PH formed reference groups. Participants underwent 3-dimensional echocardiography, right heart catheterization, and invasive RA pressure-volume loop analysis at rest and during standardized semisupine exercise. RA filling stiffness was derived from the reservoir phase. Patients with precapillary PH were stratified by median exercise RA filling stiffness. RESULTS: At rest, high- and low-stiffness groups had comparable right ventricular function, afterload, and cardiac index, but the high-stiffness group exhibited impaired phasic RA strain and venous congestion (median [interquartile range] liver stiffness, 7.1 [6.0–8.8] versus 5.2 [4.8–5.8] kPa; P =0.021). During exercise, mean RA pressure increased similarly, but the high-stiffness group had impaired peak cardiac index (3.3±1.0 versus 4.1±0.9 L/min per m 2 ; P =0.015) and RA strain. Unlike resting RA stiffness, high exerc…

title: ENTREPRENEURIAL ORIENTATION AND SMEs PERFORMANCE IN SOKOTO METROPOLIS, SOKOTO STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: The study examined the influence of entrepreneurial orientation on the performance of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Sokoto metropolis. The study was motivated by the continued performance challenges faced by SMEs despite their important role in employment generation and economic development. A quantitative survey design was adopted, and primary data were collected from a sample of 353 SME owners and managers, out of which 330 valid responses were analyzed. The research instrument was a structured questionnaire measured on a five-point Likert scale. Regression was used to test the research hypotheses. Results revealed that both pro-activeness and risk-taking showed significant positive effects on SME performance in Sokoto metropolis. The study concludes that entrepreneurial behaviours such as anticipating market opportunities and taking calculated risks are essential drivers of SME growth and competitiveness in Sokoto metropolis. It recommends that SME owners adopt proactive strategies, apply moderate risk-taking approaches, and that support agencies provide targeted training and financial assistance to strengthen entrepreneurial capability.

title: STAKEHOLDERS’ PERCEPTION OF FINANCIAL OPERATIONS OF STUDENTS’ COOPERATIVE THRIFT AS AN ALTERNATIVE FUNDING STRATEGY FOR THE IMPROVEMENT OF UNDERGRADUATES STUDENTS’ WELFARE IN BAYELSA STATE
abstract: The study ascertained stakeholders’ perception of financial operations of students’ cooperative thrift as an alternative funding strategy for the improvement of undergraduates’ students’ welfare in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. Descriptive survey design was adopted for the study. The population comprised of up of 32,652 students and staff from four public Universities in Bayelsa State during the 2020/2021 academic session. A sample size of 1,136 was selected through purposive and proportionate random sampling technique. A 12 item questionnaire instrument was utilized for data collection. The instrument was self-designed and tagged “Stakeholders Perception of cooperative thrift and alternative funding strategy for the improvement of undergraduate students’ welfare questionnaire (SPCTAFSIUSW). Data collected were analyzed using simple percentages, mean, standard deviation. The results obtained showed a significant difference on staff and students’ stakeholders’ mean rating of students’ cooperative thrift as an alternative funding strategy for the improvement of undergraduate students’ welfare in Universities in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. Hence, the study proposed the establishment of students’ cooperative thrift in Universities in Bayelsa State.

title: Ideas, Inventors, and Deals: The Innovation–M&A Nexus
abstract: This review examines how M&A reshape the creation, diffusion, and ownership of innovation. It treats M&A as one form of boundary choice over innovative assets and people, alongside licensing, alliances, corporate venture capital, minority stakes, inventor mobility, and acqui-hires. Synthesizing evidence from finance, industrial organization, strategy, and sector studies, the review explains why firm boundaries matter for knowledge flows; how innovation shapes who buys whom; and how acquisition markets affect inventive effort, start-up exits, and the build-versus-buy boundary. Post-M&A outcomes are heterogeneous because deals are selected matches and innovation has multiple margins: R&D effort, patenting, novelty, exploration, exploitation, commercialization, diffusion, and human capital reallocation. The review closes by linking property rights and labor market perspectives on inventors, teams, mobility, acqui-hiring, and labor market power and by outlining a policy-relevant agenda.

AI INVESTMENT AND THE UK STARTUP ECOSYSTEM: COMPETING WITH SILICON VALLEY IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI
abstract: This study examines the evolution and competitive positioning of the United Kingdom's AI startup ecosystem amid the rise of generative AI. Using a qualitative desk-research design based on secondary investment data, policy documents, and academic literature from 2015-2026, the study analyzes how the UK has transitioned from a research-driven niche to a globally recognized hub, leveraging world-class universities, dense financial and healthcare markets, and a principle-based regulatory framework. Growth has been propelled by a robust spinout cycle from anchor institutions and accessible early-stage capital. Despite these strengths, structural constraints threaten long-term scale, including a persistent late-stage funding gap, infrastructure bottlenecks in compute access and energy costs, and intensifying global competition for talent. The study finds the UK is best positioned to capture value in autonomous enterprise agents, AI for scientific discovery, and multimodal systems. Sustaining global competitiveness will require expanding domestic growth capital, ensuring reliable compute access, and maintaining regulatory clarity without stifling agility.

BOARD CHARACTERISTICS AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF LISTED INSURANCE COMPANIES IN NIGERIA
abstract: This study, board characteristics and financial performance of listed insurance companies in Nigeria specifically examined the effect of board characteristics proxied by board Independence, board size, and board gender diversity on financial performance of listed insurance companies in Nigeria using Return on Equity (ROE) as proxy of financial performance. Using ex-post factor research design, data was collected from annual reports of eleven (11) sampled listed insurance companies in Nigeria form year 2021 to 2025 and analysed using regression analysis. The result of the analysis shows that board size with a coefficient of -0.4488, t-value of -2.83 and p<0.05 and gender diversity with a coefficient of 0.2739, t-value of 3.45 and a p < 0.05 has effect on ROE while board independence with a coefficient of −0.2945, t-value −0.99 and a p-value of 0.327 which is greater than 0.05, indicating a negative and statistically insignificant effect on ROE of the sampled companies. The study therefore recommends that regulatory authorities provide guidance and encourage listed companies to sporadically assess the effectiveness of the board, ensure restructuring of oversized boards where necessary rather than concentrating on increasing board size and make it a policy for the inclusion of a good number of female directors among corporate boards.

title: IMPACT OF BOARD MONITORING MECHANISMS ON RETURN ON ASSET IN SELECTED CONSUMER GOODS MANUFACTURING FIRMS IN NIGERIA
abstract: This study examined the effect of accounting technology expenditure on shareholder’s return in selected consumer goods manufacturing firms in Nigeria between 2006 and 2025. Using an ex-post facto research design, secondary data were analyzed from ten (10) firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group over a 20-year period, Panel Regression Analysis was used to examine the extent to which accounting technology expenditure influence return on equity. Fixed Regression also showed that Board Gender Diversity (BOGD) is positive and significant to Return on Asset (β = 0.047967, p = 0.0000). Board IT Competence exerted strong positive and significant effect on ROA (β = 0.126435, p = 0.0000). CEO Duality has positive and significant effect on ROA (β = 0.026689, p = 0.0000). The study concluded that the model specified for the study adequately captured all variables and is of good fit. Accounting technology expenditure is significant to return on equity in selected consumer goods manufacturing firms in Nigeria. It recommends that firms should focus more on human capital investment, as it consistently improves shareholders’ returns. At the same time, management should carefully evaluate R&D and software investments to ensure that they are aligned with long-term profitability objectives rather than short-term financial pressure.

title: Pengaruh Fraud Hexagon Theory terhadap Financial Statement Fraud dengan Komite Audit sebagai Variabel Moderasi
abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of the Fraud Hexagon Theory elements on financial statement fraud in State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2018–2023 period, with the audit committee serving as a moderating variable. This study employed a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from companies' annual reports. The sample consisted of 103 firm-year observations selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using the Common Effect Model (CEM) and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The results indicate that ineffective monitoring has a positive effect on financial statement fraud, whereas change in director and political connection have negative effects. Meanwhile, financial stability, auditor change, and frequent number of CEO's picture do not significantly affect financial statement fraud. Furthermore, the audit committee only moderates the relationship between change in director and financial statement fraud but does not moderate the relationships involving the other independent variables. These findings highlight the importance of effective internal monitoring and corporate governance in reducing the risk of financial statement fraud in Indonesian SOEs.

Downstream Credit Shock and Construction Firm Debt Burden: A Dynamic Capabilities Perspective
abstract: Abstract Successive global financial and geopolitical shocks have intensified credit market tightness, heightening uncertainty in developer financing, which in turn exposes construction firms reliant on these downstream payments to acute credit shocks. However, this issue has not been sufficiently examined in the existing literature. To address this gap, this study examines the impact of downstream credit shocks on the debt burden of construction firms. Using China’s “Three Red Lines” policy as a quasi-natural experiment and a Difference-in-Differences approach with financial data from listed construction firms, we find that downstream credit shocks significantly increase firms’ debt burdens. Exposed construction firms experience a 13.2% rise in debt-to-asset ratios and an increase of 15.18 billion yuan in debt obligations on average. Drawing on the dynamic capabilities perspective, we show that digital transformation and business diversification mitigate these effects, whereas regulatory violations exacerbate financial distress. Theoretically, this study extends the dynamic capabilities perspective by demonstrating how firm-level organizational conditions shape the effectiveness of firms’ responses to downstream credit shocks. title: Bayesian Game Analysis for Risk-Sharing Effectiveness of Price Adjustment Clauses in Transportation Projects
abstract: Abstract Departments of transportation commonly adopt trigger-based price adjustment clauses (PACs) to share risks of volatile material prices. Although existing research found no statistical evidence that the inclusion of PACs lowers contractors’ bids, qualitative studies have revealed that stakeholders continue to perceive PACs as beneficial. This leaves PACs’ ability to achieve a true risk-sharing equilibrium unresolved. As such, there is a dire need for a systematic investigation of PACs incorporating market volatility, project durations, and contractor bidding and behavioral strategies. This paper evaluates the effectiveness of PACs in facilitating equitable risk-sharing under varying market scenarios and project timelines. A comprehensive three-step approach is adopted through (1) retrieving and analyzing historical price data to capture prevailing trends; (2) using a Bayesian Nash equilibrium under game theory across 324 project scenarios to derive optimal strategic insights; and (3) applying decision tree classification to generalize the findings. Findings indicated that when prices experience a significant inflation throughout the project’s lifetime, a DOT’s best strategy is to apply high trigger values. title: Minimization of Power Consumption for NOMA-Assisted UAV Uplink Networks with Imperfect SIC Receiver
abstract: Introduction: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) communication networks can move in three-dimensional (3D) space, which can lead to a higher Line of Sight (LoS) probability for wireless communication channels between network nodes. Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) techniques are one of the proposed methods to overcome emerging challenges and meet requirements in the fifth (5G) and sixth (6G) generations of cellular systems. Due to the utilisation of an imperfect Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) receiver, the performance of the NOMA scheme is vulnerable to error propagation. This paper aims to minimise the power consumption of the NOMA-UAV uplink network, which has limited energy resources. In addition, the impact of Channel State Information (CSI) on resource allocation methods is analysed. Methods: The hybrid multiple access schemes are introduced to minimise the sum power in the NOMA-UAV uplink network, subject to minimum data rate and available resource constraints. The frequency sub-bands and transmission power are jointly optimised to decrease the impact of error propagation in the SIC receiver via three hybrid multiple access models, including (i) a hybrid NOMA and OMA scheme with user grouping on multi-NOMA sub-bands, (ii) a hybrid NOMA and OMA scheme with one NOMA sub-band, and (iii) a multi-NOMA sub-bands scheme. title: Automated Detection of Roadway Obstructions to Assess Vehicle Accessibility Using Aerial and Reference Images
abstract: Abstract In the aftermath of natural disasters, roadway obstructions can hinder access to impacted communities, which can severely impact emergency response and evacuation efforts. Traditional ground-based and aerial reconnaissance methods for obstruction detection are often limited by cost, accessibility, and efficiency. This study introduces a novel framework that compares postdisaster unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) images with predisaster satellite images to detect and segment roadway obstructions and estimate remaining accessible road width to provide emergency managers with updated status of roadway networks. The approach uses the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) algorithm to segment aerial roadways, and then these are compared with predisaster reference images at the same location to identify changes in road conditions, notably reducing false positive results and enhancing detection accuracy. Due to a dearth of availability in training data for UAV-based aerial images of obstructions on roadways, synthetic data are generated through data augmentation techniques to bolster model performance. The developed framework achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 98.5% (mAP 50), which evaluates detection accuracy at an Intersection Over Union (IoU) threshold of 0.5, and 91.2% (mAP 50–95). title: The Pass-Through of Retail Crime
abstract: This paper shows retailers increase prices in response to organized retail crime. We match store-level crime data to scanner data from the universe of transactions for cannabis retailers in Washington state. Using quasi-experimental variation from robberies and burglaries, we find a 1.7–1.8 percent price increase at victimized stores and nearby competitors. This rise is not driven by short-to-medium-term demand changes but is consistent with crime-related cost shocks. Effects are larger for independent stores and less concentrated markets. We estimate crime imposes a 1 percent “hidden” unit tax on affected stores, implying $30.7 million in additional social costs, primarily borne by consumers. (JEL D22, H22, H76, K42, L81)

title: Strategic Development Framework for Strengthening Small Retail Competitiveness in a Provincial Philippine Economy
abstract: Strategic management practices are important mechanisms through which small retailers strengthen competitiveness in resource-constrained and highly localized markets. This study examined the relationship between strategic management practices and competitive advantage among small retailers in a provincial Philippine economy, particularly in Nueva Ecija. Specifically, it assessed the level of strategic management practices in terms of environmental scanning, strategy formulation, strategy implementation, and strategy evaluation, and determined the level of competitive advantage in terms of cost efficiency, differentiation, market responsiveness, and digital integration. The study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational design using survey data from 150 small retail business owners and managers. Findings show that small retailers demonstrated a high level of strategic management practices, with strategy formulation receiving the highest rating and strategy evaluation receiving the lowest. The respondents also exhibited a high level of competitive advantage, particularly in differentiation through customer relationships and service quality, while digital integration remained the weakest area. abstract: Abstract Underground pipelines play a vital role in urban operation and development, and the rapid and accurate detection of their distribution remains an urgent challenge. Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) technology has been widely adopted for underground pipeline detection. Therefore, there is currently a need for an automated solution to detect pipeline categories and measure burial depth and diameter using GPR. This study proposes an automatic recognition method of category, burial depth, and diameter for underground pipeline using GPR based on you only look once (YOLO) v12 and a machine learning algorithm. The method operates through three sequential phases. In the first phase, a well-trained YOLOv12 model detects pipeline signal regions and categories in GPR B-scan images, where the model achieves average precision (AP) scores of 0.649 for plastic–water category, 0.654 for electric-cable category, 0.755 for plastic–gas category, and 0.737 for steel–water category, with a mean average precision of 0.699 at intersection over union thresholds from 0.5 to 0.95 with a step size of 0.05. Predicting High-Risk Conflicts on Highways Using Hybrid Deep Learning Resampling and Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Abstract Accurately predicting high-risk conflicts on highways is essential yet challenging due to complex traffic maneuvering under heterogeneous conditions. This challenge is further complicated in real-world data by the prevalence of non-high-risk conflicts relative to high-risk conflicts, resulting in an extremely imbalanced dataset. To address this challenge, the present study developed three machine-learning algorithms with six resampling techniques, including a novel deep learning framework that integrates conditional tabular generative adversarial network (CTGAN)–based synthetic data generation with strategic undersampling. High-risk conflicts were identified using the surrogate safety measure modified time to collision ( MTTC < 1 s ). Spatiotemporal traffic variables (i.e., traffic density, traffic flow, standard deviation in speed and acceleration, lane change frequency, etc.) were extracted for the 5-s window prior to each conflict within a two-dimensional influence zone using high-resolution trajectory data. Results show that the random forest model outperformed others when trained on CTGAN-synthesized data combined with random undersampling (RU). This hybrid approach improved sensitivity by 30% and increased the G -mean by 11% compared to the original imbalanced dataset, validating the proposed data-balancing approach. title: From Rainfall to Absolute Landslide Probability: A Machine Learning–Based Approach
abstract: Abstract Landslides are prevalent geological hazards in mountainous and hilly regions, posing significant threats to human lives, property, and infrastructure, especially when external factors such as heavy rainfall elevate the risk of occurrence. In recent years, the rapid development of remote sensing technology, geographic information system, and big data analytics has enabled the establishment of landslide databases and the refinement of landslide hazard assessment methodologies, opening new avenues for disaster prediction and prevention research. This study focuses on the probabilistic hazard assessment of rainfall-induced landslides, using the heavy rainfall event in Nanping City, Fujian, in 2019 as a case study. The absolute probability of landslide occurrence was quantified by integrating machine learning models with Bayesian probability theory. To analyze their contributions to landslide hazard, the study comprehensively considered nine key factors: elevation, slope angle, slope aspect, topographic wetness index, fault distance, rainfall amount, topographic position index, land cover, and stratum. The findings reveal that rainfall intensity is the primary trigger for landslides. Bidding Strategy of Pumped Storage Power Plants Considering Seasonal Characteristics in Integrated Electricity Spot Markets
abstract: [Objective] The large-scale integration of high-proportion renewable energy into power systems has intensified seasonal variations in system net load. The joint clearing mechanism of the electricity spot energy market and ancillary service market further exacerbates market uncertainty， imposing substantial tail risks on the bidding decision-making of pumped storage power plants. To address this issue， this paper proposes a bidding framework for pumped storage power plants that adapts to multi-seasonal operational scenarios and fully considers market risk constraints. [Methods] First， three typical seasonal scenarios， including the spring-autumn transition season， summer， and winter， are classified based on the evolutionary characteristics of system net load. Second， a novel seasonal joint strategy index is constructed by integrating the arbitrage space characterized by the net load peak-valley difference and the tail risk characteristics of operational revenue. A 15-minute resolution bi-level bidding model is established for pumped storage power plants participating in the integrated spot market. title: How renewable energy integration reshapes smart grid cybersecurity: challenges and future directions
abstract: The rapid transition toward renewable-rich smart grids has fundamentally transformed modern power systems by driving the evolution of conventional centralized electricity networks toward more distributed, digitally coordinated, and communication-dependent cyber-physical infrastructures. The widespread deployment of renewable and distributed-energy technologies and coordination platforms, including photovoltaic (PV) systems, wind energy systems, battery energy storage systems (BESS), electric vehicles (EVs) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) infrastructures, microgrids, and virtual power plants (VPPs), has significantly increased the decentralization, flexibility, and digital connectivity of modern power systems. However, this digital transformation has simultaneously expanded the cyberattack surface of power systems by introducing extensive communication networks, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, cloud platforms, advanced control systems, and distributed automation technologies, creating new cybersecurity challenges that differ substantially from those encountered in conventional power grids. This paper presents a comprehensive review of how renewable energy integration reshapes smart grid cybersecurity by examining the evolution of modern power systems, the expansion of cyberattack surfaces, and the emerging vulnerabilities associated with renewable energy technologies. The review ana…

title: Outcomes Associated With Postoperative Dexamethasone Use After Adult Spinal Deformity Surgery
abstract: Objective: Dexamethasone is commonly prescribed following adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery; however, dexamethasone’s immunosuppressive effects on clinical outcomes in ASD surgery remain unclear. This study sought to: assess the effects of postoperative dexamethasone after ASD surgery, and evaluate the potential association between postoperative dexamethasone and complications.Methods: This TriNetX study identified adults who underwent ASD surgery from 2009–2024. Outcomes were explored at 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year time points among patients with any systemic dexamethasone exposure within 7 days of surgery. Primary outcomes included wound infection, sepsis, and perioperative hematoma. Secondary outcomes included respiratory failure, delirium, new-onset diabetes, and in-hospital mortality. Propensity score matching (PSM) and logistic regression assessed associations.Results: After PSM, 42,472 patients were included in both the dexamethasone and control cohorts. At 30 days, dexamethasone exposure was associated with higher odds of wound infection. At 90 days, these associations included elevated risks for wound infection, respiratory failure, delirium, and sepsis. By 1 year, dexamethasone use remained significantly associated with wound infection, delirium, and respiratory failure, however, hospital-recorded mortality was lower in the dexamethasone cohort.Conclusion: In this l…

title: Recovery, Healing, and Social Accountability in Medical Education: Rebuilding Learning Communities and Professional Leadership
abstract: Medical education in Korea has recently experienced an unprecedented period of social conflict and educational disruption. The prolonged interruption of students’ education, extensive changes to curricula, diminished trust between the medical profession and society, and strained relationships among students, residents, and faculty have prompted fundamental questions about the mission and responsibilities of medical education. This paper examines two questions arising from the 2024 medical crisis: how medical schools can restore damaged relationships and how they can redefine their educational and social responsibilities. This paper draws on major educational theories—including transformative learning, experiential learning, professional identity formation, psychological safety, communities of practice, and social accountability—to propose a framework for rebuilding medical education around recovery. It combines theoretical perspectives with institutional experiences of students’ return to medical school and sets out practical strategies, including recovery-oriented curriculum design, ref lective learning, mentoring, psychologically safe learning environments, reconstruction of learning communities, and strengthened education for social accountability. The central challenge for medical education after the crisis is to go beyond restoring educational operations and rebuild trust,…

title: Inequality Metrics as Early Warning Indicators of Bitcoin Market Instability
abstract: Existing Bitcoin price prediction systems mainly rely on traditional statistical models or basic financial indicators, which often fail to capture complex market patterns and the highly volatile nature of cryptocurrency markets. Many machine learning models use only historical price values and do not integrate statistical inequality measures such as the Lorenz Curve, Gini Index, or K-Value, which can provide insights into market distribution and stability. To overcome these limitations, the proposed system analysis historical Bitcoin price data from 2010 to 2021, including the open, high, low, and closing prices. The proposed framework incorporates the Lorenz Curve, Gini Index, and K-Value along with financial data, and a linear regression model is applied for time-series forecasting. The proposed model showed improvements of 1.46%, 6.87%, and 0.07% in RMSE, MAE, and MAPE, respectively, over the baseline. The results indicate that integrating inequality-based features improved prediction reliability and provided a better understanding of market behaviour.

title: AGRICULTURAL CROP-RESIDUE WASTE CONVERTED INTO ELECTRICITY IN INDIA
abstract: The importance of adopting a “waste-to-wealth” approach lies in reusing waste as a valuable resource rather than an economic burden and environmental issue. India’s agricultural residues have the potential to generate over 18,000 MW of power annually. Biogas plants are a progressive step taken by the Government of India to curb crop burning to prevent pollution. In India, as agriculture plays a pivotal role in ensuring food and nutritional security, it also generates significant waste during cultivation, harvesting, and processing. Agricultural waste is generated throughout the journey from farm to food plate. Inadequate management of agricultural waste has become a substantial source of environmental contamination affecting air, soil, and water. Agricultural waste management in India presents both significant challenges and opportunities. Traditional practices, particularly crop residue burning, although ingrained, are often unsustainable and environmentally damaging. Residue burning leads to the depletion of soil nutrients, degradation of soil health, and the emission of greenhouse gases. The implementation of advanced waste valorization methods, like thermochemical and biochemical processes, can transform agricultural waste into valuable products, contributing to the circular economy and sustainable development. Various agricultural wastes are generated in large amounts with…

title: Single-Stock Leveraged ETFs and Underlying-Market Quality: Evidence from Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix
abstract: We study changes in underlying-market quality around Korea's May 2026 introduction of single-stock leveraged ETFs, using Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix as a case study. These were the first eligible underlying stocks. We find little evidence of persistent abnormal returns, but volatility and downside risk are significantly higher for both stocks in the post-listing window. Liquidity improves for SK Hynix but not clearly for Samsung Electronics. Investor-specific net buying changes little, whereas trading participation shifts across groups. Margin balances rise, new margin trading falls, and securities-lending balances decline, indicating changes in conventional leverage activity. Earlier Hong Kong listings provide supplementary evidence that responses vary across firms and venues. Overall, volatility is the most consistent post-listing change across the two stocks. Other dimensions of the trading environment, including liquidity, investor participation, and conventional leverage activity, also change around the listings, although these changes are heterogeneous and need not represent independent ETF-specific channels.

abstract: Urban solid waste management is a major environmental challenge, particularly in markets where commercial activities generate substantial quantities of organic and non-biodegradable waste. This study aimed to characterize market biowaste generated in the urban municipality of Diffa, Niger, and to preliminarily assess its suitability for composting. The study was conducted in the central, vegetable, and fish markets using a stratified sampling approach. Waste generation was monitored through daily weighing, while representative samples of 100 kg from each market were characterized according to waste category, particle-size distribution, apparent bulk density, moisture content, and volatile organic matter. The results showed substantial differences in waste generation among the three markets. The overall mean generation rate was 3.32 ± 2.37 kg/trader/day, with the highest mean rates recorded at the vegetable market (4.32 ± 3.43 kg/trader/day) and fish market (4.07 ± 3.59 kg/trader/day), whereas the central market recorded the lowest rate (1.57 ± 0.09 kg/trader/day). Organic waste was the dominant fraction in the vegetable and central markets, whereas plastic waste predominated in the fish market. title: The Impact of Market Power and Market Concentration in Shaping the Stability of Islamic Banking in Indonesia
abstract: Introduction/Main Objectives: The increasingly concentrated market structure in Indonesia’s Islamic banking industry following the 2021 merger of Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) raises critical questions regarding the relationship between market structure and bank financial stability. Novelty: This study examines market concentration, measured by the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI), and individual bank market power, measured by the Lerner Index, in relation to the stability of Islamic banking in Indonesia over the 2019–2024 period. Research Methods: Using an unbalanced panel dataset of Islamic banking institutions in Indonesia, this study employs panel regression analysis to examine the relationships between HHI, the Lerner Index, and banking stability, measured by the Z-score. The appropriate panel estimation model is determined through model selection tests. Finding/Results: The results show that market concentration has a positive but statistically insignificant relationship with the Z-score, whereas market power has a negative but statistically insignificant relationship with the Z-score. Thus, neither variable provides statistically significant evidence of an association with Islamic banking stability under the estimated model. Conclusion: The findings provide inconclusive evidence regarding the relationship between market structure and Islamic banking stability in Indonesia…

title: Changes in K-Beauty Export Structure and Industry Case Studies, 2021–2025: Focusing on Market Diversification and Directions for Industrial Advancement
abstract: This study examines changes in the K-Beauty export structure from 2021 to 2025 and explores directions for industrial advancement through market diversification and selected industry cases. The study combines a review of previous research, trend and comparative analysis of official export statistics, market-concentration analysis using the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI), CR3, and CR5, and industry case analysis. The results show that Korean cosmetics exports reached USD 11.42 billion in 2025. China’s share of Korean cosmetics exports declined from 53.2% in 2021 to 17.7% in 2025, while the U.S. share increased from 9.2% to 19.1%. The United States became the largest export market, while Japan maintained a relatively stable share. Over the same period, the HHI declined from 3,058.8 to 892.2, while CR3 and CR5 also decreased, indicating a marked reduction in export-market concentration and a broader distribution of export destinations. Makeup and basic cosmetics remained the dominant export category, although growth was also observed in other product categories. Industry cases showed emerging forms of overseas distribution and brand deployment, as well as business expansion into beauty-tech. These cases are interpreted as illustrative examples rather than as evidence representative of the entire K-Beauty industry. Regulatory compliance, brand protection, sustainability, and incl…

A Web-Based Farmer-Buyer Partnership System for Direct Agricultural Market Connectivity
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in the Indian economy and provides livelihood opportunities for a large rural population. However, farmers often face difficulties in finding suitable buyers, accessing market information, communicating product availability, and managing agricultural sales. Traditional agricultural marketing systems may involve multiple intermediaries, resulting in limited direct interaction between farmers and buyers. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Farmer– Buyer Partnership System, a web-based platform that provides a digital connection between farmers and buyers. The proposed system enables farmers to register, create profiles, list agricultural products, specify available quantities and expected prices, and manage buyer requests. Buyers can register, search and view available agricultural products, access relevant farmer and product information, and submit partnership requests. An administrator manages users, products, and partnership activities through a centralized system. The proposed application is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend, Python Flask for the backend, and MySQL for database management. The system follows a structured approach to improve product visibility, communication, request tracking, and information accessibility. title: AgriChain: A Farmer-to-Market Intelligence Platform Integrating Satellite Imagery, Deep Learning, and Market Analytics for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Smallholder farmers in developing agricultural economies continue to face significant losses arising from delayed detection of crop stress, undiagnosed plant diseases, and volatile, opaque market pricing. This paper presents AgriChain, an endto-end farmer-to-market intelligence platform that unifies remote-sensing analytics, deep-learning-based disease diagnosis, and data-driven market forecasting within a single accessible interface. The system ingests multispectral Sentinel-2 imagery through the Google Earth Engine API to compute the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) for continuous crop-health monitoring, while a convolutional neural network trained on annotated leaf-image datasets performs on-demand disease classification from farmer-submitted photographs. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network forecasts short-term commodity prices from historical mandi (market) records, and a rule-augmented recommendation engine fuses the outputs of these three subsystems to generate actionable, field-specific guidance covering irrigation scheduling, treatment recommendations, and optimal selling windows. The platform is implemented using a React.js frontend, a Node.js/Express backend, and a PostgreSQL/PostGIS spatial database.
