abstract: Abstract The limited distribution of suitable salt caverns has stimulated interest in depleted hydrocarbon reservoirs as alternative geological media for large-scale underground compressed air energy storage (CAES). Depleted shale gas reservoirs may offer connected fracture networks for rapid air injection and withdrawal and adjacent matrix pores for additional storage, while their relatively limited mobile water may reduce the gas–water displacement losses encountered in conventional water-driven reservoirs. However, black shale contains organic matter and reduced minerals that can react with injected O2 and deplete oxygen from stored air. This process is particularly important for fuel-assisted CAES because the recovered air serves as both the expansion working fluid and the oxidant for fuel combustion. Oxygen–shale interactions in Longmaxi Formation shale were investigated using scanning electron microscopy, repeated electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) mapping, and high-pressure batch experiments under different temperatures, moisture conditions, and successive air-exposure cycles. Organic matter and Fe(II)-bearing minerals, including framboidal pyrite and ferroan dolomite, were identified as widely dispersed, potentially oxygen-reactive constituents. title: BEYOND MICROCREDIT: SELF-HELP GROUPS, SOCIAL PARTICIPATION AND PUBLIC VOICE AMONG WOMEN IN RURAL INDIA
abstract: Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are widely recognised as mechanisms for financial inclusion and livelihood support; however, their contribution to women’s social participation and public voice remains equally important. This study examines the association between SHG membership and changes in community interaction, participation in local governance and public-speaking confidence among women in Ananthapuramu district, Andhra Pradesh. A multi-stage random sampling design was used to select 320 SHG members, comprising 160 Muslim minority and 160 non-minority women across five revenue divisions. Primary data were collected through a structured interview schedule, and changes associated with SHG membership were analysed using frequencies, percentages and chi-square tests. The findings indicate substantial improvement in women’s social engagement following SHG membership. Frequent community interaction increased markedly, while non-participation in Gram Sabha and Panchayat meetings declined in both groups and active participation increased. Public expression also strengthened, with 79.06% of respondents reporting moderate or significant improvement in public-speaking confidence. Overall, the findings suggest that SHGs extend beyond their conventional microcredit function by providing collective spaces that facilitate social interaction, civic participation and confidence in public expression…

title: Perceived Barriers and Opportunities for Rural Women’s Participation in Agricultural Extension Activities in Afgoi District, Somalia
abstract: Agricultural extension services can improve farming knowledge and rural livelihoods, but access may be constrained by financial, institutional, and information barriers. This descriptive quantitative study summarizes the perceptions of 80 agricultural stakeholders in Afgoi District, Somalia. Responses were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, and five-point Likert mean scores. Limited access to agricultural information (M = 4.05), training (M = 4.03), and modern farming techniques (M = 3.94) were rated as challenges. Lack of financial support (M = 4.19) and limited access to inputs (M = 4.18) were perceived as major economic constraints. Program availability (M = 3.44) and government support (M = 3.38) received comparatively lower ratings. Proposed improvements included agricultural credit (M = 4.35), technologies and inputs (M = 4.33), extension services (M = 4.30), and training (M = 4.28). The results reflect the views of a mixed-gender stakeholder sample rather than measurements of women’s actual participation or effects of interventions. Documented reliability testing of the questionnaire was not available, and the findings are descriptive and limited to Afgoi District.

FOAM STABILITY AS A QUALITY PARAMETER FOR HERBAL SURFACE CLEANERS: CORRELATION WITH CONCENTRATION AND STORAGE CONDITIONS
abstract: Foam stability-an essential quality indicator of liquid cleaning products not just in terms of a consumer feel for performance, but as an indicator of cleaning efficacy. This study focused on investigating the foam stability of neem- Azadirachta indica and lemon- Citrus limon based herbal surface cleaners at concentrations of 3%, 4%, 5%, 6% and 7% and storage temperatures 25C, 30C and 45C for 4 weeks duration with effect on foam stability monitored and evaluated weekly by test tube dilution method. All of the formulations that tested positively (stable foam above liquid level) yielded positive initial foam test-signifying the presence of triterpenic glycosides (saponins). As the duration of storage extended the rate of foam stability reduced for all of the formulations and more than anything the effect of temperature showed a significantly high influence on degradation (p<0.001) The most sensitive test was the one at 45C where foam test became negative (full collapse of foam) with 3% at week 4, whereas the most concentrated product of 7% was most resistant to complete foam collapse.

abstract: The purpose of the study is to evaluate the impact of community participation on solid waste management in Rwanda, a case of AGRUNI Company in Rwamagana District (2021-2025)”. Research design to be used was descriptive and explanatory research design. The study used the population of 12,008 people and the sample size of 388 clients of AGRUNI Company. Questionnaire, interview were used to collect primary data and documentary review was used to collect secondary data. Descriptive statistics and inferential statistics were used to analyse data with a help of SPSS version 26. The study found that community participation significantly influences solid waste management practices in Rwamagana District, with decision-making and monitoring being the strongest predictor (B = 0.659, p = 0.000), followed by clean-up activities (B = 0.100, p = 0.000) and communication (B = 0.081, p = 0.000), while awareness and environmental education was not significant (B = 0.020, p = 0.203). Secondary data show high waste generation of 36 MT per month, only one dumping site, 324 waste bins, and low collection coverage of 40%. Transportation challenges and poor rural recycling systems further reduce efficiency, despite 80% biodegradable waste and 20% recycled materials. Regression results clearly indicate a significant positive relationship between community participation and waste management performance.…

title: Performance Evaluation Procedures for Fire Extinguishing Agents and Devices in Small-Scale Lithium-Ion Battery Fires
abstract: Small-scale lithium-ion battery fires involve thermal runaway, propagation to adjacent cells, and possible re-ignition; therefore, flame suppression alone does not adequately reflect the extinguishing performance. This study reviewed the major test elements of KFI 630 and NTA 8133 and proposed an improved procedure based on fire and extinguishing tests using small-scale pouch-type lithium-ion batteries. In the free-burn tests, thermal runaway propagated through the five-cell test specimen within approximately 60-120 s, whereas the suppression tests showed different cell temperature histories and subsequent thermal runaway propagation behaviors depending on the extinguishing agent. The proposed revision maintains the KFI test configuration, heating method, and one-hour reignition observation period, while additionally recording the cell-by-cell thermal runaway timing, flame extinguishment time, and actual agent consumption. Additionally, a supplementary procedure is also proposed to evaluate the thermal stabilization and thermal runaway propagation delay using cell-temperature histories, cooling performance, propagation time, and the total number of cells undergoing thermal runaway. Further replication is required to establish the reproducibility and quantitative acceptance criteria for these proposed indicators.

title: Fine-Tuning Universal Machine Learning Potentials Enables Efficient Computation of Li Electrode Potentials in Battery Electrolytes
abstract: Abstract The electrode potential of Li metal is fundamental to the performance and stability of Li-metal batteries, yet its accurate prediction across diverse electrolyte chemistries remains a challenge. Standard quantum chemistry using cluster models fails to account for explicit bulk solvation, while ab initio molecular dynamics is restricted by the high computational cost of thermodynamic sampling. In this work, we present an integrated framework that combines a universal machine learning potential for electrolytes with a data-efficient fine-tuning strategy to compute Li electrode potentials. This workflow achieves ab initio level accuracy using ∼200 extra density functional theory calculations per electrolyte system. Furthermore, the identified relationship between local Li+ solvation environments and electrode potential shifts provides mechanistic insights into electrolyte-dependent redox behavior and offers guidance for rational electrolyte design.

title: DATA AS A FINANCIAL ASSET: HOW FINTECH COMPANIES USE CONSUMER BEHAVIOUR DATA FOR PERSONALISATION, RETENTION, AND REVENUE GROWTH
abstract: This study examines how FinTech companies transform consumer behaviour data into financial value through artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and hyper - personalisation. It explores how transactional, behavioural, and demographic data are collected, analysed,and converted into personalised financial products, recommendations, interfaces, and communication strategies. The study further evaluates how these practices influence customer retention, customer lifetime value, return on investment, average revenue per user, customer acquisition cost, and churn. Particular attention is given to machine learning, customer segmentation, recommendation systems, and predictive models used to anticipate consumer needs and improve engagement. The paper also considers the strategic role of data in product development, cross-selling, and marketing optimization. Alongside these benefits, it critically examines privacy, consent, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, and regulatory compliance. The study concludes that AI-driven personalisation can create substantial commercial value in FinTech, but sustainable growth depends on transparent, secure, fair, and responsible use of consumer data over the long term.

title: Simulation of a PV-Integrated Dual Active Bridge Converter for EV Charging
abstract: The increasing use of renewable energy and electric vehicles (EVs) has created a growing need for efficient powerelectronic interfaces that can integrate solar energy with high-voltage battery-charging systems. This work presents the design and MATLAB/Simulink analysis of an approximately 11.56 kW photovoltaic (PV)-fed Dual Active Bridge (DAB) DC-DC converter for isolated and controllable power transfer in EV battery-charging applications. The PV array consists of 33 modules rated at approximately 350 W each, configured as 11 series-connected modules per string and three parallel strings, providing approximately 423.5 V and 27.3 A at the maximum power point. The DAB converter employs two active full bridges coupled through an 11 kVA, 50 kHz high-frequency transformer with 419/409 V windings and a 29 µH series transfer inductor. A 220 µF DC-link capacitor is connected at the output. Power transfer is controlled using single-phase-shift (SPS) modulation, where both bridges operate at approximately 50% duty cycle and the relative phase angle between their switching signals determines the transferred power. For closed-loop control, the measured DC output voltage is compared with a predefined reference, and the resulting error is processed by a PI controller to generate the required phase-shift command. title: Tuning Moving Vehicle Suspensions for Vibration Mitigation of Damped Bridges
abstract: It has been widely recognized that traversing vehicles can dampen bridge vibrations. This work clarifies the efficacy of different vehicle suspension tuning approaches for bridge vibration mitigation using an equivalent tuned mass damper (TMD) model and presents a parametric analysis of the key physical factors governing vehicle-bridge interaction. The vehicle-bridge system is modelled as a TMD traveling on an elastically supported beam. A finite element model is developed to numerically validate the analytical model. Transmissibility functions, obtained using the time-freezing technique, and complex eigenvalue loci are employed in the tuning process. For an undamped bridge, the optimal stiffness and damping ratio of the vehicle suspension are obtained from an extended fixed-point principle, under which the analytical model is equivalent to a smooth bridge coupled to a TMD and subjected to a harmonic transverse excitation at the contact point. For a damped bridge, the optimal vehicle suspension parameters are determined from the intersection of the eigenvalue loci of the system. Vehicle damping can induce curve veering of the instantaneous coupled eigenvalues during the vehicle passage, and this phenomenon is further examined through a perturbation analysis. In the parametric analysis, the root-mean-square values of the kinetic and potential energy of the bridge are used to qua…

title: OPTIMIZATION OF MIXED VEHICLE-DRONE ROUTING WITH TIME WINDOWS FOR LAST-MILE DELIVERY
abstract: The growth of e-commerce and the demand for ever shorter delivery lead times put considerable pressure on last-mile logistics operators. This article proposes a unified mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for mixed vehicle-drone routing with time windows (VRPTW-D). A conventional vehicle may, at each of its stops, launch a drone that serves a customer on its own and is then recovered by the vehicle, either at the same stop or at a later stop. The compact formulation relies on ternary flight variables, continuous time variables and an exact linearization of the vehicle-drone synchronization; it embeds valid inequalities (Dantzig - Fulkerson - Johnson subtour elimination and use - flow linking) that strengthen the continuous relaxation. For larger instances, we develop an ALNS (Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search) heuristic calibrated against the exact solutions. The exact model proves optimality on small instances (n - 10) and, beyond, provides feasible solutions together with bounds; the ALNS is the practical solution method for large instances. A reproducible instance set, generated in the style of Solomon (classes C1, R1 and RC1) with an extension of the time windows to drones, allows us to measure precisely the contribution of the drones, the value of the relaxation and the comparative performance of the exact model and the ALNS, complemented by a sensitivity analys…

title: Edge AI-Based Vehicle Surveillance System
abstract: Urban vehicle numbers have grown far faster than the capacity of traffic police to watch every intersection and parking lane, and the result is a steady stream of hit-and-run incidents, wrong-parking, and double-parking cases that pass unrecorded under conventional patrol- and CCTV-based enforcement. This paper describes an Edge AI vehicle-surveillance pipeline built to close that gap while running entirely on low-cost, offline-capable hardware — a laptop or a Raspberry Pi — with no cloud backend and no purpose-built sensors. Vehicles are localised and classified frame by frame with YOLOv8, and a DeepSORT tracker then follows each detected vehicle through the sequence so that its position can be monitored continuously. A collision is inferred when two tracked bounding boxes overlap sharply, measured through Intersection over Union, together with an abrupt motion change captured by Lucas–Kanade optical flow; if the vehicle involved does not remain at the scene within a five-second grace period, the event is recorded as a hit-and-run. Separately, restricted-zone polygons combined with a configurable stay-duration check are used to catch vehicles parked illegally or blocking a live lane. title: A TWO-PHASE DECOMPOSITION HEURISTIC VERSUS A HYBRID GENETIC ALGORITHM FOR SOLVING A MULTI-PRODUCT, MULTI-COMPARTMENT VEHICLE ROUTING PROBLEM WITH SIMULTANEOUS PICKUP AND DELIVERY AND TIME WINDOWS FOR THE TRANSPORT OF PERISHABLE PRODUCTS
abstract: We compare two approximate methods for solving the MPMC-VRPSPDTW, a vehicle routing problem for the transport of perishable products. The problem combines the following features: multiple products, multiple compartments, simultaneous pickup and delivery, time windows and a product degradation that depends on the road category. A single objective function minimizes the transport cost and the opportunity cost due to the loss of economic value of the products. The first solution method is a two-phase decomposition heuristic (TPDH) that works as follows: nearest-neighbour clustering of customers, then inter-route local search. The second is a hybrid genetic algorithm (GA) whose initial population is built from a feasible solution provided by an insertion heuristic inspired by Solomons I1. On 45 configurations derived from Solomons instances C101, R104 and RC107, the hybrid GA obtains a lower cost in 34 configurations and reduces the mean cost by 5.1% and the mean number of vehicles by 25.8%. Its mean run time is 1.5 times that of the TPDH (497 s vs 339 s).

title: OpenTyreF1: A Data-Driven Mobile Platform for Formula 1 Telemetry Analysis, Tyre-Degradation Modelling and Counterfactual Race-Strategy Simulation
abstract: Formula 1 publishes one of the richest open telemetry streams in professional sport, yet most public tools built on it are descriptive: they show what happened and stop there. This paper presents OpenTyreF1, a full-stack system that turns that data into decision support on a mobile phone. The system integrates three public sources (Jolpica-F1/Ergast, OpenF1 and FastF1) into one normalised 15-table relational corpus of 237,308 records covering 492 races from 2002 to 2026. On top of this corpusit builds a shared clean-lap filter, a gradient-boosted (XGBoost) lap-time model, a counterfactual stint-strategy simulator, a 1,500-run Monte Carlo outcome estimator, seven pit-wall decision modules and a grounded question-answering assistant, all served by a FastAPI backend to an Expo/React Native app. Evaluated on 12 completely unseen races, the model achieves a mean absolute error of 0.893 s, RMSE of 1.205 s and R 2 of 0.978, beating the strongest naive baseline by 0.270 s. An ablation shows that predicting a lap’s offset from its race median, rather than the absolute lap time, cuts error four-fold, a far larger effect than adding features. The results show that, for motorsport data of this size, careful lap admission, target design and leakage-free evaluation matter more than the choice of learner.

title: Effectiveness of Cognitive Conflict Strategy in Improving Conceptual Understanding of Evolution among Senior Secondary School Students in Zamfara State, Nigeria
abstract: Misconceptions about evolution can impede students’ understanding of natural selection, adaptation, genetic variation and evolutionary relationships. This study compared students’ conceptual understanding of evolution after instruction using the Cognitive Conflict Strategy (CCS) and conventional method. It also examined gender differences among students exposed to CCS. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control-group design involved 283 SS II Biology students from public secondary schools in Zamfara State, Nigeria. Data were collected using an adapted 30-item, two-tier Evolutionary Misconception Test (KR-20 = 0.84) and analysed using descriptive statistics and ANCOVA at the 0.05 significance level. The study revealed that students taught using CCS recorded a higher mean gain (12.86) than those taught using the conventional method (6.71). ANCOVA showed a statistically significant difference between the two groups, F(1, 280) = 71.47, p < .001, partial η² = .203. However, no statistically significant gender difference was found among students taught using CCS, F(1, 143) = 0.48, p = .490, partial η² = .003. The study concluded that CCS improve students’ conceptual understanding of evolution. It is recommended that Biology teachers incorporate CCS into evolution lessons to help students identify, examine and correct misconceptions.

title: Artificial Intelligence’s Transformative Impact on Management, Strategy, and Workplace Dynamics: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into organizations is reshaping management practice, competitive strategy, and the experience of work, yet scholarship remains fragmented across disciplines and is predominantly Western-centric. This systematic literature review synthesizes interdisciplinary evidence on how AI transforms leadership and management functions, drives business model innovation, and alters workplace dynamics, with particular attention to Southeast Asian and Philippine contexts. Peer-reviewed, English-language journal articles published between 2016 and 2025 addressing the organizational, strategic, or workforce implications of AI were included; purely technical studies and non-peer-reviewed materials were excluded from the corpus, with institutional reports used only for contextualization. Scopus, Web of Science, ABI/INFORM, Business Source Complete, and the ACM Digital Library were searched. Screening followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines: 1,245 records were identified, and 128 studies met all inclusion criteria and were synthesized thematically. First, AI integration facilitates an augmented leadership model in which effective managers combine human judgment with algorithmic capability. abstract: Implementation of Green Tourism Governance in Tojo Una-Una Regency: Policy, Governance, and Ecosystem Sustainability Analysis The purpose of this study is to analyze the implementation of green tourism governance in Tojo Una-Una Regency, identify the factors that influence the application of green governance in sustainable tourism, and formulate optimal development strategies based on SWOT analysis and the internal and external conditions of the region. This study uses a qualitative approach with a descriptive-analytical design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 24 informants from various stakeholders (government, local communities, business actors, academics/NGOs), participatory observation, and Focus Group Discussions (FGD). Data analysis was conducted using the Miles and Huberman interactive model, complemented by SWOT analysis, the Internal Factor Analysis Summary (IFAS), and the External Factor Analysis Summary (EFAS). This research was carried out in Tojo Una-Una Regency, specifically in the Togean Islands, during January-June 2024.The findings show that the implementation of green tourism governance in Tojo Una-Una Regency has made significant progress with Regional Regulation No. 7/2013 regarding RIPPARDA, which regulates sustainable tourism. abstract: This study aims to analyze digital transformation strategies in improving public service efficiency through the implementation of smart governance in Tojo Una-Una Regency, as well as to determine the strategic position and recommend strategies that can be implemented to address the geographical challenges of an archipelagic region in government digitalization. The research uses a descriptive analytical qualitative approach with purposive sampling of 25 informants, including local government officials, civil servants, academics, community members, and the private sector. Data was collected through in-depth interviews, participatory observation, document studies, and focus group discussions during the 2024-2025 period. Data analysis was conducted using the Miles-Huberman-Saldana model with eight research dimensions, reinforced by quantitative SWOT analysis through IFAS and EFAS to determine the organization's strategic position. Research results show that digital transformation in Tojo Una-Una has made significant progress with the SPBE score increasing from 2.13 to 3.06, the construction of 84 BTS towers, and the implementation of various digital innovations such as AKSI-BPKAD. However, there are still challenges with uneven infrastructure, human resource competency gaps, and organizational culture resistance. title: Impact of NCS-Based Retail Training in Beauty Retail Companies on Sales Employees’ Job Satisfaction and Sales Performance
abstract: With the rapid growth of K-beauty, the number of sales employees in domestic and international beauty retail companies in Korea has expanded accordingly. However, compared to the quantitative expansion of companies, field-oriented job training for sales employees remains insufficient. This study aimed to design and validate an educational program for beauty retail companies based on the National Competency Standards(NCS). An online survey was conducted over one month, from July to August, with 248 sales employees of a beauty retail company. Using SPSS 21.0, EFA was performed, and CFA with AMOS 21.0 was conducted to assess reliability and validity. Hypotheses were tested through regression analysis, and mediating effects were examined using bootstrap and multiple regression. The empirical results confirmed three findings: First, NCS-based beauty retail training positively influenced job satisfaction; second, job satisfaction significantly affected sales performance; and lastly, job satisfaction played a partial mediating role. Moreover, NCS-based beauty retail training impacted sales performance both directly and indirectly, with sales-oriented training showing the strongest effect. This study highlights that strengthening field-based competencies is a key factor in enhancing training effectiveness and suggests that practical competency development directly linked to sales activ…

title: The Influence of Membership Programs and Application Ease of Use on Consumer Purchasing Decisions in Modern Retail
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of membership programs and application ease of use on consumer purchasing decisions in modern retail. The subjects of this study were consumers using the membership application at Indomaret in Tangerang. A quantitative approach was employed using purposive sampling with 100 respondents. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares (PLS) with SmartPLS version 4.1.1.8. The results indicate that, partially, the membership program does not have a significant effect on consumer purchasing decisions, while application ease of use has a positive and significant effect. These findings indicate that although membership provides various benefits, consumers may consider other factors such as price, needs, store location, product quality, and direct promotions when making purchases. Meanwhile, an application that is easy to learn, understand, operate, flexible, and practical can facilitate the purchasing process and support consumer purchasing decisions.

title: RETAIL INVESTOR PARTICIPATION AND FINANCIAL INCLUSION IN INDIA
abstract: Indias retail investor base has grown nearly sixfold since March 2020, but participation remains narrow when measured against the country's near-universal bank account ownership. Total demat accounts rose from 4.09 crore in March 2020 to about 23.4 crore by July 2026, and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) crossed 13 crore unique registered investors in April 2026. Monthly SIP contributions to mutual funds reached a record â‚¹32,490 crore in September 2026. Over the same period the RBI's Financial Inclusion Index rose from 53.9 (March 2021) to 70.0 (March 2026), and Jan Dhan accounts crossed 59 crore.Yet SEBI's Investor Survey 2025 finds that only 9.5% of Indian households invest in any securities product, even though 63% are aware of one. Participation is also uneven: it is concentrated in a few states, only about one in four NSE investors is a woman, and a large share of young new entrants has moved into equity derivatives, where SEBI found that 87.7% of individual traders made net losses in FY26.Using secondary data from SEBI, NSE, the depositories (NSDL and CDSL), AMFI, the RBI, NPCI, the Ministry of Finance and the World Bank, this paper argues that India has largely solved the problem of access to the financial system and is now facing the harder problem of quality of participation. It concludes with recommendations on financial literacy, product design, investor protectio…

abstract: Abstract Background Cognitive impairment (CI) is a common and disabling feature of multiple sclerosis (MS) and is increasingly recognized as a manifestation of progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA). Recent studies have characterized cognitive PIRA as gradual, relapse-independent cognitive decline identified through longitudinal neuropsychological assessment, most commonly affecting information processing speed. However, distinguishing MS-related cognitive PIRA from comorbid neurodegenerative disorders remains challenging, particularly in younger patients, in whom diagnostic overshadowing may delay appropriate diagnosis and management. Herein, we report a case of MS with rapidly progressive, memory-predominant CI mimicking cognitive PIRA. Case presentation A 46-year-old man with a 10-year history of MS presented with rapidly progressive, memory-predominant CI developing over the preceding 5 years, mimicking cognitive PIRA. Despite the absence of clinical relapses and limited magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) activity, cognitive decline progressed and was disproportionate to physical disability. Neuropsychological assessment revealed an early amnestic-dominant profile rather than the processing speed-predominant pattern observed in MS-related CI. Despite escalation from interferon-β1a to high-efficacy anti-CD20 therapy (ofatumumab), cognitive deterioration persisted, …

title: When Algorithms Set Prices: Emerging Consumer Fairness Challenges in AI-Driven Dynamic Pricing
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is turning dynamic pricing from a standardized management decision into an individual, algorithmic experience. Algorithmic pricing improves efficiency and personalization, but its opacity and individualized prices can leave consumers feeling treated unfairly and distrustful. This short communication draws on recent research on algorithmic pricing, price fairness, price transparency, and consumer trust to build a conceptual framework. It links four features of algorithmic pricing (real-time adaptation, personalization, individualized price differentiation, and limited explainability) to perceived price fairness, which in turn shapes consumer trust and acceptance or resistance. The paper argues that fairness is a strategic management problem, not only an ethical concern. Implications for pricing managers cover price explanations, responsible personalization, and governance, and empirical research directions are proposed.

abstract: El presente artículo analiza la orientación familiar como estrategia parafortalecer la aceptación parental de Necesidades Educativas Específicas (NEE) en elcantón Otavalo. Con un enfoque mixto, se investigó la percepción de docentes, padres ypsicólogos. Se defiende que la aceptación parental no es espontánea, sino un procesomediado por la intervención profesional que reduce el duelo y la negación. Losresultados indican una brecha entre la importancia de la orientación y suimplementación real. Se propone una guía metodológica y talleres para facilitar lainclusión educativa efectiva y humana.

title: DATA PRODUCT STRATEGY FOR SCALABLE MICROSERVICE ARCHITECTURES
abstract: Applications are becoming increasingly distributed and data-centric and require scalable data management in microservice architectures. Traditional solutions tend to create complexity and bottlenecks, including managing data consistency, schema changes, cross-domain coordination, and more. While maintaining domain modularity and interoperability, a data-product-based architectural model can enhance discovery and ownership. This paper proposes a conceptual design and provides a reference architecture that includes domain-oriented design, metadata-driven governance and a self-service data platform. The results indicate that the proposed architecture provides greater throughput, lower latency, and better utilization of resources than baseline architecture. The paper also discusses key architectural components and future directions related to automated governance, interoperability of semantic data, and adaptive services of data platforms.

title: Research on Scheduling Strategy of Wind-Solar-Thermal-Storage System Based on MNSGA-II
abstract: This paper proposes an improved NSGA-II algorithm (MNSGA-II) to address the issues of local optima and insufficient population diversity in the process of solving economic dispatch strategies for power systems. The algorithm first uses Faure sequences to initialize the population, improving the quality and distribution uniformity of the initial solution; Secondly, design a dual archive maintenance strategy that updates the convergence archive through PBI values, updates the diversity archive through Manhattan distance, and combines truncation mechanism to prevent archive overflow, enhancing the algorithm’s global search capability. In the process of evolution, combining two archive information for environmental selection balances convergence and diversity. The application of MNSGA-II to the power scheduling problem of four generator units shows that compared with traditional NSGA-II and its variants, the algorithm proposed in this paper performs better in terms of optimization accuracy and stability, providing an effective solution for multi-objective optimization of power systems under complex constraints.

title: DECOUPLING OF ASSET PRICING FROM INCOME FUNDAMENTALS: A CROSS-CONTINENTAL ANALYSIS OF RENTAL YIELD COMPRESSION, SPECULATION, AND STRUCTURAL HOUSING INEQUITY
abstract: Standard financial models suggest that property values should align with rental income, yet global residential real estate consistently exhibits gross rental yields falling well below mortgage financing costs. This paper investigates why gross rental yields vary dramatically across global markets and examines the structural mechanisms distributing housing risk and return across income groups. Utilizing cross-national data from Numbeo across a 57-country national income dataset and a 339 - city continental dataset (spanning Asia, Europe, and North America), we evaluate rental yield spreads alongside key affordability and inequality indicators-including Price-to-Income Ratio (PTI), Price-to-Rent Ratio (PTR), Mortgage-as-a-Percentage-of-Income (MAPI), and Loan Affordability Index (LAI). The empirical analysis reveals four primary findings. First, gross rental yields do not vary significantly by national income classification, remaining between 5% and 6.7% globally; rather, outcomes are governed by underlying market structures and speculative orientations. Second, North American urban markets demonstrate rent-calibrated dynamics with high average yields (9.52%) where asset prices tightly track carrying costs. Third, European cities reflect policydriven yield compression (4.38%) enforced via strong tenant protections and rent controls.

title: Talent management practices for bridging the staffing strategy gap in a Gauteng-located higher education institution, South Africa
abstract: Talent management (TM) has emerged as a strategic imperative for universities globally as institutions compete for scarce academic and professional talent. Despite increasing attention to TM practices, many universities continue to experience staffing inefficiencies, weak recruitment systems, and limited workforce planning strategies. This study examines staffing practices as a core component of TM at a university in the Gauteng province of South Africa. Using a quantitative survey approach with a convenience sample of n=400 employees, data were collected from university employees who rated both the status and the importance of staffing practices on a five-point Likert scale. The findings revealed significant discrepancies between the perceived importance and current implementation of staffing practices. While respondents consider strategic staffing practices highly important for institutional performance, their implementation is rated only moderate to low. These findings highlight the need for universities to adopt integrated staffing strategies that align recruitment, workforce planning, and TM with institutional objectives. The study contributes to the literature on higher education human resource management by providing empirical evidence on staffing gaps and proposing a strategic staffing framework suitable for universities in developing contexts.

title: A Multi-Strategy Optimized Dung Beetle Algorithm
abstract: To address the shortcomings of the Dung Beetle Optimizer (DBO) in solving complex optimization problems—namely insufficient global exploration capability, relatively slow convergence, and a tendency to become trapped in local optima—this paper proposes a multi-strategy improved DBO, termed CWSADBO, and applies it to the economic dispatch problem of microgrids. The proposed algorithm integrates Cubic chaotic initialization, a black widow behavior mechanism, a sparrow-inspired perturbation strategy, and a Cauchy–Gaussian hybrid mutation mechanism to enhance both search efficiency and solution accuracy. Specifically, the Cubic chaotic map is employed to increase the diversity of the initial population; the black widow behavior mechanism strengthens global exploration during the search process; the sparrow-inspired perturbation strategy helps the algorithm escape local optima; and the Cauchy–Gaussian hybrid mutation mechanism achieves a dynamic balance between global exploratory jumps and local fine-grained exploitation. To evaluate its performance, 16 standard benchmark functions are tested, and comparative experiments are conducted against DBO, IDBO, SSA, and SABO. The results demonstrate that CWSADBO achieves faster convergence and higher optimization accuracy on most benchmark functions, with particularly notable advantages in unimodal, multimodal, and complex multimodal cases.…

title: The Impact of Gamified Learning on Student Achievement: A Narrative Literature Review
abstract: This narrative literature review explores the statistically significant relationship between gamified learning, student engagement, and academic achievement. Drawing from quasi-experimental studies, meta-analyses, and systematic reviews, the paper highlights how game-based elements—such as points, badges, leaderboards, and immediate feedback—enhance motivation and foster higher-order thinking skills. The review also examines the differential impact of gamification across achievement levels and the moderating role of socio-demographic variables such as age, sex, parental education, and school type. Findings suggest that while gamification is broadly effective, its success depends on thoughtful design and contextual alignment with learner needs.

When GPUs Fail Quietly: Separating GPU Hardware Degradation from Monitoring Failure under Degraded Observability
abstract: A missing GPU measurement in a production supercomputer is ambiguous: either the device has failed, or the pipeline that reports on it has. The two call for different responses – an engineer sent to the hardware, or a ticket raised against the collector – so the ambiguity has to be resolved before either one is right. We ask which half of that decision needs a model. Whether the monitoring path has degraded is close to directly readable: one lightweight statistic that is never fitted, the gap between the data-delivery rates on the out-of-band hardware-sensor path and the in-band host path, ranks monitoring incidents at AUPRC 0.237 where they are only 5.2 % of the units ranked, and no learned component we trained improves on it. Deciding whether already-degraded evidence has a physical cause is harder, and needs both workload-aware residuals on the hardware sensors and an explicit model of the observation process. PARALLAX supplies these, tracking device health and monitoring health as separate latent states over out-of-band IPMI measurements, in-band telemetry, workload context, and structured missingness; the configuration we recommend is the hybrid that takes its physical risk from PARALLAX and its monitoring risk from the lightweight statistic. title: TRUSTWORTHY ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR MEDICAL IMAGE ANALYSIS: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF ROBUST DEEP LEARNING TECHNIQUES FOR CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT
abstract: Medical image analysis has been revolutionized by the advent of artificial intelligence, which has made automated disease detection, segmentation and diagnosis possible across a range of imaging modalities, thus supporting clinical decisions. However, the increasing complexity of deep learning models has raised concerns regarding their reliability, interpretability, fairness, privacy, and regulatory compliance, highlighting the need for trustworthy AI in healthcare. The review focuses on recent breakthroughs in deep learning models for medical image analysis, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), segmentation networks based on U-net, Vision Transformers, and foundation models, and explores their use in clinical decision support. It also examines the fundamental principles of trustworthy AI, including explainability, robustness, fairness, privacy preservation, reliability, transparency and regulatory governance. The review summarizes the current state of the art for the strengths and limitations of current AI models and highlights some of the challenges that hamper the use of these models in the clinical workflow, such as limited data availability, domain shifts, algorithmic bias, computational complexity, and integration into the clinical workflow. New concepts like multimodal foundation models, federated learning and privacy-preserving AI are also explored as potential…

title: A Multisensor Baseline and Abstention Architecture for Low Voltage Rotating Machine Condition Assessment
abstract: Condition assessment of small rotating machines is often demonstrated with a single sensor and a fixed threshold, although operating point, mounting and environment can alter measured signals. This paper presents NEXUS PRIME V1 as a documented design for a low voltage, ESP32 based bench instrument using device specific baselines, validity checks and corroborating channels. Its proposed rule set reports NORMAL when required measurements agree with calibrated healthy bands, ABNORMAL only for a coherent pattern in at least two independent condition channels, and INCONCLUSIVE when evidence is missing or contradictory. The design specifies vibration, current, voltage, temperature and RPM sensing, with distance serving primarily as a setup validity check; it also specifies local indication and a web dashboard. The supplied 71 page blueprint reports a design audit, including 18 distinct GPIO assignments and an estimated INR 1,894 parts budget. Hardware, firmware, diagnostic accuracy and reliability have not yet been measured. The contribution is an inspectable architecture and a preregisterable validation protocol, not an experimentally demonstrated diagnostic improvement

abstract: The growth of communication technologies and advancement in cloud computing have led to an increase in the possibility of cybercrime and attacks. Traditional IDSs (Intrusion Detection Systems) are ineffective in detecting sophisticated attacks that evolve rapidly and target information systems and therefore do not provide sufficient protection. Moreover, traditional systems are slow to adapt to the appearance of new threats and produce a high number of false alarms which are often considered a nuisance. The proposed study offers an intrusion detection system framework that incorporates the hybrid techniques of machine learning to enhance the security of networks and detect cyber threats. The key aspects of the system are the following: the model uses various machine learning algorithms as well as anomaly detection methods in order to detect intrusions effectively. The effectiveness of the framework in terms of its accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and false positive index calculation is measured through conducting empirical testing applying public datasets as references for verification of the effectiveness of the proposed model. abstract: Prompt- and image-driven 3D generation can lower the interaction barrier to digital asset creation, yet model-level advances do not establish whether non-specialists can operate a complete authoring workflow. This study designed and evaluated a web-based human–AI prototype integrating a React interface, FastAPI services, ComfyUI workflow orchestration, asynchronous job processing, persistent asset storage, and browser-based 3D visualization. We implemented four modes: Text-to-3D, Text-to-3D with ControlNet, Single Image-to-3D, and Multi Image-to-3D. Evaluation combined 14 requirement-derived black-box scenarios, cross-viewer GLB compatibility checks in three viewing environments, 35 completed generation jobs, task-based observation with seven participants completing 84 task executions, System Usability Scale (SUS) responses from a separate group of 12 students, and one expert assessment of implementation and output quality. All 14 functional scenarios produced the expected outcomes, and the tested GLB outputs opened in the integrated viewer, Blender, and 3dviewer.net. Mean server-side turnaround was 66.15 s; an exploratory Kruskal–Wallis test indicated differences among the observed workload distributions (H(3) = 10.52, p = .015, ε² = .243), but did not support causal or pairwise speed claims. title: Adaptive Machine Learning in Non-Stationary Environments: A Systematic Review of Concept Drift Detection and Mitigation in Data Streams
abstract: The proliferation of high-velocity data streams in domains such as IoT, cybersecurity, and financial technology has exposed the limitations of static machine learning models. When the underlying data distribution changes over time, a phenomenon known as concept drift occurs, leading to severe model degradation `[1]`. This paper presents a systematic review of 29 foundational and contemporary studies on concept drift detection and adaptation. We categorize detection mechanisms into statistical, window-based, and model-based approaches, while evaluating adaptation strategies ranging from dynamic ensembles to lightweight incremental learning `[16]`. Furthermore, we address compounding challenges, including class imbalance and the emergence of novel classes `[2]`, `[30]`. By synthesizing recent advancements, this review provides a comprehensive roadmap for developing robust, real-time, and resource-efficient streaming machine learning systems `[27]`

title: Deep learning investigation of discrete fractional order Shingles disease model with neural networking
abstract: This study investigates the discrete fractional-order Shingles disease (DFOS) mathematical model. The considered model is framed with five compartments over time. The existence and uniqueness of solutions are determined via fixed point theory, confirming well-defined solutions. Three scenarios, each with various fractional orders, were used to study the effects of memory and fractional dynamics on disease propagation. To solve the model, we operate a discrete numerical iterative method (DNIM) linked to neural networks, specifically employing the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm, denoted DNIM-LM. This hybrid technique increases the accuracy of numerical results from neural networks. The data sets are distributed into 70% for training, 15% for validation, and 15% for testing, confirming a balanced calculation. The performance of the discrete fractional mathematical modeling is evaluated through artificial intelligence (AI), which involves training progress, error distribution, regression metrics, and overall model fit. The outcomes are thoroughly visualized via graphical illustrations, providing insights into the dynamics of each part and the impact of various fractional orders on the spread of shingles. This research addresses a novel approach to demonstrate infectious diseases with fractional dynamics and enhanced computational methods, improving our understanding of shingle …

title: Deep brain stimulation surgery under general anesthesia in patients with Parkinson’s disease: a retrospective study in Korea
abstract: Objective: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the subthalamic nucleus (STN) is conventionally performed under local anesthesia to preserve intraoperative microelectrode recording (MER) quality. However, awake surgery poses challenges for Parkinson’s disease (PD) patients with severe anxiety, respiratory compromise, or debilitating “off-medication” dystonia. This study evaluated the clinical efficacy and surgical feasibility of bilateral STN-DBS under general anesthesia.Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 29 advanced PD patients who underwent bilateral STN-DBS under general anesthesia. Thirteen patients underwent a two-stage operation (Activa implantable pulse generator [IPG]), and 16 underwent a one-stage procedure (directional leads, Percept PC IPG). Target localization relied on high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography (CT). Intraoperative MER was performed under inhalational anesthesia with sevoflurane (n=27) or desflurane (n=2). Outcomes were assessed after ≥6 months using the Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) parts III and IV and the levodopa-equivalent daily dose (LEDD).Results: Intraoperative MER successfully identified STN and substantia nigra pars reticulata boundaries in all 29 patients. UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION AND CARRIER-COLLECTION ROBUSTNESS UNDER PHYSICAL TOLERANCES IN A SERIES VERTICAL-JUNCTION SILICON SOLAR CELL
abstract: This work investigates the propagation of uncertainties in physical parameters to carrier collection in a series vertical-junction silicon solar cell. Starting from an exact dimensionless collection law, uncertainties are introduced in the base thickness H, diffusion coefficient D, carrier lifetime τ, and interface recombination velocities Sf and Sb. For each realization, the diffusion length and the reduced parameters h, f, and b are recalculated, thereby preserving the dependencies induced by the physical transformation. Twenty-seven nominal regimes and four controlled uncertainty amplitudes, from ±5% to ±30%, are investigated using a Monte Carlo campaign of 120,000 realizations per scenario. Robustness is characterized by the coefficient of variation of collection and by R90 = P(C ≥ 0.9 C0). The median coefficient of variation increases from approximately 3.13% at ±5% to 18.94% at ±30%, while the maximum value reaches 37.14%. Over the same range, the median R90 decreases from 100% to approximately 68.12%. At ±30%, some regimes retain R90 close to unity, whereas the least robust regime in the grid reaches approximately 60.17%. The regime of maximum statistical dispersion does not exactly coincide with that of minimum R90. These results show that nominal performance, statistical dispersion, and probabilistic robustness are distinct properties and establish a regime-dependent m…

title: DeepFake Shield: A Multi-Modal Generative AI Fraud Detection Pipeline with Explicit Uncertainty Handling
abstract: Synthetic media is now cheap to make and hard to judge by eye. A cloned voice can approve a payment, a generated face can get past a casual identity check, and a fluent paragraph written by a language model can pass for a statement from a real person. Most detectors cover only one of these cases, and almost all return a confident verdict even for input far outside their training data. This paper presents DeepFake Shield, a Flask-based web application that screens images, text, audio and video through one interface. Each modality is served by a pre-trained deep learning classifier, and a threshold layer turns the raw model score into one of three outcomes: authentic, synthetic or inconclusive. For video, the visual and audio streams are analysed separately and any disagreement between them is reported as a conflict. The paper gives a detailed justification for the topic, describes the architecture and decision logic, and sets out an evaluation protocol based on precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC and Brier score with thresholds tuned on validation data only. We report the engineering checks completed so far and state clearly that they are not accuracy measurements

abstract: Context-aware digital twins are emerging as enabling architectures for coordinating responses to disruptions across inventory, warehouse, and transportation operations in cloud-based supply-chain platforms. They are important because they can be used to link continually evolving operational representations with optimization services that are able to react to traffic conditions, order arrivals, equipment status, changes in inventory, and facility constraints. This article reviews peer-reviewed journal literature on digital supply-chain twins, warehouse intelligence, dynamic vehicle routing, Internet of Things-enabled logistics, microservice architectures, and computational modelling. Some studies indicate that digital-twin approaches can improve visibility, scenario evaluation, and decision coordination in specific settings, but there is very little evidence of fully integrated real-time optimization of transportation and warehouse operations. Closed-loop orchestration has not been a primary focus of existing implementations, which tend to focus on warehouse simulation or monitoring, route adjustment, or resilience analysis across logistics domains. title: Artificial Intelligence in Production and Optimization
abstract: This review is a systematic literature review-cum-bibliometric analysis of the field of Artificial Intelligence in Production and Optimization with a view to mapping the field in holistic manner. In this review the authors have attempted to identify the predominant strands in the field and identify where learning approaches have been linked to decision making frameworks and where learning approaches end at prediction. Data for the review are sourced from Elsevier's Scopus database, and are limited to English language journal articles and reviews published between 2014 and 2027 using key words. This review is based on 3,727 records in the final database. The number of documents published has increased from 38 in 2014 to 1,161 in 2026 and the top producers are China, India, and the United States. The most prevalent themes were identified as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Optimization. The formal decision model seems to be mainly in the field of scheduling, while in bioprocess and additive manufacturing, and food systems, it is not often that the decision is made to end at prediction.

title: Privacy and Data Protection Governance for Implementing Indonesia’s Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 27/2022): A Structured Literature Review
abstract: Indonesia’s Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection (PDP Law) imposes extensive duties on controllers and processors, yet organizational governance for implementation remains unevenly documented. This structured literature review, informed by PRISMA reporting principles, synthesizes 23 governance-focused peer-reviewed publications (2022–2026) identified through a transparent purposive corpus strategy. No multi-database search was conducted in this study. Implementation is influenced by legal certainty, institutional accountability (including supervisory officer models), sector capacity, third-party ecosystem risk, rights interoperability, measurable compliance tools, and automated decision-making challenges. Privacy governance (74%), audit and compliance assessment (48%), and integrated data governance (39%) are the most frequent components; data protection impact assessment is rarely explicit. Governance structures are portrayed as prerequisites for compliance where accountability, assessment instruments, and platform intermediaries align. A seven-layer implementation framework for the PDP Law is proposed. Limitations include the purposive corpus, limited Indonesian empirical evidence, and the absence of exhaustive database screening.

abstract: Follow-up of audit recommendations is usually measured by how many recommendations are closed. That measure ignores whether the money at stake is actually recovered. This study separates the two. Data come from the Supreme Audit Board's recommendation follow-up monitoring appendix for local governments, status as of Semester I 2024, covering 518 entities that reconcile on both counts and values. Across the 2018 to 2022 cohorts, local governments closed 72.13 percent of recommendations on average but recovered only 53.1 percent of the 11.34 trillion rupiah at stake. Recovery falls monotonically with the size of the recommendation, from 99.06 percent in the smallest decile to 55.71 percent in the largest, and to 39.65 percent on an aggregate basis. Closure falls by only 9.0 points across the same deciles. With cohort and entity fixed effects, a tenfold larger recommendation portfolio is associated with recovery lower by 18.7 percentage points. Resolution also stalls: closure rises by 5.12 points a year up to age eight and by 0.09 points a year thereafter, leaving 49,639 recommendations issued between 2005 and 2017 still open. The follow-up system settles small and recent matters and leaves large and old ones unresolved.

title: Future directions on integrated wildlife monitoring based on non-invasive approaches in Europe
abstract: Abstract The growing trend of emerging diseases at the wildlife-livestock-human interface underscores the need to establish integrated surveillance strategies within a One Health framework. In Europe, Integrated Wildlife Monitoring (IWM) tends to focus on specific pathogens, often with limited spatial and temporal scope. In this perspectives article, we address some of the most recent technological advances that could strengthen future IWM programs, with special emphasis on non-invasive approaches for monitoring wildlife populations and pathogen communities. We analyse the potential complementarity of different monitoring tools, such as camera traps, unmanned aerial vehicles, acoustic recording, and especially the detection of environmental nucleic acids (ENAD) using next-generation sequencing techniques, for the simultaneous characterization of pathogen and host communities. Despite the potential of molecular tools for large-scale monitoring, the lack of methodological standardization, the limited capacity to obtain quantitative information (e.g. population abundance or pathogen prevalence), and the difficulty of inferring the epidemiological significance of findings (e.g. whether molecular detection indicates viable pathogen) remain key challenges that limit their application. Finally, we argue that integrating these technologies with artificial intelligence (AI) represents a…

title: A Dempster-Shafer-Based Expert System for Personalized Higher Education Major Recommendation
abstract: Selecting a study program at a State University (Perguruan Tinggi Negeri/PTN) is a decision that many senior high school students approach without a systematic review of their interest, aptitude, achievement, and career goals, a gap made more pressing by the limited counseling capacity available at most schools. Earlier expert systems for major recommendation have relied on Forward Chaining or Certainty Factor, methods that combine evidence into a single rule outcome or scalar confidence without explicitly representing the uncertainty left by incomplete evidence. This study developed and implemented a web-based expert system, Peta Kampus, that applies Dempster-Shafer evidence theory to generate a personalized major recommendation from a student's answers to a structured questionnaire. The knowledge base was constructed with school counselors and an education practitioner into 275 evidence-linked questions covering 55 majors across 21 faculties, each carrying an expert-assigned belief value. The system was built on a native PHP Model-View-Controller architecture with MySQL as the data store, and its inference engine combines successive evidence using Dempster's rule of combination while tracking residual uncertainty and evidentiary conflict. The system was verified through Black Box Testing of its functional modules, with all 15 tested scenarios passing, and evaluated through an…

title: A Case Study on the Development of a Support System for Resolving Software Defects in webOS TV
StreamHub - Multi - Agent Framework for Movie Recommendation System Using Langchain
abstract: The rapid growth of digital entertainment platforms has made it difficult for users to discover suitable movies and music from a large collection of content. Conventional platforms commonly depend on separate search interfaces and recommendation features, which may not provide a unified or context-aware experience. This paper presents StreamHub, an OTT and Music Multi-Agent Recommendation System that combines movie discovery, music discovery, personalized recommendations, user interaction, and premium-content access in a single web application. A Supervisor Agent coordinates user requests and directs them to specialized agent functions. The Movie/Content Agent integrates the TMDB API to retrieve available movie and television information, while the Music Agent connects to an external royalty-free music API to obtain available tracks and related metadata. User preferences, watch history, ratings, and watchlists can be maintained through a MySQL database to support more relevant content suggestions. The system uses React.js for the frontend and FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and Pydantic for backend services. JWT-based authentication supports protected access, while the modular multiagent design separates responsibilities and supports future extension. The platform demonstrates how Al-assisted interaction, external APIs, persistent user information, and coordinated agents can simplify ente…

title: INVESTIGATING CHALLENGES IN TOEFL IBT INTEGRATED SPEAKING: EVIDENCE FROM HIGH-QUALITY PROGRAM STUDENTS AT PTIT, VIETNAM
abstract: Integrated Speaking in the TOEFL iBT exam presents significant cognitive and linguistic demands as it requires test-takers to synthesize information from multiple input modalities (reading and listening) before producing an oral response. This study investigates the primary subjective and objective challenges faced by non-English major students enrolled in the High-Quality (HQ) program at the Posts and Telecommunications Institute of Technology (PTIT), Vietnam, where the English curriculum is benchmarked against the TOEFL iBT standard. Data were gathered through a mixed-methods approach involving a quantitative survey ($N = 120$) and semi-structured interviews ($n = 12$) with students working at the B1 CEFR proficiency level. Findings reveal three dominant categories of difficulty: linguistic limitations (insufficient vocabulary and limited listening synthesis), lack of systematic instruction in speaking strategies, and affective barriers (low self-efficacy and anxiety). Based on these empirical insights, targeted pedagogical solutions are proposed, including structured note-taking frameworks, integrated skills scaffolding, and strategy-based instruction to enhance student performance.

title: Comparative Study on the Perceptions of Residents and Inspectors Regarding the In-Unit Fire Safety Inspection System in Multi-family Housing
abstract: In this study, a survey was conducted with residents and inspectors in multifamily housing to identify ways to improve the effectiveness of the in-unit fire safety inspection system. Their perceptions, satisfaction levels, perceived problems, and support system requirements were comparatively analyzed. Residents recognized the necessity of in-unit inspections but lacked understanding of the system and inspection methods, whereas inspectors showed a high level of institutional understanding but lower recognition of the need for in-unit inspections, confirming a perception gap. Satisfaction was significantly lower among the inspectors. Both groups identified inspectors' awareness as the primary problem, whereas inspectors additionally pointed to the result collection method and residents’ inspection frequency. Both groups agreed on the need for a support system, with residents prioritizing information provision and inspectors administrative support. The findings empirically identify the stakeholder perception gap and provide baseline data for institutional improvements and support system design.

Tenant-Aware HR Master Data Harmonization: A Logical Bronze-Silver-MDM-Gold Workflow for Multi-Tenant HCM Data
abstract: Enterprise human resources (HR) systems often apply inconsistent labels to shared employee master-data attributes. This study evaluates an ordered, tenant-aware harmonization workflow represented by Bronze, Silver, master data management (MDM), and Gold logical layers; it does not claim an implemented transactional lakehouse platform. Four synthetic HR datasets contribute 3,000 core employee records. A fixed-seed simulation creates four tenants and introduces controlled categorical corruption, missingness, and duplicate identifiers while retaining independent canonical labels. Exact, normalized, synonym, and bounded fuzzy matching run in sequence, and unresolved nonmissing values are referred for manual review. At a fuzzy cutoff of 0.82, the study records 8,842 nonmissing field values, 8,731 canonical assignments, and 8,480 correct assignments, giving 98.74% assignment coverage, 95.91% recall under the study definition, and an F1 of 0.9651. Field-level denominators reconstructed from the method-by-field matrix allow independent arithmetic checking and identify 251 erroneous assignments across all four matching tiers. In the deduplicated employee classification population, department and job-title vocabularies shrink from 228 raw labels to 37 mastered labels. The downstream comparison gives mixed point estimates: ROC-AUC rises by 0.0321 and PR-AUC by 0.0005, while F1 falls by 0.…

title: HOUSEHOLD SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT IN THE URBAN COMMUNE OF DIFFA, NIGER: PRACTICES, PERCEPTIONS AND GOVERNANCE CHALLENGES
abstract: Rapid population growth, urbanization and changing consumption patterns are increasing the quantity and complexity of household solid waste generated in low- and middle-income cities. In Niger, solid waste management remains constrained by limited infrastructure, weak institutional coordination, predominantly informal collection practices and very limited source separation. In the urban commune of Diffa, these constraints are particularly important because household waste is largely managed individually and disposed of at nearby uncontrolled dumpsites. This study assessed household solid waste-management practices, knowledge and perceptions, as well as selected governance and willingness-to-pay dimensions in the urban commune of Diffa, Niger. A cross-sectional household survey was conducted from August to September 2026 using a structured questionnaire administered through Kobo Collect. Simple random sampling was used to select 152 households distributed across 13 neighbourhoods. Data were exported to Excel for organization and graphical presentation, while descriptive statistical analyses and willingness-to-pay calculations were performed using Minitab 18. Kitchen waste was reported by 89.47% of households and packaging waste by 60.53%. A majority of households (58.55%) had no waste container, while 41.45% used a container. title: A Review on Pharmaceutical Marketing and Management
abstract: Pharmaceutical marketing and management occupy a distinct position among commercial disciplines because they operate at the intersection of profit-driven business objectives and public health responsibility. Thisreview examinesthe strategic, operational, and ethical dimensions of pharma marketing and management, drawing on recent literature covering promotional practices, digital transformation, supply chain operations, and regulatory oversight. The review finds that traditional promotional tools such as medical representative (MR) visits, free drug samples, and continuing medical education (CME) sponsorships remain influential in shaping physician prescribing behaviour, even as digital channels, artificial intelligence (AI), and data analytics increasingly reshape how companies engage healthcare professionals (HCPs) and patients. On the management side, the Indian pharmaceutical supply chain continues to face structural challenges including fragmentation, import dependence on active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), cold chain limitations, and counterfeit products, even as digital tools and regulatory reforms attempt to close these gaps. Ethical concerns persist around inducements, exaggerated promotional claims, and inconsistent enforcement of codes such as the Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP), which became legally binding in 2024. title: Leveraging Industry 4.0 to overcome supply chain challenges in Gauteng manufacturing small- and medium-sized enterprises: A Supply Chain Operations Reference model perspective
abstract: Background: Manufacturing small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Gauteng, South Africa, face persistent supply chain challenges that hinder performance and sustainability. Although Industry 4.0 technologies offered opportunities to improve supply chain performance, limited research had linked these technologies to specific challenges across the Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) model. Objectives: This study aimed to identify and validate supply chain challenges affecting manufacturing SMEs and recommend Industry 4.0 technologies to address them across SCOR processes. Method: The study was conducted among supply chain professionals employed in manufacturing SMEs in Gauteng, South Africa. This quantitative study, grounded in the positivist paradigm, included 252 supply chain professionals. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and snowball sampling. IBM SPSS Statistics and SmartPLS 4 were used for descriptive analysis and measurement model evaluation. Results: Significant challenges were identified across all SCOR processes, including forecasting inaccuracies, supplier unreliability, inadequate visibility and traceability, inventory inaccuracies, poor returns monitoring, and miscommunication. The measurement model demonstrated strong reliability and validity, with Cronbach’s alphas above 0.86 and composite reliabilities exceeding 0.89. A SCOR Technolo…

title: Neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy and surgical innovation reshape multimodal management of esophageal cancer
abstract: Abstract Esophageal cancer requires multimodal management that accounts for histology, resectability and operative fitness. This narrative review examines selected literature published through December 2025 on neoadjuvant systemic therapy, minimally invasive esophagectomy and perioperative decision-making. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy and chemoradiotherapy have established roles, but their relative benefits depend on the population and regimen. CROSS demonstrated a survival benefit over surgery alone, whereas ESOPEC favored perioperative FLOT over CROSS chemoradiotherapy in resectable esophageal adenocarcinoma. For esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, randomized phase III trials have demonstrated higher pathological complete response rates with selected chemoimmunotherapy regimens than with chemotherapy alone. However, pathological response should not be equated with an established survival benefit, and mature comparisons against chemoradiotherapy remain important. Evidence from gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma also requires careful interpretation before extrapolation to esophageal primary tumors. The TIME, MIRO and ROBOT randomized trials support reductions in postoperative pulmonary morbidity with the minimally invasive approaches evaluated compared with open esophagectomy. title: Correction: Perioperative Management of Patient with Systemic Mastocytosis Going for Total Thyroidectomy
abstract: In the case report by AlShaker et al., “Perioperative Management of Patient with Systemic Mastocytosis Going for Total Thyroidectomy”, published in The Journal of Medicine, Law & Public Health, Volume 5, Issue 2 (2025), pages 573–577, https://doi.org/10.52609/jmlph.v5i2.183, the published article did not include a statement on consent for publication.The authors have confirmed in writing that written informed consent for publication was obtained from the patient. The following statement has been added to the HTML and XML versions of the article:“Consent for publication: Written informed consent for publication of this case report was obtained from the patient.”The article now also states that it was handled by an independent editor with no involvement of the author-editor in the peer review or editorial decision process, as one of its authors serves on the journal’s editorial team.The PDF, which is the version of record, is unchanged. The authors agreed to this correction.

title: Public Financial Management and Rural Development in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria: Evidence from 2008–2017
abstract: Public financial management is widely regarded as a key determinant of development outcomes in resource-dependent economies, yet the extent to which it translates into tangible rural development remains under-examined at the subnational level in Nigeria. This study investigates the relationship between public financial management and rural development in Akwa Ibom State between 2008 and 2017, focusing on whether the pace of rural development kept pace with the state's rising public budgets and expenditures. Anchored in John Rawls's Theory of Justice, the study adopted a historical/descriptive survey design, drawing a sample of 182 respondents from five public establishments in the state using proportional stratified random sampling. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using percentage tables and chi-square statistics. Findings show that the calculated chi-square value (9.75) was less than the critical value (21.03) at the 0.05 significance level, leading to the acceptance of the null hypothesis: the level of rural development recorded in Akwa Ibom State was not commensurate with the state's rising public expenditure over the period. title: The Effect of Digital Payments, Financial Literacy, Financial Access, and Mental Accounting on Microenterprise Performance
abstract: Introduction/ Main Objectives: This study investigates the effects of digital payment, financial literacy, financial access, and mental accounting on the performance of microenterprises in Kuningan Regency, Indonesia. Using the Resource-Based View (RBV) framework, these four factors are conceptualized as technological, financial, and cognitive capabilities that may enhance business outcomes. Novelty: This study lies in integrating digital payment, financial literacy, financial access, and mental accounting into a single empirical model and testing their simultaneous effects on microenterprise performance within the specific context of Kuningan Regency using SEM-PLS. Research Methods: The research employed a quantitative survey method with 277 respondents selected from a population of 901 registered microenterprises, determined using the Slovin formula. Data were collected through structured questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. Finding/Results: The results show that the research model has adequate explanatory and predictive capabilities. Digital payment, financial literacy, financial access, and mental accounting have positive and significant effects on microenterprise performance. title: РЕЗИЛЬЄНТНІСТЬ СИСТЕМИ ДЕРЖАВНОГО ФІНАНСОВОГО КОНТРОЛЮ ЯК ДЕТЕРМІНАНТА ЕФЕКТИВНОСТІ ВИКОРИСТАННЯ БЮДЖЕТНИХ РЕСУРСІВ У ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННІ НАЦІОНАЛЬНОЇ БЕЗПЕКИ УКРАЇНИ
abstract: В умовах тривалих економічних, безпекових та інституційних викликів особливого значення набуває здатність системи державного фінансового контролю гарантувати безперервність контрольних функцій, своєчасно реагувати на бюджетні ризики та сприяти збереженню й ефективному використанню публічних ресурсів. Метою дослідження є теоретичне обґрунтування та емпірична оцінка резильєнтності системи державного фінансового контролю як детермінанти ефективності використання бюджетних ресурсів і чинника забезпечення національної безпеки України. У статті запропоноване визначення стабільності державної системи фінансового контролю та систематизовані її основні компоненти: інституційний, операційний, цифровий та адаптивний. На основі цього розроблено концептуальну модель взаємозв'язку між державним фінансовим контролем, бюджетною ефективністю та національною безпекою, що відображає взаємодію інституційного, регіонального та макрофінансового рівнів. На цій основі проаналізована фінансова, витратна та інвестиційна спроможність місцевих бюджетів України 2024 року, що виявляє значні регіональні відмінності в обсязі витрат і частці капітальних витрат.
