The Fall of Bodies, the Gravitational Self-Energy, and the Schwarzschild Radius as the Boundary of the Unattainable Region
abstract: This work underscores the fundamental role of self-energy in reinterpreting the Schwarzschild radius. In close analogy with the classical electron radius, the Schwarzschild radius defines the unattainable region, thus eliminating the problem of the singularity of gravitation. The simplicity and the physical foundations of an alternative elementary derivation of General Relativity results based on the Equivalence Principle and Special Relativity are reasserted.

title: Evaluation of Hospital Information System Integration to Support Interunit Information Flow at Grand Med Hospital in 2026
abstract: Integration of the Hospital Management Information System (SIMRS) determines whether registration, examination, diagnostic service, pharmacy, and administrative data are available to the next unit in a timely manner. This article aims to develop a framework for evaluating SIMRS integration at Grand Med Hospital in 2026. The method consists of a narrative review of regulations, interoperability standards, and research on health data exchange, followed by the design of a mixed methods case study. The units of analysis are information transfers among registration, outpatient clinics or the emergency department, laboratory, radiology, pharmacy, inpatient wards, and the cashier. Key indicators include data completeness, latency, transaction failures, duplicate data entry, consistency of patient identity, and traceability of request status. The proposed assessment matches patient and visit identifiers across systems, measures the time from data transmission until the receiving unit can use the data, and records failed transactions or those requiring manual correction. Indonesia’s Minister of Health Regulation No. 24 of 2022 on Medical Records provides the regulatory reference, while HL7 FHIR, the standard used by SATUSEHAT, provides a reference for tracing relationships among patient, encounter, examination request, and result data. The review produces an audit matrix, operational de…

title: Melatonin implantation and dietary energy level in relation to locomotor activity rhythms in ewes
A Multicolor Electrochromic Device Enabled by Shared-Zn Energy Routing for Self-Powered Wearable Displays
abstract: Abstract Wearable displays remain constrained by high energy consumption and a heavy reliance on external power during repeated refreshing. Here, we develop a multicolor electrochromic device based on shared-Zn energy routing for self-powered wearable displays. An intermediate Zn mesh couples an upper W/WO3 display electrode with a lower MnO2 energy-storage electrode, enabling self-driven coloration and internally powered bleaching through separate electrochemical circuits. The upper Nylon-66/W/WO3 optical cavity determines the visible color and optically shields the underlying storage electrode, decoupling display color from energy-storage chemistry. The device achieves coloration and bleaching within 10 s and sustains at least 500 consecutive refresh cycles. Integration with a microcontroller and heart-rate sensor demonstrates its potential for wearable physiological monitoring. This compact architecture combines display refreshing, optical memory, and electrical energy output, providing a route toward self-powered wearable displays with integrated sensing and energy functions.

title: Harnessing BIM–lean integration to elevate quality and drive sustainability in construction projects
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how building information modeling (BIM) and lean construction practices influences sustainability and quality performance of construction projects in the UK. The study further investigates the mediating role of project management principles and productivity on sustainability and performance, and also how technical and project related limitations impacts BIM-lean outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A cross-section questionnaire survey was conducted, and 410 valid responses were collected. Respondents were professionals with expertise in BIM, lean construction or project delivery experience within the UK construction industry. Data analyses were conducted using descriptive statistics, reliability and validity assessment strategies. Analysis techniques including hierarchical regression, structural equation modeling (SEM) were adopted, with machine learning techniques including random forest and decision tree as complementary predictive evidence. Given the cross-sectional design and high correlation among constructs, the findings were interpreted as statistical relationships rather than definitive causal associations. Findings Lean construction practices were positively associated with sustainability and quality performance, whereas the direct relationship between BIM and quality was not statistically significant. Productivity was significant to…

title: LEVERAGING AI INTEGRATION FOR FOSTERING INNOVATIVE WORK BEHAVIOR: A HYBRID SEM-ANN APPROACH IN THE IT SECTOR
abstract: This study examines the relationship between Perceived Artificial Intelligence (AI) Integration and Innovative Work Behavior (IWB) among IT professionals in India by investigating the mediating role of Employee Engagement (EE) and the moderating role of AI Literacy (AIL), drawing on Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) Theory and Social Exchange Theory (SET). A hybrid Structural Equation Modelling-Artificial Neural Network (SEM-ANN) approach was employed to examine and predict IWB. Data collected from 630 IT professionals revealed that Perceived AI Integration positively influences IWB, with EE partially mediating this relationship. AIL negatively moderates this relationship, weakening the positive relationship between Perceived AI Integration and IWB. The structural model explained 73.1% of the variance in IWB, while the ANN analysis provided complementary evidence of predictive stability within the study sample and identified the relative predictive importance of the model predictors. The study extends the AI and innovation literature by explaining how perceived AI-enabled work opportunities and EE contribute to IWB, while identifying AIL as a boundary condition. The findings provide practical guidance for managers seeking to support EE, develop AI capabilities, and design AI-enabled work environments that facilitate innovation.
authors: T. N. V. R. L. SWAMY

title: An Energy-Efficient Cooperative DDoS Attack Mitigation Using a Federated Deep Learning Framework in SDN
abstract: A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack can be launched through the huge number of edge-connected devices on software-defined AIoT systems. The lack of modern labeled training data makes it impossible to keep defending it in a centralized way, and privacy issues prevent the sharing of sensitive traffic information. In this work, a trustworthy federated learning (FL) architecture is proposed to tackle these challenges in a decentralized defense framework for AIoT. The framework incorporates three elements. First, a private model update exchange scheme based on secure multiparty computation can be used to enable privacy-preserving exchange of local model updates, while being robust to outliers. Second, a horizontal cooperation-based mitigation mechanism minimizes packet loss and decreases the effect of the attack on regular traffic. Third, a semi-supervised FL-based anomaly detection strategy is used to correctly classify attack classes and minimize the number of false alarms, based on a limited number of labeled outliers. Experimental evaluation on real-world datasets (CICIDS2017 and InSDN) demonstrates the effectiveness and efficacy of the proposed approach compared to SOP systems based on software-defined networking (SDN) in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The study also looks at FL enabled by SDN as a paradigm that contributes to enhancing security and minimizing trai…

EXPERIMENTAL EVALUATION OF A MODIFIED GENETIC ALGORITHM FOR LIBRARY ELEMENT SUBSTITUTION WITH MEASURED METADATA ON AN OPEN FPGA DESIGN FLOW
abstract: The efficiency of a modified genetic algorithm (MGA) with threshold selection and two-stage fitness evaluation is studied for designing computer device cores by substituting library elements. A library of 44 parameterised VHDL modules (111 variants in nine categories) was developed; its metadata were measured on the open GHDL, Yosys and nextpnr flow for Lattice ECP5 FPGAs. For the ALU-8 core, all 512 implementation variants were evaluated exhaustively, which provides the true optimum for comparison. With a median of 9 full syntheses, the MGA finds solutions from the top 5.7 % of the design space (Fmax rises from 45.3 to 103.9 MHz), i.e. it needs 4.4–11.8 times fewer syntheses than the classical GA, with a statistically insignificant difference in quality. For the FIR-16 core (|DS| ≈ 5.4·10⁸), the MGA with a median of 21 syntheses outperforms the classical GA with a budget of 40 syntheses in all 25 pairs of runs. Neither algorithm finds the solution that requires simultaneous replacement of eight identical parallel units, and a simple calibration of the fast estimate reduces the area error from 24–89 % to 3–11 %.

title: Design and Development of Pakai Lagi: Buyer-Centered Interface for Second-Hand Marketplace
abstract: The purchase of second-hand goods has become a popular trend in Indonesia due to social, economic and environmental factors. Second-hand goods offer sustainable solutions for waste reduction while providing economic value. However, transaction uncertainty and perceived quality risk remain significant barriers in online transactions. This study presents the design, development, and functional evaluation of Pakai Lagi, a localized second-hand marketplace built on client-server architecture. The system utilizes CodeIgniter 3 and MySQL for data administration and backend services, paired with a cross-platform Flutter mobile client for buyers. Development focuses on buyer-centric modules including product discovery, quality and condition displays, seller profiles and instant peer-to-peer communication to mitigate information asymmetry. Empirical evaluation was conducted using the black-box testing method across 14 functional areas comprising 49 test cases. The results demonstrate a functional feasibility for core operational modules. Certain peripheral presentation sub-components, specifically chat layout and complex filtering controls were noted as being under development for future iteration. Ultimately, this study confirms the practical feasibility of a lightweight, low-overhead backend-to-mobile infrastructure for sustainable community-driven e-commerce.

title: واقع توظيف تقنيات التعليم في ضوء مبادئ التصميم التعليمي: مراجعة تحليلية للأدبيات العربية
abstract: تُعد العلاقة بين تقنيات التعليم ومبادئ التصميم التعليمي من القضايا المركزية في تطوير بيئات التعلم الرقمية، إذ لم يعد توظيف التقنية داخل التعليم مرهونًا بتوافر الأدوات الرقمية فقط، بل بمدى إدماجها ضمن تصميم تعليمي منهجي يربط بين الأهداف، وخصائص المتعلمين، والمحتوى، والأنشطة، وأساليب التقويم. لذلك، تهدف هذه المراجعة إلى تحليل واقع توظيف تقنيات التعليم في ضوء مبادئ التصميم التعليمي، والكشف عن أنماط التكامل بين التقنية والتصميم كما عرضتها الأدبيات العربية ذات الصلة. اعتمدت الدراسة على منهج المراجعة التحليلية للأدبيات، من خلال تحليل أربع عشرة دراسة عربية تناولت تقنيات التعليم، والتصميم التعليمي، وبيئات التعلم الرقمية، ومعوقات الدمج بين تقنيات التعليم الحديثة والتصميم التعليمي. وقد أظهرت نتائج التحليل أن تقنيات التعليم تُسهم في تعزيز التفاعل، وزيادة دافعية المتعلمين، ودعم التعلم الذاتي، ومراعاة الفروق الفردية، إلا أن فاعليتها ترتبط بمدى توظيفها وفق خطوات التصميم التعليمي، مثل تحليل احتياجات المتعلمين، وتحديد الأهداف، واختيار الوسائط المناسبة، وتصميم الأنشطة، وتقويم نواتج التعلم. كما تتمثل أبرز المعوقات في ضعف التدريب، ومحدودية الجاهزية التقنية، والتمسك بالأساليب التعليمية التقليدية، وضعف الربط بين استخدام التقنية والأهداف التعليمية. وعليه، توصي الدراسة بتبني نماذج تصميم تعليمي مرنة تدمج التقنيات الحديثة بصورة منهجية، وتطوير برامج تدريبية للمعلمين والمصممين التعليميين، بما يعزز جودة بيئات التعلم ومخرجاتها.

title: Translating Place Identity into Textile Motif Design
abstract: Place identity is expressed through symbols, practices, and visual representations. Translating regional identity into textile motifs requires a systematic approach that connects local visual sources with meaningful design decisions. This study aims to identify Pangandaran's visual identity sources, translate them into textile motif compositions, and evaluate the resulting prototype. A practice-based design research approach was employed using a modified design thinking process incorporating a visual-semantic translation matrix. Five visual sources were identified and classified, with the Marlin Fish Monument serving as the primary motif, supported by coastal landscapes, fishing activities, marine biota, and vegetation. These sources were transformed through stylization, visual hierarchy, and repeat pattern development into three design alternatives. The selected coastal panorama composition was evaluated as a digital prototype by 17 respondents comprising textile industry experts, textile design academics, and potential users. Descriptive analysis revealed favourable perceptions of recognizability, visual distinctiveness, aesthetic quality, and textile applicability, with pooled mean scores ranging from 4.3 to 4.9. The findings provide preliminary evidence of perceived regional associations rather than independently verified recognition. This study contributes a traceable visu…

title: Sapogenin-Based Molecular Switches: Design and Synthesis of Azobenzene-Linked Steroid Dimers
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a mild and effective synthesis of steroid–azobenzene molecular switches from steroid sapogenin precursors. The strategy employs a sequence of stereospecific transformations at the C3 position, starting with an iodine-mediated substitution. A detailed analysis reveals that the reaction pathway—competitive E2 elimination vs SN2 substitution—is strictly controlled by the axial or equatorial orientation of the C3-hydroxyl group associated with the distinct A/B ring junctions. The iodinated intermediates were efficiently converted into azides, followed by the reduction to the corresponding C3 amines employing a one-pot Staudinger protocol. Final assembly with azobenzene-4,4′-dicarbonyl dichloride provided a series of dimeric conjugates. These hybrid architectures, characterized by rigid frameworks, serve as well-defined models for studying light-induced dynamics. The described methodology offers reliable access to photoresponsive steroid dimers with tunable stereochemical properties for supramolecular applications.

The Uniform Convexity and Uniform Smoothness of Variable Exponent Lebesgue Spaces and Contractive Semigroups
abstract: In this article, we investigate the geometrical structure of the variable exponent Lebesgue spaces, their uniform convexity, and uniform smoothness. Employing uniform convexity, we establish the asymptotic properties of semigroups of nonlinear operators. The existence of uniquely defined common fixed points is established under the Lipschitzian growth condition.

title: PERSEGUIÇÃO VIRTUAL E AMEAÇAS ONLINE CONTRA MULHERES: ENQUADRAMENTO PENAL E EXTENSÃO PROTETIVA DA LEI MARIA DA PENHA
abstract: A expansão das tecnologias digitais modificou as formas de interação social e também possibilitou novas manifestações de violência contra a mulher, como perseguições e ameaças praticadas por meio de redes sociais e aplicativos de mensagens. O presente artigo tem como objetivo analisar o tratamento penal dessas condutas e a aplicação da proteção prevista na Lei Maria da Penha em situações de violência praticadas no ambiente virtual. A pesquisa possui abordagem qualitativa e caráter exploratório, desenvolvida por meio de levantamento bibliográfico e documental, com análise da legislação, doutrina e jurisprudência. Os resultados demonstram que as condutas praticadas virtualmente podem receber tratamento penal quando presentes os elementos legais dos respectivos crimes, e que a ausência de contato físico não impede, por si só, a aplicação da Lei Maria da Penha, desde que preenchidos seus requisitos. Conclui-se que a proteção jurídica deve acompanhar as novas formas de violência digital, especialmente quanto à preservação da prova e à aplicação das medidas protetivas.

title: Virtual Linguistic Landscape on Social Media: Brand Image Construction of Japanese Beverages in Japan and Indonesia
abstract: This Study examines how Japanese beverage brands construct brand images through language use on Instagram across Japanese and Indonesian markets. Drawing on the concept of the virtual linguistic landscape (VLL), it investigates how linguistic choices foreground “Japaneseness” and how this emphasis varies across brands and market contexts. The study employs a descriptive qualitative approach, combining thematic analysis of promotional content with an examination of noun frequencies and Japan-related lexical items. Data comprise captions published on the official Japanese and Indonesian Instagram accounts of Pocari Sweat and ITO EN’s Oi Ocha between November 2025 and April 2026. The findings reveal distinct patterns of brand positioning. In Indonesia, Oi Ocha combines its green tea as an authentic Japanese beverage suited to a contemporary lifestyle. Pocari Sweat Indonesia emphasizes hydration and functional benefits through references to local routines and religious observances, with little explicit emphasis on Japanese origin. In Japan, Oi Ocha foregrounds international sports endorsements and Japanese tea identity, whereas Pocari Sweat emphasizes photography, youth, and everyday lifestyles. These findings suggest that Japaneseness functions as a selective branding resource whose prominence varies according to product positioning and market context.

Plant-Mediated Green Nanoparticles in Modern Drug Delivery: Advances in Synthesis, Characterization, Therapeutic Applications, and Safety Challenges
abstract: Background: With the increasing demand for biocompatible, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly nanocarriers, plant-mediated (green) synthesis of metallic and metal-oxide nanoparticles has become a major direction in pharmaceutical research. Phytochemical synthesis uses the polyphenols, flavonoids, terpenoids, and proteins available in plant extracts as reducing and capping agents to produce nanoparticles that are less toxic and more biologically active than those produced by conventional physicochemical methods. Objective: This study aims to summarise the literature on the synthesis, characterisation, and therapeutic potential of plant mediated nanoparticles over the past five years (2020-2025), focusing on their incorporation into current drug delivery systems. Methodology: We used PubMed, ScienceDirect, Web of Science/Scopus, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar to conduct the structured narrative review. We screened articles published from January 2020 to September 2025 using combinations of keywords, including green synthesis, characterisation, phytochemicals, drug delivery, plant-mediated nanoparticles, and nanotoxicology. We included articles only if they reported a synthesis mechanism, physicochemical characterisation, or a biomedical/toxicological outcome. Silicon application improves drought tolerance in peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) under variable planting densities
abstract: Although silicon (Si) fertilization and increased planting density have individually shown promising results in improving crop growth and yield, little is known about their combined effects, particularly under drought conditions. This study evaluated the effects of Si concentrations (0, 50, 100 and 200 ppm) and planting density (5, 10 and 15 plants pot−1) simultaneously on growth responses of peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) under two water regimes (well-watered: 60% water holding capacity (WHC) and water stress: 20% WHC) in the greenhouse. Si significantly enhanced most shoot parameters across water treatments. Higher planting density (15 plants pot−1) significantly reduced most shoot growth parameters while promoting root attributes regardless of water treatments. Si stimulated proline accumulation by 312.7% under water-stressed conditions compared with 170.0% under well-watered conditions. Proline concentration was positively correlated (r = 0.46, P < 0.01) with peroxidase activity. All these results indicate that Si application combined with appropriate planting density can potentially improve peanut plant performance under drought stress while enhancing land-use efficiency in water-limited and land-scarce agricultural systems. This study also suggests future research to evaluate the combined effects of Si fertilization and planting density on the yield attributes of peanut …

title: Correlation and Path Coefficients Analysis of Yield and Yield Attributes in Indian Mustard (Brassica juncea L.)
abstract: A field experiment was conducted during the Rabi season 2024–2025 at the Pili Kothi Farm of T.D.P.G. College, Jaunpur. The breeding material comprised ten varieties and one check variety of Indian mustard, namely Kranti, RH-406, Laxmi, Seeta, DRMR-15-31, Pusa Mustard 21, Radhika, Maya, Brijraj, Pusa Agrani, and Varuna (check variety). Thus, a total of eleven genotypes were evaluated in a randomized block design (RBD) with three replications. The genotypes were obtained from the Directorate of Rapeseed and Mustard Research, Bharatpur, Rajasthan, and Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. Correlation analysis revealed that seed yield per plant (SYPP) had a positive and significant association with length of main raceme (LMR), indicating its importance in yield improvement. Positive but non-significant associations were observed between SYPP and harvest index (HI), plant height (PH), and leaf area index (LAI). The number of siliquae per plant (NSP), test weight (TSW), and seeds per siliqua (SPS) showed weak or negative associations with seed yield. Overall, LMR, HI, and PH may be useful selection criteria for improving seed yield in Indian mustard. Path analysis revealed that LMR had a positive and significant correlation with SYPP and exerted a high positive direct effect, identifying it as an important selection criterion. Harvest i…

title: الاستراتيجية الكبرى الروسية في مرحلة ما بعد الحرب الباردة: تحليل مقارن لوثائق الأمن القومي (1993–2021) في ضوء نظريات القوة والتعددية القطبية
abstract: على الرغم من الأهمية الكبرى التي يحتلها التحليل الوثائقي المنهجي لاستراتيجيات الأمن القومي الروسي، يظل الفهم المقارن التراكمي لتطور هذه الوثائق عبر مراحلها المتعاقبة محدوداً في الأدبيات العربية المتخصصة في الدراسات الاستراتيجية. تهدف هذه الدراسة إلى تحليل الاستراتيجيات الكبرى لروسيا الاتحادية في مرحلة ما بعد الحرب الباردة، عبر فحص خمس وثائق أمن قومي متعاقبة امتدت من عام 1993 إلى عام 2021، وتشخيص عناصر القوة الصلبة والناعمة التي وظّفتها موسكو في كل مرحلة. اعتمدت الدراسة على المناهج الوصفي التحليلي والمقارن والتاريخي، وأدوات تحليل المضمون للوثائق الرسمية الروسية، مستندةً إلى بيانات كمية من مصادر دولية بارزة كمعهد ستوكهولم الدولي لأبحاث السلام (SIPRI) وصندوق النقد الدولي وموقع غلوبال فاير باور. كشفت النتائج أن الاستراتيجية الروسية مرّت بثلاث مراحل متمايزة: انفتاح فاشل على الغرب في عهد يلتسين، وتأكيد نفوذ متصاعد في عهد بوتين، ثم مواجهة مفتوحة مع الغرب في أعقاب حرب جورجيا عام 2008. وتكشف المؤشرات الكمية عمق هذا التحول؛ إذ بلغ الإنفاق العسكري الروسي 86.4 مليار دولار عام 2022، وتحتل قواتها المسلحة المرتبة الثانية عالمياً من بين 138 جيشاً، فيما تمتلك نحو 1600 رأس حربي نووي استراتيجي منتشر، في حين لا يتجاوز ناتجها المحلي الإجمالي (2.2 تريليون دولار عام 2022) 9% من الناتج الأمريكي، مما يكشف عن تفاوت بنيوي حاد بين الطموح العسكري والقدرة الاقتصادية. وتبقى قدرات القوة الناعمة الروسية محدودة قياساً بإسقاطها للقوة الصلبة. تُسهم هذه الدراسة في سد الفجوة المعرفية المُشار إليها من خلال تقديم إطا…

title: Hubungan Power Tungkai dan Ketepatan Shooting Sepak Bola di SMA Negeri 11 Muaro Jambi
abstract: Ketepatan shooting menjadi sebuah keterampilan yang sangat penting dalam permainan sepak bola karena keterampilan ini menjadi sebuah penyelesaian dalam pertandingan permainan sepak bola pada saat melakukan serangan dan mencari peluang dalam mencetak gol. Kualitas shooting tidak hanya dipengaruhi oleh penguasaan teknik saja, tetapi juga didukung oleh kondisi fisik pemain, salah satunya kemampuan power tungkai. Adapun dilakukannya penelitian ini ialah untuk mengetahui hubungan diantara power tungkai dan ketepatan shooting pada peserta ekstrakurikuler sepak bola di SMA Negeri 11 Muaro Jambi. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode korelasional. Populasi pada penelitian ini berjumlah 25 siswa. Dimana seluruh anggota populasi dijadikan sampel melalui teknik total sampling. Pengumpulan data dalam penelitian dilakukan menggunakan tes Standing Broad Jump untuk mengukur power tungkai dan tes shooting ke sasaran untuk mengukur ketepatan shooting. Data dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif dan korelasi Pearson Product Moment setelah memenuhi persyaratan uji normalitas dan linearitas. Hasil penelitian yang diperoleh dari penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa terdapat hubungan positif dan signifikan antara power tungkai dan ketepatan shooting dengan nilai koefisien korelasi sebesar 0,662 dan nilai signifikansi 0,001 (<0,05). Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa siswa yang m…

title: Farg'ona viloyati sharoitida takroriy ekilgan mosh navlari uchun ekish muddati, ko'chat qalinligi va oziqlantirish me'yorlarini maqbullashtirish
abstract: Maqolada Farg'ona viloyati sug'oriladigan yerlari sharoitida kuzgi bug'doydan keyin takroriy ekilgan mosh navlari uchun ekish muddatlari, ko'chat qalinligi va mineral oziqlantirish me'yorlarini o'zaro uyg'unlashtirish masalalari tahlil qilindi. Takroriy ekinda vegetatsiya davrining cheklanganligi sababli ekishni kechiktirmaslik, maqbul ko'chat sonini shakllantirish hamda fosfor-kaliy fonida mo'tadil azotli oziqlantirish hosildorlikni belgilovchi asosiy omillar sifatida qaraldi. Namunaviy tajriba sxemasida uch ekish muddati, uch ko'chat qalinligi va uch oziqlantirish darajasi qiyoslandi. Model hisoblarda 20–25 iyun muddatida ekish, 350–400 ming tup/ga atrofidagi ko'chat qalinligi hamda N30P60K40 kg/ga darajasidagi oziqlantirish moshning hosil elementlari va don hosildorligini shakllantirish uchun nisbatan qulay kombinatsiya sifatida namoyon bo'ldi. Maqolada keltirilgan miqdoriy ko'rsatkichlar tajriba maketini shakllantirish uchun namunaviy bo'lib, yakuniy nashrda muallifning haqiqiy dala ma'lumotlari bilan aniqlashtirilishi lozim.

title: Yeryong'oqning "Salomat" navida tup qalinligi va o'simliklar saqlanuvchanligiga ekish sxemasi, mineral o'g'it va biostimulyatorlarning ta'siri
abstract: В статье анализируется влияние схем посева, норм минеральных удобрений и биостимуляторов «Оксигумат Экстра» и «Рокогумин» на густоту всходов и сохранность растений арахиса сорта «Саломат» в условиях орошаемых лугово-сероземных почв Андижанской области. В 2021 году изучались схемы 70×10-1 и 70×20-1, фоны минерального питания N60P110K40 и N90P165K65 кг/га, а также биостимуляторы в нормах 1, 2 и 3 л/га. Средняя сохранность растений составила 98,98% при схеме 70×10-1 и 99,36% при схеме 70×20-1. При повышенном фоне минерального питания отмечена тенденция к снижению гибели растений. Наиболее устойчивые низкие показатели выпадения растений наблюдались преимущественно при применении биостимуляторов в нормах 2-3 л/га.

title: Flower bulbs protect faithful chromosome segregation in Lycoris meiosis under heat stress
Efisiensi Biaya dan Skala Ekonomi PLTA dan PLTP PT PLN Indonesia Power: Pendekatan Frontier Stokastik
abstract: The transition toward a low-carbon electricity system has made the cost efficiency of renewable energy power plants, particularly hydropower (PLTA) and geothermal power plants (PLTP), a strategic issue. This study aims to measure cost efficiency, estimate cost–input elasticities and economies of scale, and identify the determinants of inefficiency in power plants managed by PT PLN Indonesia Power. The study uses a balanced panel dataset comprising 22 power plant units over the 2016–2025 period, yielding 220 unit-year observations. The analysis employs the Generalized True Random Effects Stochastic Frontier Analysis (GTRE-SFA), combined with a linearly homogeneous translog cost function and a heteroskedastic inefficiency model. The results indicate that the translog function combined with GTRE-SFA is the most appropriate specification. The average cost efficiency across all units is 0.832, with hydropower plants achieving 0.879 and geothermal plants 0.743. The economies of scale value of 1.247 indicates the potential to reduce average costs through capacity expansion. Plant age, installed capacity, capacity factor, equivalent availability factor, and technology type are significant determinants of inefficiency. These findings provide insights for optimizing asset management, maintenance strategies, and renewable energy capacity planning to improve operational cost efficiency.
venue: Journal of Sustainability and Science Economics

title: CLE25 peptide enhances drought tolerance in cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) by inducing abscisic acid biosynthesis
abstract: Drought is a leading abiotic factor affecting agricultural productivity. While AtCLE25 enhances drought tolerance by inducing abscisic acid (ABA) accumulation in Arabidopsis thaliana, the mechanisms by which GhCLE25 regulates drought tolerance in cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) remain unclear. In this study, the role of GhCLE25 in cotton drought tolerance was investigated using virus-induced gene silencing and exogenous CLE25 peptide treatment. GhCLE25 expression was significantly induced in both roots and leaves under natural and polyethylene glycol 6000 (PEG 6000)-simulated drought. Silencing GhCLE25 inhibited stomatal closure, increased water loss, and decreased drought tolerance, whereas exogenous CLE25 improved drought tolerance by inducing stomatal closure. Consistently, ABA content was decreased in GhCLE25-silenced plants but increased in CLE25-treated plants. Silencing GhCLE25 downregulated ABA biosynthetic genes (NCED2, NCED3, NCED5, and NCED9) but upregulated the ABA catabolic gene CYP707A1. Conversely, the expression of ABA biosynthetic and catabolic genes showed an opposite trend under CLE25 peptide treatment. Moreover, the ABA-responsive genes Late Embryogenesis Abundant (LEA) and RD29B were reduced in GhCLE25-silencing plants but increased following CLE25 treatment. Thus, these results suggest that GhCLE25 may regulate ABA levels by modulating the expression of ABA me…

title: Analysis of the Power Output and Efficiency of a 100-Wp Photovoltaic Module with Varying Glass Reflector Inclinations
abstract: Flat glass reflectors offer a simple method for increasing the solar irradiance received by a photovoltaic (PV) module. However, reflector inclination may influence both electrical output and conversion efficiency. This study investigated the power output and efficiency of a 100-Wp PV module fitted with two flat glass reflectors at inclination angles of 15°, 30°, and 45°. An identical 100-Wp module without reflectors was used as the reference. Outdoor measurements were conducted at the Mechanical Engineering Laboratory, Universitas Muslim Indonesia, Makassar, from 8 to 10 February 2026. Each reflector angle was evaluated on a separate day, with solar irradiance, voltage, current, and output power recorded at 10:00, 12:00, and 14:00 WITA. Incident solar power and conversion efficiency were calculated independently for both modules using the measured irradiance and a module area of 0.6901 m². The reflector-assisted module produced higher output power at all nine measurement points, with increases ranging from 2.89% to 20.86%. The maximum output power was 76.1 W at a reflector inclination of 15° and 12:00 WITA, compared with 71.0 W for the reference module. At the same observation point, the corrected efficiency of the reflector-assisted module was 10.76%, while the reference module reached 11.16%. The findings indicate that the glass reflectors consistently increased the power ou…

title: Kaleidoscope Analysis: a multi-theoretical framework for exploring lived experience, identity and structural power
abstract: Purpose Kaleidoscope Analysis is a multi-theoretical framework for examining how lived experience, identity and structural power interact within qualitative research. The framework responds to limitations in existing methods, many of which engage experiential, identity based and structural perspectives without an explicit framework for integrating them, by offering an approach that holds these analytic planes in dynamic relation. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in a critical realist ontology, intersectionality as a non-negotiable analytic foundation and informed by Black feminist epistemology, Kaleidoscope Analysis integrates three lenses: Lived Experience, Intersectionality and Structural–Systemic Analysis. Analytic movement is conceptualised as kaleidoscopic: shifting vantage points reveal different patterns of meaning, allowing idiographic depth to sit alongside critical, systemic interpretation and giving rise to an Integrative Kaleidoscopic View. Positionality operates as method, recognising researchers as situated knowers whose identities and structural locations shape interpretive insight. A worked example from the author's empirical study illustrates how the lenses interact in practice. Findings Kaleidoscope Analysis illuminates patterned relationships between individual meaning making, intersecting identities and socio-political structures. Moving across lenses en…

Assessment of Integrated Nutrient Management for Enhancing Productivity of Barley (Hordeum vulgare L.)
abstract: Barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) productivity depends on balanced nutrient supply, and integrated nutrient management offers a means of combining mineral fertilisers with organic nutrient sources. A field experiment was conducted during the Rabi season of 2025–26 at the Agricultural Research Farm, Faculty of Agriculture, Tantia University, Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, to assess combinations of the recommended dose of fertilisers (RDF), farmyard manure (FYM), and vermicompost. The experiment used a randomised block design with three replications and eight treatments ranging from the control to 100%, 75%, and 50% RDF combined with FYM or vermicompost. Yield attributes and yield differed among treatments. Treatment T₄ (100% RDF + vermicompost at 2.5 t/ha) recorded the highest number of effective tillers (322.33/m²), grains per spike (49.64), spike length (8.21 cm), test weight (42.59 g), grain yield (54.72 q/ha), straw yield (60.77 q/ha), and biological yield (115.49 q/ha). These responses were generally followed by T₃ (100% RDF + FYM at 10 t/ha) and T₂ (100% RDF). Harvest index did not differ significantly among treatments and ranged from 45.10% to 47.76%. Under the conditions of this experiment, the combination of 100% RDF with vermicompost produced the highest measured yield attributes and yields, indicating the potential value of integrating organic nutrient sources with the recommen…

Smoking and the Need to Belong: Peer Conformity as a Psychosocial Determinant among Junior High School Adolescents
abstract: Adolescent smoking is not simply an individual choice; it is embedded in everyday relationships and the need to belong. Peer conformity is particularly relevant during adolescence, when acceptance by friends can shape decisions about risky behaviors. This study examined the association between peer conformity and smoking behavior among male students at SMP Negeri 19 Kota Serang. An analytic cross-sectional design was used, with total sampling involving 95 ninth-grade students. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed using the Chi-square test. Fifty-one participants (53.7%) were classified in the high peer-conformity category, and 54 (56.8%) were classified in the high smoking-behavior category. Cross-tabulation showed that high smoking behavior occurred in 34 of 44 participants (77.3%) with low peer conformity and in 20 of 51 participants (39.2%) with high peer conformity. Peer conformity was significantly associated with smoking behavior (p = 0.001; OR = 0.190). These findings highlight peer conformity as a relevant psychosocial process within adolescent smoking behavior and show that the relationship is embedded in a broader social context in which all participants had a family member who smoked. School-based prevention should therefore move beyond communicating the harms of smoking to include refusal skills, assertive communication, supportive peer n…

title: ENERGY SECURITY AND THE CASPIAN STATUS: A QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF PUBLIC STRATEGIC RISK PERCEPTIONS
abstract: This study combines legal analysis with empirical data on public risk perception to examine the impact of the Caspian Sea legal regime on Azerbaijan’s energy security. While the 2018 Aktau Convention is a milestone, unresolved delimitation issues and environmental concerns continue to pose strategic risks. Using a survey of 433 participants and statistical analysis (Factor Analysis, Regression), the study reveals that Geopolitical and Cyber risks are the main drivers of overall risk perception. Furthermore, regression results show that increased awareness of environmental and security risks is significantly associated with public support for the transition to renewable energy sources. The results suggest that ensuring Azerbaijan’s long-term energy security requires not only resolving legal disputes in the Caspian, but also accelerating green energy diversification to reduce perceived environmental and geopolitical threats.

title: Geopolitical risk, artificial intelligence, and clean energy markets: Nonlinear effects and dynamic connectedness
abstract: This study examines the dynamic relationships among geopolitical risk, artificial intelligence (AI), and clean energy markets. The Geopolitical Risk Index (GPR) is used to represent geopolitical risk; the STOXX Global Artificial Intelligence Index, Indxx Global Robotics & Artificial Intelligence Index, and Nasdaq CTA Artificial Intelligence & Robotics Index represent AI markets; and the FTSE Environmental Opportunities Renewable & Alternative Energy Index, NASDAQ Clean Edge Green Energy Index, and S&P Global Clean Energy Index represent clean energy markets. Using daily data from December 18, 2017 to May 1, 2026, the study employs Wavelet Quantile-on-Quantile Regression (WQQR), Quantile-on-Quantile Connectedness (QQCON), and Frequency Quantile Connectedness (FQCON) approaches. The findings reveal that the effects of geopolitical risk on AI and clean energy markets are nonlinear, heterogeneous, and dependent on market regimes and time horizons. Moreover, AI and clean energy markets exhibit asymmetric connectedness, while their net transmitter and receiver roles vary across quantiles and over time. These findings provide important implications for investors, portfolio managers, and policymakers regarding risk management, portfolio diversification, and the coordination of green and digital transformation policies.

title: AI-Enabled Intelligent Energy Optimisation for Smart Commercial Infrastructure Using IoT and Digital Twin Technologies
abstract: Intelligent, sustainable management systems are needed to address rapid urbanisation and rising energy consumption in commercial facilities. Traditional Building Management Systems (BMS) are reactive, non-predictive, and non-automated, and they lack AI support for decision-making. This paper introduces EcoMind, an Internet of Things (IoT)- based intelligent energy optimisation framework for smart commercial infrastructures, supported by artificial intelligence. It is implemented in a cloud-native system that incorporates IoT telemetry simulation, predictive analytics, Digital Twin monitoring, sustainability assessment, and a telemetry-based conversational AI module. Anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, occupancy-aware intelligence, and rule-based optimisation mechanisms provide real-time analysis of HVAC, lighting, elevator, escalator, parking, and environmental sensor data. The definitions used for this study are as follows: occupancy utilisation: ratio of actual occupancy over maximum occupancy; total energy consumption: total energy consumed by HVAC, lighting, elevator, escalator and parking systems; anomaly deviation: dif erence between the current sensor reading and the historical normal behaviour; optimisation efficiency: ratio of reduction in energy consumption after applying optimisation strategies to the total energy consumption. The major innovation is using the…

title: Rational design of multifunctional pseudohalide anions for synergistic defect passivation and suppressed ion migration in perovskite solar cells
abstract: To enhance both the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), an ideal interface needs to be formed; that is, defect passivation, efficient charge transport and suppression of ion migration must be achieved simultaneously. We rationally designed a series of multifunctional pseudohalide (PH) anions in this study, including APCA, APCA2OH, and APCA3OH, and systematically and synergistically regulated the interfacial properties by introducing functional groups such as -COO-, -OH, -NH2, -CN, and aromatic rings. First-principles calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations indicate that the optimal APCA3OH molecule anchors to the perovskite surface via strong multidentate chelation. Cooperative coordination can reduce both deep and shallow trap states effectively by breaking up the harmful Pb3 trimers and Pb2 dimers associated with Pb-I antisite (PbI) and iodine vacancy (VI) defects. From an electronic standpoint, the intrinsic dipole moments of the designed PH anions can adjust the surface work function to reduce the energy-level mismatch at the electron-selective contact and promote non-radiative carrier extraction. In addition, the synergistic chemical bonding and prominent steric hindrance caused by the ortho-hydroxyl group in APCA3OH increase the activation energy for iodide migration to 10.72 eV and thus inhibit halide diffusion. The functio…

title: A system dynamics approach to energy, green spaces, and sustainability in cities
abstract: This study applies a system dynamics modelling framework to assess long-term sustainability strategies for urban environments across four policy scenarios, focusing on energy production, land use, and consumption behaviour. Scenario 1 simulates the expansion of solar infrastructure to meet rising energy demands, resulting in significant carbon dioxide emission reductions and improved quality-of-life indicators – consistent with prior research on renewable energy benefits. Scenario 2 evaluates regulatory interventions aimed at conserving green spaces and controlling construction activities. The outcomes include increased vegetation cover and a notable decline in urban pollution, supporting evidence from urban ecological planning studies. Scenario 3 integrates the first two strategies, yielding optimal results in reducing emissions and enhancing livability; however, these improvements also attract higher population inflows, increasing energy demand. To address this challenge, Scenario 4 introduces a targeted energy efficiency strategy, incorporating per-capita consumption controls through technological advancements and behavioural change mechanisms. This scenario achieves a 35% reduction in total energy use and a 25% decline in carbon dioxide emissions. The findings highlight the synergistic potential of combined policy approaches and underscore the importance of managing rebound…

title: Supervised Classification via Energy-Based Learning on CIFAR10 CIFAR100 and CELEBA
abstract: This research evaluates a Joint Energy Model (JEM) approach to perform supervised classification on the CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and CELEBA datasets. We implement a range of architectures, including custom shallow and deep CNNs and an adapted ResNet-18 modified with 3x3 first-layer convolution to prevent the loss of critical spatial information for small image classification. Following a rigorous experimental protocol involving multiple independent runs, we provide statistical validation via mean and standard deviation for all performance metrics. Our models achieved F1-scores exceeding 86% for both CIFAR datasets and a 90.34% accuracy of CELEBA multi-label classification. Beyond accuracy, we conducted a systematic analysis of the learned energy landscapes. While results confirm a systemic calibration failure in standard discriminative training for CIFAR objects, they reveal the emergence of a robust, globally coherent “face manifold” detector for the CELEBA dataset. These findings quantify the calibration limitations of standard classifiers and demonstrate how post-hoc energy interpretation can reveal the underlying structure of learned visual representations.

title: The The Effect of Celery (Apium graveolens L.) Fermentation Solution as a Natural Biopreservative and Storage Duration on the Physical Quality and Total Plate Count of Muscovy Duck (Cairina moschata) Meat
abstract: Muscovy duck (Cairina moschata) meat has high nutritional value. However, it also has certain shortcomings such as a relatively tougher texture, a distinct, pungent odor and susceptible to microbial contamination.This study aimed to analyze the effects of celery (Apium graveolens L.) fermentation solution as a natural biopreservative and storage duration on the physical quality and Total Plate Count (TPC) of muscovy duck (Cairina moschata) meat. The physical quality parameters observed included pH, cooking loss, water-holding capacity and TPC. The study used a completely randomized design (CRD) with a factorial pattern involving two factors: the dose of celery fermentation solution (P0 = 0 mL, P1 = 60 mL, P2 = 80 mL, and P3 = 100 mL) and storage duration (L0 = 0 hours, L1 = 12 hours, L2 = 24 hours, and L3 = 36 hours). Each treatment combination was replicated twice. The results showed that the application of the celery fermentation solution and storage duration affected the physical quality and microbial count of duck meat. Increasing the dose of the celery fermentation solution reduced the pH value and cooking loss, increased water-holding capacity, and reduced the Total Plate Count. The treatment combination of 100 mL of celery fermentation solution and 12 hours of storage produced better physical quality characteristics and microbial counts compared to the other treatments. …

title: Association of Program Performance and Community Participation in Posyandu Activities with Nutritional Status among Children Under Five
abstract: Childhood malnutrition remains a major public health concern in Indonesia, characterized by the coexistence of undernutrition and increasing overnutrition. Community-based growth monitoring through Posyandu plays an important role in monitoring child nutritional status, as reflected in program performance (N/D) and community participation coverage (D/S). This analytical observational study employed a cross-sectional design using secondary data from the SiGizi system of Puskesmas Pohjentrek, Pasuruan District, collected in August 2024. All registered children under five years of age were included using total sampling. The independent variables were N/D and D/S, while nutritional status as the dependent variable was assessed according to WHO standards using weight-for-age (WAZ), height-for-age (HAZ), and weight-for-height (WHZ). Data were analyzed descriptively and using chi-square tests. Most children had normal nutritional status, although undernutrition and overnutrition were still observed. The mean N/D and D/S were 47.66% and 87.57%, respectively. N/D was not significantly associated with WAZ or HAZ (p>0.05), but was significantly associated with WHZ (p<0.05). In contrast, D/S was significantly associated with all anthropometric indicators (p<0.001). These findings indicate that community participation in Posyandu is more broadly associated with child nutritional status than…

title: Leveraging Trail Running Events for Local Sport Participation: The Role of Event Organizers Mountain Marathon Festival in Indonesia
abstract: Trail running events can create entry points into physical activity, but sustained local sport participation depends on how organizers connect event exposure with preparation, social support, stakeholder networks, and post-event opportunities. This study analyzes the role of the Mountain Marathon Festival (MMF) event organizer across the Sembalun Mountain Marathon (SMF), Bali Mountain Marathon (BMF), and Java Mountain Marathon (JMM). Using a qualitative embedded single-case design, the study comprised 42 informants, 12 observation sessions, and 58 event documents collected in 2025. Data were analyzed thematically through within-unit and cross-event comparison, informed primarily by sport event leveraging and social capital, with self-determination theory used as a supplementary lens. The findings show that the organizer functioned as an experience designer, participation facilitator, and network broker. Twenty-four community-facing informants reported increased knowledge of trail running, while 17 reported increased physical activity during event preparation; 11 joined group training more regularly, eight entered a trail-running event for the first time, and six volunteers began training to become participants. Ten of the 17 informants who increased activity were still training regularly two to three months after the event, indicating a legacy gap. Cross-event comparison showed…

title: From goal framing to participation experience: a cognitive-affective process perspective on mass participation sport events
abstract: Purpose This study opens the “psychological black box” of participation experiences in mass participation sport events (MPSEs) by examining how goal frames are associated with experiential outcomes through cognitive engagement and psychological empowerment. Drawing on goal-framing theory and the cognitive-affective processing system (CAPS), it proposes a process model linking goal frames to participation experiences, with social connectedness as a boundary condition. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted with participants in Taiwan who had engaged in non-elite sport events within the past year (N = 405). Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM with bootstrapping, employing established scales to measure goal framing, cognitive engagement, psychological empowerment, event enjoyment, subjective vitality, and social connectedness. Findings All three goal frames were positively associated with cognitive engagement and psychological empowerment. Cognitive engagement was positively associated with both event enjoyment and subjective vitality, whereas psychological empowerment was positively associated with subjective vitality but not event enjoyment. Social connectedness significantly moderated the relationship between psychological empowerment and subjective vitality, while the other moderation effects were not statistically significant. The indirect effects furthe…

title: The Relationship Between Mothers' Participation Levels in Posyandu and the Nutritional Status of Children Under Five
abstract: Nutritional issues among toddlers remain a public health concern, and the monitoring of growth and early detection of nutritional problems at Posyandu (integrated healthcare posts) are influenced by the level of maternal participation. This study aimed to examine the relationship between the level of maternal participation in Posyandu activities and the nutritional status of toddlers in Tanjung Botung Village, Padang Lawas Regency. A quantitative approach was employed using an analytical observational, cross-sectional study design. The study population consisted of 185 mothers with toddlers aged 0–59 months, from which a sample of 125 participants was selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected through questionnaires and anthropometric measurements, then analyzed using the Chi-Square test with a significance level of 0.05. The findings indicate that 77 mothers (61.6%) demonstrated an active level of participation, while 48 mothers (38.4%) were less active. The majority of the toddlers (64, or 51.2%) were classified k as having poor nutritional status, whereas 36 toddlers (28.8%) had a normal nutritional status. The study revealed a significant relationship between the level of maternal participation in Posyandu and the nutritional status of toddlers, with a p-value of 0.002 (p < 0.05). Increasing maternal participation, providing nutrition education, and strengthenin…

title: Sn@C Composite with an Ultra-high Initial Coulombic Efficiency via Interfacial Engineering for Sodium-Ion Battery Anodes
abstract: Abstract Tin (Sn)-based anodes are attractive candidates for sodium-ion batteries due to their high theoretical capacity and low operating potential. However, their practical viability is severely constrained by drastic volume changes, unstable solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation, and intrinsically low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE). Herein, an interfacial regulation strategy to enhance the ICE and cycling stability of Sn-based anodes is proposed. That is, we construct Sn-MOF-derived Sn@C composites with submicron Sn particles uniformly confined in a conductive carbon matrix via hydrothermal synthesis and subsequent pyrolysis. This architecture yields an exceptional ICE of 96.4% (725/752 mA h g–1 at 0.1 A g–1), far surpassing that of commercial Sn powder (77.9%). Mechanistic investigations reveal a reversible stepwise alloying pathway from Sn to Na9Sn4 and subsequently to Na15Sn4, while the carbon matrix promotes a thin, uniform NaF-rich SEI that curbs electrolyte decomposition and Na+ loss. In situ EIS-DRT analysis further corroborates the progressive reduction of interfacial resistances during sodiation–desodiation. As a result, the anode sustains 378 mA h g–1 after 500 cycles at 1 A g–1. title: Engineering a closed-loop electrochemical pathway for cadmium recovery and aqueous battery reutilization
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) waste is an unavoidable toxic by-product of zinc processing, but its electrochemical reutilization remains limited by the lack of routes that couple selective recovery with stable metal-anode operation. Here, we report a closed-loop electrochemical strategy that transforms model Cd-containing waste electrolytes into regenerable aqueous Cd metal anodes. A three-step potential-programmed electrodeposition process selectively recovers Cd while constructing compact Cd(002)-textured electrodes with tunable areal capacity. To preserve this recovered structure during cycling, cesium iodide is introduced to reconstruct the Cd-electrolyte interface, enabling iodide-dominated and cesium-assisted regulation of desolvation, ion flux, corrosion, and Cd growth. The resulting Cd anode achieves 99.98% average Coulombic efficiency and stable high-rate plating/stripping. Cd||I 2 coin and pouch cells validate full-cell operation under high loading and reduced excess Cd. Failed Cd anodes can be reextracted, regenerated, and reused, completing a recovery-operation-regeneration loop.

Life cycle assessments of vehicle components: an overview
abstract: Abstract The development and manufacturing of automotive components with reduced environmental impacts is needed to decrease the overall ecological burden of vehicles. Although individual vehicle components have been scientifically evaluated and the findings published for decades, there is still a lack of a summarized listing of these case studies. This study presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of life cycle assessments (LCAs) on vehicle components, excluding batteries and tires. After exclusion of unrelated publications, 129 results were used for further analysis. This sample contains 160 LCA studies conducted since 1995. The analysis identified recurring themes and key trends in impact categories, methodologies, and software tools. Structural and powertrain components appeared to be the most frequently assessed. While lightweight and material selection emerged as the most prominent and still trending aspects, climate change and energy demand turned out as to be dominant indicators. Besides insights into the current state of LCA implementation within the automotive (supply) industry, this research also reveals a few gaps.

title: Does the opsen scheme reduce provincial tax effectiveness? Motor vehicle tax and title transfer fee in North Sulawesi Province
abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of motor vehicle tax (PKB) and motor vehicle title transfer fee (BBNKB) revenue in North Sulawesi Province over 2021–2025, a period that spans the implementation of Law Number 1 of 2022 on Financial Relations between the Central Government and Regional Governments (UU HKPD) and the introduction of the opsen (tax-sharing surcharge) scheme. A descriptive quantitative approach is used, supported by qualitative data. Effectiveness is measured as the ratio of revenue realization to target and classified using the criteria of Ministry of Home Affairs Decree Number 690.900.327 of 1996. Target, realization, and opsen data were obtained from the Regional Revenue Agency (BAPENDA) of North Sulawesi Province, and interviews with three BAPENDA officials were used to interpret the results. PKB effectiveness remained in the “effective” category in every year (90.43%–96.89%) except 2022, when it reached 101.22% (“very effective”). BBNKB effectiveness was more volatile (79.82%–96.77%) and fell to “less effective” (79.82%) in 2025, the first year of full opsen implementation. Adding the opsen revenue distributed directly to district/city governments (Rp187.65 billion), combined PKB and BBNKB revenue in 2025 reached Rp698.52 billion, about 1.1% above 2024. According to the informants, the 2025 declines largely reflect this direct distribution, which removes p…

Constructing ethical leadership through talk: a linguistic analysis of CEO letters to shareholders
abstract: Purpose Drawing on hundreds of CEO letters to shareholders from companies recognised for ethical practices, this paper aims to examine how ethical leadership is constructed through discourse in CEOs’ written communication. Design/methodology/approach A dataset of 369,661 words from companies listed on the World’s Most Ethical Companies Honoree List (2019–2023) was analysed using two complementary methods: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for thematic identification and Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC-22) for quantitative linguistic analysis, benchmarked against hubristic, non-hubristic leadership communication and the general public. Findings The analysis reveals a distinct set of linguistic signals that differentiate ethical leadership communication, including a markedly higher “we” to “I” ratio, elevated clout scores and greater prosocial and analytical language. Four macro-level themes emerge as central to how ethical leadership is constructed: resilience, sustainability, organisational strategy and collaboration and cooperation. Originality/value This paper introduces a framework for ethical leadership communication that conceptualises ethical leadership as a set of socially accomplished discursive practices that manage meaning and construct organisational reality for stakeholders. It also provides the first large-scale evidence that sustainability language is cent…

title: A unified lattice–surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries
abstract: Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O 2 evolution during lattice O 2− /O 2 2− redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a “coat–sinter–wash” synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a “chemical rivet” and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g −1 (0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm −2 and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg −1 . This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

title: Analysis of the Effects of Purified Used Cooking Oil Consumption on Nutritional Absorption Status: An Anti-Stunting Promotion Strategy
abstract: Stunting remains a critical global public health priority due to its long-term impacts on cardiometabolic disorders and neurocognitive deficits resulting from chronic malnutrition. At the household level, a hidden risk factor potentially triggering infection and nutrient malabsorption is the repeated use of cooking oil (used cooking oil). Chronic exposure to foods processed with used cooking oil can lead to nutritional malabsorption, indirectly increasing the risk of stunting in children. Although the adverse effects of used cooking oil have been widely documented, exploration into the efficacy of oil purification methods in restoring or improving nutritional status remains highly limited. This study employed an experimental research design with a factorial layout. Data analysis was performed using a One-Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) to compare differences across treatment groups, followed by a Tukey Post-Hoc test to determine specific statistically significant differences among the administered treatments. The Tukey Post-Hoc test revealed that the Purified Oil Treatment group (P) yielded the highest mean hepatic protein level (9,30±0,03%). This value was statistically significant (p < 0,05) compared to all other groups, namely the Control group (7,64±0,34\%), the fresh oil group (7,99±0,26%), and the used cooking oil (J) groups (7,60±0,45%). Meanwhile, no significant differ…

title: Executive Function Decay: Why Managerial Judgment Fails Under Pressure and How Organizations Can Respond
abstract: Mental-health strain has become a routine feature of organizational life, yet managers and organizations continue to struggle to explain why capable employees make avoidable errors, why teams lose coordination under pressure, and why judgment quality deteriorates during periods of sustained stress. This article argues that executive function decay—the temporary or chronic degradation of working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility—is a central but underrecognized mechanism linking mental strain to workplace performance failures.Drawing on research from cognitive neuroscience, clinical psychology, and organizational behavior, I explain how common forms of mental-health morbidity and burnout impair the cognitive capacities that support judgment, emotional regulation, and adaptive decision-making. I show how executive function decay produces predictable patterns of managerial behavior, team dysfunction, and organizational drift that are misattributed to motivation, attitude, or character.The article introduces a multilevel framework connecting executive function impairment to outcomes at the individual, team, and organizational levels. I then translate this framework into practical implications for leaders and HR systems, highlighting how job design, leadership behavior, workload architecture, and organizational norms can either stabilize or erode cognitive capaci…

title: Summer School as an Academic Recovery Strategy After COVID-19: Evidence from Summer 2023
abstract: Abstract Many school districts used summer school as a strategy for addressing declines in student achievement after COVID-19. This study extends a prior analysis of 2022 summer programs by examining the association between 2023 program participation and academic recovery across eight large U.S. districts and, in four districts, comparing students who participated in both summers with students who participated in 2023 for the first time. Using value-added models, we find modest but significant improvements in student math achievement (average effect = 0.024 standard deviations) associated with participating in 2023, but no significant improvements in reading. Estimates were similar to 2022, despite small declines in participation and dosage. In the subsample of four districts, we find students attending for a second consecutive summer generally benefited as much or more than first-time attendees.

Blue Growth Under Fiscal Constraints: A Qualitative Literature-Based Cost-Benefit Assessment of Maritime Industrialization as a Strategy to Mitigate Pakistan’s Balance of Payments Crisis
abstract: Pakistan has been grappling with balance of payments problems for decades. Pakistan is still faced with the threat of lack of foreign exchange because the tendency of imports is faster than that of exports. The major reason for this is the high dependency on energy, industrial equipment and raw materials. In this case, maritime industrialization appears to be a potential solution. The large coast line offers a significant unexploited potential in Pakistan in the maritime industries like shipping, ports, fisheries, shipbuilding, coastal tourism and others. This paper seeks to establish whether maritime industrialization may serve as a buffer for the balance of payments issues that Pakistan is experiencing under stringent budget constraints. The study employs a qualitative analysis framework as opposed to a quantitative approach, survey, or economic test. It shows that maritime industrialization can be relied upon to help stabilize Pakistan’s external sector as long as the process is pursued in a strategic, gradual, and well-governed manner. Some of the advantages of pursuing this approach include diversification of exports, reduction of logistics costs, creation of jobs, improved port performance, foreign investments, and decreased reliance on external shipping companies. The challenges associated with this approach are also significant, including huge financial requirements, in…

title: Volumetric dilution nasal spray as a harm reduction strategy for intranasal psychoactive substance use: a practical framework and rationale
abstract: Abstract Background Intranasal insufflation of psychoactive substances, including cocaine, MDMA, and ketamine, is associated with a well-documented spectrum of nasal and sinonasal complications. These result from at least three distinct but interacting mechanisms: mechanical trauma from particulate matter, vasoconstriction-induced mucosal ischaemia (primarily relevant for cocaine), and chemical irritation from adulterants. Harm reduction (HR) programmes have traditionally focused on hygiene, shared equipment, and product testing, but the form of the substance itself, solid powder versus aqueous solution, has received little formal attention. Main body Volumetric dilution nasal spray (VDNS) is an approach in which the substance is dissolved in sterile saline and delivered via a calibrated spray device. This method eliminates mechanical mucosal trauma from powder particles, delivers the substance in a hydrated vehicle compatible with mucosal physiology, and converts an uncontrolled line-based dosing practice into a quantifiable per-spray unit. Drawing on pharmaceutical nasal delivery science, existing HR resources from community organisations, and field feedback from harm reduction professionals, this article describes the rationale, practical implementation, limitations, and field integration of this approach for cocaine, MDMA, and ketamine. The method is grounded in the pharmac…

title: Estimation of Systematic Risk of Capital Asset Pricing (CAP) Model using Quantile Regression: Evidence from Pakistan Stock Exchange
abstract: Capital asset pricing (CAP) model describes a relationship between expected risk and return in pricing of risky securities. Traditionally ordinary least square regression methods focus on the means of the distributions in estimating the systematic risk of CAP model. The focuses of the present study are on quantile regression (QR) application to estimate the systematic risk, examine the behavior of stock risk along the market and to analyze the extreme values in the return distribution for the textile, food and chemical sectors of Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) at different quantiles. Volatile behavior of estimates of systematic risk was observed at the lower and upper quartiles for all the companies of these sectors. Empirical results of QR showed the significance of systematic risk at both tails of returns distribution. The findings of this study are a source of interest for risk managers and investors.

A self-powered finger-worn wireless tracking interface for human-machine interaction
abstract: Continuous touch positioning and trajectory tracking are essential for immersive human-machine interaction, yet conventional interfaces are fundamentally limited by rigid power supplies and tethered data transmission. Here, we present a completely self-powered, finger-worn interface that wirelessly transmits spatial trajectory data driven solely by biomechanical motion. The device integrates a miniaturized (3.7 cm 2 ) corona-discharge triboelectric nanogenerator with a flexible electromagnetic transmitter, converting multidirectional fingertip movement directly into wireless communication signals. By coupling these signals with three non-collinear receivers and a machine-learning-assisted decoding algorithm, the system achieves sub-millimeter localization accuracy (<0.9 mm). We demonstrate the interface’s capability for the high-fidelity reconstruction of handwritten inputs, enabling robust human-machine control. By synergizing motion-energy harvesting with precise spatial tracking, this work offers an untethered, self-contained paradigm for next-generation interactive intelligent systems.

title: Predicting 30-Day Hospital Readmission in Diabetic Patients Using Machine Learning
abstract: Hospital readmissions are a significant problem in healthcare, particularly in diabetic patients. The research question guiding this study was: Can 30-day hospital readmission for diabetic patients be predicted using common machine learning models applied to hospital record data? This study aims to predict this using three machine learning models: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost. The analysis was conducted on the Diabetes 130-US Hospitals dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository, which contains over 100,000 patient records. After data cleaning, 98,053 complete records with 20 features were used for model training and evaluation. Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy at 88.73%, Logistic Regression at 88.67%, and XGBoost at 88.59%. Moreover, the XGBoost model’s Area Under the Curve (AUC) was only 0.653, indicating performance slightly better than random guessing. The number of lab procedures were found to be the strongest predictor of readmission, followed by different diagnoses and number of medications. The models struggled to identify readmitted patients due to dataset imbalance, with only 11.3% of patients readmitted. These findings suggest that while machine learning can predict readmission status with reasonable overall accuracy, current models are not reliable enough for clinical use without additional features and improved data quality.

title: An Analysis of Dimensions of English Learning Motivation among Female Secondary School Students in Quetta, Balochistan
abstract: Motivation significantly influences second and foreign language learning by impacting learners' behaviors, including their involvement, effort, persistence, and participation in related activities. This study aimed to examine the aspects of English learning motivation of female secondary school students in government schools in Quetta, Pakistan. A quantitative descriptive survey design was utilized, focusing on female students in Grades 9 and 10 from government girls' secondary schools in Quetta, with a sample of 364 students chosen through simple random sampling. The data were obtained by using a structured questionnaire to measure four dimensions of English learning motivation which are namely engagement, interest, persistence, and intrinsic/extrinsic motivation. Descriptive statistics such as frequency, percentage, and mean and standard deviation were used to analyze the data. The findings showed that the students' overall level of English learning motivation was high, the mean score of which was 3.55 and the standard deviation was 0.70. The mean scores for the four dimensions were: intrinsic/extrinsic motivation (M = 3.79), interest (M = 3.68), engagement (M = 3.50), and persistence (M = 3.29). The study revealed that students exhibited a good level of motivation for learning English, although their persistence remained moderate. While overall attitudes toward learning Engl…

title: Exploring Outcomes of a Learning Theory–Driven Pilot Medical Pathway Program: A Preliminary Evaluation
abstract: Background/Introduction Premedical pathway programs serve as vehicles to advance equity and access for students who have experienced systemic barriers to education, yet few explicitly address the academic skill development necessary for success in rigorous science courses. Undergraduate premedical students face significant cognitive load, and success requires not only content knowledge but also the metacognitive learning strategies (MLS) needed to process, integrate, and retrieve information. Methods This pilot study examined whether a learning-theory-driven summer intensive delivered by a trained learning specialist was associated with statistically significant gains on the Learning and Study Strategies Inventory (LASSI) scales based on the foci of the curriculum. A pre-post design was employed with 16 students in the Program. All ten LASSI scales were administered at program entry and exit. Six scales targeted by the curriculum were designated primary outcomes, and the remaining four were reported as secondary outcomes. Open ended survey responses were analyzed using deductive thematic coding. Results/Findings Paired samples t-tests revealed significant gains on all six targeted scales, each of which remained significant after Holm correction: Information Processing (p = .011), Selecting Main Ideas (p = .012), Test Strategies (p = .003), Self-Testing (p = .003), Time Manageme…

title: Effect of Team Assisted Individualization on Fabric Embellishment Practical Learning Outcomes
abstract: Students in vocational practical courses start with uneven skills, so an instructional model has to cope with that gap without losing sight of individual accountability. This quasi-experimental pretest–posttest study compared Team Assisted Individualization (TAI) with conventional instruction in a Fabric Embellishment Techniques course of a Diploma III Fashion Design program. Two intact parallel classes of 13 students each (N = 26) took part in the second semester of academic year 2024–2025, and a lottery decided which class received TAI. Practical performance was scored on a 0–100 scale before and after instruction. The TAI class rose from 72.38 to 88.85 and the conventional class from 70.77 to 81.31, mean gains of 16.46 and 10.54 points. The classes did not differ significantly at pretest (p = .231), although the TAI class started 1.62 points higher. At posttest the difference was 7.54 points, t(24) = 4.42, p < .001, and the difference in gains was 5.92 points, t(24) = 6.48, p < .001. Because each condition was delivered to a single intact class, these student-level tests cannot separate the teaching model from class-specific influences, and the results are best treated as preliminary evidence.

title: Islamic Financial Technology (Fintech): Menjembatani Kesenjangan Literasi dan Inklusi Keuangan Syariah di Indonesia
abstract: Aims: This study aims to identify the need for Islamic financial technology (Islamic fintech) as an alternative to support Islamic financial literacy and inclusion in Indonesia. It also describes the factors that hinder the conversion of Islamic financial knowledge into the actual use of formal financial services and summarizes governance pillars, drawn from the literature and oriented toward Maqashid al-Shariah, to promote equitable and sustainable financial inclusion. Method: This study employs a library research method with a qualitative-descriptive approach. Data were collected through a review of scientific literature, regulations, and official reports relevant to Islamic financial literacy, financial inclusion, and the development of Islamic fintech in Indonesia. The literature was identified, selected, classified into five dimensions (Table 1), and synthesized descriptively to describe the literacy-inclusion gap, its contributing factors, and the opportunities and challenges of Islamic financial digitalization. The study does not apply thematic coding, empirical testing, or the development of a formal framework. Results: The findings reveal a substantial gap between Islamic financial literacy and Islamic financial inclusion in Indonesia, as reported in national survey data. This gap indicates that public knowledge has not been fully translated into the utilization of Isl…
