title: Establishment of an efficient and marker-free transformation system for major cultivars of Lycium barbarum L.
Reactive current injection based modified LVRT control for grid interfaced converter-less solar PV system
abstract: Abstract As the integration of renewables like solar PV, wind etc. with utility is increasing day by day, the main issue arises is to maintain the stability of grid. In order to maintain this criteria grid operators are frequently upgrading the grid codes. According to these grid codes, it is required that during momentary disruption in the utility side, solar PV inverters will remain connected and this aspect is often termed as low-voltage-ride-through (LVRT) of solar PV inverters. For such purpose, PV inverters are assembled with certain control logics to ensure smooth operation and ride through the disturbance period according to the grid code. This article proposed an enhanced LVRT controller for grid-connected photovoltaic inverters. The controller features an adaptive reactive current injection mechanism based on maintaining constant dc link voltage in a converter-less solar PV system. These innovations improve inverter compliance with grid codes and enhance voltage dip recovery. Simulation of grid interfaced PV system is done in MATLAB and tested on OPAL-RT during real time scenarios.
venue: International Journal of Emerging Electric Power Systems

title: ETDP: a high-performance transportation delay prediction framework with explanations for supply chains
abstract: Purpose This work aims to develop a transportation delay prediction framework to improve prediction performance while providing explanations for its predictions. Design/methodology/approach An ETDP (high-performance Transportation Delay Prediction Framework with Explanations) for supply chains is proposed, in which we design an LGFT (Local-Global Fusion Transformer) model for high-performance prediction, and integrate LGFT with SHAP to explain its predictions. LGFT captures local feature interaction patterns via 1D CNN and global nonlinear relationships via an MLP, which are then fused through a Transformer Encoder to model long-range contextual dependencies. Integrated with SHAP, ETDP formalizes a three-level explanation mechanism that can analyze global feature importance, key feature dependency, and instance-level attribution. Findings The ETDP framework is evaluated on three public supply chain datasets covering binary delay prediction, last-mile logistics, and five-class supply chain risk classification. On DataCo, ETDP achieves the highest precision and remains competitive across the other evaluation indicators. On India, it obtains the best recall, F1-score, and MCC in the held-out test evaluation. On Mendeley, it reaches the best accuracy, recall, MCC, and lowest FNR, while remaining descriptively close to XGBoost in F1-score, though below it in precision and probabilit…

title: Studying negotiation makes leaders: an empirical study on the impact of negotiation training on self-perceived emotional intelligence and leadership potential
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine whether studying negotiation with a scientific approach, combining theory and role-playing, is associated with changes in self-perceived emotional intelligence (EI) and leadership potential. Building on the view that leadership is inherently relational and that EI is a key attribute of effective leaders, the study explores the reverse relationship between negotiation and EI. More specifically, it investigates whether negotiation training, conceived as a structured form of relational and reflective practice, may strengthen individuals’ self-perceptions across four dimensions of EI: self-awareness, self-management, social awareness and relationship management. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a quasi-experimental, survey-based design. It compares graduate students enrolled in a negotiation-focused course (Experimental Group) with students attending a non-negotiation course within the same MSc program (Control Group) over four years (2021–2024). Data were collected through a web-based questionnaire administered at the beginning and at the end of each course. The analysis examines changes in self-perceived EI and leadership potential between Time 1 and Time 2 across the two groups. Findings Participants in the Experimental Group reported significant increases in self-perceived EI and leadership potential between the beginning and the e…

title: Effects of Combined Sound and Working Memory Therapy on Medial Olivocochlear System and Auditory Sensory Gating in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Preliminary Investigation Using Contralateral Suppression of Transient Evoked Otoacoustic Emission
A novel seasonal time-varying discrete grey power model and its application in solar power generation forecasting
abstract: Purpose Solar power generation exhibits significant time-varying seasonal fluctuations and nonlinear trends, which pose a challenge to existing forecasting techniques. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel grey forecasting framework that integrates seasonal decomposition, nonlinear modeling, and time-varying adaptation, namely the seasonal time-varying discrete grey power model. Design/methodology/approach Firstly, seasonal dummy variables are introduced to separate periodic fluctuations from the trend. Secondly, the seasonal effect is innovatively decomposed into fixed and time-varying components, precisely capturing the temporal evolution patterns across different periods. Concurrently, the double-power index structure quantifies the nonlinear driving effects of both historical values and temporal factors on the current state. The hiking optimization algorithm is employed for hyper-parameter tuning. Findings The new model was validated using datasets from the three major economies of the U.S., India, and China, and compared with six competitive models representing different types. Results show that the new model exhibits superior predictive accuracy. Furthermore, robustness tests across multiple time windows further validate the stability of the model under varying scenarios. Practical implications Forecasts for 2025–2027 indicate sustained growth in solar power generation a…

title: Language of care: euphemism and emotional management in Jordanian healthcare
abstract: Abstract This study explores how Jordanian physicians choose their words carefully when talking to patients about sensitive medical issues. To understand this process, a discourse completion task (DCT) was administered to 24 physicians, and responses were analyzed using both quantitative and qualitative approaches grounded in established frameworks on euphemism. The analysis revealed seven main strategies that physicians reported or produced in response to clinically plausible scenarios: synonymy, understatement, religious references, vagueness, part-for-whole substitution, overstatement, and loanwords. When discussing long-term treatment plans, their elicited responses centered on four themes: reassurance and normalization, balancing honesty with optimism, emotional and holistic support, and treatment as a manageable journey. These findings suggest that euphemism, as reflected in physicians’ pragmatic judgments and preferred formulations, is understood not merely as a politeness device but as a culturally embedded resource for managing emotional sensitivity, sustaining patient trust, and balancing accuracy with care in Jordanian healthcare communication.

title: Fluorescence Quenching and Polarization Analysis of DNA Aptamers Binding to Green Fluorescent Protein: A Model System for Protein-Binding Aptamers and Assay Development
abstract: Abstract Protein-binding aptamers are widely used in biosensing and therapeutics, yet reliable solution-phase methods for validating aptamer binding remain limited. Here, we establish green fluorescent protein (GFP) as a self-reporting benchmark system for homogeneous analysis of aptamer-protein interactions. A previously identified GFP-binding DNA aptamer, GFP-1, was modified at the 3′ terminus with a fluorescence quencher, generating a dual-readout probe that simultaneously reports binding through fluorescence quenching and fluorescence polarization. The quencher modification preserved nanomolar affinity for GFP while producing a substantially more sensitive change than polarization alone. Using this probe, we developed a homogeneous competitive displacement assay that revealed overlapping binding sites among three distinct GFP aptamers. We further implemented a reverse-chase kinetic format which enabled the direct determination of apparent dissociation rate constants (koff) from solution-phase fluorescence traces. The kinetic ranking placed GFP-1 with the slowest dissociation and GFP-3 with the quickest. Both affinity and kinetic parameters were preserved in 10% human serum, demonstrating assay robustness in complex biological media. This fluorescence-based platform operates entirely in solution and provides a practical framework for validating aptamer-target interactions, m…

title: Self-Management Behaviours and Health Literacy in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Background: Self-management of diabetes is significantly affected by health literacy; however, its role in affecting specific behaviours is not well understood. This scoping review synthesised the existing evidence on the mechanisms, mediators, and contextual factors through which health literacy influences self-management behaviours among adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). Methods: The scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodological framework and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A systematic search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar from inception to July 2026. Studies were eligible if they examined health literacy and diabetes self-management among adults with T2DM in any healthcare or community setting worldwide. Following screening, twenty-four studies were included. Data were charted and synthesised into themes based on Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory. Results: Findings were organised into two themes. Theme 1 identified cognitive, behavioural, psychological, and interpersonal mechanisms—including diabetes knowledge, self-efficacy, social support, and digital health literacy—through which health literacy influences self-management. Theme 2 identified individual, social, cult…
venue: Asian Journal of Medicine & Health Sciences

title: Profiles in safety
abstract: ABSTRACT Although today’s health care system has achieved unprecedented advances, geriatric adults remain vulnerable to iatrogenic complications associated with traditional hospitalization, including acute cognitive delirium, rapid functional decline, medical errors, and health care–associated infections. To improve patient safety, an organization initiated an acute hospital-at-home pilot program from June 2023 through February 2024. Building on the removal of prepandemic regulatory and reimbursement barriers, the pilot was formally expanded and rebranded as the Hospital From Home (HfH) Program. An evaluation of 673 patients over 25 months showed an improved safety profile, with zero serious safety events and a 7.47% 30-day unplanned readmission rate. The program achieved a 100% discharge-to-home rate while successfully managing a slightly above-average to moderately complex Case Mix Index of 1.45. Furthermore, standardized patient experience measures demonstrated higher scores across key nursing leadership domains, including nurse-to-patient communication, interdisciplinary care coordination, and overall patient satisfaction.

title: Speaking up for safety
abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Type 2 workplace violence (WPV), defined as violence perpetrated by patients or visitors against health care workers, remains a significant threat to nurse safety, well-being, and retention. Inadequate communication regarding patients’ history of violent behavior may leave nurses unprepared to manage escalating situations and contribute to underreporting of WPV incidents. Purpose: To evaluate the impact of a structured Potentially Violent Patient Handoff (PVPH) tool on nurses’ confidence in managing potentially violent patients and on Type 2 WPV reporting within an inpatient neurology/neurosurgery unit. Methods: This quality improvement project used a pre-post design over 6 months in a high-risk inpatient unit. The PVPH tool was implemented through education, stakeholder engagement, and Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles. Outcomes included nurse confidence measured by the Clinical Confidence in Coping with Patient Aggression scale, perceptions of handoff effectiveness and safety, and Type 2 WPV event reports. Results: Mean confidence scores increased from 58.1 to 66.3 following implementation. Nurses reported improvements in perceived safety, support, collaboration, and adequacy of handoff information. Agreement regarding the importance of reporting violent events increased from 69% to 88%. Although reported violent events increased from 19 to 37, reporting trends de…

title: Strategic leadership in patient safety through AI-enabled fall prevention technology
abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Inpatient falls present significant clinical and financial challenges, yet traditional prevention strategies, like bed alarms, often fail due to a multitude of reasons, such as alarm fatigue and high operational costs. Purpose: Evaluate the implementation of an AI-enabled light detection and ranging (LiDAR) sensor platform designed to mitigate inpatient falls. Methods: This quality improvement project was conducted at Emory Healthcare utilizing the CFIR 2.0 to help guide the implementation process of deploying the LiDAR sensor platform in a pilot unit with spread to several hospitals across the system. Local and system nursing leadership, along with the system’s digital team, developed the initiative, deployed the technology, and refined the process. Process and outcome metrics were collected and monitored. Results: Implementation of the LiDAR sensor platform on the pilot unit with strong local nursing leadership demonstrated a reduction in total falls and falls with injury. The implementation process that was developed with the pilot unit was utilized to implement the technology at five other hospitals across the system with their local nursing leadership. Conclusions: Integrating the LiDAR sensor platform offered a scalable, nurse-centric solution that improved patient safety outcomes for Emory Healthcare. Nurse leaders are essential when implementing inn…

title: Environmental sensitization, advocacy and resource-management training in a resource-limited paediatric surgical educational setting
abstract: Aim A policy framework for Paediatric surgical training to address sustainable surgical resource utilization and environmental-disease interplay in a low-to-middle income country (LMIC) setting is presented. Methods Using the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) Education Pillars for Sustainable Development (EPSD), existing and potential integration of environmental education in undergraduate and postgraduate paediatric surgical training is described at an LMIC academic hospital, in conjunction with a narrative review of environmental underpinnings of existing paediatric surgical English literature. Pedagogical techniques are conceptualized to demonstrate the 3-way interactions between paediatric surgical services and social/ built, economic and natural/ climactic environments, on individual and community level. This is illustrated by the context of the surgically managed congenital abdominal wall defect gastroschisis, amongst other examples. Results Gastroschisis is a Paediatric Surgical key topic that highlights the imperative for comprehensive environmentally sensitive patient-orientated care. Some curricular content and LMIC situational awareness already exists in our setting regarding resource stewardship, environmental teratogens and socioeconomic interactions. The local surgical procedure-related carbon footprints and interaction with…

title: Talent management insights from a multinational automobile company in India: a case of glocalised resilience
abstract: Purpose This study explores how a multinational automobile subsidiary in India navigates institutional duality to develop a glocalised talent management (TM) approach. It investigates the interplay between global corporate mandates and local cultural, structural and ecological constraints, offering insights into strategic human resource management within a capital-intensive automobile manufacturing sector in India. Further, this paper explores how multi-national corporations (MNC) manufacturing units are addressing the TM challenges when located in a remote industrial cluster and examines the tension between structured TM systems and the demands for agility and inclusivity. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative single-case study was conducted using semi- structured interviews with 18 senior managers and human resources (HR) professionals in an MNC Subsidiary Automobile Manufacturing Company in India, supplemented by internal documents and archival data. Analysis followed the Gioia methodology, enabling systematic data reduction from 27 first-order codes to 10 second-order themes to 04 aggregate theoretical dimensions that capture the organisation’s TM strategy. Findings The organisation achieves glocalised resilience through four interlinked mechanisms: cultural synthesis blending parent-company discipline with Indian workplace norms; structurally rigorous talent pipelines;…

title: Categories and concepts of the budget resource distribution system (Income and Expenses)
abstract: Subject. Financial categories and concepts of the budget resource allocation system. Objectives. To substantiate the essential characteristics of financial categories and concepts, to structure their semantic and value‑based foundations, and to justify the definitions of scientific terms within the system of budget revenue and expenditure allocation. Methods. General scientific methods were employed (analysis and synthesis, induction and deduction, analogy, systematization and classification, the logical method), along with empirical methods (observation, comparison) and specialized methods of economic analysis. Results. The essential characteristics of the key financial categories and concepts within the system of budget revenue and expenditure allocation have been substantiated, and their semantic and value‑based foundations have been structured. The concept of “budget resources (revenues and expenditures)” has been introduced and defined in academic discourse; the definition of the term (terminological construct) “allocation of budget resources (revenues and expenditures)” has been formulated; and the definitions of other scientific terms in public finance have been clarified. Conclusions and Relevance. The provided substantiation of the essential characteristics of financial categories and concepts, as well as the clarification of definitions and the systematization of a nu…

title: Adaptive Religious Governance in Times of Crisis: Balancing Human Rights and Religious Freedom in Indonesia
abstract: Religious governance during times of crisis requires governments to respond to changing public risks while maintaining human rights and freedom of religion or belief. However, existing scholarship has often examined rights-based restrictions and institutional adaptation through separate analytical perspectives, leaving insufficient explanation of how contextual flexibility can operate without weakening consistent rights protection. This study examines how adaptive religious governance operates in Indonesia and how institutional adaptation can be reconciled with human rights and religious freedom. A qualitative document-based design with an interpretive analytical approach was employed, using the COVID-19 crisis as the primary empirical context. Data were drawn from national and subnational regulations, decrees, circulars, protocols, task-force instructions, official statements, and documents issued by religious authorities and organizations, supplemented by relevant scholarly and institutional literature. The materials were examined through qualitative content analysis, thematic coding, cross-document comparison, and chronological analysis. The findings reveal a shift from relatively uniform restrictions toward differentiated implementation, increasing interaction between national standards and local discretion, and an intermediary role for religious organizations in interpreti…
venue: AMUYA: INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT REVIEWS

title: Forecasting residential property values in Jinhua City, China: a machine learning framework integrating Gaussian process regressions
abstract: Purpose The Chinese real estate sector underwent a period of rapid growth during the previous decade, followed by a contraction phase commencing in late 2021. This structural transition, precipitated by dynamic macroeconomic shifts, has introduced significant complexities in property valuation forecasting for both regulatory authorities and market participants. The purpose of this study is to demonstrate the building of a machine learning model for addressing the complicated property price forecasting problem. Design/methodology/approach In response to these methodological challenges, this investigation uses Gaussian process regression (GPR) incorporating multiple kernel configurations and basis functions to systematically examine monthly residential price fluctuations in Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province, using a comprehensive data set spanning April 2015 through July 2024. Findings The modeling framework was developed through Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and rigorous cross-validation techniques, demonstrating robust predictive accuracy during the out-of-sample evaluation period (September 2022–July 2024), as evidenced by a relative root mean square error metric of 0.1165%. Originality/value The empirical outcomes provide substantive foundations for enhancing theoretical models of urban housing market dynamics while offering practical insights for policy formulation, eith…
venue: Journal of Financial Management of Property and Construction

title: Climate risk and health expenditure: extreme drought in herb-producing regions and the price of Chinese medicine
abstract: Introduction Climate risk is understood to raise health expenditure by increasing illness and the demand for care. A second route has received little attention. Botanical medicines are grown, so climatic stress where they are cultivated alters the cost of a medical input and may raise what households and insurers pay even when population health is unchanged. This study examines that route in China. Methods We assemble a monthly national price index for Chinese medicinal materials, official consumer price indices (CPIs) for Chinese medicine, Western medicine and medical services, and a provincial panel of household health expenditure. Climatic stress is measured as a standardized accumulated water deficit and weighted twice over the same events, by herb-producing area and by population, separating the input-cost route from the illness route. Estimation is by local projection with season-preserving permutation inference, supported by falsification, influence and confounding analyses. Results Extreme drought in herb-producing regions is associated with a rise in the wholesale price of medicinal materials of about 10–20 percent over 6–18 months and in the consumer price of Chinese medicine of about 2–4 percent. Western medicine and medical service prices show no comparable rise, and the same deficit weighted by population is unrelated to either. The association is robust to alterna…

title: Forecasting financial support for government institutions using artificial intelligence: The case study of museums
abstract: Subject. Forecasting the financial support of public institutions based on regional panel data of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. Objectives. To develop and test a methodology for forecasting the financial support of museums using artificial intelligence methods. Methods. A panel dataset of 85 constituent entities of the Russian Federation for 2018–2024 was compiled. Machine learning methods were applied, including gradient boosting, regularized linear models, and their ensembles. Hyperparameter tuning was carried out using an artificial intelligence agent (AI agent) based on the Qwen3.5‑27B language model. Thirty‑two computational experiments were conducted. Forecast accuracy was assessed using the median absolute percentage error (MdAPE); rolling validation was applied over four test years (2021–2024). Results. The gradient boosting model achieves an MdAPE of 8.1% across regions, outperforming the best naive forecast by 1.9 percentage points and the previous‑year forecast by 4.6 percentage points. The average MdAPE under rolling validation was 12%. For 64% of the regions, the forecast error does not exceed 15%. Infrastructure‑related characteristics of institutions (28.6%) and personnel‑related characteristics (22%) demonstrate the highest predictive power. A systematic tendency to underestimate forecasts for large regions was identified; this is driven by…

title: Methodology of forecasting the development of socio-economic systems of the Arctic multiethnic regions
abstract: Subject. Forecasting regional growth to ensure balanced sustainable development of the multiethnic regions of the Arctic zone of the Russian Federation. Objectives. Substantiation of the predictive potential of the ARIMA model in relation to the quantitative assessment and short–term forecasting of key indicators of the regional development of the ethnographic and economic systems of the Arctic polyethnic regions using the example of forecasting one of the indicators of traditional economic activity of indigenous peoples – the dynamics of reindeer herding in the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug. Methods. The initial processing and structural analysis of the time series were performed using the ARIMA method. Almon's method of distributed lags was used for short-term forecasting. Results. The analysis of the dynamics of the reindeer population in 1936–2025 was carried out and a forecast for 2026–2029 was made based on the application of the ARIMA method. Conclusions. The choice of autoregression models – integrated moving average – is determined by their ability to work with time series that demonstrate instability and seasonal fluctuations, which is especially important for Arctic socio-ecological systems with their pronounced cyclical nature and economic processes. The use of forecasting tools in the practice of territorial planning forms the institutional basis for achieving bal…

title: Unilever Indonesia: selling sustainability to price sensitive consumers
abstract: Learning outcomes Case overview/synopsis This case examines the tension between consumer attitudes and purchasing behaviour toward sustainable products in Indonesia, one of the world’s largest and most complex emerging markets. The organisational setting is PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk, a fast-moving consumer goods company; the case focuses on its Home Care division and covers the period from 2019–2024, with the decision point set at a quarterly strategy review in March 2025. The protagonist (the division’s Marketing Director, a pseudonymous composite character) must recommend, within thirty days, one of three strategic pathways: (A) a premium focus on affluent urban Green Pioneers; (B) value-based expansion toward price parity for mass market Pragmatic Adopters; or (C) a partnership-based approach with government and non-governmental organisations to reach rural and low-income consumers. Despite 79% of Indonesian consumers expressing willingness to pay premium prices for sustainable products, actual adoption remained below 25% in urban areas and below 10 percent in rural regions (Rakuten Insight, 2024), while Indonesia’s middle class contracted from 21.45% to 17.13% of the population between 2019 and 2024 (BPS-Statistics Indonesia, 2024). The case is designed for teaching in international marketing, consumer behaviour, sustainability management and emerging-market strategy. The c…

title: Explainable Industry-Aware Social Media Virality Prediction Using Temporal and Categorical Features
abstract: This study proposes an explainable, industry-aware machine learning framework to predict social media post virality using pre-publication metadata. Utilizing 528 observations (January 2025–February 2026) from Instagram and TikTok across the IT, F&B, and manufacturing sectors, virality was defined using a leakage-free 75th-percentile engagement threshold. Several classifiers, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost, and CatBoost, were evaluated using five-fold stratified cross-validation and time-based testing. Model interpretability was addressed using SHAP analysis, and optimal posting times were simulated via a marginal approach.During cross-validation, the categorical-only XGBoost achieved an F1-score of 0.4158 and ROC-AUC of 0.6046, while the operational simulation model (combined_main_no_client) yielded a lower F1-score of 0.3581. In chronological final-test evaluation (January–February 2026), the model suffered severe performance decay due to temporal covariate shift, dropping to an F1-score, Recall, and Precision of 0.2917, while missing 70.83% of actual viral cases. SHAP analysis identified month index and IT industry affiliation as the strongest predictive features. These findings highlight the challenges of pre-publication virality forecasting and emphasize the vulnerability of static classifiers to temporal shifts in low-sample environments.
venue: International Journal of Advances in Data and Information Systems

title: Transformer-based eye opening factor prediction in upgraded 32-channel DWDM networks
abstract: Abstract Eye opening factor (EOF) captures the combined effect of noise, dispersion, and nonlinearity at the receiver decision threshold. This work predicts EOF in a 32-channel DWDM system from physical link parameters alone, excluding optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) and Q-factor from the inputs. A reproducible closed-form model combining Gaussian-noise nonlinear interference, amplified spontaneous emission, direct-detection Q-factor, and dispersion- and PMD-induced eye closure generates 5,000 samples over 432 configurations (80–320 km, 8–32 channels, −5 to +10 dBm, 10–40 Gb/s, NRZ/RZ/DPSK). The link is upgraded with dispersion-compensating fiber (DCF), Raman amplification, variable optical attenuator (VOA) equalization, and idealized nonlinear compensation. Six regressors are compared. A Transformer with multi-head self-attention achieves the best held-out performance ( R 2 = 0.9928, RMSE = 0.0180). It is statistically tied with support vector regression under tenfold cross-validation and retains R 2 = 0.9930 when entire link configurations are withheld. Exact Shapley attribution identifies bit rate and residual chromatic dispersion as the dominant EOF determinants. A component ablation at 320 km shows that DCF is the enabling component, raising EOF from 0 to 0.745 at 10 Gb/s. At 40 Gb/s, only DPSK sustains BER < 10 −9 over 320 km, whereas NRZ and RZ reach this limit near…

title: Development and internal validation of a prediction model for new-onset macular oedema following vitrectomy for diabetic retinopathy: a single-centre retrospective analysis
abstract: Objective To develop and internally validate a compact model for estimating the 1-year risk of new-onset postoperative macular oedema in patients with diabetic retinopathy undergoing vitrectomy. Methods This single-centre retrospective cohort included 650 recorded patients treated from January 2023 to April 2025. The primary analysis comprised 607 patients with ascertainable 1-year outcomes, with one study eye per patient; 43 patients lost to follow-up were assessed separately. New-onset macular oedema required new intraretinal cystoid spaces and/or subretinal fluid on optical coherence tomography during postoperative days 30–365, together with central macular thickness ≥300 μm or an increase ≥30 μm from baseline. The five-predictor logistic model used pre-incision measurements and was fitted in all 607 patients. Internal validation used 1, 000 bootstrap resamples; a 32-candidate, 10-fold cross-validated least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) analysis with selection-inclusive bootstrap validation assessed the stability of the separate LASSO procedure. Results New-onset postoperative macular oedema occurred in 207 of 607 patients (34.1%). The apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.823 and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.818. The corresponding Brier scores were 0.159 and 0.163; the corrected calibration intercept and slope we…

title: Geometric fidelity dominates dynamic prediction accuracy in Bio-Inspired FWMAV wings: a validated 3D-DIC and FE modelling study
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to establish a noninvasive, high-fidelity workflow for capturing 3D geometry and structural dynamics of bio-inspired flapping wings, enabling accurate dynamic prediction for flapping-wing micro air vehicles (FWMAVs). Design/methodology/approach An integrated approach combining projected-speckle 3D digital image correlation (3D-DIC) with image-based finite element (FE) modeling is developed to generate digital twins of ultra-thin wings. Dragonfly hindwings serve as representative structures to compare conventional fluorescent sprayed speckles with a novel computer-generated projected-speckle method in terms of geometric accuracy, measurement noise, and mass loading. Findings The projected-speckle technique reduces 3D point-cloud noise by 37%, improves corrugation accuracy to within 3% of ground truth and adds no measurable mass. FE models from projected-speckle geometries predict the fundamental frequency within 2.1% of experiments (157 Hz versus 153.8 Hz) and achieve Modal Assurance Criterion values above 0.87 for bending and coupled modes, whereas sprayed-speckle-based models overestimate frequency and fail to capture torsional coupling. Inverse identification returns vein and membrane elastic moduli of 6.1 ± 1.2 GPa and 1.5 ± 0.3 GPa, respectively, showing that geometric fidelity dominates predictive accuracy. Originality/value This work introduces and…

title: MetaHARP: Meta-Learning-Driven Rapid Adaptation for Individual-Heterogeneity-Aware Behavioral Risk Prediction
abstract: Behavioral risk prediction increasingly relies on longitudinal signals from wearable devices, smartphones, online activities, and multimodal health records. However, individual behavioral patterns and risk-triggering mechanisms are highly heterogeneous, making population-level predictors difficult to adapt to new individuals with limited observations. This paper proposes MetaHARP, a meta-learning-driven rapid adaptation framework for individual-heterogeneity-aware behavioral risk prediction. MetaHARP treats each individual as a meta-task, encodes support observations into a heterogeneity prototype, retrieves adaptation priors from behaviorally similar individuals, and generates lightweight low-rank adapters for personalized risk prediction. An individual-conditioned calibration module is further introduced to improve the reliability of predicted risk probabilities. Experiments on four public behavioral and health-related datasets show that MetaHARP consistently outperforms recent time-series and foundation-model baselines in predictive performance, few-shot adaptability, probability calibration, and adaptation efficiency. These results demonstrate that heterogeneity-aware meta-adaptation provides an effective solution for personalized behavioral risk prediction.
venue: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence

title: A physics-guided NARX-inspired network for accurate roll and pitch prediction of quadrotor UAVs
abstract: Purpose To develop a lightweight and physically interpretable approach for accurate one-step quadrotor attitude prediction. The study aims to reduce the learning burden of purely data-driven models by incorporating first-order rotational kinematics into a NARX-inspired neural architecture while retaining the ability to learn nonlinear dynamics and modeling errors. Design/methodology/approach A Physics-Guided NARX-inspired (PG-NARX) architecture is proposed, combining learnable autoregressive state propagation, a trainable physics-guided kinematic branch initialized using first-order rotational kinematics, and a neural residual branch. The approach is evaluated using flight-wise partitioned PX4-Gazebo Software-in-the-Loop data. PG-NARX is compared with MLP, NARX-inspired, Persistence, and Kinematic baselines using an unseen test trajectory, computational measurements, and angular-velocity noise experiments. Findings PG-NARX achieves roll and pitch RMSE values of 0.0206 rad and 0.0098 rad, with corresponding R2 values of 0.9558 and 0.9880. Compared with the Kinematic baseline, it reduces clean-test roll and pitch RMSE by approximately 10.8% and 17.6%, respectively. The model contains 18,602 trainable parameters and achieves a measured inference latency of 0.2667 ms. Additional experiments indicate relatively consistent performance under zero-mean Gaussian angular-velocity noise. …

title: Real-time Evaluation and Anticipation of Causal disTillation early prediction for cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (REACT-01): study protocol for a single-center prospective randomized clinical trial
Hydrogen fuel cells for green shipping: A machine learning-based power prediction framework
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cells offer a promising route toward low-emission maritime electrification, but reliable prediction of electrical power is essential for their integration into shipboard energy-management systems. This study develops a compact, explainable machine-learning framework using 119 observations from a publicly available stationary hydrogen fuel-cell installation. Ambient, fuel-cell gas, and coolant outlet temperatures; power-generation and consumption setpoints; auxiliary consumption; and operating status were used to predict power supplied to the grid. Linear regression (LR) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were evaluated using a chronological 80:20 training–testing split, with parity plots, residual diagnostics, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) supporting model assessment. LR fitted the training observations closely (R² = 0.9960) but failed to generalize to testing data (R² = -33.8364; RMSE = 65.651). In contrast, XGBoost achieved consistent training and testing performance (R² = 0.9740 and 0.9770, respectively), with a testing RMSE of 1.687 and MAE of 1.273. SHAP identified auxiliary consumption (mean absolute SHAP = 9.82) and the power-consumption setpoint (2.45) as dominant predictive features. The analysis addresses grid-delivered power rather than propulsion demand or directly measured hydrogen utilization. The findings demonstrate the value of int…

title: Bridging Clinical Prediction and Workplace Exposure: A Data-Driven Risk Stratification and Prediction Model for Occupational Respiratory Diseases.
abstract: Abstract Occupational respiratory disease (ORD) surveillance remains largely reactive, with diagnosis often occurring only after clinically significant symptoms develop. Existing risk stratification tools are primarily clinically derived and rarely incorporate occupational exposure variables such as exposure intensity, duration, and workplace hazards, limiting early identification of at-risk workers. This review synthesizes current evidence on predictive modelling and risk stratification tools for respiratory diseases, evaluates their applicability to occupational health, and proposes a data-driven framework for proactive risk stratification. A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2021 and 2025. Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and free-text terms related to occupational respiratory diseases, predictive modelling, prognostic tools, and occupational exposure assessment were combined using Boolean operators. Extracted data included study characteristics, modelling approaches, predictors, and model performance metrics, which were narratively synthesized using thematic mapping. Of 618 records identified, six representative evidence approaches were retained for detailed comparative synthesis. Clinical models such as BODE and DOSE provided useful prognostic information but lacked occupational exposure parameters…

title: Construction cost prediction using TabPFN-based stacking model with SHAP analysis
abstract: Purpose Construction cost prediction is essential for improving budget management, risk reduction, and resource allocation in the construction industry. This study aims to enhance prediction accuracy by proposing a stacked ensemble model that integrates Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN), CatBoost, and Gradient Boosted Decision Trees “GBDT” while incorporating SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) value analysis for interpretability. Design/methodology/approach This study develops a two-layer stacking ensemble model using San Francisco building permit data, where Estimated Cost denotes the permit-declared pre-commencement cost estimate. TabPFN and CatBoost are used as first-layer base learners, and their out-of-fold predictions are combined with original project features as inputs to a second-layer GBDT meta-learner. Model performance is evaluated using 10 independent random train-test splits. In each run, the training set is used for leakage-controlled 5-fold cross-validation and model tuning, and final performance is reported as the mean ± standard deviation across the 10 runs. RMSE, MAE, and MAPE were employed in comparison with baseline models, and SHAP values are applied for model interpretation. Findings The proposed TabPFN + CatBoost-GBDT model achieves robust performance, with a MAPE of 1.89% for recorded permit-estimated costs. This indicates close alignment bet…

title: Comparing machine learning, principal component analysis and conventional regression for body weight prediction in Murrah buffaloes (Bubalus bubalis)
abstract: Context Body weight guides feeding, breeding, health and marketing decisions in buffaloes, but weighing large buffaloes on a scale is often impractical on smallholder farms, so weight is estimated from body measurements taken with a tape. Principal component analysis (PCA) combined with machine learning has been proposed for this task, though whether it predicts better than the simple methods already in use has not been tested. Aims To benchmark PCA-based machine learning against chest-girth regression, multiple linear regression and published buffalo equations for estimating body weight in Murrah heifers and adults. Methods Eleven morphometric traits and body weight were recorded on 62 heifers and 127 adult Murrah buffaloes. PCA was applied to the eleven traits with body weight excluded. Eight machine learning algorithms, together with multivariate adaptive regression splines, were trained on the principal components and on the raw traits using five-fold cross-validation repeated over resamples, with all transforms fitted inside each training fold and hyperparameters tuned within a nested loop. Model differences were tested with Friedman and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Key results Chest girth was most correlated with body weight (r = 0.93 heifers, 0.86 adults). The first principal component explained 76.8% (heifers) and 61.3% (adults) of trait variation. In heifers, multiple l…

title: Factors associated with self-care in older adults with heart failure presenting with composite and domain-specific intrinsic capacity impairment
abstract: Objective This study aimed to characterize intrinsic capacity (IC) impairment in older adults with heart failure and to investigate its association with self-care across composite and domain-specific domains. Methods This cross-sectional study recruited 215 patients with heart failure from two tertiary hospitals in Wuxi, China. IC was assessed across five domains in line with WHO guidelines: cognition, locomotion, vitality, sensory, and psychological. Self-care was evaluated using the Self-Care Heart Failure Index version 6.2. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation coefficients, multiple linear regression, and exploratory interaction analyses. Results Our study found that 99.5% of participants exhibited impairment in at least one IC domain, with the most common co-occurring impairment in cognition, vitality, and locomotor domains. Older age was significantly associated with poorer self-care maintenance (B = −0.37, 95% CI [−0.67, −0.07], P = 0.014), self-care management (B = −0.64, 95% CI [−1.02, −0.26], P = 0.001), and self-care confidence (B = −0.38, 95% CI [−0.77, −0.0004], P = 0.049). Higher educational level was significantly associated with better self-care maintenance (B = 9.80, 95% CI [3.87, 15.73], P = 0.001). A higher composite IC score was significantly associated with poorer maintenance (B = −2.81, 95% CI [−4.68, −0.95], P = 0.003) and l…

title: Waste-derived feedstocks and industrial microwave drying influence antioxidant capacity and immune-associated protein composition in black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens)
abstract: Abstract Black soldier fly larvae ( Hermetia illucens ) are increasingly used as a sustainable protein source in animal feeds. Beyond macronutrient value, black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) contain antioxidant compounds and immune-associated proteins that may contribute to their functional value. However, the extent to which rearing substrate and processing influence these components remains poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of feedstock and industrial microwave drying on antioxidant capacity and immune-associated protein composition in BSFL. Larvae were reared on three waste-derived feedstocks (fruit and vegetable waste, soy okara and brewer’s spent grain). Antioxidant capacity was measured using Folin-Ciocalteu, FRAP and DPPH assays. Immune-associated proteins and AMP candidates were characterised using LC-MS/MS proteomics. Industrial microwave drying was evaluated relative to freeze-drying. Antioxidant capacity differed significantly among feedstocks (ANOVA, ). Brewer’s spent grain increased total phenolic content and reducing capacity, while fruit and vegetable waste resulted in the highest radical scavenging activity. Total immune protein richness did not differ among diets; however, immune functional composition varied significantly (PERMANOVA, R 2 = 0.907, ). Larvae reared on fruit and vegetable waste showed increased representation of immune effector p…

title: Digital metanational capacity and liability of outsidership: bounded complementarity in SME international performance
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether and when digital capability helps small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) cope with the liability of outsidership (LoO). Drawing on Metanational Theory and the Information Processing View, it conceptualises LoO as generating a metanational capability gap that constrains firms' ability to sense, mobilise, and operationalise dispersed international knowledge, and introduces Digital Metanational Capacity (DMC) as a digitally enabled capability for performing these functions despite limited foreign-market presence. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 257 middle managers of internationally active Vietnamese SMEs are analysed using PLS-SEM. Supplementary analyses include PLSpredict, CVPAT, Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA), Gaussian-copula, nonlinearity, and heterogeneity tests. Findings LoO is negatively and DMC positively associated with international performance, and DMC negatively moderates the LoO–performance relationship. The performance return to DMC is greatest when outsidership is low and contracts by roughly two-thirds between low and high levels of outsidership, supporting bounded complementarity rather than substitution. A median-split NCA suggests that the minimum level of DMC required for high performance is higher under stronger outsidership. DMC thus appears to become more necessary but less sufficient as outsidership in…

title: Optimization of BESS Capacity Based on Kubu Solar PV Output Variability to Support Energy Shifting and Reduce Fuel-Fired Power Plant Operations in the Bali Power System
abstract: This study is motivated by the high dependency of the Bali power system on oil-based generation, the significant difference in available generation capacity between daytime and nighttime, and the limited utilization of intermittent renewable energy. This research aims to analyze the variability of the Kubu solar power plant output and to determine the optimal capacity of a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) to enable Energy Shifting, as well as to improve system efficiency and flexibility. The method employs a quantile-based scenario approach to construct probabilistic scenarios, which are integrated into a stochastic optimization model with the objective of maximizing operational cost savings. In addition, this study utilizes Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze the relationships among key variables within the system. The results indicate that the proposed method is capable of producing a more representative and robust BESS capacity, while effectively reducing the operation of oil-based power plants through the utilization of solar energy during nighttime periods. The novelty of this study lies in the integration of actual solar output data with a scenario-based stochastic optimization approach, complemented by statistical analysis. The findings imply that BESS has strong potential to enhance system flexibility and support a sustainable ene…

title: Mapping the architecture of innovation capacity in MENA: a systemic fuzzy DANP analysis of interdependent drivers and causal pathways
abstract: Purpose This study aims to model the complex causal architecture and network interdependencies of national innovation capacity in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, moving beyond linear composite indices to identify key leverage points and systemic dynamics. Design/methodology/approach Using a Fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory-based Analytic Network Process (Fuzzy DANP) methodology, the authors analyze 25 indicators across five dimensions: human capital, institutional framework, knowledge creation, green innovation and market sophistication. As a proof of concept, they use a literature-informed influence matrix and a synthetic data set, constructed from realistic parameter ranges for 20 MENA economies, to enable the analysis of causal weights, net effects and influence networks. The model’s structural logic is benchmarked against the Global Innovation Index (GII). Findings The results illustratively reveal green innovation as the most influential dimension, followed by institutional framework and human capital. The analysis identifies regulatory quality, R&D expenditure and environmental taxes as pivotal net-cause variables. The causal mapping shows institutional framework and human capital as foundational drivers, while the network analysis visualizes a strong institutional-knowledge core and positions green innovation as a systemic integrator.…

title: Correction to “Unlocking the Capacity of Li−S Batteries via a Solvation-Mediated Trade-Off between Anode Stability and Cathode Kinetics”
K-12 Equity Directors seeking to build capacity for district equity work: a sociotransformative constructivist approach
abstract: Introduction The purpose of this study was to explore how K-12 Equity Directors seek to build capacity in others for district equity work. Methods Using a sociotransformative constructivist approach, we interviewed 20 Equity Directors in two U.S. states. Results Results indicate the Equity Directors sought to build capacity in others for equity work through engaging in conversations intentionally, collaborating in authentic activity, working towards a sense of equity consciousness, and illuminating social location. Discussion The results may assist other school district office leaders who may or may not have someone designated as an Equity Director to build capacity in others beyond the district office to engage in equity work.

title: The requirement for the person submitting the request for access to public information to have legal capacity
abstract: Prawo dostępu do informacji publicznej jest na tyle istotne, że znalazło swoje odzwierciedlenie w samej ustawie zasadniczej. W ustawie o dostępie do informacji publicznej wskazano literalnie, że „każdy” może to uprawnienie zrealizować. Natomiast, w doktrynie toczy się dyskusja na temat tego jak przywołane słowo „każdy” można rozumieć. Jeden z wątków tej debaty dotyczy tego, czy również osoby nieposiadające zdolności do czynności prawnych mogą samodzielnie występować z wnioskiem o udostępnienie informacji publicznej. title: Mechanism by which NCOA4 promotes osteoarthritis progression through iron overload-induced mitochondrial dysfunction in chondrocytes
The influence mechanism of coffee brand image design on consumers' purchase intention: a mixed–methods study based on the S–O–R theory
abstract: Purpose Grounded in the S–O–R framework, this study examines how design–related stimuli and brand identification are associated with consumers' purchase intention, both directly and through brand loyalty and brand–lifestyle congruence in the chain coffee context. Design/methodology/approach An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was adopted. Structural equation modeling and bootstrapped mediation analysis were applied to 372 valid questionnaires to test direct and indirect relationships, while semi–structured interviews with 16 consumers were used to interpret the underlying mechanisms. Findings The quantitative results show that brand visual symbols, brand identification, and brand design perception are positively associated with brand loyalty, brand–lifestyle congruence, and purchase intention. Brand loyalty and brand–lifestyle congruence are also positively associated with purchase intention. Bootstrapping further showed that brand loyalty and brand–lifestyle congruence significantly mediated all six indirect relationships between the three antecedents and purchase intention. Qualitative findings helped explain these pathways and suggested that consumption purpose, price sensitivity, and product quality may shape the relevance of brand design. Originality/value This study extends the S–O–R framework in the chain coffee context by distinguishing specific brand visual …

title: Regulatory Mechanism of Melon Fruit Morphology Based on Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Analysis
Novel Insights into the Regulatory Mechanism of the Sweet-Fruity Aroma Quality of Flavored Black Tea Based on Metabolomics and Molecular Docking
abstract: Abstract To address the pronounced bitterness, astringency, and lack of sweet-mellow taste and floral-fruity aroma in summer–autumn black tea, yellow peach, Wonhwang pear, and Yinhongli plum juices were added during fermentation. Sensory evaluation, physicochemical analyses, volatile profiling, and molecular docking were used to investigate the sweetness-modulating mechanisms of these Rosaceae fruits. Yellow peach and Wonhwang pear markedly improved the sweet-mellow mouthfeel and fruity aroma, lowering the polyphenol-to-amino acid ratio from 3.79 (water-added control) to 3.46 and 3.10, respectively, increasing free amino acids (up to 3.41%), and moderately reducing tea polyphenols. Yinhongli plum introduced an undesirable sourness. The odor activity values of sweet-fruity compounds such as linalool (up to 65.06) and phenylacetaldehyde were significantly elevated and correlated positively with sensory scores. Molecular docking showed that linalool, phenylacetaldehyde, and methyl salicylate bind strongly to the T1R2/T1R3 sweet taste receptor (binding energies −6.0 to −4.7 kcal/mol) via hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions with residues including GLN237, LEU223, and LEU242. These findings preliminarily elucidate the molecular basis by which Rosaceae fruits enhance the sweet-mellow flavor of summer–autumn black tea, providing a theoretical foundation for quality control and …

title: Role and mechanism of ribosomal protein S3 in tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance in chronic myeloid leukemia
abstract: Introduction Resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) remains a major cause of treatment failure in chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). This study investigated the role of ribosomal protein S3 (RPS3) in TKI resistance and its association with NF-κB signaling. Methods Exploratory RNA sequencing and an RNA-binding protein database were used to prioritize a candidate for subsequent clinical expression and functional analyses. RPS3 expression was examined in an independent clinical cohort and resistant cell models. RPS3 knockdown and pharmacological modulation were used to evaluate drug sensitivity, apoptosis, cell cycle distribution, and NF-κB-associated signaling. Results RPS3 was upregulated in clinical samples from patients with TKI resistance or poor responses and in resistant cell models. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that RPS3 expression discriminated between resistant/poor-response patients and good responders in the validation cohort. RPS3 knockdown lowered imatinib and nilotinib IC 50 values, with increased apoptosis and G 0 /G 1 -phase arrest following TKI exposure. These effects were accompanied by reduced p65 phosphorylation, a lower p65 nuclear/cytoplasmic fluorescence ratio, and decreased MCL-1 and BCL-XL mRNA levels. TNF-α treatment increased TKI tolerance and reduced TKI-induced apoptosis in RPS3-knockdown cells, whereas co-treatment with BAY…

title: Integrated equilibrium model for electrified logistics and power systems
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated equilibrium model to characterize the complex interactions between electrified logistics systems and electric power delivery systems. The model consists of two major players: an electrified logistics operator (ELO) and a power system operator (PSO). The ELO aims to maximize its profit by strategically scheduling and routing its electric delivery vehicles (e-trucks) for deliveries and charging, in response to the locational marginal price (LMP) set by the PSO. The routing, delivery, and charging behaviors of e-trucks are modeled by a perturbed utility Markov decision process (PU-MDP) while their collective operations are optimized to achieve the ELO's objective by designing rewards in the PU-MDP. On the other hand, PSO optimizes the energy price by considering both the spatiotemporal e-truck charging demand and the base electricity load. The equilibrium of the integrated system is formulated as a fixed point, proved to exist under mild assumptions, and solved for a case study on the Hawaii network via Anderson's fixed-point acceleration algorithm. Along with these numerical results, this paper provides both theoretical insights and practical guidelines to achieve sustainable and efficient operations in modern electrified logistics and power systems.

Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning based demand response and energy management for heavy industries with discrete manufacturing systems
abstract: Energy-centric decarbonization of heavy industries, such as steel and cement, necessitates their participation in integrating Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and effective Demand Response (DR) programs. This situation has created the opportunities to research control algorithms in diverse DR scenarios. Further, the industrial sector’s unique challenges, including the diversity of operations and the need for uninterrupted production, bring unique challenges in designing and implementing control algorithms. Reinforcement learning (RL) methods are practical solutions to the unique challenges faced by the industrial sector. Nevertheless, research in RL for industrial demand response has not yet achieved the level of standardization seen in other areas of RL research, hindering broader progress. To propel the research progress, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL)-based energy management system designed to optimize energy consumption in energy-intensive industrial settings by leveraging dynamic pricing DR schemes. The study highlights the creation of a MARL environment and addresses these challenges by designing a general framework that allows researchers to replicate and implement MARL environments for industrial sectors. The proposed framework incorporates a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) to model energy consumption and production processes w…

title: Energy poverty and children’s subjective well-being: evidence from young lives data
abstract: This study examines the impact of energy poverty on the subjective well-being of children in four developing countries: Ethiopia, India, Peru, and Vietnam. We assess energy poverty using a multidimensional approach, leveraging data from the Young Lives study, which conducted surveys in 2006, 2009, 2013, and 2016 (Rounds 2 to 5). Our analysis focuses on the young cohort (Rounds 3 to 5) and the older cohort (Rounds 2 to 5), as these rounds include questions on children’s subjective well-being. To mitigate potential endogeneity concerns and establish causal relationships, we employ a two-stage least squares regression, using residential electricity prices at the country level as an instrumental variable. Our findings reveal that energy poverty significantly reduces children’s subjective well-being, with boys and older children more affected. Robustness checks confirm the validity of these results. Additionally, we find that health status mediates the impact of energy poverty on children’s well-being, highlighting the importance of targeted policy interventions.

title: Market-oriented operational strategy for biomass-geothermal combined power generation and hydrogen production plant
Capacity remuneration mechanisms for decarbonized power systems
abstract: Motivated by generation system adequacy concerns, many European countries have introduced capacity remuneration mechanisms (CRMs) to ensure sufficient investments in power generation . However, it is uncertain whether the existing CRMs will promote sufficient adequacy and flexibility in a decarbonized power system , where supply and demand will become more weather-dependent. We assess the effectiveness of a centralized capacity market, a strategic reserve , and a decentralized capacity market via capacity subscriptions in a climate-neutral, weather-driven power system. We develop a co-simulation of two agent-based models simulating myopia in both operational and investment decisions. We simulate weather uncertainty by running the model with 40 different weather years. Our results from a case study based on the Netherlands indicate that a strategic reserve may increase electricity price volatility in the long-term. A centralized capacity market is more cost-effective than a strategic reserve, but administratively setting its parameters is prone to over- or underprocurement. Capacity subscription allows consumers to select their desired level of reliability. Results indicate that these decentralized capacity markets may yield a clearer signal for the needed dispatchable capacity and promote demand-side response, but it may be challenging to provide long-term certainty for investo…

title: Local energy monitoring to support smart energy management and decarbonized town development
abstract: Introduction With the increase in variable renewable energy and liberalization of the electricity retail market, the integrated energy management of demand and supply has become crucial, complementing traditional energy-saving efforts. Therefore, high-resolution energy demand-side information, accounting for household attributes and owned equipment, is essential. However, previous studies have identified energy consumption based on surveys of utility bill payments; this approach does not provide detailed, hourly data on electricity demand, which changes over time owing to lifestyle patterns and weather conditions. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the actual electricity consumption in residential buildings in Shinchi Town using the developed electricity monitoring system.Material and Method In support of regional disaster recovery initiatives, we developed a regional information and communication technology (ICT) system as a network interface for residents. As part of a social experiment, network terminals of the local ICT system were distributed to approximately 100 households in the town. Power monitoring data were collected via equipment installed in home distribution boards and centrally managed by a cloud server.Results and Conclusion We analyzed electric power consumption patterns, focusing on household attributes, seasonal variations in hot-water-supply device usage, an…

title: Impact of Regional and Seasonal Characteristics on Battery Electric Vehicle Operational Costs in the U.S.
abstract: This study investigates the operational cost competitiveness of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) in the United States, considering regional climates, energy prices, and driving patterns. By comparing BEVs with plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), and the alternative use of BEVs and conventional vehicles (Convs), the analysis incorporates thermal dynamometer tests, real-world vehicle miles traveled (VMT), and state-specific energy prices. Using detailed simulations, the study evaluates energy consumption across varying temperatures and driving distances. The findings reveal that, while BEVs remain cost-effective for short trips in moderate climates, PHEVs are more economical for long-range trips and cold environments, due to the excessive cost of using external direct current fast chargers (DCFCs) and reduced BEV efficiency at low temperatures. HEVs are identified as the most cost-efficient option in regions like New England, characterized by high residential electricity prices. These insights are critical for shaping vehicle electrification strategies, particularly under diverse regional and seasonal conditions, and for advancing policies on alternative energy and fuels.

title: Sharing the shortfall: Algorithmic solutions for fair demand curtailment in zonal power markets
Online Multivariate Regularized Distributional Regression for High-dimensional Probabilistic Electricity Price Forecasting
abstract: Probabilistic electricity price forecasting (PEPF) is vital for short-term electricity markets, yet the multivariate nature of day-ahead prices - spanning 24 consecutive hours - remains underexplored. At the same time, real-time decision-making requires methods that are both accurate and fast. We introduce an online algorithm for multivariate distributional regression models, allowing efficient modeling of the conditional means, variances, and dependence structures of electricity prices. The approach combines multivariate distributional regression with online coordinate descent and LASSO-type regularization (absolute shrinkage and selection operator), enabling scalable estimation in high-dimensional covariate spaces. Additionally, we propose a regularized estimation path over increasingly complex dependence structures, allowing for early stopping and avoiding overfitting. In a case study using historical data from the German day-ahead market, the proposed method yields interpretable and well-calibrated joint prediction intervals for the 24-dimensional price distribution and provides robust performance across a range of proper scoring rules. The results underscore the importance of modeling the dependence structure of electricity prices. Furthermore, we analyze the trade-off between predictive accuracy and computational costs for batch and online estimation and provide a high-pe…
